# tosijs-3d

> Declarative 3D/XR framework built on Babylon.js and the tosijs web component framework.

---

# tosijs-3d

[github](https://github.com/tonioloewald/tosijs-3d/) | [live demo](https://3d.tosijs.net) | [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tosijs-3d)

<div style="text-align: center; margin: 20px">
  <img style="width: 280px; height: 280px;" alt="tosijs-3d logo" src="https://3d.tosijs.net/favicon.svg">
</div>

**tosijs-3d is a library for building 3D web apps** — and standalone apps, if
that is what you want. Under the hood it uses Babylon.js for rendering, glTF/GLB
for models and the usual bitmap formats for textures — but it also leans on
**SVG**, for textures and for the entire user interface.

Free and open source, and light for what it is (Babylon is not small; this
adds little to it). Scenes are composed from **web components**, so a world is
markup you can read:

```javascript
b3d(
  b3dSun(),
  b3dSkybox({ timeOfDay: 6 }),
  b3dLoader({ url: './scene.glb' }),
  b3dWater({ y: -0.2 })
)
```

The [doc site](https://3d.tosijs.net) has about a hundred live demos you can
edit in place; the [b3d page](https://3d.tosijs.net/tosi-b3d/) is that scene
running.

## Getting started

```bash
npm install tosijs-3d tosijs @babylonjs/core @babylonjs/gui @babylonjs/loaders @babylonjs/materials
```

Babylon (`^9`) and `tosijs` (`^1.9.2`) are peer dependencies: you install
them, so there is exactly one copy of the engine in your app. `jolt-physics`
is an optional peer, needed only if you use `b3dPhysics`.

A first scene, with no model file to find:

```javascript
import { b3d, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dGround, b3dBox, b3dSphere } from 'tosijs-3d'

document.body.append(
  b3d(
    b3dSun(),
    b3dSkybox({ timeOfDay: 10 }),
    b3dGround({ size: 24, texture: 'checker' }),
    b3dBox({ x: -1.5, y: 0.5, color: '#c8553d' }),
    b3dSphere({ x: 1.5, y: 1, diameter: 2, color: '#ffd166' })
  )
)
```

Give `tosi-b3d` a size in CSS (`tosi-b3d { width: 100vw; height: 100vh }`) and
you have a lit scene with shadows and an orbit camera. Then:

- **Your own model:** [b3d-loader](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-loader/) takes a
  GLB; name suffixes on its meshes (`_collide`, `_mirror`, `_nocast`) set how
  they behave.
- **Something to drive:** a [character](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-biped/), a
  [car](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-car/) or an
  [aircraft](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-aircraft/), inside an
  [input focus](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-input-focus/) so keyboard, gamepad,
  touch and VR controllers all work.
- **A world:** [terrain](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-terrain/),
  [water](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-water/) and a
  [sky](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-skybox/); [Land and
  Sky](https://3d.tosijs.net/land-and-sky/) is all of it at once.
- **Controls that work in a headset:** the `scenePanel` hook on
  [b3d](https://3d.tosijs.net/tosi-b3d/) and the
  [widget set](https://3d.tosijs.net/widgets3d/).

## Four things you may not have seen in a 3D library

**Flat 3D and VR are the same app.** You can enter and leave an immersive
session without the simulation resetting — the scene, the physics and your
place in the world all survive the transition, because nothing is torn down to
make it.

**One user interface, in three places.** The SVG-powered widget set renders
identically as a DOM overlay, on a plane inside a 3D scene, and in VR. Not three
implementations that drift — one, with three presentations, where any divergence
is treated as a bug.

**One control system, every input.** Keyboard and mouse, gamepads, VR
controllers and touch all arrive as the same `ControlInput`. You write the
behaviour once; supporting a new device is a new provider, not a rewrite.

**The simulation is testable without a GPU.** The flight model, the combat
maths, the world state and the layout engine are deliberately Babylon-free,
deterministic, and unit-tested — so the interesting logic can be exercised in
milliseconds rather than in a browser.

## Finding things

**Search the [attribute index](https://3d.tosijs.net/attributes.txt)** before
assuming a capability does not exist — one greppable line per attribute,
generated from source on every build. There is a [JSON
form](https://3d.tosijs.net/attributes.json) for tools, and both ship **inside
the package**, so an agent already in a consumer project reads
`node_modules/tosijs-3d/static/attributes.txt` with no network.

It exists because the recurring adopter failure is not a missing feature, it is
a feature that ships, is documented, and cannot be found: three issues in one
week turned out to be capability that was already there. One `grep water` finds
`submersible`; reading two hundred doc pages does not.

**Upgrading?** See [Migration](https://3d.tosijs.net/Migration/) for the
breaking changes and what to do about them, and the
[Changelog](https://3d.tosijs.net/CHANGELOG/) for the full detail, one page per
version. Both ship inside the package (`Migration.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` with
its `changelog/` folder), so they work from `node_modules` too.

## Highlights

**Procedural astronomical objects** — [planets](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-planet/),
[stars and star systems](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-star-system/),
[galaxies](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-galaxy/), and
[black holes](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-black-hole/) with accretion disk, photon
ring and lensing. Generated, not modelled — a solar system is a few attributes.

**Procedural terrain** — [streaming LOD terrain](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-terrain/)
with a [biome shader](https://3d.tosijs.net/biome-chart/) that runs one material
from seafloor to mountain, a floating origin so worlds can be large, and
[carved landforms](https://3d.tosijs.net/sdf-lattice/) — volcanoes with lava
tubes bored through them, arches, caverns.

**Biped control** — a [character controller](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-biped/)
with an animation state machine and follow/XR cameras, from a GLB: walk, run
and sprint, jump, swim, climb ledges, and hold a gun that
[points where you aim](https://3d.tosijs.net/aim-ik/), crouched or standing.
[Crowds](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-crowd/) of thousands are drawn on the GPU,
and each figure can be moved, turned and re-clipped.

**Any character on one animation library** — [retargeting](https://3d.tosijs.net/retarget/)
plays the Universal Animation Library's clips on a Mixamo, Kenney or
Blender-named rig, A-pose or T-pose. A mesh with no skeleton at all is
[auto-rigged](https://3d.tosijs.net/rig-build/) from eight markers, fingers and
tail found from its shape and bound by bone heat. Hair, tails and capes hang on
[spring bones](https://3d.tosijs.net/spring-chain-babylon/). The
[rig tool](https://3d.tosijs.net/rig-tool/) does it in the browser and saves a
recipe a game applies in one call, and an editor can mount it in its own scene.

**Effects as data** — an [effect](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-effect/) is
particles, light and sound as layers on one clock, with one `activity` dial (a
volcano dormant, semi-active or erupting is one recipe). Presets for
volcanoes, geysers, explosions, fireballs, splashes and sparks; sprites and
sounds generated, no files. The [effect tool](https://3d.tosijs.net/effect-tool/)
edits them live.

**Vehicles and a city to drive them in** — a [car](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-car/)
and a [tank](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-tank/) on one
[pure vehicle model](https://3d.tosijs.net/ground-vehicle/) (springs, tyre grip,
skid steer; no physics engine), with a chase camera that orbits, booms up to
overhead and climbs over what is in its way, flat and in a headset. A
[procedural city](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-city/) of Kenney's kits with
traffic, street lights, lit windows and their sound;
[City Drive](https://3d.tosijs.net/city-drive/) and
[Cross Country](https://3d.tosijs.net/cross-country/) are the demos.

**Aircraft control** — a [forgiving flight model](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-aircraft/)
that flies like a drone below transition speed and like a plane above it, with
VTOL, bank-to-turn, a HUD and radar.

**One UI for flat, in-scene and VR** — the [widget set](https://3d.tosijs.net/widgets3d/)
renders as a DOM overlay, as a texture on a surface in the scene, and as a
floating panel in a headset, from the same declaration. Includes a
[flowing box model](https://3d.tosijs.net/box/), [menus and panels](https://3d.tosijs.net/surface/),
a data table, and an on-screen keyboard — because a headset has nowhere to type.
A [system bar](https://3d.tosijs.net/system-bar/) of buttons and
[cascading menus](https://3d.tosijs.net/bar-menu/) sits in the corner flat and
up ahead in VR.

**SVG textures** — [draw with SVG](https://3d.tosijs.net/svg-texture/), use it as
a live texture. Designer artwork becomes a HUD, a gauge, or a control surface
without a round-trip through a bitmap.

...and a few things that are less visible but are why the rest works:

**Every input device behind one interface** — keyboard/mouse, touch, hardware
gamepads and XR controllers all produce the same `ControlInput`, so an entity is
driven identically by a thumbstick, a glass pad, or an AI. Vehicle enter/exit and
input focus come with it. Most frameworks hand you the input surface and wish you
luck.

**Simulation that doesn't know about the renderer** — a pure, deterministic
world store with a documented contract, so an external driver (a narrative
engine, a test, a headless run) can drive a world the simulation never had to
anticipate.

**Adaptive by default** — a device-capability probe vends per-tier budgets, and
performance-sensitive settings resolve to `auto` rather than to a number that is
always wrong for something. A Quest and a workstation get different worlds.

**A character core for any engine** — the character creator's working parts
(body, shape, rig, retargeting, hair, clothes, the character file) are
[engine-free subpaths](https://3d.tosijs.net/character-core/), so a three.js app
or a server imports them without Babylon.

**Pure models, actually tested** — the flight model, ballistics, guidance, biome
classification, layout and text editing are engine-free and unit-tested (about
3,900 tests, run in about a minute with no GPU). If it can be a function of its inputs,
it is.

## Development

Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh).

```bash
bun install
bun tls     # once: local HTTPS certificates (needs mkcert)
bun start   # the doc site and dev server, rebuilding on change
bun test
```

The dev server runs on https://localhost:8030.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/

# Getting started

**From nothing to a lit scene you can walk around, then where to go next.**

## Install

```bash
npm install tosijs-3d tosijs @babylonjs/core @babylonjs/gui @babylonjs/loaders @babylonjs/materials
```

Babylon (`^9`) and `tosijs` (`^1.9.2`) are peer dependencies: you install them,
so your app has exactly one copy of the engine. `jolt-physics` is an optional
peer, needed only for [b3d-physics](/b3d-physics/).

## A first scene

No model file needed. This is the whole app, running:

```js
import { b3d, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dGround, b3dBox, b3dSphere } from 'tosijs-3d'

preview.append(
  b3d(
    b3dSun(),
    b3dSkybox({ timeOfDay: 10 }),
    b3dGround({ size: 24, texture: 'checker', textureTiles: 12 }),
    b3dBox({ x: -1.5, y: 0.5, color: '#c8553d' }),
    b3dSphere({ x: 1.5, y: 1, diameter: 2, color: '#ffd166' })
  )
)
```
```css
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

In your own page, append to `document.body` instead of `preview`, and give the
element a size in your CSS (`tosi-b3d { width: 100vw; height: 100vh; }`).

`b3d(...)` creates a `<tosi-b3d>` element, which owns the engine and the scene;
everything nested inside it adds itself when the scene is ready and removes
itself when it leaves the page. You get an orbit camera, shadows, and (on a
device that supports it) an Enter VR button, without asking. The
[Primitives](/b3d-primitives/) page has more of these shapes.

## The same scene as markup

The functions are element creators, so the scene is also plain HTML: no
script beyond importing the library once. An attribute is the property's name
in kebab case (`timeOfDay` is `time-of-day`); `shadows="off"` on the sun
would turn its shadows off:

```html
<tosi-b3d style="width: 100%; height: 100%">
  <tosi-b3d-sun></tosi-b3d-sun>
  <tosi-b3d-skybox time-of-day="14"></tosi-b3d-skybox>
  <tosi-b3d-ground size="24" texture="checker" texture-tiles="12"></tosi-b3d-ground>
  <tosi-b3d-box x="-1.5" y="0.5" color="#3d7ac8"></tosi-b3d-box>
  <tosi-b3d-sphere x="1.5" y="1" diameter="2" color="#7bd166"></tosi-b3d-sphere>
</tosi-b3d>
```

(The afternoon sky and the colours are changed only so you can tell the two
apart.) In your own page, `import 'tosijs-3d'` once from your bundle; that
defines the elements, and markup that is already there comes to life.

## Then what

| You want | Start at |
| --- | --- |
| Your own model | [b3d-loader](/b3d-loader/) loads a GLB. Mesh name suffixes (`_collide`, `_mirror`, `_nocast`) set behaviour: [Material Conventions](/b3d-utils/) |
| Something to drive | [b3d-biped](/b3d-biped/), [b3d-car](/b3d-car/) or [b3d-aircraft](/b3d-aircraft/), inside a [b3d-input-focus](/b3d-input-focus/) so keyboard, gamepad, touch and VR controllers all work |
| A world | [b3d-terrain](/b3d-terrain/), [b3d-water](/b3d-water/), [b3d-skybox](/b3d-skybox/). [Land and Sky](/land-and-sky/) is all of it at once |
| Controls that work in a headset | The `scenePanel` hook on [b3d](/tosi-b3d/), built from [widgets3d](/widgets3d/) |
| Things that blow up | [Combat](/combat/) |
| A world something else drives | [World Sim](/world-sim/) |

## Finding a capability

Search the [attribute index](https://3d.tosijs.net/attributes.txt) before
deciding something is not there: one line per attribute of every element,
generated from source. It also ships in the package, at
`node_modules/tosijs-3d/static/attributes.txt`.

## How the pages are organised

Each section lists the **elements** you put in a scene. Tucked under an element
are the pure models and helpers it is built from (the flight model under the
aircraft, the biome chart under the terrain). You can use those directly, and
they are where the tests are, but you do not need them to get started.

Coming from an earlier version? [Upgrading](/upgrading/) has the migration
notes and the changelog.

# Biped Playground

**A place to run around and murder things in.** One call returns a whole
arena — ground, light, cover, crates, a catwalk and something to shoot — as
ordinary scene children, so it composes into any demo rather than being one.

```js
import { assetUrl, b3d, b3dBiped, b3dLauncher, b3dLibrary, button3d, characterStore, holdGrip, inputFocus, playground, select3d, studioEnvironment, ualAnimationStates, WORKING_CHARACTER } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'
import { demoLoadout } from 'tosijs-3d/demo-utils'

// TONIO'S WEAPONS (CC BY 4.0), the character builder's: every one is made
// the same way (origin at the grip, +Y up the grip, +Z forward, real size), so
// one grip holds them all, and the blades another. (Line comments in this
// demo: a block comment inside a fence would close the enclosing doc comment.)
const weapons = b3dLibrary({
  url: assetUrl('tonio/weapons-classic/weapons.glb', 2),
  type: 'weapons',
})
// Where the hand holds each one: the character builder's defaults, placed
// with its manipulator in the hand's socket frame (x/y/z is the grip).
// One grip per class of item (hold-grip): every one-handed blade alike.
const gripFor = (name) => {
  const { scale, ...grip } = holdGrip(name)
  return grip
}
// What each one is in the inventory (slot tags, mass, its picture), and for the
// guns how it fires. Only guns are raised: UAL's ranged clips are Pistol_*,
// so the rifles are fired from a one-handed stance. Anything else is a melee
// weapon (`holdingWeapon`): on guard, and the trigger swings it.
const WEAPONS = {
  Pistol: { tags: ['side', 'hand'], mass: 1, art: 'pistol', fire: { fireRate: 6, muzzleSpeed: 45, damage: 25, projRadius: 0.08, gravity: -2 } },
  SMG: { tags: ['side', 'hand'], mass: 2.5, art: 'pistol', fire: { fireRate: 14, muzzleSpeed: 50, damage: 12, projRadius: 0.06, gravity: -2 } },
  'Assault Rifle': { tags: ['back', 'hand', 'two-handed'], mass: 3.5, art: 'rifle', fire: { fireRate: 9, muzzleSpeed: 80, damage: 20, projRadius: 0.06, gravity: -1 } },
  'Rocket Launcher': { tags: ['back', 'hand', 'two-handed'], mass: 7, art: 'rifle', fire: { fireRate: 0.8, muzzleSpeed: 25, damage: 120, projRadius: 0.16, gravity: -1 } },
  Dagger: { tags: ['side', 'hand'], mass: 0.4, art: 'knife' },
  'Short Sword': { tags: ['side', 'hand'], mass: 1, art: 'sword' },
  'Long Sword': { tags: ['side', 'hand'], mass: 1.5, art: 'sword' },
  'Hand and a Half': { tags: ['back', 'hand', 'two-handed'], mass: 2, art: 'sword' },
  'Plasma Blade': { tags: ['side', 'hand'], mass: 1, art: 'sword' },
  Spear: { tags: ['back', 'hand', 'two-handed'], mass: 2, art: 'sword' },
  Buckler: { tags: ['back', 'hand'], mass: 2.5, art: 'shield' },
}

// ONE LAUNCHER, carrying whatever is in your right hand. `socket` parents it
// to the hand BONE, so it follows the animation, and with a socket x/y/z/rx/
// ry/rz are the grip in the hand's frame. Swapping the item swaps its model.
const gun = b3dLauncher({
  library: 'weapons', meshName: 'Pistol',
  socket: 'right-hand',
  ...gripFor('Pistol'),
  ...WEAPONS.Pistol.fire,
  ammo: 999, reloadRate: 40, projColor: '#ffdd66',
})

// A QUATERNIUS UAL RIG, not omnidude, and the arena is the reason rather than
// the animation count. Every height in here is authored against a 1.8m person:
// the low wall is 1.1 so that crouching hides you and standing does not, and
// the crates are 0.4 / 0.9 / 1.6 to sit either side of what `mantle` will
// attempt. omnidude measures 0.88m — the 1.1m "crouch cover" is taller than he
// is, and the 0.9m "mantle" crate is over his head — so the playground could
// not demonstrate the one thing it was built to demonstrate.
//
// The wider clip set is the bonus: `Jog_Bwd_Loop` and the `Crouch_*` clips give
// a real backwards jog and a crouch to sneak in.
//
// OR A CHARACTER YOU BUILT: the settings panel lists the characters the
// character builder saved in this browser, and picking one swaps the hero for
// a biped made from it (`characterDoc`), carrying what you hold across.
const MANNEQUIN = 'UAL mannequin'
const makeHero = (doc, at) => b3dBiped(
  {
    ...(doc ? { characterDoc: doc } : { url: assetUrl('quaternius/UAL1_core.glb', 3) }),
    animationStates: ualAnimationStates(),
    // WHERE THE ARENA IS IN FRONT OF YOU. Spawning at the origin put `pillar-b`
    // (0, -12.3) literally touching your muzzle line, so every shot from the
    // start hit it — which is precisely what "just cause explosions in front of
    // me" was. From here the cover line is 22m ahead with the low wall to the
    // left and the railing to the right, which is the comparison the arena is
    // built around, and there is room to see a round travel.
    x: at.x, z: at.z, ry: at.ry ?? 0,
    player: true, cameraType: 'follow',
  },
  gun
)
let hero = makeHero(null, { x: -4, z: 10 })

// THE INVENTORY says what you hold: the loadout (a button on the system bar)
// starts with the pistol on your hip and the rest in the bag. Whatever is in
// your right hand is what the launcher carries; a gun in hand is up (aim and
// fire), anything else is held with the weapon down. The weapon button draws
// from the hip or back, or puts away what is in hand; dragging works too.
const loadout = demoLoadout({ catalogue: WEAPONS, equip: { right_side: 'Pistol' } })
const body = (slot) => ({ holder: 'hero', container: 'body', slot })
const slotsNow = () => loadout.inv.doc.holders.hero.containers.body.slots
const inRight = () => slotsNow().hand_right.holds
const wire = (h) => {
  h.whenWeapon = () => {
    const held = inRight()
    // Put away: the first place it goes (a hip, then the back).
    const away = ['right_side', 'left_side', 'back']
    if (held) {
      const to = away.find((s) => !slotsNow()[s].holds && !loadout.inv.check({ item: held, to: body(s) }).length)
      if (to) loadout.inv.move({ item: held, to: body(to) })
      return
    }
    // Draw: what is on the right hip, then the left, then the back.
    const from = away.map((s) => slotsNow()[s].holds).find(Boolean)
    if (from) loadout.inv.move({ item: from, to: body('hand_right'), swap: true })
  }
  return h
}
const hold = (h) => {
  const id = inRight()
  const w = id ? WEAPONS[id] : null
  if (w && gun.meshName !== id) {
    Object.assign(gun, gripFor(id), w.fire ?? {}, { meshName: id })
    gun.reloadModel()
  }
  h.holdingWeapon = w != null && w.fire == null
  h.setGunplay(w?.fire != null)
}
wire(hero)
loadout.inv.subscribe(() => hold(hero))

// The characters saved in this browser, and swapping the hero for one. The
// figure open in the character builder is one of them, under its own label.
const store = characterStore()
const BUILDER = 'from the character builder'
const stored = (name) => (name === BUILDER ? WORKING_CHARACTER : name)
const { playChar } = tosi({ playChar: { pick: MANNEQUIN } })
let saved = []
const listSaved = (host) =>
  Promise.all([store.list(), store.get(WORKING_CHARACTER).catch(() => null)]).then(([names, working]) => {
    const all = working ? [BUILDER, ...names] : names
    if (all.join() === saved.join()) return
    saved = all
    host?.refreshScenePanel?.()
  }).catch(() => {})
listSaved()
const useCharacter = async (name) => {
  const doc = name === MANNEQUIN ? null : await store.get(stored(name)).catch(() => null)
  // Gone (forgotten, or another browser's): the menu says who you are.
  if (name !== MANNEQUIN && !doc) { playChar.pick.value = MANNEQUIN; return }
  // Where the hero is now and which way he faces, so the new one takes over there.
  const was = hero.entries?.rootNodes[0]
  const p = was?.position
  const yaw = was?.rotationQuaternion?.toEulerAngles().y ?? 0
  const at = p ? { x: p.x, z: p.z, ry: (yaw * 180) / Math.PI } : { x: -4, z: 10 }
  const next = wire(makeHero(doc, at))
  hero.replaceWith(next)
  hero = next
  hold(next)
  playChar.pick.value = name
  try { localStorage.setItem('playground-character', name) } catch {}
}
// Who you play: the builder's "play in Biped Playground" (`?character=…`),
// else the one you picked last time, else the mannequin.
const asked = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('character')
let last = null
try { last = localStorage.getItem('playground-character') } catch {}
const start = asked ? (asked === WORKING_CHARACTER ? BUILDER : asked) : last
if (start && start !== MANNEQUIN) useCharacter(start)
else playChar.pick.value = MANNEQUIN

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      style: 'width:100%;height:100%',
      // Something for the weapons' metal to reflect: without it a PBR metal
      // has nothing to show and renders nearly black.
      sceneCreated(el) {
        studioEnvironment(el.scene, { sky: '#7d9cc4', horizon: '#e8e4da', ground: '#55604a' })
      },
      // The glass pad shows only what this demo USES. These are control names,
      // not a mapping name (`gamepad: 'biped'` names nothing and draws nothing).
      // Move, aim, shoot, jump, sneak, sprint; `Y` switches first/third person.
      // Clicking the left stick sneaks, the right one raises the weapon.
      gamepad:
        'left_stick,right_stick,left_stick_click,right_stick_click,A,B,X,Y,right_bumper,left_bumper,left_trigger,right_trigger',
      // Not armed on load. Right bumper (or the on-screen RB) raises and lowers
      // the weapon.
      scenePanel: (host) => {
        listSaved(host)
        return [
          select3d({
            label: 'character',
            value: playChar.pick,
            options: [MANNEQUIN, ...saved],
            handleChange: (name) => useCharacter(String(name)),
          }),
          button3d({
            label: 'make your own character…',
            handleClick: () => { location.href = '/character-builder/' },
          }),
        ]
      },
    },
    weapons,
    ...playground(),
    ...loadout.panels(),
    inputFocus(hero)
  )
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

**Two modes, and the right bumper (or clicking the right stick) is the
switch.** You start with a pistol on your hip and the rest of
[Tonio's weapons](/character-builder/) in the bag: open the loadout from its
button on the system bar and drag any of them onto a hip, your back or your
right hand. With the weapon down you are walking: **R** sprints. Press **right
bumper** and you draw what is on your hip (or back), and if it is a gun it
comes up: now **R** fires, **Q** aims down the sights, and a ring shows where
the round will actually land, sinking as the range grows because it is the
real ballistic arc rather than a dot in the middle of the screen. You cannot
sprint with the gun up, which is why the trigger is free to do both jobs.
Each gun fires its own way (the SMG fast, the rocket launcher slow and heavy).
A blade, the spear or the buckler takes a guard (UAL's `Sword_Idle`) and **R**
swings it (`Sword_Attack`, played through; held, it swings again). Press the
bumper again to put away what is in your hand. Only the right hand is drawn.

**WASD** moves, **arrow keys** look, **space** jumps, **left shift** sneaks,
**E** interacts, **Y** switches between third and first person. On a pad,
clicking the left stick sneaks.

**Play as a character of your own.** Make one in the
[character builder](/character-builder/) (or press **make your own
character…** in this page's settings panel, the goggles on the bar) and press
**play in Biped Playground** there, or save it and pick it from **character**
here. It takes the hero's place where he stands, holding what you held. Characters
belong to the browser that made them.

Things to try: put the pistol in the bag and try to raise it (nothing to raise), drag the rifle into your hand (it comes up, and both hands are taken); carry a sword on your hip and draw it; swim and dive in the pool; climb the crates onto the catwalk; shoot from behind the low wall
and watch the ring disappear behind it until you stand; walk the cover line and
compare the railing with the wall beside it.

## Using it

It is a list of scene children, so it spreads into a scene of your own:

```javascript
b3d(
  { style: 'width:100%;height:100%' }, // your own scene options
  ...playground(),
  inputFocus(hero)
)
```

Every piece in here exists to exercise something the biped can do, and the
arrangement is a test you walk around in rather than one you read.

## What each part is there to prove

| | exercises |
| --- | --- |
| the **low wall** (1.1m) | crouch cover — `stanceFor` says crouch, and crouched you are fully hidden |
| the **pillars** | cover you can lean past on either side — `peekSide` returns `both` |
| the **bunker** (an L) | cover from a threat the wall does not face, which is why `shelterFrom` searches an arc |
| the **railing** | cover that ISN'T. Same height, same distance, gap underneath. The one everybody's first implementation gets wrong |
| the **crate steps** (0.4 / 0.9 / 1.6m) | the band between a step and a wall — `mantle` |
| the **catwalk** | verticality, a firing position, and something to fall off |
| the **targets** | something to murder |
| the **pool** | swimming, diving (aim down and swim), surfacing, and a shelving ramp to walk in on slowly |

## Everything is an ELEMENT, deliberately

No `sceneCreated` hook, no `el.make` calls, no imperative build step — the
playground is a list of scene children, which means a caller can splice it,
override a piece, or take half of it. It also means the whole arena is already
in the shape a data format would want: *"the standard arena, plus the thing I am
showing you"* can be one line of data.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/playground/

---

# Solar System

Our own solar system, built from the parts the rest of this site documents:
every planet and moon a [planet](/b3d-planet/), the giants banded and
ringed ([gas-giant](/gas-giant/)), the rocky worlds and moons drawn by
[rocky-world](/rocky-world/)'s looks (the Moon, Mercury, Mars, Venus, Io,
Titan, ice moons), Phobos, Deimos, Vesta and Pallas as lumpy rocks, and an
asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

Pick a body under **look at** and the camera follows it round its orbit.
Switch on **real maps** and the Earth, the Moon and Mars are drawn from NASA's
and NOAA's own height and colour maps instead of being made up.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, b3dStarSystem, spaceBackdrop, SOL, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, select3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { sol } = tosi({
  sol: { maps: false, focus: 'Earth', animate: true, showOrbits: true, belt: 1500, time: 3600 },
})

const system = b3dStarSystem({ scale: 5, orbitScale: 3, animate: 'on', showOrbits: 'on', maps: 'off', beltCount: sol.belt.value, timeScale: sol.time })
// Our own system, as data, instead of a star from the galaxy.
system.system = SOL

sol.maps.observe(() => {
  system.maps = sol.maps.value ? 'on' : 'off'
  system.regenerate()
})
sol.belt.observe(() => {
  system.beltCount = sol.belt.value
  system.regenerate()
})
sol.animate.observe(() => (system.animate = sol.animate.value ? 'on' : 'off'))
sol.showOrbits.observe(() => {
  system.showOrbits = sol.showOrbits.value ? 'on' : 'off'
  system.updateOptions()
})

// Simulated time per real second, in the unit that reads best.
const perSecond = (v) =>
  v < 60 ? `${v.toPrecision(2)} s/s`
  : v < 3600 ? `${(v / 60).toPrecision(2)} min/s`
  : v < 86400 ? `${(v / 3600).toPrecision(2)} h/s`
  : `${(v / 86400).toPrecision(3)} days/s`

// Every body, inmost first: the star, each planet then its moons, the belt.
const names = [
  SOL.star.name,
  ...SOL.planets.flatMap((p) => [p.name, ...(p.moons ?? []).map((m) => m.name)]),
  ...(SOL.belt ?? []).map((b) => b.name),
]

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      clearColor: '#000000',
      scenePanelOpen: true,
      panelTitle: 'Solar System',
      scenePanel: () => [
        select3d({ label: 'look at', value: sol.focus, options: names }),
        toggle3d({ label: 'real maps (Earth, Moon, Mars)', value: sol.maps }),
        toggle3d({ label: 'orbit', value: sol.animate }),
        // Real time up to a year every ten seconds.
        slider3d({ label: 'time', value: sol.time, min: 1, max: 3.16e6, scale: 'log', format: perSecond }),
        toggle3d({ label: 'show orbits', value: sol.showOrbits }),
        slider3d({ label: 'belt rocks', value: sol.belt, min: 0, max: 6000, step: 250 }),
      ],
      sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
        const camera = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera('sol', -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI / 2.6, 40, BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(), el.scene)
        camera.lowerRadiusLimit = 1
        camera.upperRadiusLimit = 900
        camera.minZ = 0.05
        camera.maxZ = 6000
        camera.wheelDeltaPercentage = 0.02
        camera.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
        el.setActiveCamera(camera)
        // FOLLOW THE CHOSEN BODY: ease onto it every frame, and on choosing,
        // pull in to a few of its radii.
        let following = ''
        let around = 0
        el.scene.onBeforeRenderObservable.add(() => {
          const body = system.bodies.find((b) => b.name === sol.focus.value)
          if (body == null) return
          const at = body.node.getAbsolutePosition()
          // In place: ASSIGNING an orbit camera's target keeps the camera
          // where it is and changes its distance instead.
          BABYLON.Vector3.LerpToRef(camera.target, at, 0.15, camera.target)
          // Where round the Sun the body is. The camera turns with it, so
          // the light on the body stays where it was (and dragging still
          // orbits it): a fixed camera slid onto the night side as it went.
          const now = Math.atan2(-at.z, -at.x)
          if (sol.focus.value !== following) {
            following = sol.focus.value
            camera.radius = Math.max(2, body.radius * 7)
            // Come in from the sunlit side (the Sun is at the centre).
            if (at.length() > 0.01) camera.alpha = now + 0.5
          } else if (at.length() > 0.01) {
            let turn = now - around
            if (turn > Math.PI) turn -= Math.PI * 2
            if (turn < -Math.PI) turn += Math.PI * 2
            camera.alpha += turn
          }
          around = now
        })
      },
    },
    // A little fill, so a night side is not a hole in the stars.
    b3dLight({ intensity: 0.12 }),
    // The star sky, without a sun: the Sun is the system's own star. TILTED
    // AS IT REALLY IS: the planets orbit about 60.2 degrees to the galaxy's
    // plane. The sky's galaxy is baked level with its centre along -X, so a
    // turn about X tips the band and leaves the centre on the line where the
    // two planes cross (the real one is 5.5 degrees south of the ecliptic).
    ...spaceBackdrop({ sky: '/sky', sun: false, tilt: '60.2,0,0' }),
    system
  )
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

## What is true and what is not

- **True:** the order of the planets and moons, their relative sizes (squeezed
  by a square root so the small ones are still visible), which moons go with
  which planet, and with real maps on, the ground of the Earth, the Moon and
  Mars.
- **Squeezed:** distances, on a log scale, or the planets would be specks a
  screen apart (see [b3d-star-system](/b3d-star-system/)).
- **True:** every period. Each planet's day and year and each moon's month
  are the real ones (Venus and Uranus turn backwards, Triton goes round
  backwards); the **time** slider says how fast they run, from real time to a
  year every ten seconds. Fast, a day is too quick to see; slow, a year
  barely moves.
- **Exaggerated:** the asteroid belt. The real one is so sparse that from
  inside it you would see nothing.
- **Made up:** every surface without a map. The looks are right in kind
  (Io's sulfur, Titan's haze, Saturn's rings), not in detail.

The system itself is the data in `SOL` (see [b3d-star-system](/b3d-star-system/)); give a star system your own
`SystemSpec` to draw another.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/solar-system/

# Weapon Fit

**Dial a weapon into a character's hand and copy out the numbers.** A biped, a
weapon library, and a panel of coordinates wired to the thing you are looking
at — so placement is something you SEE rather than something you compute.

```js
import { assetUrl, b3d, b3dBiped, b3dLauncher, b3dLibrary, b3dManipulator, b3dGround, b3dLight, b3dSkybox, b3dSun, inputFocus, ualAnimationStates, euler3d, vector3d, select3d, label3d, button3d, toggle3d, slider3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { orbitCam } from 'tosijs-3d/demo-utils'

const weapons = b3dLibrary({
  url: assetUrl('kenney/libraries/weapon-pack.glb'),
  type: 'weapons',
})

const gun = b3dLauncher({
  library: 'weapons', meshName: 'pistol',
  socket: 'right-hand',
  x: -0.04, y: 0.051, z: -0.059,
  rx: -105, ry: -15, rz: -165,
  modelScale: 0.86,
  muzzleSpeed: 45, fireRate: 6, ammo: 999, reloadRate: 40,
})

const hero = b3dBiped({
  url: assetUrl('quaternius/UAL1_core.glb', 3),
  animationStates: ualAnimationStates(),
  player: true, cameraType: 'none',
})
hero.append(gun)

// A PLAIN OBJECT, not a bound tosijs leaf.
//
// The first version bound these and read them back with `.valueOf()` inside the
// change handler — which produced a weapon that flipped upside down and ignored
// whatever you typed, because it was applying something that was not the number
// on screen. The widgets already hand the new value to `handleChange`; taking it
// from there removes the question entirely.
//
// It still survives a panel rebuild, because `panel()` reads `fit` when it runs
// and `fit` outlives the panel.
const fit = { name: 'pistol', x: -0.04, y: 0.051, z: -0.059, rx: -105, ry: -15, rz: -165, scale: 0.86 }

const apply = () => {
  gun.x = fit.x; gun.y = fit.y; gun.z = fit.z
  gun.rx = fit.rx; gun.ry = fit.ry; gun.rz = fit.rz
  gun.modelScale = fit.scale
}

const n = (v) => Math.round(v * 1000) / 1000
const snippet = () =>
  `b3dLauncher({\n  library: 'weapons', meshName: '${fit.name}',\n` +
  `  socket: 'right-hand',\n` +
  `  x: ${n(fit.x)}, y: ${n(fit.y)}, z: ${n(fit.z)},\n` +
  `  rx: ${n(fit.rx)}, ry: ${n(fit.ry)}, rz: ${n(fit.rz)},\n` +
  `  modelScale: ${n(fit.scale)},\n})`

// DRAG IT, do not type it: fine-tuning a position by typing numbers is
// miserable. The manipulator targets the LAUNCHER ELEMENT rather than
// its mesh, which matters: an element owns its transform and `render()` rewrites
// the mesh from `x/y/z`/`rx/ry/rz` every frame, so a gizmo that moved the mesh
// directly would be undone before you let go. `b3d-manipulator` already knows
// that and writes the attributes.
const gizmo = b3dManipulator({
  target: 'tosi-b3d-launcher',
  move: 'on',
  turn: 'on',
  size: 0.09,
  // READ THE ELEMENT BACK, do not read the transform.
  //
  // The transform the gizmo hands you is in WORLD space and names its angles
  // `rx/ry/rz`, not `x/y/z`. Taking position from it put world coordinates in a
  // snippet whose numbers are meant to be local, and taking rotation from the
  // wrong keys gives `rx: NaN, ry: NaN, rz: NaN` next to a position plausible
  // enough to trust.
  //
  // The element has already been written by the time this fires, and it holds
  // exactly the numbers the snippet needs. Ask it.
  whenChange: () => {
    fit.x = gun.x; fit.y = gun.y; fit.z = gun.z
    fit.rx = gun.rx; fit.ry = gun.ry; fit.rz = gun.rz
  },
  whenCommit: () => { scene && scene.refreshScenePanel && scene.refreshScenePanel() },
})

const panel = () => [
  label3d({ text: 'Weapon fit' }),
  select3d({
    label: 'weapon', value: fit.name,
    options: weapons.getNames ? weapons.getNames().filter((w) => !w.startsWith('ammo')) : ['pistol'],
    handleChange: (v) => { fit.name = v; gun.meshName = v; gun.reloadModel() },
  }),
  label3d({ text: 'offset from the joint (metres)', muted: true }),
  vector3d({
    value: { x: fit.x, y: fit.y, z: fit.z }, step: 0.01, scrub: 0.002,
    handleChange: (v) => { fit.x = v.x; fit.y = v.y; fit.z = v.z; apply() },
  }),
  label3d({ text: 'rotation (degrees)', muted: true }),
  euler3d({
    value: { x: fit.rx, y: fit.ry, z: fit.rz }, step: 5, scrub: 0.5,
    handleChange: (v) => { fit.rx = v.x; fit.ry = v.y; fit.rz = v.z; apply() },
  }),
  slider3d({
    label: 'scale', value: fit.scale, min: 0.4, max: 1.6, step: 0.01, showValue: 'always',
    handleChange: (v) => { fit.scale = v; apply() },
  }),
  toggle3d({
    label: 'rotate (off = move)', value: gizmo.turn === 'on' && gizmo.move === 'off',
    handleChange: (v) => { gizmo.turn = v ? 'on' : 'off'; gizmo.move = v ? 'off' : 'on' },
  }),
  button3d({
    label: 'copy snippet',
    handleClick: () => { navigator.clipboard && navigator.clipboard.writeText(snippet()) },
  }),
  label3d({ text: 'pose: aiming — the stance placement must look right in', muted: true }),
]

const scene = b3d(
    {
      style: 'width:100%;height:100%',
      scenePanelOpen: true,
      scenePanel: panel,
      sceneCreated(el) {
        // In FRONT of him, close: placement errors are invisible over the shoulder.
        orbitCam(el, { alphaDeg: -49.9, betaDeg: 74.5, radius: 1.6, target: [0, 1.3, 0] })
        // WAIT FOR THE CLIPS, do not guess a delay. A fixed timeout can fire
        // before the rig finishes loading, after `setAnimationState` has
        // settled on `idle`, and nothing re-evaluates it, so the character
        // holds a pistol in his walking pose.
        //
        // (Line comments: a block comment inside a fence would close the
        // enclosing doc comment.)
        const ready = setInterval(() => {
          const groups = hero.entries && hero.entries.animationGroups
          if (!groups || !groups.some((g) => /Pistol_Idle_Loop/.test(g.name))) return
          clearInterval(ready)
          hero.setGunplay(true)
          hero.setAnimationState('idle')
          apply()
        }, 250)
      },
    },
    b3dSkybox({ timeOfDay: 10 }),
    b3dSun({ shadowMaxZ: 30, activeDistance: 20 }),
    b3dLight({ intensity: 0.7, groundColor: '#55604a' }),
    b3dGround({ meshName: 'ground_nocast', width: 20, height: 20, color: '#7f8a6c' }),
    weapons,
    gizmo,
    inputFocus(hero)
)

preview.append(scene)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

## Why the numbers are not multiples of 90

They look like they should be. Both conventions ARE axis-aligned — a weapon is
authored barrel-along-+Z, and this rig's hand bone measures as an identity
rotation against its parent (`bindX [1,0,0]`, `bindY [0,1,-0.02]`,
`bindZ [0,0.02,1]`). So a quarter turn ought to do it.

It does not, and the reason is which frame the correction is actually against.
The weapon hangs on the hand, and the hand's orientation is the whole arm chain
composed — shoulder, elbow, wrist, each with its own bind rotation and its own
pose on top. None of those are round, so their product is not either. The clean
candidate, `-90, 0, 180`, aligns the barrel and the sights to the hand's own axes
by dot product, and puts the pistol through the wrist on screen.

Which is an argument for `_grip` rather than a quirk to live with. A `_grip`
node is authored IN THE WEAPON, so the offset it declares is measured in the
weapon's own frame — and the correction collapses to identity no matter what the
arm is doing. The round numbers are available; they are just not available from
this end.

## Why a tool

Placement is six numbers per weapon per rig, and it needs tuning for every mesh,
which is what makes it a tool rather than a constant. There is no single correct
offset: it depends on the weapon's own origin (Kenney authors
props bottom-centre, not by the grip), on the rig's hand frame (this one has +Y
forward and +Z up, so a barrel-along-+Z weapon needs a quarter turn), and on the
stance the character holds it in.

## The camera is close on purpose

It opens two and a half metres from the character's hands, because that is the
distance at which placement errors are visible. A weapon that reads fine over
the shoulder can be through the wrist close up, or pointing at the sky: invisible
in third person, unmissable down the sights.

## What to do with the numbers

`copy snippet` gives you a `b3dLauncher` call with the offsets baked in. Better
still, the offsets belong in the MODEL, as a `_grip` node carrying position and
orientation, so one asset is right for every consumer instead of every consumer
discovering it again. For assets without one, this is where the numbers come
from.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/weapon-fit/

# hold grips

**One grip per kind of thing held, not per item.** A pistol and an SMG are
held the same way, and so are a dagger and a long sword, so where the hand
holds an item is set for its CLASS: adjust the grip on one sword and every
one-handed blade follows.

| class | held like | Tonio's weapons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pistol` | a handgun, one hand | Pistol, SMG |
| `rifle` | a long gun, two hands | Assault Rifle |
| `heavy` | on the shoulder | Rocket Launcher |
| `melee1h` | a blade, one hand | Dagger, Short Sword, Long Sword, Plasma Blade |
| `melee2h` | a long blade or a pole, two hands | Hand and a Half, Spear |
| `bow` | a bow | |
| `shield` | on the forearm | Buckler |

```javascript
import { holdClassOf, holdGrip } from 'tosijs-3d'

holdClassOf('Long Sword') // 'melee1h'
holdGrip('Long Sword') // { x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, scale }: the class's default
holdGrip('Long Sword', { melee1h: { ry: 170 } }) // with your adjustment
```

A grip is the item's grip point and turn in the hand's socket frame (metres
and degrees; see [[character-builder]]'s Hold). An item not in the table is
held as a `pistol`; pass your own table as `classes` to name a library's. Only the
`pistol` and `melee1h` defaults were placed by hand; the others start from the
nearest of those two until someone places them.

Pure: no DOM, no Babylon.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/hold-grip/

---

# hand socket

**Where a hand holds things, on any rig.** A hand bone's axes are the rig
maker's choice, so a grip dialled in against one rig's bone holds the item at
a wrong angle on another. A hand's SOCKET is a frame under the hand set by its
ANATOMY instead (the forearm's direction, the thumb's side), calibrated so
that on UAL's mannequin it is the hand bone itself. A grip (see
[[hold-grip]]) is a point and a turn in that frame, so one set of numbers
holds an item the same way in every hand.

This is the arithmetic, with no engine. `handSocket` in
[[b3d-launcher|the launcher]] runs it on a Babylon skeleton (the character
builder's Hold), and `riggedBodyGlb`'s `held` option on an exported body, so
the socket in a file is where the builder shows it.

```javascript
import { socketWorld, gripMatrix, gripPoint, mat4Multiply } from 'tosijs-3d/hand-socket'

// Joint positions in the scene's frame (Babylon's, left-handed).
const socket = socketWorld('r', hand, lowerarm, thumb)
const grip = mat4Multiply(gripMatrix({ x, y, z, rx, ry, rz }), socket)
gripPoint(itemPositions) // the middle of the item's lowest third
```

Matrices are Babylon's layout: 16 numbers, row-major, for ROW vectors
(`p' = p·M`, so `a·b` is a then b). A grip's turn is Babylon's
`Quaternion.FromEulerAngles(rx, ry, rz)` in degrees (yaw about y, then pitch
about x, then roll about z).

Pure: no DOM, no Babylon.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/hand-socket/

---

# Rig tool

**Put a character on our animations, give it hair or a tail, and save the
result.** Pick one of the demo characters or load your own GLB. Check which
bone plays which role, hang spring chains on it, and try it with any of the
Universal Animation Library's clips, beside the mannequin they were made on.
Save the recipe: `applyRigRecipe` puts the same rig on the same model in a
game.

```js
import { rigTool } from 'tosijs-3d/rig-tool'

preview.closest('tosi-example')?.style.setProperty('--tosi-example-height', '600px')
preview.append(rigTool())
```

## Using it

It opens standing still in its REST pose (a T or an A), in the front view.
A mesh with no skeleton of its own (an OBJ, or a GLB without one, like the
weasels and the space marine) gets UAL's fitted to it from eight red
**markers** on its body, Mixamo's way: drag each onto its joint (chin,
groin, elbows, wrists, knees). They start where they are guessed from the
outline. A model with a skeleton of its own shows a dot on the bone each
**role** uses instead: tap a dot (it turns yellow), then the body where that
bone is.

`view` snaps to a face (front, back, left, right, top, bottom), which is how
you line a marker, joint or handle up with the flesh, and stands it still;
`free` orbits. Turn on `animate` (or pick a clip) to see it move: a mesh
whose markers or joints moved is bound to them again then (binding takes a
second or two and shows nothing at rest). In a headset you are the camera,
so the view only switches between still and playing.

The panel has these sections, its job first.

- **Markers**, for a mesh bound from them. `symmetry` moves both sides
  together; `tail` adds a tail (place its tip from the side view; it is a
  bone chain, `tail_01` on, for a spring); `guess markers` starts again from
  the outline; `spread fingers` lays both hands out afresh from the wrists
  (a glove guessed into a knot), each finger apart, and shows the joints to
  drag into place. `hands` says how much hand is rigged: thumb and four
  fingers, a mitten (a thumb and one finger, for a glove: the other fingers
  lie on it and take no skin) or none (the hand alone); `as found` leaves it
  to the fit. The joints follow the markers. The fit puts each marker's
  joint at the middle of the body's thickness (the pelvis behind the
  thighs, as the mannequin's is); from the side view, drag a marker forward
  or back to set its depth. The depth is kept as an offset from the fit, so
  it stays when the marker moves again from the front. `move joints` shows every
  joint (blue) to drag by hand from the view that suits: shoulders from the
  front, fingers and thumbs from the top, feet from the side. What hangs from
  a joint comes with it; set `dragging` to turn what hangs from it instead
  (a hand or foot at an angle). Each finger's and thumb's tip (orange) pulls
  its finger: the joints after its first turn and stretch about the first,
  so the finger keeps its curl and reaches where you drop the tip. Markers
  and moved joints are saved in the
  recipe as `binding`.
- **Roles**, for a model on its own skeleton: which bone is the hips, the
  head, the left forearm, each finger joint. They are guessed from the
  names; fix one by tapping, as above, or pick a role and then the bone that
  plays it, or `(none)` to leave it out. Set `clicking sets` to the chain and
  a tap hangs the chosen spring chain there instead.
- **Motion.** `animate` and the clip; `floor` moves the body up or down
  from where its soles stand (they are put on the floor at rest, and kept
  there as a clip plays), for one that still floats or sinks; `arm space`
  turns the arms out from the body, for a character whose arms are long for
  its height; `foot turn` turns both feet in or out in every clip, for a
  body modelled with its feet turned out (a foot's turn at rest is the
  body's own, so it walks splay-footed otherwise);
  `load animations…` adds the clips in a GLB made on another rig to the
  list: Mixamo's, a mocap file's, another library's. Which bone is which is
  read from the names (UE, Mixamo, Kenney and Blender spellings), so each
  clip is retargeted onto the character, and onto the mannequin to compare.
  Mixamo downloads are FBX, which a browser cannot read: import them into
  Blender and export a GLB (with the skin).
- **View.** `view`; `mannequin` shows UAL's mannequin (a ghost) playing the
  original beside it; `bones` draws the skeleton.
- **Model.** A demo character, or `load model file…` for a GLB or OBJ of
  your own (a single file: a `.gltf` with separate buffers cannot be opened
  this way). It should face +Z, standing, arms out or down. A model with a
  skeleton of its own can `use its own skeleton`, or be bound from markers
  like any mesh.
- **Springs.** `+ strand` hangs a new chain with a tube from a bone (a
  ponytail): lay out its path with the orange handles (`+ point` for another
  beyond the tip), choose how many `links` it has (they are spaced evenly
  along the path), size it, and tune how it swings. A straight one can also
  be set by `offset`, `yaw`, `pitch` and `length`. `+ bone chain` simulates
  bones the model already has (a tail): pick the chain's first bone.
  Stiffness and damping change live; the rest rebuild the chain.
- **Recipe.** `save` downloads the recipe as JSON, `load` reads one back,
  `copy` puts it on the clipboard. The working recipe is also kept in this
  browser, per model, so a reload does not lose it.

## A recipe in a game

```
import { applyRigRecipe, readSkeleton, retargetClip } from 'tosijs-3d'

const rig = applyRigRecipe(scene, root, skeleton, recipe)
const walk = retargetClip(ualWalk, readSkeleton(ualSkeleton, ualRoot), rig.read, {
  scene,
  armSpaceDeg: recipe.armSpaceDeg,
  footTurnDeg: recipe.footTurnDeg,
})
walk.start(true)
```

The element `rigTool()` returns carries `.rig`: `recipe` (get a copy, set
one to apply it), `applied` and `load(model)`, for a page or an editor
driving the tool.

`rig.problems` lists anything in the recipe the model does not have (a bone
renamed since it was saved), and `rig.springs` the live chains, whose
`bones.params` can be changed while it runs.

## In an editor: mounting it in your scene

`mountRigTool(b3d, options)` opens the tool in a `<tosi-b3d>` you already
have: an editor opens it on a character and keeps the recipe
in its own document.

```javascript
import { mountRigTool } from 'tosijs-3d/rig-tool'

const tool = mountRigTool(scene, {
  models: [{ label: 'hero', url: '/hero.glb' }],
  recipe: doc.recipe, // start from the document's
  files: false, // no save / load / copy, nothing kept in the browser
  stage: false, // no floor or light: the scene's own lighting
  camera: editorCamera, // driven, and put back exactly on unmount
})
tool.addEventListener('change', (e) => preview(e.detail.recipe))
tool.addEventListener('commit', (e) => doc.record(e.detail.recipe)) // an undo step
// …
tool.unmount() // everything it added goes; safe to call twice
```

- **`change`** fires on every edit, **`commit`** once per finished gesture
  (a release on its panel or in the scene, a role assigned), each with a copy
  of the recipe.
- **Undo and redo** (the arrows at the top of its panel, ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z) step
  through those commits, markers and binding included; the body is bound
  again when you animate or press done. Each model has its own history.
- **Its panel is a system panel** (a button on the system bar, beside the
  host's), with the view's camera menu beside it.
- **`unmount()`** removes every mesh, material, texture, observer and panel it
  added, also if it is called while the first model is still loading, and
  restores the camera it was given: angles, distance, target, projection and
  limits. Without a camera it brings its own and puts the active one back.
- `tool.api` is the same API as the page's `.rig`; setting `api.recipe`
  applies it without echoing a `change`.

**Rigging one body for a host** (the [character builder](/character-builder/)
does this): give it `handleDone` and the panel has **done** and **cancel**
at its top. Done unmounts the tool and hands the callback the rig: the
`recipe`, and the `body` bound from its markers (a
[rigged body](/rigged-body/), ready for `buildBody` and `applyRigRecipe`).

```javascript
mountRigTool(scene, {
  models: [{ label: 'body', url: '/body.glb' }],
  recipe: { version: 1, binding }, // bind from these markers
  files: false,
  handleDone: ({ recipe, body }) => wear(body, recipe),
  handleCancel: () => {},
})
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/rig-tool/

---

# Effect tool

**Make an effect: particles, light and sound on one clock.** Start from a
preset (a volcano at any activity, a geyser, a splash, an explosion, a
fireball, sparks), change any layer and see it at once, then save the recipe
for `<tosi-b3d-effect>` to play in a game.

```js
import { effectTool } from 'tosijs-3d/effect-tool'

preview.closest('tosi-example')?.style.setProperty('--tosi-example-height', '600px')
preview.append(effectTool())
```

## Using it

Tap the scene once so the browser lets it make sound.

- **Effect**: the preset, `play` (a one-shot plays again), `stop`, the
  `activity` dial (a volcano: dormant, semi-active, erupting), `mute`, and
  `listen from`: how far away you are (in a headset the effect moves away
  from you instead). Sound travels at 343 m/s, so at 300 m an explosion's
  boom comes almost a second after its flash. `time of
  day` shows the lights at night.
- **Layers**: choose one and change it. Particles: how many, how long they
  live, how fast and big, gravity, wind, height, the first and last colour.
  `picture` swaps the sprite for your own image or SVG (embedded in the
  recipe, so a saved one carries it). A light: its colour, intensity, range
  and flicker. A sound: its voice,
  gain and pitch. Every layer: when it starts and how long it lasts.
- **Recipe**: `save` downloads the recipe as JSON, `load` reads one back,
  `copy` puts it on the clipboard, `start over` goes back to the preset. The
  working recipe is kept in this browser, per preset.

The element carries `.effect`: `recipe` (a copy; set one to play it) and
`player`, for a page or an editor driving the tool.

## In an editor: mounting it in your scene

`mountEffectTool(b3d, options)` opens the tool in a `<tosi-b3d>` you already
have, on the same contract as the rig tool's `mountRigTool`:

```javascript
import { mountEffectTool } from 'tosijs-3d/effect-tool'

const tool = mountEffectTool(scene, {
  recipe: piece.recipe,
  target: piece.node, // where it plays
  files: false, // the host keeps the recipe
  stage: false, // no ground or backdrop
  camera: editorCamera, // put back exactly on unmount
})
tool.addEventListener('commit', (e) => doc.record(e.detail.recipe))
tool.unmount()
```

`change` on every edit, `commit` once per finished gesture, each with a copy
of the recipe; hosted, its panel is a system panel; `unmount()` (safe twice)
returns the scene's counts to where they were, including the effect player's
shared driver and sprites, which go with a scene's last player.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/effect-tool/

---

# Character Builder

**Make a person, and watch them walk.** The first steps of the character
creator (CHARACTER-DESIGN.md): MakeHuman's CC0 body
([human-pack](/human-pack/)), reshaped by sliders for gender, age, muscle,
weight, height and ancestry ([human-morph](/human-morph/)), with UAL's
skeleton placed from its own joint cubes ([human-rig](/human-rig/)) so it
plays UAL's clips at any shape.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dSun, b3dLight, row3d, slider3d, select3d, toggle3d, label3d, text3d, assetUrl, DEFAULT_HUMAN_BODY, HAIR_COLOURS, colorPicker3d, clothRecipe, materialPicker3d, studioEnvironment, irisColor, lipSync, readSkeleton, retargetClip, retargetSourceClip, readBvh, clipStore, clipKind, button3d, ui, writeGarmentGlb, writeGarmentObj, readGarment, writeCharacter, readCharacter, tailorPanel, garmentStore, barMenu, fitPanel, chooseFile, b3dPanel, panel3d, makeCharacter, loadCharacterAssets, undoHistory, holdGrip, holdClassOf, HOLD_CLASS_LABELS, picturesIn, pictureData, registerPicture, DEFAULT_CHARACTER, CHARACTER_SLOTS, CHARACTER_SOURCES, AI_CHARACTER_SOURCES, characterStore, WORKING_CHARACTER, nameCharacter, inspectView, viewMenu, b3dLibrary, handSocket, heldGrip, vector3d, euler3d, b3dManipulator, playback3d } from 'tosijs-3d'

// A name asked for in a popup (works in a headset too): refused with its
// reason, and a confirm before it replaces ANOTHER saved character.
const namePopup = (pop, { prompt, initial, current, verb, act }) => {
  let typed = initial
  const go = () => {
    const d = nameCharacter(typed, character.saved, current)
    if (!d.ok) return pop.show(form(d.message))
    if (!d.replaces) {
      pop.close()
      return act(d.name)
    }
    pop.show([
      text3d({ text: `${d.name} is already saved. Replace it?` }),
      button3d({ label: 'replace', handleClick: () => { pop.close(); act(d.name) } }),
      button3d({ label: 'cancel', handleClick: () => pop.close() }),
    ])
  }
  const form = (message) => [
    text3d({ text: message }),
    ui.inputField({ value: typed, placeholder: 'name', autofocus: true, handleChange: (v) => { typed = v }, handleEnter: (v) => { typed = v; go() } }),
    button3d({ label: verb, handleClick: go }),
    button3d({ label: 'cancel', handleClick: () => pop.close() }),
  ]
  return form(prompt)
}
// The character (character.ts): what the panel sets, made in the scene.
let ch = null
// The pack's proxies, once it has loaded (the panel lists an outfit's looks).
let packProxies = {}
// What can be worn, one of each at a time; the pack says which slot each garment fills.
// A bodysuit is a base layer and armour goes over anything; an outfit replaces a top and bottom.
const SLOTS = CHARACTER_SLOTS
// The everyday clips first; the rest of the library (shoot, sword, interact…)

const EVERYDAY = ['Idle_Loop', 'Walk_Loop', 'Jog_Fwd_Loop', 'Sprint_Loop', 'Dance_Loop', 'Crouch_Fwd_Loop']
let clips = [...EVERYDAY]
// Clips from a file (a Mixamo or Meshy character's GLB, or a BVH capture):
// name → the clip and the skeleton it was made on, retargeted like UAL's when

const fileClips = new Map()

const clipBytes = new Map()
let openClips = () => {}
let forgetClip = () => {}
// Where the body comes from: MakeHuman's, which the sliders shape, or a mesh

const fileBytes = new Map()
const keepBytes = (file) => {
  if (!fileBytes.has(file)) fileBytes.set(file, file.arrayBuffer().then((b) => void fileBytes.set(file, new Uint8Array(b))))
  return Promise.resolve(fileBytes.get(file))
}
// Where a mesh body comes from, as a character file says it.
const bodyOf = (name) => {
  const from = SOURCES[name]
  if (!from) return null
  const pick = from.pick != null ? { pick: from.pick } : {}
  if (from.url) return { url: from.url, ...pick }
  const bytes = from.file && fileBytes.get(from.file)
  return bytes instanceof Uint8Array ? { file: { name: from.file.name, bytes }, ...pick } : null
}

}
const setGrip = (patch) => {
  const name = walker.held.value
  const kept = gripsKept()
  delete kept[name]
  walker.grips.value = { ...kept, [holdClassOf(name)]: { ...gripOf(name), ...patch } }

const holdRows = () => {
  const name = walker.held.value
  const g = gripOf(name)
  return [
    label3d({ text: 'Hold', icon: 'bipedHandgun', collapsible: true }),
    select3d({ label: 'right hand', value: walker.held, options: heldNames, stayOpen: true }),
    ...(name === 'none'

          label3d({ text: 'turned (degrees)', muted: true }),
          euler3d({ value: { x: g.rx, y: g.ry, z: g.rz }, step: 5, scrub: 0.5, handleChange: (v) => setGrip({ rx: v.x, ry: v.y, rz: v.z }) }),
          slider3d({ label: 'scale', value: g.scale, min: 0.4, max: 1.6, step: 0.01, handleChange: (v) => setGrip({ scale: v }) }),
          button3d({
            label: 'reset grip',
            handleClick: () => {
              const all = gripsKept()
              delete all[name]
              delete all[holdClassOf(name)]
              walker.grips.value = all
              applyGrip()
            },
          }),
        ]),
  ]
}
const slider = (label, key) =>
  slider3d({ label, value: walker[key], min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 })

preview.append(

        label3d({ text: 'Face', icon: 'face', collapsible: true }),

        colorPicker3d({ label: 'highlights', value: walker.hairHighlight, alpha: false, defaultPresets: 'off', presets: Object.entries(HAIR_COLOURS).map(([name, c]) => ({ name, value: c.highlight })) }),
        // A hand adjustment after the fit: dragged up and forward on the head
        // (no turn, no sideways: hair stays symmetrical), and a scale. For the

        ...(walker.hair.value === 'none' || packProxies[walker.hair.value] ? [] : [toggle3d({
          label: 'manipulator',
          value: hairHandles,
          handleChange: (v) => {

            showHairHandles(v)
          },
        }),

        select3d({ label: 'beard', value: walker.beard, options: choices('beard'), stayOpen: true }),
        select3d({ label: 'moustache', value: walker.moustache, options: choices('moustache'), stayOpen: true }),

        ...holdRows(),
        label3d({ text: 'Motion', icon: 'motion', collapsible: true }),

        ...(clipFiles.has(walker.clip.value) ? [button3d({ label: `forget ${walker.clip.value}`, handleClick: () => forgetClip() })] : []),
        ...exportRows(),
      ] : [
        // A body of anyone's: what MakeHuman's carries (shape, face, hair,
        // clothes) is not there; the clips and the skin are.
        label3d({ text: 'Body', icon: 'mesh', collapsible: true, open: true }),
        select3d({ label: 'source', value: walker.source, options: sourceNames(), stayOpen: true }),
        button3d({ label: 'open a mesh…', handleClick: () => openBody() }),
        ...(ch?.problem ? [text3d({ text: ch.problem })] : []),
        // Its rig is the rig tool's: markers, tail, springs, arm space. The
        // recipe is kept with the character.
        ...(rigging
          ? [
              text3d({ text: 'Rigging: in the Rig panel (on the bar). Done there brings the body back.' }),
            ]
          : [button3d({ label: 'rig…', handleClick: () => openRig() })]),
        // Its file's materials, each as made or the skin.
        ...surfaceRows(),
        label3d({ text: 'Skin', icon: 'skin', collapsible: true }),
        slider3d({ label: 'tone', value: walker.tone, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'redness', value: walker.redness, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 }),
        ...clothesRows(),
        ...holdRows(),
        label3d({ text: 'Motion', icon: 'motion', collapsible: true }),
        select3d({ label: 'clip', value: walker.clip, options: clips, stayOpen: true }),
        playbackRow(),
        button3d({ label: 'clips from a file…', handleClick: () => openClips() }),
        ...(clipFiles.has(walker.clip.value) ? [button3d({ label: `forget ${walker.clip.value}`, handleClick: () => forgetClip() })] : []),
        ...exportRows(),
      ],
      async sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
        const scene = el.scene
        refreshPanel = () => el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        el.setLoading('loading the animations…')
        // Something for gloss and metal to reflect.
        studioEnvironment(scene)
        const cam = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera('c', Math.PI / 2 - 0.5, 1.35, 4, new BABYLON.Vector3(0, 0.9, 0), scene)
        cam.minZ = 0.05
        // Close enough for a face, far enough for the whole floor.
        cam.lowerRadiusLimit = 0.3
        cam.upperRadiusLimit = 10
        cam.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
        el.setActiveCamera(cam)
        // THE VIEWS: the body square on from each side, and the right hand
        // close up, followed through the clip (is the item held right?). The
        // hand view orbits like the perspective one, round the hand.
        let views = null
        const inspect = inspectView(cam, { handleChange: () => views?.update() })
        const home = { target: cam.target.clone(), radius: cam.radius }
        let handNode = null
        let knuckleNode = null
        let handOf = null
        const rightHand = () => {
          const shown = ch?.shown
          if (shown !== handOf) {
            handOf = shown
            // The shown body's own hand: the node its skeleton's bone is
            // linked to (other skeletons, the clips' source, have one too).
            const bones = shown?.built?.skeleton?.bones ?? []
            const node = (name) => bones.find((b) => b.name === name)?.getTransformNode() ?? null
            handNode = node('hand_r')
            knuckleNode = node('middle_01_r')
          }
          // The palm, where a grip is: between the wrist and the middle
          // finger's knuckle (the wrist alone when there are no fingers).
          const a = handNode?.getAbsolutePosition()
          if (a == null) return null
          const b = knuckleNode?.getAbsolutePosition()
          return b == null ? a : a.add(b).scaleInPlace(0.5)
        }
        // THE CHARACTER is the document, not a tab: a menu on the system bar,
        // beside the panel's button (save, select, rename… like a File menu).
        // Its name prompts are the scene's modal.
        const modal = (build) => {
          let close = null
          const pop = {
            show(ws) {
              close?.()
              const { svg, height } = fitPanel(ws, { width: 320 })
              close = el.showModal(svg, height)
            },
            close() {
              close?.()
              close = null
            },
          }
          pop.show(build(pop))
        }
        const saveAs = (initial, current) => modal((pop) => namePopup(pop, { prompt: 'save as', initial, current, verb: 'save', act: (name) => character.save(name) }))
        el.append(barMenu({
          icon: 'character',
          title: 'Character',
          layout: 'list',
          options: () => {
            const current = walker.characterName.value
            const saved = character.saved
            return [
              {
                label: 'Select',
                items: () => saved.length
                  ? saved.map((n) => ({ label: n, checked: n === current, handleSelect: () => { if (n !== current) character.load(n) } }))
                  : [{ label: 'nothing saved yet', disabled: true }],
              },
              {
                label: 'Delete',
                disabled: saved.length === 0,
                // A name, then a second step to confirm: it cannot be undone.
                items: () => saved.map((n) => ({ label: n, items: [{ label: `delete ${n}`, handleSelect: () => character.remove(n) }] })),
              },
              { label: current ? `Save ${current}` : 'Save…', handleSelect: () => (current ? character.save(current) : saveAs('', '')) },
              { label: 'Save as…', handleSelect: () => saveAs(current, current) },
              {
                label: 'Rename…',
                disabled: !current,
                handleSelect: () => modal((pop) => namePopup(pop, { prompt: `rename ${current} to`, initial: current, current, verb: 'rename', act: (name) => character.rename(current, name) })),
              },
              { separator: true },
              { label: 'Open mesh…', handleSelect: () => openMesh() },
              { separator: true },
              { label: 'Export JSON', handleSelect: () => character.exportJson() },
              { label: 'Load JSON…', handleSelect: () => character.importJson() },
              { separator: true },
              { label: 'Go to Playground', handleSelect: () => character.play() },
              ...(character.note ? [{ separator: true }, { label: character.note, disabled: true }] : []),
            ]
          },
        }))
        let onHand = false
        views = viewMenu(inspect, el, {
          always: true,
          // Rigging: what is shown beside the mesh.
          items: () => rigging
            ? [
                { label: 'Mannequin', icon: 'personStanding', checked: rigging.api.mannequin, handleSelect: () => { rigging.api.mannequin = !rigging.api.mannequin } },
                { label: 'Bones', icon: 'rig', checked: rigging.api.bones, handleSelect: () => { rigging.api.bones = !rigging.api.bones } },
              ]
            : [],
          extras: [{
            value: 'hand',
            label: 'right hand',
            icon: 'bipedHandgun',
            active: () => onHand,
            select: () => {
              onHand = true
              inspect.face = 'free'
              inspect.follow = rightHand
              // From the outside of the hand (the character's right is +X).
              cam.alpha = 0
              cam.beta = 1.3
              cam.radius = 0.6
            },
            leave: () => {
              onHand = false
              inspect.follow = null
              cam.target.copyFrom(home.target)
              cam.radius = home.radius
            },
          }],
        })
        // THE ANIMATION on the bar: play or pause, and which clip, in one
        // place, flat and in a headset. The transport (scrub, speed) is its
        // own small panel, opened from the menu (it has no button of its own).
        const playbackPanel = b3dPanel({ icon: 'playCircle', title: 'Playback', exclusive: 'off', barButton: 'off' })
        playbackPanel.svg = panel3d({ width: 300 }, playbackRow())
        const clipOption = (name) => ({ label: name, checked: name === walker.clip.value, handleSelect: () => { walker.clip.value = name } })
        // UAL's names lead with what they are (Pistol_…, Sword_…): the rest of
        // the library is grouped by that, so no list runs off the view.
        const moreClips = () => {
          const groups = new Map()
          for (const name of clips.slice(EVERYDAY.length + fileClips.size)) {
            const group = name.split('_')[0]
            if (!groups.has(group)) groups.set(group, [])
            groups.get(group).push(name)
          }
          return [...groups].map(([group, names]) =>
            names.length === 1 ? clipOption(names[0]) : { label: group, items: () => names.map(clipOption) }
          )
        }
        el.append(barMenu({
          icon: 'motion',
          title: 'Animation',
          layout: 'list',
          options: () => [
            // While rigging the view is the pose: play goes to perspective,
            // pause back to the face it was held to last.
            rigging
              ? rigging.api.view === 'free'
                ? { label: 'Pause', icon: 'pause', handleSelect: () => rigging?.api.play(null) }
                : { label: 'Play', icon: 'play', handleSelect: () => rigging?.api.play() }
              : walker.paused.value
              ? { label: 'Play', icon: 'play', handleSelect: () => { walker.paused.value = false } }
              : { label: 'Pause', icon: 'pause', handleSelect: () => { walker.paused.value = true } },
            { label: 'Playback controls', icon: 'playCircle', checked: playbackPanel.isOpen, handleSelect: () => playbackPanel.toggle?.() },
            { separator: true },
            ...EVERYDAY.map(clipOption),
            ...(fileClips.size ? [{ separator: true }, ...[...fileClips.keys()].map(clipOption)] : []),
            { separator: true },
            { label: 'More clips', items: moreClips },
          ],
        }))
        el.append(playbackPanel)
        // A floor with a metre grid (and faint quarters), which takes the sun's shadow.
        const floor = BABYLON.MeshBuilder.CreateGround('floor_nocast', { width: 12, height: 12 }, scene)
        const tile = new BABYLON.DynamicTexture('floor-grid', { width: 256, height: 256 }, scene, true)
        const ctx = tile.getContext()
        ctx.fillStyle = '#5d6672'
        ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 256, 256)
        ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.12)'
        ctx.lineWidth = 2
        for (const at of [64, 128, 192]) {
          ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(at, 0); ctx.lineTo(at, 256); ctx.moveTo(0, at); ctx.lineTo(256, at); ctx.stroke()
        }
        ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.45)'
        ctx.lineWidth = 4
        ctx.strokeRect(0, 0, 256, 256)
        tile.update()
        tile.wrapU = tile.wrapV = BABYLON.Texture.WRAP_ADDRESSMODE
        tile.uScale = tile.vScale = 12
        tile.anisotropicFilteringLevel = 8
        const floorMat = new BABYLON.StandardMaterial('floor', scene)
        floorMat.diffuseTexture = tile
        floorMat.specularColor = new BABYLON.Color3(0.05, 0.05, 0.05)
        floor.material = floorMat
        el.register({ meshes: [floor] })

        // UAL's mannequin is only the clips' source: it stays hidden. The
        // builder's own pack: the loops that test a rig (locomotion, crouch,
        // the pistol, sword, shield and bow), not the bipeds' set.
        const ual = await BABYLON.LoadAssetContainerAsync(assetUrl('quaternius/UAL_builder.glb'), scene)
        el.setLoading('loading the body…')
        ual.addAllToScene()
        for (const g of ual.animationGroups) g.stop()
        // The everyday clips, then a file's, then the rest of UAL's.
        const listClips = () => {
          const mine = [...fileClips.keys()]
          clips = [...EVERYDAY, ...mine, ...ual.animationGroups.map((g) => g.name).filter((n) => !EVERYDAY.includes(n) && !fileClips.has(n)).sort()]
        }
        listClips()
        const ualRoot = ual.meshes.find((m) => m.name === '__root__')
        const source = readSkeleton(ual.skeletons[0], ualRoot)
        ualRoot.setEnabled(false)
        // THE HELD ITEM: an instance of the library's model on the shown
        // body's right-hand socket, made again when the item or body changes.
        const weapons = el.querySelector('tosi-b3d-library')
        let held = null
        applyGrip = () => {
          const name = walker.held.value
          const shown = ch?.shown
          if (held && (held.name !== name || held.shown !== shown || rigging)) {
            held.node.dispose()
            held = null
            gizmo.node = null
          }
          if (name === 'none' || !shown || rigging) return
          if (!held) {
            const skeleton = shown.built?.skeleton
            const hand = skeleton?.bones.find((b) => b.name === 'hand_r')?.getTransformNode()
            const node = hand && weapons?.instantiate?.(name, { canonical: true })
            if (!node) return
            node.parent = handSocket(skeleton, 'hand_r', 'r', hand) ?? hand
            // Its grip (a pistol's handle), measured once: that point, not
            // its origin, goes where the numbers say, as on a launcher.
            held = { node, name, shown, grip: heldGrip(node) ?? BABYLON.Vector3.Zero() }
          }
          placeHeld(gripOf(name))
        }
        // The item at a grip: that point and turn in the hand's socket frame.
        const placeHeld = (g, handle = true) => {
          const d = Math.PI / 180
          const turn = BABYLON.Quaternion.FromEulerAngles(g.rx * d, g.ry * d, g.rz * d)
          // Scaled with the item, so its grip point stays on the grip.
          const spun = held.grip.scale(g.scale).applyRotationQuaternion(turn)
          held.node.position.set(g.x - spun.x, g.y - spun.y, g.z - spun.z)
          held.node.rotationQuaternion = turn
          held.node.scaling.setAll(g.scale)
          // THE GRIP'S HANDLES: a node at the grip, in the same frame, for
          // the manipulator to drag; the item follows it.
          gripNode.parent = held.node.parent
          if (handle) {
            gripNode.position.set(g.x, g.y, g.z)
            gripNode.rotationQuaternion = turn.clone()
          }
          gizmo.node = gripHandles ? gripNode : null
        }
        const gripNode = new BABYLON.TransformNode('grip-handle', el.scene)
        const fromHandle = () => {
          const p = gripNode.position
          const e = gripNode.rotationQuaternion.toEulerAngles()
          const mm = (v) => Math.round(v * 1000) / 1000
          const deg = (v) => Math.round((v * 1800) / Math.PI) / 10
          return { x: mm(p.x), y: mm(p.y), z: mm(p.z), rx: deg(e.x), ry: deg(e.y), rz: deg(e.z) }
        }
        const gizmo = b3dManipulator({
          move: 'on',
          turn: 'on',
          size: 0.09,
          // Live: the item follows; kept (and the numbers shown) on release.
          whenChange: () => held && placeHeld({ ...gripOf(held.name), ...fromHandle() }, false),
          whenCommit: () => {
            setGrip(fromHandle())
            el.refreshScenePanel?.()
          },
        })
        el.append(gizmo)
        showGripHandles = (on) => {
          gripHandles = on
          gizmo.node = on && held ? gripNode : null
        }
        // THE HAIR'S HANDLE: a node on the Head bone at the skull's middle plus
        // the adjustment. Dragging moves the hair's meshes as they are; the
        // adjustment is kept, and the hair placed again, on release.
        const hairNode = new BABYLON.TransformNode('hair-handle', el.scene)
        let hairDrag = null
        let hairFrom = null
        const placeHairHandle = () => {
          const anchor = hairHandles ? ch?.hairAnchor?.() : null
          hairGizmo.node = null
          if (!anchor) return
          const c = anchor.centre
          hairNode.parent = anchor.node
          hairNode.rotationQuaternion = BABYLON.Quaternion.Identity()
          hairNode.position.set(c.x, c.y + walker.hairUp.value, c.z + walker.hairForward.value)
          hairFrom = hairNode.position.clone()
          hairGizmo.node = hairNode
        }
        const hairGizmo = b3dManipulator({
          move: 'on',
          // Up and forward: no sideways (it shows the y and z arrows and the
          // pad between them).
          lockMove: 'x',
          turn: 'off',
          size: 0.09,
          whenChange: () => {
            const anchor = ch?.hairAnchor?.()
            if (!anchor) return
            hairDrag ??= { meshes: anchor.meshes, at: anchor.meshes.map((m) => m.position.clone()) }
            const d = hairNode.position.subtract(hairFrom ?? hairNode.position)
            hairDrag.meshes.forEach((m, i) => m.position.copyFrom(hairDrag.at[i].add(d)))
          },
          whenCommit: () => {
```
