```js
            const anchor = ch?.hairAnchor?.()
            hairDrag = null
            if (!anchor) return
            const mm = (v) => Math.round(v * 1000) / 1000
            walker.hairUp.value = mm(hairNode.position.y - anchor.centre.y)
            walker.hairForward.value = mm(hairNode.position.z - anchor.centre.z)
          },
        })
        el.append(hairGizmo)
        showHairHandles = (on) => {
          hairHandles = on
          placeHairHandle()
        }
        // Undo, a loaded character or a new body puts the handle back.
        walker.hairUp.observe(() => placeHairHandle())
        walker.hairForward.observe(() => placeHairHandle())
        weapons?.ready.then(() => {
          heldNames = ['none', ...weapons.getNames().filter((n) => !n.startsWith('ammo')).sort()]
          applyGrip()
          el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        })
        walker.held.observe(() => {
          applyGrip()
          el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        })
        // An undo (or a loaded character) puts the grip back: the item moves.
        walker.grips.observe(() => applyGrip())

        // CLIPS FROM A FILE: any skinned GLB with animations (Mixamo's,
        // Meshy's), its skeleton read like UAL's, or a BVH motion capture;
        // its clips listed and retargeted onto the body shown, and the file
        // kept in this browser (restored quietly on the next visit).
        const keptClips = clipStore()
        const addClips = async (file, restoring = false, keep = !restoring) => {
          const kind = clipKind(file.name)
          if (!kind) return console.warn(`character builder: ${file.name} is not a GLB or BVH`)
          try {
            const bytes = new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer())
            let names = []
            if (kind === 'bvh') {
              const from = readBvh(await file.text(), { name: file.name.replace(/\.bvh$/i, '') })
              fileClips.set(from.clips[0].name, { source: from, clip: from.clips[0] })
              names = [from.clips[0].name]
            } else {
              const c = await BABYLON.LoadAssetContainerAsync(file, scene)
              const skeleton = c.skeletons[0]
              if (!skeleton || c.animationGroups.length === 0) {
                console.warn(`character builder: ${file.name} has no skeleton or no animations`)
                c.dispose()
                return
              }
              const from = readSkeleton(skeleton, c.rootNodes[0])
              for (const g of c.animationGroups) {
                g.stop()
                fileClips.set(g.name, { group: g, from })
              }
              names = c.animationGroups.map((g) => g.name)
            }
            for (const n of names) clipFiles.set(n, file.name)
            clipBytes.set(file.name, { kind, bytes })
            if (keep) keptClips.put({ name: file.name, kind, bytes }).catch((e) => console.warn('character builder: could not keep the clips', e))
            listClips()
            if (!restoring) walker.clip.value = names[0]
            el.refreshScenePanel?.()
          } catch (e) {
            console.warn('character builder: could not read the clips', e)
          }
        }
        openClips = () => chooseFile('.glb,.gltf,.bvh').then((file) => file && addClips(file))
        forgetClip = () => {
          const file = clipFiles.get(walker.clip.value)
          if (file == null) return
          for (const [n, f] of [...clipFiles]) if (f === file) { clipFiles.delete(n); fileClips.delete(n) }
          clipBytes.delete(file)
          keptClips.delete(file).catch(() => {})
          listClips()
          walker.clip.value = 'Walk_Loop'
          el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        }
        keptClips.all().then((list) => Promise.all(list.map((c) => addClips(new File([c.bytes], c.name), true)))).then(() => {
          // A character saved playing one of them plays it again.
          if (fileClips.has(walker.clip.value)) play()
        }).catch(() => {})
        // The forget button comes and goes with whether the clip is your own.
        let ownClip = false
        walker.clip.observe(() => {
          // Rigging, a clip from the Animation menu plays on the rig.
          if (rigging) rigging.api.clip = walker.clip.value
          if (clipFiles.has(walker.clip.value) === ownClip) return
          ownClip = !ownClip
          el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        })

        // MakeHuman's pack and Quaternius' hairstyles, shared by any character.
        const assets = await loadCharacterAssets(scene).catch((e) => {
          el.setLoading(`could not load the body: ${e.message}`, { spin: false })
          throw e
        })
        const pack = assets.pack
        packProxies = pack.manifest.proxies ?? {}
        const plain = (v) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(v))
        const save = (data, name, type) => {
          const a = document.createElement('a')
          a.href = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([data], { type }))
          a.download = name
          a.click()
          setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href), 1000)
        }

        // THE CLIP, on whatever body is shown, standing on the floor.
        let playing = null
        const play = () => {
          playing?.dispose()
          playing = null
          if (!ch?.skeleton || rigging) return
          // A file's clip (gone after a reload: the walk instead), or UAL's.
          const own = fileClips.get(walker.clip.value)
          const clip = own?.group ?? ual.animationGroups.find((g) => g.name === walker.clip.value) ?? ual.animationGroups.find((g) => g.name === 'Walk_Loop')
          playing = own?.source
            ? retargetSourceClip(own.source, own.clip, ch.skeleton, { scene, armSpaceDeg: ch.recipe?.armSpaceDeg, footTurnDeg: ch.recipe?.footTurnDeg })
            : clip ? retargetClip(clip, own?.from ?? source, ch.skeleton, { scene, armSpaceDeg: ch.recipe?.armSpaceDeg, footTurnDeg: ch.recipe?.footTurnDeg }) : null
          playing?.start(true, clipSpeed)
          ch.groundFor(playing)
          if (walker.paused.value) playing?.pause()
        }
        // The transport reads and moves the clip playing now.
        const clipFps = () => playing?.targetedAnimations[0]?.animation.framePerSecond || 30
        clipState = () => {
          if (!playing) return null
          const fps = clipFps()
          const frame = playing.animatables[0]?.masterFrame ?? playing.from
          return { time: (frame - playing.from) / fps, duration: (playing.to - playing.from) / fps, playing: !walker.paused.value, speed: clipSpeed }
        }
        seekClip = (t) => playing?.goToFrame(playing.from + t * clipFps())
        speedClip = (s) => { if (playing) playing.speedRatio = s }

        // The saved garments, in IndexedDB: per browser, nothing shared yet.
        const garmentFiles = garmentStore()
        const savedGarments = await garmentFiles.all().catch((e) => {
          console.warn('tailor: no saved garments (storage unavailable)', e)
          return []
        })

        // THE CHARACTER: everything the panel sets that is about it (not the
        // clip, the tailor's work or the save controls).
        // A first visit (nothing kept) starts on one of the AI bodies, at
        // random; after that the working figure says which.
        if (!(await characterStore().get(WORKING_CHARACTER).catch(() => null))) {
          const first = Object.keys(AI_CHARACTER_SOURCES)
          walker.source.value = first[Math.floor(Math.random() * first.length)]
        }
        const OWN = Object.keys(DEFAULT_CHARACTER).filter((k) => k in START)
        const settings = () => ({ ...Object.fromEntries(OWN.map((k) => [k, plain(walker[k].value)])), hideClothes: walker.tailorAlone.value })
        ch = await makeCharacter(scene, assets, {
          settings: settings(),
          sources: SOURCES,
          garments: savedGarments ?? [],
          gaze: () => scene.activeCamera?.globalPosition ?? cam.position,
          handleStatus: (m) => el.setLoading(m),
          handleMeshes: (meshes) => el.register({ meshes }),
          handleShown: (shown) => {
            // A garment being cut is cut from the body as it is now.
            if (shown && tailor?.tool && tailor.editing?.source === shown.source) tailor.tool.setBody(shown.body, shown.built)
            else if (tailor?.open && !tailor.tool) tailor.begin()
            applyGrip()
            showHairHandles(hairHandles)
            el.refreshScenePanel?.()
            play()
          },
        })
        el.builder = {
          character: null,
          pack,
          get ch() { return ch },
          get built() { return ch.shown?.built },
          get body() { return ch.shown?.body },
          get tailorShapes() { return tailorShapes },
          set tailorShapes(v) { tailorShapes = v },
          get tailor() { return tailor?.tool ?? null },
          get tailorPanel() { return tailor?.panel },
          openTailor: () => tailor?.panel.show?.(),
          garmentFile: (f, alone) => tailor?.garmentFile(f, alone) ?? null,
          importFrom: (d, n) => tailor?.importFrom(d, n),
          forget: () => tailor?.forget(),
          saved: ch.garments,
          get message() { return importError || tailor?.message || '' },
          get expressions() { return ch.expressions },
        }
        // Each of the character's settings goes to it as it changes.
        for (const k of OWN) walker[k].observe(() => ch.set({ [k]: plain(walker[k].value) }))
        walker.tailorAlone.observe(() => ch.set({ hideClothes: walker.tailorAlone.value }))
        // An outfit replaces a top and bottom, and either replaces an outfit.
        walker.outfit.observe(() => { if (walker.outfit.value !== 'none') { walker.top.value = 'none'; walker.bottom.value = 'none' } })
        for (const k of ['top', 'bottom']) walker[k].observe(() => { if (walker[k].value !== 'none') walker.outfit.value = 'none' })
        // Picking a base preset brings its usual highlight.
        walker.hairBase.observe(() => {
          const pair = Object.values(HAIR_COLOURS).find((c) => c.base === walker.hairBase.value)
          if (pair && walker.hairHighlight.value !== pair.highlight) walker.hairHighlight.value = pair.highlight
        })
        // Wearing something else: its row gets its swatch (the character
        // resets its look).
        for (const slot of SLOTS) walker[slot].observe(() => el.refreshScenePanel?.())
        // MakeHuman's own hair has no hand adjustment: its rows go, and the handle.
        walker.hair.observe(() => {
          if (walker.hair.value === 'none' || packProxies[walker.hair.value]) showHairHandles(false)
          el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        })
        // The microphone drives the lips (it asks first, so it is never saved).
        let stopMic = null
        walker.mic.observe(async () => {
          stopMic?.()
          stopMic = null
          if (!walker.mic.value) return
          try {
            const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true })
            const ctx = new AudioContext()
            const analyser = ctx.createAnalyser()
            ctx.createMediaStreamSource(stream).connect(analyser)
            const stop = lipSync(scene, ch.expressions, analyser, { gain: 1.5 })
            stopMic = () => { stop(); stream.getTracks().forEach((t) => t.stop()); ctx.close() }
          } catch (e) {
            walker.mic.value = false
            console.warn('lip sync: no microphone', e)
          }
        })
        // Another body: the rig tool on this one goes, and the tailor when it
        // was cutting from the one before.
        walker.source.observe(() => {
          if (rigging) { rigging.unmount(); rigging = null; ch.hide(false) }
          // The tailor keeps what it was making on the body before.
          if (tailor?.open) void tailor.keep().then(() => tailor.open && tailor.begin())
        })

        // GARMENTS OF YOUR OWN: what a garment was made on (MakeHuman's body,
        // its slider values; or a mesh's, its source, the only body it is
        // worn on), and the files kept in this browser.
        const bodyValues = () => Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(DEFAULT_HUMAN_BODY).map((k) => [k, Number(walker[k].value)]))
        const baseMeta = (from = walker.source.value) =>
          from === 'MakeHuman'
            ? { format: 'tosijs-garment', version: 1, base: pack.manifest.base, pack: pack.manifest.version, body: bodyValues(), name: 'tailored', slot: 'top' }
            : { format: 'tosijs-garment', version: 1, source: from, name: 'tailored', slot: 'top' }
        // THE TAILOR, always on the bar (tailor-panel): this page keeps its
        // draft, its slot and what each slot wears.
        const kept = (key) => ({ get: () => walker[key].value, set: (v) => { walker[key].value = v } })
        tailor = tailorPanel(el, {
          character: () => ch,
          target: () => tailorTarget() ?? (rigging ? 'The rig tool has the body: done or cancel in the Rig panel, then tailor it.' : 'loading the body…'),
          slots: SLOTS,
          choices: (slot) => choices(slot),
          worn: (slot) => walker[slot].value,
          wear: (slot, name) => { walker[slot].value = name },
          madeOn: (from) => baseMeta(from),
          reserved: (name) => !!packProxies[name],
          store: garmentFiles,
          draft: {
            get: () => ({
              cut: { shapes: tailorShapes, thickness: walker.tailorThickness.value, skirt: walker.tailorSkirt.value, drape: walker.tailorDrape.value, mesh: walker.tailorMesh.value },
              look: plain(walker.tailorLook.value),
              name: walker.tailorName.value,
            }),
            set: ({ cut, look, name }) => {
              tailorShapes = cut.shapes
              walker.tailorThickness.value = cut.thickness
              walker.tailorSkirt.value = cut.skirt
              walker.tailorDrape.value = cut.drape === true
              walker.tailorMesh.value = cut.mesh ?? 'body'
              walker.tailorLook.value = look
              walker.tailorName.value = name
            },
          },
          slot: kept('tailorSlot'),
          hideOthers: kept('tailorAlone'),
          includeBody: kept('exportBody'),
          helperBody: () =>
            madeHuman() ? { positions: ch.human.positions, triangles: pack.triangles } : ch.shown && { positions: ch.shown.body.positions, triangles: ch.shown.body.indices },
          save: (data, name, type) => save(data, name, type),
          handleChange: () => character.changed?.(),
          handleWardrobe: () => el.refreshScenePanel?.(),
          handleMessage: () => el.refreshScenePanel?.(),
        })

        // A MESH FILE becomes a body source (a choice in the list) and is shown.
        openBody = () => {
          chooseFile('.glb,.gltf').then((file) => file && openFile(file))
        }
        const openFile = (file) => {
          ch.addSource(file.name, { file })
          SOURCES[file.name] = { file }
          // Kept again once it can carry the file.
          keepBytes(file).then(() => character.changed?.())
          if (walker.source.value !== file.name) walker.source.value = file.name
        }
        el.builder.openFile = openFile
        // OPEN MESH (the Character menu): rigging, it is the mesh the rig tool
        // works on; otherwise a GLB or glTF is the body, and an OBJ, which has
        // no skeleton, opens in the rig tool to be rigged.
        openMesh = () => chooseFile('.glb,.gltf,.obj').then((f) => {
          if (!f) return
          if (rigging) void rigging.api.load(f)
          else if (/\.obj$/i.test(f.name)) openRig(f)
          else openFile(f)
        })
        // THE RIG TOOL'S BUTTON is always on the bar: it rigs the body shown
        // (a mesh's), or a mesh file opened in it, and done makes what it
        // rigged the builder's body (a choice under source). The character's
        // body steps aside while the tool shows the same mesh bound from the
        // same recipe; cancel puts it back as it was.
        const rigPanel = b3dPanel({ icon: 'rig', title: 'Rig', exclusive: 'off' })
        const idleRig = () =>
          panel3d(
            { width: 300 },
            label3d({ text: 'rig a mesh to play the clips (Character → Open mesh…)', muted: true, compact: true }),
            ...(madeHuman() ? [] : [button3d({ label: `rig ${walker.source.value}`, handleClick: () => openRig() })])
          )
        rigPanel.svg = idleRig()
        el.append(rigPanel)
        walker.source.observe(() => { if (!rigging) rigPanel.svg = idleRig() })
        openRig = (file = null) => {
          if (rigging) return
          if (!file && (madeHuman() || !ch.recipe)) return
          // The tailor keeps what it made and waits for the body back.
          if (tailor.tool) void tailor.keep().then(() => tailor.begin())
          const opened = file ? file.name : walker.source.value
          const from = file ? { file } : SOURCES[opened]
          ch.hide(true)
          playing?.stop()
          // The hand view follows the builder's character, which is hidden.
          if (onHand) { onHand = false; inspect.follow = null; cam.target.copyFrom(home.target); cam.radius = home.radius; views.update() }
          const done = () => {
            rigging = null
            ch.hide(false)
            if (tailor.open && !tailor.tool) tailor.begin()
            applyGrip()
            rigPanel.svg = idleRig()
            rigPanel.hide?.()
            // The Body and Tailor sections wait on it.
            el.refreshScenePanel?.()
          }
          rigging = mountRigTool(el, {
            models: [{ label: opened, url: from.url ?? '', file: from.file, pick: from.pick }],
            // A file starts from nothing: bound from markers, or on its own
            // skeleton when it has one.
            recipe: file ? undefined : plain(ch.recipe),
            // The body it already wears: shown as it is, not bound again.
            body: file ? undefined : ch.shown?.body,
            files: false,
            stage: false,
            camera: cam,
            // One view menu: the builder's, which the rig tool follows.
            inspect,
            // Its playback and view come from the bar's Animation and View menus.
            hostMenus: true,
            panel: rigPanel,
            // The rig it hands back is worn as it is: the body the tool bound,
            // its recipe kept with the character.
            handleDone: ({ recipe, body, model }) => {
              done()
              delete recipe.model
              // What it rigged: the model it opened on, or a file loaded in it.
              const loaded = model instanceof File ? model : model?.file ?? null
              const name = model instanceof File ? model.name : model?.label ?? opened
              // A file new to the builder only: re-adding the one it already
              // has would dispose the materials the body handed back wears.
              if (loaded && SOURCES[name]?.file !== loaded) {
                SOURCES[name] = { file: loaded }
                ch.addSource(name, { file: loaded })
                keepBytes(loaded).then(() => character.changed?.())
              }
              if (body) ch.adopt(name, body, recipe)
              walker.rigs.value = { ...plain(walker.rigs.value), [name]: plain(recipe) }
              if (walker.source.value !== name) walker.source.value = name
              else play()
            },
            handleCancel: () => {
              done()
              play()
            },
          })
          // It plays the clip the Animation menu has.
          rigging.api.clip = walker.clip.value
          // The item goes while the rig tool has the body.
          applyGrip()
          el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        }
        el.builder.rigTool = () => rigging
        el.builder.addClips = (file) => addClips(file)
        el.builder.openRig = (file) => openRig(file)

        // CHARACTERS (character-file): the figure you are working on is kept
        // in this browser as you change it and comes back when the page opens;
        // named ones are saved beside it; a file carries one anywhere.
        // In this browser's character store, which keeps a mesh once
        // however many saves wear it, and which other pages read too.
        const WORKING = WORKING_CHARACTER
        const store = characterStore()
        const snapshot = (name) => {
          const kept = Object.fromEntries(KEPT.map((k) => [k, plain(walker[k].value)]))
          // The garments of your own it wears travel inside it.
          const garments = {}
          for (const slot of SLOTS) {
            const g = ch.garments.get(walker[slot].value)
            if (g?.bytes) garments[walker[slot].value] = g.bytes
          }
          const cloth = Object.fromEntries(SLOTS.map((slot) => [slot, plain(ch.cloth(slot))]))
          // And its body, when it is a mesh: where it comes from, or the file.
          const body = bodyOf(kept.source)
          const bodies = body ? { [kept.source]: body } : {}
          // The pictures its materials use (chosen from disk), by key.
          const pictures = Object.fromEntries(picturesIn({ kept, cloth }).map((k) => [k, pictureData(k)]).filter(([, b]) => b))
          // The clip it plays, when that is one of your own: its file.
          const clipFile = clipFiles.get(kept.clip)
          const clips = clipFile && clipBytes.has(clipFile) ? { [clipFile]: clipBytes.get(clipFile) } : {}
          return writeCharacter({ name, settings: kept, cloth, tailor: plain(tailorShapes), garments, bodies, pictures, clips }, { saved: new Date().toISOString() })
        }
        const tell = (message) => { character.note = message; el.refreshScenePanel?.() }
        let restoring = false
        const apply = async (doc) => {
          // What the tailor was making is kept before another character comes.
          if (tailor?.tool) await tailor.keep()
          const slotLooks = Object.fromEntries(SLOTS.map((slot) => [slot, plain(ch.cloth(slot))]))
          const { character: c, warnings } = readCharacter(doc, { settings: Object.fromEntries(KEPT.map((k) => [k, START[k]])), slots: slotLooks })
          restoring = true
          try {
            // Its pictures first, so its materials find them.
            for (const [key, b64] of Object.entries(c.pictures ?? {})) registerPicture(key, b64)
            // Its own garments first, so the slots can wear them.
            for (const [name, bytes] of Object.entries(c.garments)) {
              if (ch.garments.has(name)) continue
              await garmentFiles.put(name, bytes).catch(() => {})
              await ch.addGarment(bytes)
            }
            // A body the file carries and this page does not have becomes a source.
            for (const [name, b] of Object.entries(c.bodies ?? {})) {
              if (name in SOURCES) continue
              const file = b.file ? new File([b.file.bytes], b.file.name) : null
              if (file) fileBytes.set(file, b.file.bytes)
              const from = { ...(file ? { file } : { url: b.url }), ...(b.pick != null ? { pick: b.pick } : {}) }
              SOURCES[name] = from
              ch.addSource(name, from)
            }
            // A clip file it carries and this browser does not have: read and kept.
            for (const [name, clip] of Object.entries(c.clips ?? {})) {
              if (!clipBytes.has(name)) await addClips(new File([clip.bytes], name), true, true)
            }
            if (c.settings.source !== 'MakeHuman' && !(c.settings.source in SOURCES)) {
              warnings.push(`body ${c.settings.source}: open that file again; MakeHuman's shown`)
              c.settings.source = 'MakeHuman'
            }
            // An outfit before a top and bottom (each clears the other).
            const keys = ['outfit', ...KEPT.filter((k) => k !== 'outfit')]
            for (const k of keys) walker[k].value = c.settings[k]
            // The character takes them now, then the slots' looks (which
            // wearing something new resets).
            ch.set(Object.fromEntries(OWN.map((k) => [k, plain(c.settings[k])])))
            for (const slot of SLOTS) ch.setCloth(slot, c.cloth[slot])
            await ch.ready()
            tailorShapes = c.tailor
            walker.characterName.value = c.name === WORKING ? '' : c.name
          } finally {
            restoring = false
          }
          if (warnings.length) console.warn('character builder: loaded with changes', warnings)
          tell(warnings.length ? `loaded; ${warnings.length} setting(s) skipped (see the console)` : '')
        }
        const listSaved = async () => {
          character.saved = await store.list().catch(() => [])
          // Deleted (here or in another tab): the figure is no longer saved.
          if (!character.saved.includes(walker.characterName.value)) walker.characterName.value = ''
          el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        }
        // Kept a moment after the last change, so a slider drag is one write.
        let pending = null
        const keepWorking = () => {
          clearTimeout(pending)
          pending = setTimeout(() => {
            // Under the name it is being edited as, so a reload knows which
            // saved character this is (the key, not the name, marks it working).
            store.put(WORKING, snapshot(walker.characterName.value || WORKING)).catch((e) => console.warn('character builder: could not keep the working figure', e))
          }, 800)
        }
        character.changed = () => {
          if (restoring) return
          keepWorking()
          awaitStep()
        }

        // UNDO (#3878): the character recorded as each change settles, a
        // slider drag or a placed grip being one step. A step is the snapshot
        // without its files' bytes (garments and bodies stay loaded, so a step
        // only names them), and undo applies it as loading a character does.
        // Not the clip or playback: watching is not editing.
        const TRANSIENT = ['paused', 'clip', 'talk', 'blink', 'exportBody', 'tailorAlone']
        const undoable = () => ({
          settings: Object.fromEntries(KEPT.filter((k) => !TRANSIENT.includes(k)).map((k) => [k, plain(walker[k].value)])),
          cloth: Object.fromEntries(SLOTS.map((slot) => [slot, plain(ch.cloth(slot))])),
          tailor: plain(tailorShapes),
        })
        const history = undoHistory({ limit: 100 })
        let stepTimer = null
        const buttons = () => `${character.canUndo()}${character.canRedo()}`
        const record = () => {
          const was = buttons()
          clearTimeout(stepTimer)
          stepTimer = null
          history.record(undoable())
          if (buttons() !== was) el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        }
        const awaitStep = () => {
          const was = buttons()
          clearTimeout(stepTimer)
          stepTimer = setTimeout(record, 400)
          if (buttons() !== was) el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        }
        let stepping = false
        const restore = async (step) => {
          if (!step) return
          stepping = true
          const name = walker.characterName.value
          const settings = { ...Object.fromEntries(KEPT.map((k) => [k, plain(walker[k].value)])), ...step.settings }
          try {
            await apply(writeCharacter({ name: name || WORKING, settings, cloth: step.cloth, tailor: step.tailor, garments: {}, bodies: {} }))
          } catch (e) {
            tell(`could not undo: ${e?.message ?? e}`)
          } finally {
            stepping = false
          }
          walker.characterName.value = name
          // Kept, but not a new step (redo stays).
          keepWorking()
          el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        }
        // Not while a tool has the body: the rig tool undoes its own edits.
        const idle = () => !stepping && !rigging && !tailor?.tool
        character.canUndo = () => idle() && (history.canUndo || stepTimer != null)
        character.canRedo = () => idle() && stepTimer == null && history.canRedo
        character.undo = () => {
          if (!character.canUndo()) return
          // A change still settling is a step of its own.
          if (stepTimer != null) record()
          return restore(history.undo())
        }
        character.redo = () => character.canRedo() && restore(history.redo())
        const onKey = (e) => {
          if (!(e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) || e.key.toLowerCase() !== 'z') return
          if (e.target?.closest?.('input, textarea, [contenteditable]')) return
          // The tailor, while it is open, undoes its own edits.
          if (tailor?.tool && !stepping) {
            e.preventDefault()
            if (e.shiftKey) tailor.tool.redo()
            else tailor.tool.undo()
            return
          }
          if (!idle()) return
          e.preventDefault()
          if (e.shiftKey) character.redo()
          else character.undo()
        }
        window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
        el.whenDisposed?.(() => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey))
        for (const k of KEPT) walker[k].observe(() => character.changed())
        character.save = async (name) => {
          try {
            await store.put(name, snapshot(name))
          } catch (e) {
            return tell(`could not save: ${e?.message ?? e}`)
          }
          walker.characterName.value = name
          tell(`saved ${name}`)
          listSaved()
          character.changed()
        }
        // Put under the new name, then the old one goes.
        character.rename = async (from, to) => {
          if (to === from) return
          try {
            const doc = await store.get(from)
            if (!doc) return tell(`no character called ${from}`)
            await store.put(to, { ...doc, name: to })
            await store.delete(from)
          } catch (e) {
            return tell(`could not rename: ${e?.message ?? e}`)
          }
          if (walker.characterName.value === from) walker.characterName.value = to
          tell(`renamed ${from} to ${to}`)
          listSaved()
          character.changed()
        }
        character.load = async (name) => {
          const doc = name && (await store.get(name).catch(() => null))
          if (!doc) return tell(`no character called ${name}`)
          await apply(doc).catch((e) => tell(`could not load: ${e?.message ?? e}`))
          character.changed()
        }
        // The saved copy goes; the figure stays, unsaved, as the working one.
        character.remove = async (name) => {
          if (!name) return
          try {
            await store.delete(name)
          } catch (e) {
            return tell(`could not delete: ${e?.message ?? e}`)
          }
          if (walker.characterName.value === name) walker.characterName.value = ''
          tell(`deleted ${name}`)
          character.changed()
          listSaved()
        }
        character.exportJson = () => {
          const name = walker.characterName.value.trim() || 'character'
          save(JSON.stringify(snapshot(name), null, 1), `${name.replace(/[^\w-]/g, '_')}.character.json`, 'application/json')
        }
        character.importJson = () => {
          chooseFile('.json,application/json').then(async (file) => {
            if (!file) return
            try {
              await apply(await file.text())
              character.changed()
            } catch (e) {
              tell(`${file.name}: ${String(e?.message ?? e).replace(/^character-file: /, '')}`)
            }
          })
        }
        // Straight into the playground as this figure: kept now (not after
        // the autosave's pause), then the playground loads it by name.
        character.play = async () => {
          clearTimeout(pending)
          try {
            await store.put(WORKING, snapshot(walker.characterName.value || WORKING))
          } catch (e) {
            return tell(`could not keep it: ${e?.message ?? e}`)
          }
          location.href = `/playground/?character=${encodeURIComponent(WORKING)}`
        }
        el.builder.character = { snapshot, apply, store }
        // The figure you were working on, as you left it.
        const working = await store.get(WORKING).catch(() => null)
        if (working) await apply(working).catch((e) => console.warn('character builder: the working figure would not load', e))
        // Undo starts from the figure as it opened.
        history.clear(undoable())
        await listSaved()
        el.setLoading(false)
        play()
        el.refreshScenePanel?.()
        walker.clip.observe(play)
        walker.paused.observe(() => (walker.paused.value ? playing?.pause() : playing?.play(true)))
      },
    },
    // Things to hold: Tonio's weapons (CC BY 4.0), each with its grip at its origin.
    b3dLibrary({ url: assetUrl('tonio/weapons-classic/weapons.glb', 2), type: 'weapons' }),
    b3dSun({ timeOfDay: 16.5, shadowTextureSize: 2048, shadowMaxZ: 20, shadowNormalBias: 0.008 }),
    b3dLight({ intensity: 0.5 })
  )
)
```
```css
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

**Undo and redo** are the arrows at the top of the panel (⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z):
every change to the character as it settles, so a slider drag or a placed
grip is one step ([undo-history](/undo-history/)). The clip and its playback
are not steps. While the rig tool has the body, they undo the rig tool's
edits, and while the tailor is open, the tailor's.

**Source** picks the body. A first visit starts on one of four AI-made
characters at random (a woman and a man, each in underwear and in a
spacesuit; CC0, rigged when they load); after that the builder keeps the one
you chose. MakeHuman's is the one the sliders shape and the clothes, hair and
face are made for. The others are meshes from elsewhere (Blender Studio's
Human Base Meshes, Quaternius' superheroes), or
your own with **open a mesh…** (GLB or glTF). A file skinned to UAL's
skeleton already, as Quaternius' characters are, is taken as it is: its own
joints and weights ([rigged-body](/rigged-body/)). Bind your own mesh to that
skeleton in Blender and it is too; it comes with Quaternius'
[Universal Animation Library](https://quaternius.itch.io/universal-animation-library)
and [Universal Base Characters](https://quaternius.itch.io/universal-base-characters)
(CC0, pay what you want). Any other mesh has UAL's skeleton fitted to its
outline and its skin bound by bone heat ([auto-rig](/rig-build/)), in a
second or two. They walk, wear their own materials or the skin, and take
the tailor (below); the rest of the panel is MakeHuman's and is hidden for
them.

**Rig…** opens the [rig tool](/rig-tool/) on that body (its panel is on the
bar): drag the markers onto the joints and it is bound again on release; add
a tail, springs (a ponytail, a tail) or arm space. **Done** (at the top of the
Rig panel) brings the body back bound from that recipe, and the recipe is
saved with the character; **cancel** keeps the one it had. The first binding is a guess read
off the body's outline.

**Motion** plays a clip on whatever body is shown: UAL's library (the
everyday clips first), retargeted. **Clips from a file…** adds the clips of
any skinned GLB (a Mixamo or Meshy character's, say) or a BVH motion capture
([bvh](/bvh/)), retargeted the same way and listed after the everyday ones.
They are kept in this browser ([clip-store](/clip-store/)) and come back on
the next visit; **forget** drops the file a clip came from.

**View** (the camera on the bar) holds the body square on from any side, or
follows the **right hand** close up through the clip, to see how an item sits
in it. The rig tool uses the same menu. In a headset it leaves the bar: the
camera is your head.

**Animation** (on the bar) plays or pauses the clip and picks it: the
everyday clips, a file's, then the rest of the library grouped by kind.
**Playback controls** in that menu opens the transport (scrub, speed) as its
own small panel.

**Hold** puts an item from Tonio's textured weapons
(`tonio/weapons-classic/weapons.glb`, CC BY 4.0: guns, blades, a plasma
blade, a spear, a buckler) in the right hand, on the hand's
socket (a frame normalised to the hand's anatomy, so one grip fits any
body's hand). Every item is made the same way, its origin at its grip (a
`_grip` node), +Y up the grip and +Z forward, at its real size, so one grip
holds them all. Its **grip** says where the item's grip point goes, turned
and scaled, and is set per class of item ([[hold-grip|hold grips]]: pistols,
rifles, heavy weapons, one- and two-handed blades, bows, shields), so
placing it on one sword places every one-handed blade; the grips are kept
with the character. Play a clip
made for it (`Pistol_Idle_Loop`, the shoot loops) and check it in the hand
view. The numbers are a launcher's: `b3dLauncher({ socket: 'right-hand', x,
y, z, rx, ry, rz, modelScale })` holds it the same way on a biped.

**Character** (on the system bar, beside the body button) keeps your work,
as a File menu does. The figure you are working on is kept in this browser as
you change it and comes back when you open the page again. **Save** keeps it
under its name, asking for one the first time; **Save as…** under another
(asking first before replacing a saved character); **Rename…** renames it.
**Select ▸** lists the saved characters (the one on screen ticked): pick one
and it loads. **Delete ▸** picks one, then asks again. **Export JSON** takes
it elsewhere and **Load JSON…** brings one in: a file carries everything the
panel sets, and the garments of your own the character wears travel inside
it ([character-file](/character-file/)). **Go to Playground** plays it in the
biped playground.

Open the panel (the body button): the body sliders reshape it
while it walks, since every body carries its own joints. The skin weights are
bone heat's, worked out from the mesh once when the page loads. The eyes
([human-face](/human-face/)) follow the camera, and the hair
([human-hair](/human-hair/)) is Quaternius' CC0 hairstyles, made for another
head and fitted to this one.

**The tailor** is always on the bar (scissors). Open it, pick a **slot**
and a **garment** for it: one you cut before opens on its outline, ready to
edit; **(new garment)** starts one; anything else (MakeHuman's clothes, an
import with no outline) is simply worn. Click out an outline over the body's
front view (you draw the character's left, on your right; the other side is
its mirror), and the skin inside it, front and back, becomes cloth. A
rectangle from the waist to the ankles is a pair of trousers. Give it a
thickness, a material and a **name**. There is no done or cancel: what you
make is kept as you go, in this browser and worn in its slot, when you switch
slot or garment or close the panel, and **undo** and **redo** on the
tailor's bar (⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z) step through the edits. A new garment's outline is
kept with the character until it is closed, so the tailor carries on where
you left it. **Forget** removes one of your own.

A cut is a start, not a finished garment: **export** it (GLB or OBJ, the
garment and the body it was made on), shape it in Blender (a collar, pockets,
its own UV unwrap), and **import a garment** to bring it back as a choice in
its slot. It is bound to the body again by its shape, so it fits every body
like the rest ([garment-file](/garment-file/)). Or **export the body alone**
and model a garment from nothing beside it. In Blender, tick Include →
Custom Properties when exporting, so the file still says which body it was
made on.

A mesh's body (a file, the Blender or Quaternius bodies) has a tailor and a
wardrobe of its own: a garment cut or imported on it is worn on that body
only, and MakeHuman's clothes are MakeHuman's. Its **surfaces** (under the
source, on the Body tab) set each of the file's materials **as made** (its
textures, metal, glass) or in the
**skin**. Rig a tail before cutting round the hips: cloth is not cut from a
tail's skin.

New objects come in as part of the garment. Anything hard (a knee pad, a
plate, a visor) gets a `rigid` custom property so it keeps its shape instead
of bulging with the body under it ([proxy-rigid](/proxy-rigid/)).

Its surface is made in Blender too: the garment's material comes back with
its base colour, normal, roughness and alpha maps, and its **material** set
to **as made** with **recolour** at 0 shows it untouched. Recolour above 0
tints the base colour map, read as grey.

## humanBody

`humanBody(scene, pack)` draws a pack's body as one unrigged mesh, and
`update(positions)` reshapes it in place: for a body that only needs to be
looked at.


The pack is RIGHT-HANDED (as OBJ and glTF are), so the body sits under a
container that mirrors it the way glTF's `__root__` does, and stands with its
feet at the container's origin. Move the body by moving `root`. The mesh keeps
every vertex the targets move (helpers and joint cubes too), but draws only the
body's triangles.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/character-builder/

---

# human-pack

A **human pack** is a base body as data: its mesh, its joints and its shape
targets, converted from MakeHuman's CC0 assets by `static-assets`'
`bin/makehuman-pack.ts`. It is what the character creator (CHARACTER-DESIGN.md)
morphs; [human-morph](/human-morph/) says which targets a body uses and sums them.

A pack is a manifest (`hm08.json`) plus binaries named by their content hash,
so the binaries cache forever and a target is fetched the first time a body
asks for it. `loadHumanPack(url)` reads the manifest, the positions and the
body's triangles; `pack.target(name)` fetches one target (once).

What the manifest holds:

- **vertexCount**: every vertex, body and helpers (19,158 for hm08); targets move all of them
- **positions**: float32 xyz, metres, RIGHT-HANDED (as OBJ and glTF are)
- **body**: the triangles to draw (uint32, in threes), indexing the positions
- **joints**: a joint name → the vertices whose centroid it is (MakeHuman's joint cubes)
- **bones**: a bone → its parent, and the joints at its head and tail
- **regions**: a mask name (`lips`) → a uint8 per vertex, for tinting without UVs
- **proxies**: clothes, hair and brows bound to the base (MakeHuman's `.mhclo`: three base vertices, weights and a scaled offset per vertex), with their mesh, UVs, the base vertices they cover, and textures; see [proxy-fit](/proxy-fit/)
- **parts**: extra geometry on the body's own vertices (`eyes`, `eyelashes`), so every target moves it with the body: the pack vertices it uses (uint32), triangles indexing that list (uint32), and UVs (float32 pairs) where it has a texture
- **targets**: a target name → its file, its int16 step (metres), and whether it is dense

A dense target is int16 xyz for every vertex in order; a sparse one is `count`
uint32 vertex indices followed by `count` int16 xyz. Multiply by `step` for
metres.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/human-pack/

---

# character-file

**A character as one JSON document**: everything the
[character builder](/character-builder/) sets (where the body comes from, its
shape, skin, eyes, face, hair, clothes and their materials, the clip, the
tailor's work in progress) and the garments of your own it wears, so a file
opened on another machine dresses the same figure. The builder keeps the
figure you are working on in this browser (IndexedDB) and saves named ones
there too; **export** and **import** move them as files.

```javascript
import { writeCharacter, readCharacter } from 'tosijs-3d'

const doc = writeCharacter({ name: 'Ada', settings, cloth, tailor, garments })
const json = JSON.stringify(doc)
// …later, anywhere…
const { character, warnings } = readCharacter(json, defaults)
```

THE DOCUMENT IS VERSIONED. `format` is `tosijs-character` and `version` the
layout it was written in; `readCharacter` migrates an older one forward and
refuses one newer than it knows, rather than guess.

IT IS READ AGAINST THE PAGE'S DEFAULTS, so a document can never put the page
in a state it cannot draw: a setting the page does not have is dropped, one
of the wrong type is dropped, one that is missing keeps its default, and each
is listed in `warnings` (a document from a newer page, or a hand edit, then
loads as far as it can and says what it skipped).

GARMENTS TRAVEL INSIDE IT. A garment saved from the tailor lives in the
browser that saved it; the document carries each one the character wears as
its GLB (base64), so the figure is whole wherever it is opened.

SO DO ITS PICTURES: a print or texture chosen from disk for a material is
named in its recipe by a key ([material-pictures](/material-pictures/)), and
`pictures` carries each one the character's materials use (key → base64).

SO DOES ITS BODY, when it is a mesh. `bodies` says where the body on show
comes from: a URL (and the object picked in it) when it has one, or the file
itself (base64, with its name) when it was opened from disk. A page that
does not have that body makes it from there.

AND THE CLIP IT PLAYS, when that is one of your own: `clips` carries the file
it came from (a BVH capture or a GLB's animations, by file name, with its
kind), so a page that has never seen the file reads it as the builder did
([clip-store](/clip-store/)).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/character-file/

---

# character-store

**The characters this browser keeps**: the [character builder](/character-builder/)
saves here (the figure you are working on, and named ones), and any page on
the same site reads them back, so a game can offer the characters you built
(the [biped playground](/playground/) does).

```javascript
import { characterStore } from 'tosijs-3d'

const store = characterStore()
const names = await store.list()          // named saves, sorted
const doc = await store.get(names[0])     // a character document, whole
biped.characterDoc = doc
```

A MESH IS KEPT ONCE. What a document carries as bytes (a body opened from a
file, garments of your own) is stored apart, keyed by a hash of its content,
and each save keeps a reference to it; `get` puts the bytes back, so what
comes out is the same self-contained document that went in. Ten saves of one
figure on your own mesh hold that mesh once, and a mesh no save refers to
any more is let go. Saves made before this (the whole document in one
record) read as they are.

It lives in IndexedDB (`tosijs-characters`), so it is this browser's: a
character saved on one device is on another only if you export the file and
open it there.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/character-store/

---

# human-morph

The body sliders of the character creator (CHARACTER-DESIGN.md), as pure
functions over a [human pack](/human-pack/): which targets a body uses and how
much, and the sum that turns them into positions.

MakeHuman's macro targets are sculpted at the CORNERS of a grid: female or
male, baby, child, young or old, three muscle and three weight levels, and
three ancestries. A body between corners is a weighted mix of the corners
around it, and every slider is a position on one axis of that grid. The rules
here are written from MakeHuman's file names and documented behaviour; none of
their (AGPL) code is used. One number is MakeHuman's behaviour rather than its
data: the child corner at age 0.1875 (11 years) is where MakeHuman's own age
slider puts it (`apps/human.py`, `setAge`), reproduced so a slider value
means the same body in both.

The sliders, each from 0 to 1:

- **gender**: female at 0, male at 1
- **age**: 1 year at 0, 11 at 0.1875, 25 at 0.5, 90 at 1
- **muscle** and **weight**: least at 0, average at 0.5, most at 1
- **height**: shortest at 0, average for the rest of the body at 0.5, tallest at 1
- **proportions**: uncommon at 0, neutral at 0.5, ideal at 1
- **waist**: narrowest at 0, as the rest of the body has it at 0.5, widest at 1
  (MakeHuman's waist circumference, plus a pinch toward the centre line below
  0.5, because that target mostly takes depth off)

`african`, `asian` and `caucasian` are an ancestry MIX, normalised to sum to 1
(all zero is an even mix).

```javascript
const pack = await loadHumanPack(assetUrl('makehuman/hm08/hm08.json'))
const weights = macroWeights({ ...DEFAULT_HUMAN_BODY, height: 0.9 }, (n) => pack.has(n))
const positions = await morphHuman(pack, weights)
```

A dense macro costs about 0.03 ms to add on a desktop, so a body is morphed on
the spot rather than in a worker.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/human-morph/

---

# human-rig

UAL's 65-joint skeleton on a [human pack](/human-pack/)'s body, placed from
the body itself: every joint is the centre of one of MakeHuman's **joint
cubes**, small groups of vertices inside the mesh that the shape targets move
along with the skin. So a morphed body carries its own joint positions, and
nothing is fitted or guessed.


The [character builder](/character-builder/) shows it: the body walking while its sliders move.

## How it works

MakeHuman's own 163-bone skeleton is not used, only where its joints are. The
result is a `FittedRig`, the same thing the auto-rig produces from markers, so
the rest of that pipeline applies unchanged: `skinSegments` and `boneHeat`
bind the skin, `buildRig` makes the Babylon skeleton, and `retargetClip` plays
UAL's clips on it. The skin weights depend only on the mesh's topology, so
they are computed once per base and reused for every body.

`HM08_UAL` is the table, a row per UAL joint: its parent and the joint cube
it sits at (`bone____head` or `bone____tail`, in MakeHuman's naming), or a
rule for the two that have no cube (`root` is on the floor under the pelvis).
A base with different joint cubes brings its own table.

The pack is right-handed and a character faces +Z with its left on +X, as
`rig-fit` assumes, so MakeHuman's `.L` is UAL's `_l`.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/human-rig/

---

# tailor tool

**Cut a garment out of a body, and hand it back.** Draw an outline over the
body's front view and the skin inside it, front and back, becomes cloth:
a rectangle from the waist to the ankles is a pair of trousers. The tool
works on any [rigged body](/rigged-body/) (MakeHuman's, or a mesh the
[rig tool](/rig-tool/) bound), previews the cut on the body as it moves, and
on **done** hands your callback the garment. The
[character builder](/character-builder/)'s **tailor…** opens it.

```javascript
import { mountTailorTool } from 'tosijs-3d'

const tailor = mountTailorTool(scene, {
  body, // a RiggedBody: what it cuts from
  built, // the body on screen (buildBody): what the cut is shown on
  slots: ['top', 'bottom', 'outfit'],
  handleDone: ({ garment, name, slot, look, cut }) => wardrobe.add(garment, { name, slot, look, cut }),
  handleCancel: () => {},
})
```

**Its panel is a system panel** (scissors, on the bar). A bar pinned to its
top carries **undo**, **redo**, **cancel** and **done**; below it:

- **the outline**: you draw the character's left, on your right, and the
  other side is its mirror. Click out points, click the first to close a
  shape, drag a point to move it, press an edge to add one;
- **cloth mesh**: **as the body** (the default) cuts the body's triangles
  themselves, the cheapest and surest; or the cloth is cut from an even
  surface laid over the body ([remesh](/remesh/)), **coarse**, **medium** or
  **fine** (edges about 3, 2 or 1.2 cm), whatever the body's own triangles
  are;
- **thickness** (thicker cloth bridges more of the chest, where the body
  says where its nipples are);
- **made by**: **cutting the skin** (the cloth follows the body),
  **draping cloth** (a front and a back piece laid over the body, sewn where
  the outline runs up and down past its edge and settled under gravity, so
  it bridges hollows and hangs: dresses, tunics, robes; see
  [cloth drape](/cloth-drape/)), or **rings** (round the outline at each
  height: skirts, kilts);
- **material**, **name** and **slot**.

**Undo and redo** (and ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z through `undo()` / `redo()`, which a host's
keys call while the tool is open): each settled edit, a point dropped or a
slider let go, is a step.

WHAT DONE HANDS BACK is the garment as a mesh at rest, on the body it was
cut from (`garment`: positions, triangles, UVs unwrapped like a sewing
pattern), with what it was cut from (`cut`: the outlines, thickness, how it was made)
so it can be opened again, and the name, slot and material recipe. Binding it
to a body to wear (`bindGarment`) is the host's: a garment file carries the
same mesh.

A host that keeps the garment itself passes `persistent` (no cancel or
done), its own system panel as `panel`, and rows of its own above and below
(`rows: { top, bottom }`); the character builder does, so its tailor is
always on the bar.

`handleChange` hears every edit (a work in progress to keep); `setBody`
moves the cut onto a body reshaped while the tool is open; `unmount` (or
done, or cancel) removes everything it added.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/tailor-tool/

---

# tailor-recipe

A tailor's garment as a RECIPE that fits any body: its outlines, its
thickness and how it is made (cut from the skin, a skirt, draped cloth), plus
where the joints of the body it was drawn on were. `recutGarment(body, cut)`
makes it again on another rigged body: MakeHuman's at any slider setting,
or a mesh rigged from markers.

Outlines are drawn in metres in the front view, so on a taller or wider body
the same numbers fall in the wrong place. A recipe therefore carries its
body's LANDMARKS (the joints, seen from the front: hips, knees, ankles,
shoulders, elbows, wrists, the spine), and each outline point is carried to
the new body by a smooth warp that takes those joints exactly onto the new
body's (a thin-plate spline). A hem drawn at the knee lands at the knee, a
cuff at the wrist; between joints the outline bends smoothly with the body,
and beyond them (a cloak's hem below the feet) it carries on the same way.

- `outlineLandmarks(rig)`: a body's landmarks.
- `warpOutline(shapes, from, to)`: outlines from one body's landmarks to another's.
- `fitCut(cut, rig)`: a cut on the body it is about to be cut from (its
  shapes warped there, `on` updated).
- `tailorBody(body)`: the body as cutting needs it (the chest smoothed so
  cloth bridges it, which skin a skirt may go round, a tail left out).
- `recutGarment(body, cut)`: the garment, made on `body` (async: a draped
  cut settles a simulation).

Pure: no engine. The tailor tool records `on` with every cut it makes, and
keeps a cut's outlines on the body when the body changes shape.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/tailor-recipe/

---

# tailor panel

**The tailor, always on the system bar, and the wardrobe it keeps.** This is
the [character builder](/character-builder/)'s tailor as a piece any page
with a character can mount: a scissors button opens a panel with a slot and a
garment picker. A garment of your own made on the body shown opens on its
outline in the [tailor tool](/tailor-tool/); **(new garment)** starts one;
anything else is worn and the panel says why it cannot be cut. There is no
done or cancel: switching slot or garment, or closing the panel, keeps a
closed outline as a garment file (kept in a store, worn in its slot), and
undo covers the edits. Forget, export (GLB or OBJ, with the body as a helper
or alone) and import (a GLB or OBJ from Blender) are at the bottom.

```
const tailor = tailorPanel(b3dEl, {
  character: () => ch,
  target: () => ch.shown ?? 'loading the body…',
  slots: CHARACTER_SLOTS,
  choices: (slot) => ch.choices(slot),
  worn: (slot) => ch.settings[slot],
  wear: (slot, name) => ch.set({ [slot]: name }),
  madeOn: (source) => ({ format: 'tosijs-garment', version: 1, source }),
  draft: { get: () => draft, set: (d) => { draft = d } },
  save: (data, name, type) => download(data, name, type),
})
```

The host keeps what outlives the panel: the new garment's DRAFT (its outline,
thickness, mode, look and name, which a character file carries), the slot,
and what each slot wears. The store keeps garment files by name; the default,
`garmentStore()`, is this browser's IndexedDB (`tosijs-garments`), shared by
every page on the site.

The host also tells the tailor when to step aside: `keep()` before the body
changes under it (another source, the rig tool), `begin()` when it is back,
and the tool's `setBody` after a reshape (`editing.source` says which body it
was cutting). `tool` is the tailor tool while one is open, for undo and redo.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/tailor-panel/

---

# skin-tone

A skin's colour from one dial, very fair (0) through to very dark (1), plus
a `redness` dial for undertone. Pure: no Babylon, so a recipe's skin can be
checked or previewed headless. The [character builder](/character-builder/)
paints its body with it.

The dial runs through the ten tones of the **Monk Skin Tone Scale**
(Dr. Ellis Monk and Google, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/),
[skintone.google](https://skintone.google)), chosen because it was built to
cover the range of real skin evenly, the dark end included. Between two tones
it blends in linear light, as paint would mix, not in sRGB.

The scale's colours are swatches, meant to be SEEN on a screen, and they are
nearly neutral: tone 1 reflects only 18% more red than blue. Skin measured as
a surface is far warmer (fair skin about 1.7 times as much red as blue,
because blood under it absorbs blue and green), and a body painted with the
swatches looks grey and bloodless. So `skinAlbedo`, the colour for a
material, takes only each tone's LIGHTNESS from the scale, at a plausible
reflectance (fair skin reflects about 60% of red light, not 90%), and gives
it skin's own warmth: pinker at the fair end, more golden in the middle,
and nearly white at the very end (porcelain). `redness` is gentle near its
middle and strong at its ends: 0 drains the skin to a grey-white (a vampire,
or a goth's powder), 1 is flushed.
`skinColor` is the scale's swatch, for a UI.

IRIS colour is a dial too: `irisColor(t)` runs from dark brown through
brown, hazel, green and blue to grey, the order real eyes come in from most
melanin to least.

HAIR is two pigments too: `hairColor(light, red)` runs black to platinum,
with red from none to copper.

```javascript
hairColor(0.2, 0.8)   // auburn, linear
irisColor(0.6)        // green-blue, sRGB 0..1
skinColor(0)          // the scale's tone 1, sRGB 0..1
skinColor(1)          // tone 10
skinAlbedo(0.5, 0.6)  // a mid tone, a little ruddy, linear, for a material
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/skin-tone/

---

# skin-shading

Skin that reads as skin without a subsurface pipeline: three cheap terms a
material plugin adds to a PBR material, lit by the scene's sun. The
[character builder](/character-builder/) uses it on every body.

- **Scatter**: light wraps a little past the shadow line, reddened, the way
  light that went into skin comes out again beside where it went in. It
  softens the terminator, which is most of what makes a lit body look like
  painted plastic.
- **Rim**: a soft lift at grazing angles, the fine hair and oil on skin.
- **Back-light**: light from behind shows through the THIN parts (ears, the
  nose, fingers), reddened. Thinness is per vertex, worked out once from the
  mesh by `skinThinness`, and carried in the vertex colour's alpha. Babylon's
  own translucency needs a thickness texture, and without one it lit the
  whole back of a torso red.

`skinShading(material, options)` attaches it and returns the plugin, whose
`scatter`, `rim` and `backlight` can be changed live. It reads the scene's
first directional light each frame (or the `sun` you give it).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/skin-shading/

---

# human-face

Eyes and eyelashes for a [character builder](/character-builder/) body, and
a gaze that looks at something.

A pack's eyes are not a separate model fitted into the sockets: MakeHuman's
base mesh carries the eyeballs and eyelash cards as helper vertices, which
every shape target moves with the face, and the pack's `eyes` and
`eyelashes` PARTS are faces (and the eyes' UVs) over those vertices. So any
body has eyes that fit it, with nothing to fit.

`humanFace(scene, built, rig, pack, positions, parts)` hangs them on the
skeleton's head: each eye on its own pivot at the eyeball's centre (MakeHuman's
`eye` joint), so turning the pivot turns the eye. `eyeTexture` draws the eye
in code (sclera, a striated iris of any colour from `irisColor`, the pupil)
on MakeHuman's eye UV layout, so the iris is a dial and no image is shipped;
given a `style` (`basic`, `anime`) it paints Tonio's eye art instead
([eye-art](/eye-art/)), its iris recoloured the same way, the picture an
export bakes. The drawn eye shows while the art loads, or if it cannot.

`eyeGaze(scene, face, target)` points both eyes at a world point every frame,
after the clip has posed the head: they converge on it, stop at `maxDeg`
from straight ahead, and make small saccades, the jumps eyes really make
(they never glide), so a held gaze looks alive.

A FILE'S EYES work the same way: `bodyEyes(scene, built, eyes, material)`
hangs a rigged body's `eyes` (eyeballs that are objects of their own in the
file, as in Blender's Human Base Meshes) on pivots at their centres under the
head, mapped onto the same eye texture (`eyeUvs`), so the iris dial and
`eyeGaze` work on them too. Such a body has no lid targets, so its blink is
made from its shape: `lidBlink(positions, eye)` finds the opening in the
skin round the eyeball and turns the lids over it, a morph the same
`blinker` drives (and `lidsFollow` half-closes when the eyes look down). The
character builder gives lids to bodies rigged from markers, not to files
that come skinned.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/human-face/

---

# human-expression

A [character builder](/character-builder/) face that blinks, talks and
smiles. MakeHuman's CC0 face pose units (lids, jaw, lips, mouth corners,
brows, cheeks, tongue: 59 of them) are baked into the [human pack](/human-pack/)
as shape targets (`expression/<Unit>`), so at runtime an expression is only
weights: morph targets on the body, on the eyelashes, and on anything worn
on the face (a beard follows the jaw), with the body's skeleton untouched.

- `faceDeltas(pack, units)` loads the units' movements (xyz per pack vertex).
- `humanExpressions(scene, deltas)` makes the face; `attach(mesh, deltaFor)`
  adds a mesh that moves with it (`deltaFor` turns a pack-wide movement into
  that mesh's), and `layer(name)` is a set of weights (blink, speech, a
  mood), summed per unit, so behaviours never fight over a slider.
- `blinker(scene, face)` blinks at a person's rhythm: every 2 to 6 seconds,
  a quick close and a slower open, sometimes twice.
- `lidsFollow(scene, face, eyes)` drops the upper lids as the eyes look down
  and lifts them as they look up, as real lids do. Without it a downward
  look shows white above the iris and reads as a stare.
- `lipSync(scene, face, analyser)` mouths any Web Audio source by loudness
  (the jaw) and by where the sound's energy is (bright sounds widen the mouth,
  dark ones round it). No phonemes needed, so it works on any voice, live.
- `babble(scene, face)` talks with no audio at all: syllables at a speaking
  rate, phrases and pauses, for a crowd or a demo.

`VISEMES` are the mouth shapes as unit weights; `UNITS` lists every unit.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/human-expression/

---

# human-hair

Hairstyles, beards and eyebrows from a library made for another head, worn
by a [character builder](/character-builder/) body. The library is
Quaternius' CC0 hairstyles (`quaternius/libraries/hairstyles.glb` on the
CDN: 19 adult styles, their teen versions and six pairs of eyebrows), each
modelled in place on Quaternius' base head.

`loadHairLibrary(scene, url)` reads the library once: each piece's vertices
in the file's own frame (right-handed, +Z forward, the frame a human pack
uses), its UVs, its triangles and its material, and the HEAD it was
modelled on (`Reference_Head`, Quaternius' Regular_Male). The placing is
engine-free, in [hair-place](/hair-place/) (which also reads the library
with no engine); this module loads it into Babylon. `headScalp(...)`
warps that head's skin onto a body's ([hair-fit](/hair-fit/)): a per-axis
fit, then each skin point's own correction, the scalp and the face
separately. `humanHair(...)` carries any piece through the warp, so every
hair keeps its height above the scalp under it, and hangs it on the Head
bone so it moves with the clip.

Fitting the hair itself to the skin does not work: a style is one outer
shell with no underside, so laid on the skin it sinks by its own thickness.

The library's hair texture is a neutral grey meant to be tinted, so
`hairMaterial` gives one material per colour from `hairColor`: black to
platinum, plus red.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/human-hair/

---

# hair-shading

Hair coloured the way a colourist describes it: a BASE colour and a
HIGHLIGHT colour. A material plugin tints the hair texture with the base,
leans its brighter strands toward the highlight (so a dark base with caramel
highlights reads as highlighted hair, not a flat tint), and colours the
strand sheen with the highlight too.

`HAIR_COLOURS` are presets in pairs, natural and dyed: each base with the
highlight it usually comes with, which a picker can then move anywhere.

`hairShading(material, { desaturate })` attaches it; `desaturate` reads a
texture that is already coloured (MakeHuman's hair and beards) as grey first,
so the same colours apply to every library's hair.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/hair-shading/

---

# hair-fit

Hair made for one head, worn on another. A hairstyle library such as
Quaternius' is modelled around ITS base head, in world space; a
[character builder](/character-builder/) body has a different skull for
every slider setting. The style is carried from the head it was modelled
on to this one, skin to skin, all pure:

1. **`headRegion(skin, landmarks, region)`** picks the same region on any
   head from where its eyes are: the `scalp` (above the brow, and down to the
   nape behind the face) or the `face` (chin to forehead).
2. **`shellWarp(source, target)`** warps one head's region onto the other's:
   `fitToScalp`, a scale and offset per axis by iterated nearest points (ICP
   without rotation: both heads face +Z, up +Y), then what that fit missed,
   measured at each source skin point as the step to the nearest target skin.
   Given the target's normals, a `clearance` is added out along them.
3. **`applyWarp(positions, warp)`** carries hair through it: the fit, then the
   correction of the few source skin points nearest each hair vertex, so a
   hair keeps its height above the scalp under it whatever the skulls' shapes.
4. **`conformOutside(positions, skin, normals, margin)`** pushes any vertex
   still inside the skin back out along the skin's normal: a guard.

Fitting the HAIR to the skin, which this did first, does not work: a style
is one outer shell with no underside, so laid on the skin it sinks by its own
thickness. The library's styles are also tucked into their own skin in
places, which a warp keeps and the clearance covers.

`vertexNormals(positions, triangles)` gives a skin's normals (counter-clockwise
outward, as OBJ and glTF wind).

```javascript
const warp = shellWarp(
  headRegion(libraryHead, libraryEyes, 'scalp'),
  headRegion(bodyHead, bodyEyes, 'scalp')
)
const placed = applyWarp(styleVertices, warp)
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/hair-fit/

---

# human-proxy

A [human pack](/human-pack/)'s clothes, hair and brows on a built body:
fitted by [proxy-fit](/proxy-fit/)'s binding (so they follow every body
shape), skinned to the body's own skeleton with weights borrowed from the
skin they are bound to (so they bend with it), and drawn with their own
textures. `coverBody` hides the skin a garment covers, so it cannot poke
through.

The [character builder](/character-builder/) dresses its walker this way:
MakeHuman's CC0 casual, work and formal suits, shoes, a fedora, and its hair
and brows beside Quaternius'.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/human-proxy/

---

# proxy-fit

Clothes, hair and anything else made for a base body, fitted to every shape
of it. This is MakeHuman's `.mhclo` binding, read from the format and
re-implemented (no MakeHuman code): each proxy vertex is a weighted point on
a triangle of the base (three base vertices and their weights) plus an
OFFSET, and the offset is scaled per axis by how far apart two reference
vertices are on the body being fitted, so a coat is as loose on a large body
as on a small one. Morph the body and every proxy follows: no per-body work,
nothing to re-fit.

It is the one runtime fitter of the character creator (CHARACTER-DESIGN.md
step 4): MakeHuman's CC0 clothes, hair and brows come with their bindings in
the [human pack](/human-pack/), and hair made for another head is meant to be
imported as a binding too.

Pure, so a recipe's outfit is fitted or checked headless:

- `fitProxy(proxy, positions)` places the proxy's vertices on a body (every
  pack vertex, the pack's frame)
- `drawnPositions(proxy, fitted)` expands them to the drawn vertices (split
  where a UV seam needs it)
- `proxyWeights(proxy, vertexWeights)` gives each drawn vertex its skin
  weights from the base vertices it is bound to, so a garment bends with the
  body on the body's own skeleton
- `nearestWeights(...)` lends weights to vertices that have none (the base's
  helper vertices, which clothes bind to)
- `coveredTriangles(triangles, deleted)` drops the body triangles a garment
  hides, so skin never shows through it
- `underCover(hat, hair, triangles)` drops the hair a hat covers, so hair
  never pokes through a hat
- `smoothUnder(positions, triangles, mask)` smooths the body where `mask`
  says (the pack's `nipples` region), for clothes to be fitted over: cloth
  bridges a small bump, it does not follow it

A binding with `rigid` groups keeps those parts' shape in all three
(position, weights, expression movement): see [proxy-rigid](/proxy-rigid/).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/proxy-fit/

---

# cloth-shading

What makes cloth read as cloth at any distance is how it takes light, not its
texture: soft, rough cotton; a velvet that glows where it turns away; a satin
with a long, bright highlight; leather that is smooth and a little glossy.
`FABRICS` are those as presets over Babylon's PBR material (roughness, and its
SHEEN, the grazing-angle glow fibres give cloth), plus finishes that are not
cloth at all: vinyl, foil, chrome, brushed steel, gold and copper, for armour,
helmets and the cheap space suit. A metal needs something to reflect: give
the scene an environment (`studioEnvironment`), or it renders nearly black.
`clothShading` puts one on a garment's material, with a RECOLOUR on top.

The recolour reads the garment's texture as grey (its shading: folds,
stitching, a weave) and tints it, blended by `amount`: 0 keeps the texture's
own colours, 1 is the colour wholly, and a print shows through in between.
One sweater becomes a red one, a pastel one and a black one. A garment with
no texture (one cut from the body) takes the colour as its albedo.

```javascript
const shade = clothShading(material, { fabric: 'denim' })
shade.set({ fabric: 'wool', colour: '#7a2e2e', amount: 0.8 })
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/cloth-shading/

---

# garment-cut

A garment cut out of the body: draw a polygon over the front view (a
rectangle from the waist to the ankles is a pair of trousers), and the skin
inside it, front and back, is cut out along the outline, pushed out by a
thickness, and given a hem. The result is an ordinary proxy binding, so it
fits every body shape and bends with every clip exactly as MakeHuman's clothes
do ([proxy-fit](/proxy-fit/)).

- The outline is a **prism through the body**: everything inside the polygon
  in the front view, front and back. An optional side-view outline is
  intersected with it (a garment that stops short of the back, a bib).
- Several polygons are **one garment** (their union): two gloves, or a top
  and its sleeves drawn separately.
- The skin is cut **along** the outline, not at the nearest triangle edge, so
  a hem is a straight line, and neighbouring triangles share their cut points,
  so the hem has no cracks.
- A cut that goes **round a limb** (a sleeve, a trouser leg) is square to
  the limb, wherever the outline's line crosses it; a cut round the body
  (a waist, a hem) follows the line. A neckline drawn level is cut a little
  lower in front than behind (15°), as most are; a V or a scoop is cut as
  drawn.
- `thickness` pushes the cloth out along the body's normals; `ease` relaxes it
  across creases (between the legs, under the buttocks), so cloth bridges a
  hollow instead of following the skin into it.
- A **hem** joins the outer surface back to the skin, so a cut edge reads as
  cloth with a thickness rather than a paper shell.
- `delete` lists the body vertices the garment covers (for `coverBody`).

`skirtGarment` takes the same outlines and makes a skirt, kilt or robe
instead: at each height, the cloth goes round the CONVEX outline of
the body inside the cut (both legs as one, or the torso and arms), so it
spans the gaps instead of following each leg. Below its widest ring it hangs
straight down. It is an open tube, no top or bottom, to be drawn two-sided.
It is for the torso and legs: skirts, kilts, robes.
Each point is bound between the nearest skin on the left and on the right,
blended across the middle, so it moves with both legs and tears between
neither. `anchor` says which skin a skirt may go round; the builder leaves out the
arms (a skirt cannot follow a swinging arm without cloth simulation), so a
robe drawn over the arms is a skirt over the body and its sleeves a cut.

Pure: positions and triangles in, a binding out.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/garment-cut/

---

# outline field

**Polygons drawn over a body's front view.** The drawing half of
[garment-cut](/garment-cut/): the body's silhouette, and the outlines a
garment is cut along, clicked out point by point.

- **Click** to place points; click the first one again to close the shape.
- **Drag** a point to move it; press on an edge to add a point there.
- `undoPoint()` takes back the last point of the shape being clicked out
  (`redoPoint()` puts it back); a host's undo calls it before its own.
- `removeSelected()` deletes the last point touched (a button, since a
  controller has no reliable third gesture); a shape left with fewer than
  three points goes too. `clear()` removes everything.

Symmetry is on by default: you draw the character's left (on your right),
and the other side is drawn faint. A point dropped near the centre line snaps
onto it, and a shape with an edge on the centre line is one garment across
the body (trousers); any other is mirrored as a pair (gloves).
`mirrorOutline(field.value)` makes the polygons `cutGarment` takes.

It is an ordinary scene-panel control, so it works on a page, in the scene
and in a headset alike.

## Usage

```javascript
import { outlineField3d, mirrorOutline, cutGarment } from 'tosijs-3d'

const field = outlineField3d({
  positions, indices,   // the body, as triangles (left on +X, facing +Z)
  value: halves,        // half outlines, [x, y] on the +X side
  handleCommit: (halves) => recut(mirrorOutline(halves)),
})
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/outline-field/

---

# remesh

A surface with even triangles, laid over a mesh that has bad ones: the
tailor's DUMMY. A body from a file (a scan, an AI model) is long slivers and
islands split along its UV seams, and cloth cut from it inherits both. This
builds a new surface of nearly equilateral triangles at the edge length you
ask for and pulls it onto the old one, so the cloth is cut from good
topology whatever the body was made of.

```javascript
import { remesh } from 'tosijs-3d'
const dummy = remesh(body.positions, body.indices, { edge: 0.02 })
dummy.positions   // on the body's surface
dummy.ref         // each vertex's body triangle (three vertices)...
dummy.weight      // ...and where on it (barycentric)
dummy.project(x, y, z)  // any point onto the body, as the same pair
```

THE SIZE FOLLOWS THE SHAPE. One edge length cannot do a body: 2 cm is right
for a torso and wider than a finger, so a glove came out as mittens. Where
the body is thin, each point's target is `perRadius` times its radius there
(the largest ball inside the skin under it): about 6 mm on a finger or a
toe, the full `edge` on an arm or a chest, never below `minEdge`. It grows no
faster than half a metre per metre across the surface, so the triangles
grade from hand to arm instead of jumping. Thickness, not curvature: a scan's
bumps curve tightly everywhere and asked for tiny triangles all over.

It is Botsch and Kobbelt's isotropic remeshing (2004), each pass:

- **split** every edge longer than 4/3 of the target at its middle;
- **collapse** every edge shorter than 4/5 of it, unless that would make an
  edge too long, fold a triangle over or pinch the surface;
- **flip** edges toward six edges at every vertex (four on a boundary);
- **relax** each vertex toward the middle of its neighbours, along the
  surface only;
- **project** every vertex back onto the original surface (its nearest
  point, through [mesh-sdf](/mesh-sdf/)).

The input is welded first (vertices at one position become one), so UV seams
do not survive into it. Boundary vertices stay where they are and boundary
edges are never collapsed or flipped, so holes (eyes, a cut-off neck) keep
their shape. An edge shared by three or more triangles is left alone too.

Pure: positions xyz and triangles in threes in, counter-clockwise outward;
the result has the same winding.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/remesh/

---

# cloth drape

**Cloth laid over a body instead of cut from its skin.** An outline drawn in
the front view is a pattern piece: flat cloth is meshed from it, a front and
a back, laid on the body and settled. Where the outline goes past the body's
edge (between the legs, under an arm, out at a flared hem) the two pieces are
SEWN together and hang there; where it crosses the body (a neckline, a
waist, a cuff) they stay open, pinned to the skin. The cloth then bridges the
hollows a skin cut follows (between the breasts, the small of the back) and
falls where nothing holds it up.

```javascript
import { remesh, drapeGarment } from 'tosijs-3d'
const dummy = remesh(body.positions, body.indices, { edge: 0.02 })
const dress = drapeGarment(dummy, body.positions, {
  front: [[[-0.2, 1.45], [0.2, 1.45], [0.35, 0.5], [-0.35, 0.5]]],
})
// a GarmentCut: bound to the body like any cut, drawn with fitProxy
```

It works on the tailor's DUMMY ([remesh](/remesh/)): the even surface laid
over the body is what the cloth is placed on and collides with, and each
vertex of the settled cloth is bound to the body through it (its nearest
point on the body, plus its offset), so it is worn exactly like a cut
garment.

THE STEPS:

1. **The piece**: the outline's edge resampled to the cloth's edge length,
   triangulated, then remeshed flat so its triangles are even.
2. **Lift**: each vertex goes onto the front of the body (front piece) or the
   back (back piece) along the view direction, `thickness` out. Vertices
   whose ray misses the body are filled in from their neighbours, and the
   edge outside the body is shared by both pieces: the seam. So is an edge
   running along the body's RIM (the top of an arm or a shoulder, the side of
   a hip or a thigh; within 2.5 cm, just outside or just inside it): one vertex
   on the rim, pinned, so the cloth goes over the limb rather than hanging off
   its front and back.
