3. **Bridge**: a few passes pull each free vertex toward its neighbours and
   back out of the body, as cloth under a little tension does. Its lengths
   then are the cloth's.
4. **Settle**: gravity, the lengths held (position-based dynamics), the body
   pushed out of, the open edges pinned, until it stops.

Pure: the dummy and the body's positions in, a `GarmentCut` out.

`drapeGarmentAsync` is the same drape in time slices (about 8 ms of work
between tasks), stopped by an `AbortSignal`: an editor starts one per edit and
stops the one before, so moving a point never waits for a stale drape.
`drapeSteps` is the generator both run.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/cloth-drape/

---

# body-sweep

Clothes, shoes and hair as SWEEPS: a profile taken from the body and carried
along a path, with curves along the way. This is the primitive under the
tailor, the barber and the cobbler (see CHARACTER-DESIGN.md, step 11).

`loftGarment` is the LOFT: rings round the body's cross-section, carried
along a chain of bones (a leg, an arm, the foot). Each ring is the convex
HULL of the body's slice there, so it bridges hollows, plus `thickness` and
an `ease` that may change along the sweep (a flared trouser leg, a puffed
sleeve, a bucket top).

- The slice at a station takes only the skin of that station's BONE (its
  skin weights), so a ring round the shin never takes in the foot, and a
  ring round the thigh never the other leg. `piece` narrows it further: the
  body between its cuts.
- Where the chain bends (the ankle, the elbow), rings square to each bone
  would cross. The join is a MITRE: the ring at the joint lies in the plane
  halfway between the bones, and the rings either side are kept behind it,
  as in a pipe elbow. `steps` rounds the bend instead: that many rings
  turning gradually along a curve through the joint. 0 is the clean mitre,
  which is the default because it round-trips to a modelling tool cleanly.
- Each end is `open` (a free edge: it may stand off the body), `sealed`
  (it meets the body or the next piece: the ease fades to nothing there),
  or `cap` (closed, a toe).
- `length` carries the last ring on past the end of the chain (a hem below
  the ankle, a toe allowance).
- UVs come free: u is round the ring, v along the sweep, in metres.

The result is an ordinary garment binding (as [garment-cut](/garment-cut/)
makes), each ring point bound to the skin it was sliced from, so it fits
every body shape and bends with every clip.

Pure: a rigged body in, a binding out.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/body-sweep/

---

# garment-bind

Any mesh made around a body, bound to it: each vertex becomes the nearest
point on the body's skin (a body triangle and weights) plus an offset, the
same binding MakeHuman's clothes and [garment-cut](/garment-cut/) use, so
the mesh then fits every body shape and bends with every clip
([proxy-fit](/proxy-fit/)).

This is how a garment modelled by hand comes in: export one from the
character builder (the garment and the body it was made on,
[garment-file](/garment-file/)), shape it in Blender (a collar, pockets, its
own UV unwrap), and import it. Binding needs nothing from the file but the
positions, so it does not matter what an editor did to the vertex order.

```javascript
import { bindGarment, fitProxy } from 'tosijs-3d'

// `body`: the body the garment was modelled on (every base vertex).
const binding = bindGarment(body, pack.triangles, garment.positions)
const fitted = fitProxy(binding, anotherBody)
```

Geometry added in an editor binds like the rest: a collar, a pocket or a
whole new object (every mesh in the file but the body is read). Each vertex
follows its own nearest skin, which is right for cloth; anything hard (a knee
pad, a visor) should be marked rigid ([proxy-rigid](/proxy-rigid/)) or it
bulges with the body under it.

Each vertex goes with the skin nearest to it, so a loose part between two
limbs (a wide sleeve against the side) can follow the wrong one. Close-fitting
clothes, collars and trims bind cleanly.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/garment-bind/

---

# garment-file

**A garment out to Blender and back.** `writeGarmentGlb` saves a garment and
the body it was made on, so it can be reshaped by hand (a collar, pockets,
its own UV unwrap), and `readGarment` brings the edited file back for
[garment-bind](/garment-bind/) to bind to the body again.

The file holds the **`garment`** as worn, with its normals and UVs, and,
when `body` is given, a **`body-reference`**: the body it was made on, as a
HELPER to model against. It is marked so (`helper: true` and
`role: 'reference'` in its custom properties) and drawn translucent, and it
is left out on the way back in, so it can stay in the Blender file.

What the garment was made on travels as glTF `extras` (on the scene and on
the garment), under `tosijs`: the base (`hm08`), the pack version, the body's
slider values, the garment's name and slot. Blender keeps `extras` as custom
properties; **tick Include → Custom Properties when exporting** so they come
back. Without them the garment is bound to whatever body is loaded.

Coordinates are the pack's and glTF's own: metres, +Y up, the body facing
+Z with its left on +X, so nothing is converted. Blender's glTF importer turns
that into its Z-up and its exporter turns it back.

The garment's **material** comes back too (`material`): it is glTF's own
metallic-roughness material, which is what Blender's Principled BSDF exports,
so a surface is made in Blender and not here. Plug images into Base Color
(its alpha is the garment's alpha), Normal (through a Normal Map node) and
Roughness (and Metallic); set the material's blend mode to Alpha Clip or
Alpha Blend for a cut-out or see-through one. The exporter packs roughness
and metalness into one image, and the images travel inside the GLB. Where the
parts use several materials, the first part's is the one read
(`materialCount` says how many there were). `unwrapGarment` gives a garment UVs from
its shape ([uv-unwrap](/uv-unwrap/)): a front and a back for each side, like
a sewing pattern, packed into the unit square, so a map can be painted on it
or a pattern run across it. The character builder unwraps a cut before
exporting it; unwrap it again in Blender if you want other seams.

Leave out the `garment` to export the body alone, to model a garment from
nothing: every object you add beside it comes back as the garment. The body
carries the metadata then.

OBJ is the escape hatch: plain text that a few lines of your own code can
read and write, for processing a garment outside any editor. It is kept
simple on purpose: `v`, `vt` and `f` lines, one `o` per part, rigidity in the
part's name (`_rigid`, `_rigidParts`), the metadata in a first-line comment.
`writeGarmentObj` writes it and `readGarment` reads either format. Blender
drops the OBJ's metadata comment, so the body helper's NAME carries the body
as well: `body-reference_hm08_p15_weight72_muscle100` is the base, the pack
version, and each slider that is not the default as a whole percentage
(`referenceName` / `metaFromName`). Keep the name when you edit the file. It
is read when nothing better is there, a glTF exported without custom
properties included; the garment's name and slot do not travel in it.

```javascript
import { writeGarmentGlb, readGarment } from 'tosijs-3d'

const bytes = writeGarmentGlb({ garment, body, meta })
// …edited in Blender…
const { garment, meta } = readGarment(await file.arrayBuffer())
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/garment-file/

---

# uv-unwrap

**UVs for a mesh, worked out from its shape.** A garment exported to
Blender gets a layout an artist can paint on and a pattern can run across,
without anyone marking seams: the mesh is cut along the two planes through its
middle, the one between left and right and the one between front and back, so
a ball falls into four pieces and a pair of trousers into a front and back for
each leg, the way a sewing pattern has them. Each piece is flattened by
**least-squares conformal maps** (Lévy et al. 2002), which keeps angles, so a
check stays square; scaled to its true area; turned so the mesh's up is up;
and the pieces are packed into the unit square.

The seams are straight. A vertex within a quarter of an edge of a plane is
taken as on it, and a triangle that crosses a plane is cut where its edges
meet it, so the seam runs through existing vertices where they are close and
through new points between them where they are not. `unwrapUvs` returns the
mesh as cut, with a vertex on a seam once for each piece it borders: its
`positions`, and for each vertex the input vertices it is made of (`ref`,
`weight`, four each), so normals, weights or anything else per vertex
carry over (`carryUnwrapped`). `metresPerUnit` is how many metres one UV
unit spans, for a tiling texture at its real size.

```javascript
import { unwrapUvs, carryUnwrapped } from 'tosijs-3d'

const u = unwrapUvs(positions, triangles)
// u.triangles index u.positions and u.uvs
const normals = carryUnwrapped(inputNormals, 3, u)
```

Seams are the two planes by default, through the middle of the mesh's
bounds: `seams: { x: 0, z: false }` puts the left/right seam at x = 0 and
makes no front/back seam. A piece the planes leave in several parts (two legs
in one quarter) becomes several pieces. A closed piece with no boundary of its
own (a sphere quarter has one; a whole sphere would not) is fine, because the
planes always open it.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/uv-unwrap/

---

# garment proxy

**A garment of your own, bound to a body, with no engine.** A garment file
(from the [tailor](/tailor-tool/) or Blender, see [[garment-file]]) is a mesh
and a note of the body it was made on. `garmentProxy` binds it to that body
and hands back the same `HumanProxy` MakeHuman's own clothes are (a binding,
triangles, uvs, a name, a slot, category `clothes`), so it goes through the
same path: `fitProxy` onto any shape of the body, `coverSkin`, weights,
morphs. A character in the builder wears it this way, and an exporter
writes it this way.

```javascript
import { readGarment } from 'tosijs-3d/garment-file'
import { garmentProxy, garmentMadeOn } from 'tosijs-3d/garment-proxy'
import { morphHuman, macroWeights } from 'tosijs-3d/human-morph'

const content = readGarment(bytes)
// MakeHuman's body in the shape it was made on (its sliders are in the file).
const on = morphHuman(pack, macroWeights(garmentMadeOn(content.meta), (n) => pack.has(n)))
const proxy = garmentProxy(content, { positions: on, triangles: pack.triangles })
proxy.material.baseColorTexture // { bytes, mimeType }, or null
proxy.material.gltf // the look as glTF factors, where it has a plain reading
```

The material is DATA, not URLs: the file's pictures as bytes, its factors,
`twoSided` (a skirt or a draped garment is seen from inside), and `look`, the
material recipe it was worn with when saved. `gltf` reads that look as glTF
metallic-roughness factors (and sheen, for cloth) where it has a plain
reading: a flat colour on a garment with no picture of its own, a flat
roughness and metalness. A look that recolours the garment's own picture has
no factor reading; `recolourCloth` (cloth-bake) bakes it into the picture.

A garment made on a mesh's body (its `meta.source` names the mesh) binds to
that body the same way: pass the rigged body's `positions` and `indices`.

MAKEHUMAN'S OWN CLOTHES go out the same way. They are bound to the pack's
every vertex, helpers included, and the skin a MakeHuman body draws is a part
of them (or a lighter body proxy over them), so `onSkin` binds the piece as
worn to that skin instead, carrying the skin it deletes across; and
`packGarmentMaterial` is a pack proxy's material as data, its pictures as
bytes the caller fetched.

```javascript
const drawn = drawnPositions(proxy, fitProxy(proxy, body.full))
const garment = {
  ...onSkin(proxy, drawn, { positions: body.positions, triangles: body.indices, vertices: body.skin.vertices }),
  material: packGarmentMaterial(proxy, { diffuse }, look),
}
riggedBodyGlb(body, { garments: [garment], bake: bakeClothLook }) // from 'tosijs-3d/cloth-bake'
```

Pure: no DOM, no Babylon.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/garment-proxy/

---

# proxy-rigid

Parts of a garment that must keep their shape: an armour plate, a helmet's
visor and its locking ring, a buckle. A bound garment otherwise follows the
skin point by point, which is right for cloth and wrong for anything hard:
on a heavier body a knee pad bulges with the knee, and in a clip it bends
with it.

A rigid part moves as one piece. On a new body shape it is placed where its
flexible fit would put it, by the best rotation, uniform scale and
translation (Horn's method), so it keeps its shape and is sized to the body.
Its skin weights are the part's average, so the clip carries every vertex of
it by the same transform and nothing bends.

Rigidity is a dial per vertex, `0` (cloth) to `1` (hard), so a part can be
partly rigid: the fabric of a spacesuit's neck can run from flexible at the
shoulders to rigid where it meets the ring, by blending each vertex between
its own fit and the part's.

Which vertices belong together is a GROUP. A rigid object is one group; a
rigid object made of separate plates can be a group per plate (its loose
islands); and objects that must move together (the visor and the ring) share
a named group.

Set in Blender as custom properties on an object (exported with Include →
Custom Properties, see [garment-file](/garment-file/)):

| `rigid` | means |
| --- | --- |
| `1` (or a tick) | the object is one rigid piece |
| a number below 1 | the whole object is that rigid |
| `parts` | each loose island of the object is its own rigid piece |
| `paint` | rigidity painted as the vertex colour's red, islands as pieces |
| any other word | a named group: every object with the same word is one piece |

A float attribute named `_rigid` (exported with Data → Mesh → Attributes)
sets each vertex's dial instead of the object's number. Paint is the mesh's
active colour layer, which Blender exports by default when the object has no
material; with a material, set Data → Mesh → Vertex Color to Active. A name
ending `_rigid` or `_rigidParts` does the same as the first and third rows,
for files without custom properties (an OBJ).

All of these have been round-tripped through Blender 5.2's glTF exporter, and
the suffixes through its OBJ exporter.

Pure: `rigidGroups` resolves the groups from a mesh and its parts, and
`fitProxy`, `proxyWeights` and `proxyDelta` honour a binding's `rigid`.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/proxy-rigid/

---

# character

**A character from its settings, ready to animate.** The
[character builder](/character-builder/) is a panel over this: what it sets is
a character's SETTINGS (a body, a skin, hair, clothes, a face, a rig), and
`makeCharacter` turns them into a dressed, rigged body in a scene. The same
settings, read from a [character file](/character-file/), make the same
character anywhere: a game puts it under a biped and plays clips on it.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dBiped, b3dSun, b3dLight, b3dGround, inputFocus, ualAnimationStates } from 'tosijs-3d'

preview.append(
  b3d(
    { style: 'width:100%;height:100%', gamepad: 'left_stick,right_stick' },
    b3dSun({ timeOfDay: 15, shadowTextureSize: 2048 }),
    b3dLight({ intensity: 0.5 }),
    b3dGround({ width: 40, height: 40, color: '#5d6672' }),
    inputFocus(
      b3dBiped({
        character: '/characters/casual.character.json',
        animationStates: ualAnimationStates(),
        player: true,
        cameraType: 'follow',
      })
    )
  )
)
```
```css
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

A character file exported from the [character builder](/character-builder/)
(**export JSON**), walking under a `<tosi-b3d-biped character="…">`: move with
WASD or the left stick, look with the mouse or the right stick. The biped
makes the character from the file and retargets UAL's clips onto it, so its
states are UAL's (`ualAnimationStates`). Making it takes a few seconds: the
body's skin is bound when it is made.

## In code

```
const assets = await loadCharacterAssets(scene)
const character = await makeCharacter(scene, assets, {
  settings: readCharacter(doc).character.settings,
  gaze: () => camera.position,
})
character.root.parent = someNode           // move it by this
const walk = retargetClip(ualWalk, ualSkeleton, character.skeleton, {
  scene, armSpaceDeg: character.recipe?.armSpaceDeg,
  footTurnDeg: character.recipe?.footTurnDeg,
})
walk.start(true)
character.set({ smile: 0.6, hair: 'short02' })  // change it live
```

The body is MakeHuman's, shaped by its sliders, or a mesh from a file (a
`source`: Blender's Human Base Meshes, Quaternius' characters, your own),
rigged from its rig recipe (`rigs`, the [rig tool](/rig-tool/)'s) or its own
skin when it is skinned to UAL's skeleton. MakeHuman's body wears MakeHuman's
clothes, hair and face; any body wears the garments made on it
(`addGarment`, from the [tailor](/tailor-tool/) or Blender).

`set(changes)` applies only what changed: a slider reshapes the body, a slot
dresses it again, a colour repaints. The work is in `ready()`.

## The settings

`DEFAULT_CHARACTER` lists them with their defaults: MakeHuman's macro sliders
(`DEFAULT_HUMAN_BODY`), `tone` and `redness` (the skin), `iris` and
`irisColour`, `eyeStyle` (Tonio's eye art, `basic` or `anime`, or `drawn` in
code), `stubble`, the hair (`hair`, `beard`, `moustache`, `brows`,
`hairBase`, `hairHighlight`, and `hairUp`, `hairForward`, `hairSize` to
nudge it), one setting per clothes slot (`CHARACTER_SLOTS`, a garment's name
or `none`), the face (`smile`, `browsUp`, `frown`, and `blink`, `talk`),
`source` (`MakeHuman` or a mesh's name), `rigs` (each mesh's rig recipe) and
`surfaces` (each mesh's materials, `as made` or `skin`). `hideClothes` takes
everything worn off for a moment (the tailor's "hide other clothes"), and
`hideSlot` one slot's garment (the one being tailored, which the tailor
draws itself).

Each slot's material is separate (`setCloth(slot, { look, material })`): a
garment's colourway and a material recipe over it.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/character/

---

# character sources

**The bodies a character can have besides MakeHuman's**, as data: where each
mesh is on the asset CDN, which node to take, and for Tonio's AI-made cast
(CC0, `tonio/ai`) the rig he placed by hand in the [rig tool](/rig-tool/):
the front markers, joints moved after the fit, and how much hand to rig (the
spacesuits' gloves are mittens). Engine-free, so an exporter or another engine
rigs the cast the way the [character builder](/character-builder/) does:

```javascript
import { AI_CHARACTER_SOURCES } from 'tosijs-3d/character-sources'
import { glbRigTriangles } from 'tosijs-3d/glb-rig'
import { bodyFromMarkers } from 'tosijs-3d/rigged-body'
import { riggedBodyGlb } from 'tosijs-3d/rigged-body-glb'

const source = AI_CHARACTER_SOURCES['eurasian-male-spacesuit']
const bytes = new Uint8Array(await (await fetch(source.url)).arrayBuffer())
const body = bodyFromMarkers(glbRigTriangles(bytes, { pick: source.pick }), source.recipe.binding)
const glb = riggedBodyGlb(body, { recipe: source.recipe })
```

A source's `url` is read when it is used, under the asset base
(`assetUrl`), so set the base first. `rigFromMarkers` is how a hand-placed rig
is written down: the left side, mirrored to the right.

Pure: no DOM, no Babylon.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/character-sources/

---

# Skybox Baker

**Stand inside a galaxy and photograph the sky.** Six 90° renders from one point
become a cube map — a starfield with real structure, for the cost of a texture
fetch at runtime instead of tens of thousands of particles every frame.

The point is not that it is cheaper, though it is. It is that **the sky you bake
is the galaxy you can fly to**: you are photographing actual star positions from
an actual system, so the constellations a character sees from the ground are the
same objects on the navigation chart. A decorative starfield can never be that,
however pretty.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dGalaxy, bakeSkyboxCube, bakeSkyPair, starsFromVoxelGalaxy, facesToZip, defaultBakePose, SHIPPED_SKY, button3d, label3d, slider3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { bake } = tosi({
  bake: { seed: 1234, stars: 10000, particleSize: 0.7, outFraction: 0.55, offPlane: 1, roll: 0, face: 1024, status: 'ready' },
})

let sceneEl = null

// THE GALAXY DOES NOT REBUILD ITSELF. Changing `starCount` sets a property and
// nothing more — `regenerate()` is what rebuilds the particle systems, so an
// observer below calls it. Without that every slider here would be inert.
//
// Debounced: a drag would otherwise queue one rebuild per step.
const galaxy = b3dGalaxy({
  seed: bake.seed,
  starCount: bake.stars,
  // The shipped sky's dim budget: dim stars only exist near the bake point,
  // so this costs nothing until the pair bake gathers them.
  dimBudget: SHIPPED_SKY.voxel.dimBudget,
  particleSize: bake.particleSize,
  coreSize: 0.12,
  radius: 100,
})

let pending = 0
for (const key of ['seed', 'stars', 'particleSize']) {
  bake[key].observe(() => {
    clearTimeout(pending)
    pending = setTimeout(() => galaxy.regenerate(), 400)
  })
}

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      style: 'width:100%;height:100%',
      clearColor: '#01020a',
      panelTitle: 'Bake a sky',
      scenePanel: () => [
        // 10k to work with, 100k to finish with — see "Framing, then baking".
        slider3d({ label: 'stars', value: bake.stars, min: 5000, max: 100000, step: 5000 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'particle size', value: bake.particleSize, min: 0.1, max: 1.5, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'out from core', value: bake.outFraction, min: 0.1, max: 0.9, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'off plane', value: bake.offPlane, min: 0, max: 6, step: 0.25 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'roll', value: bake.roll, min: -180, max: 180, step: 5 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'face px', value: bake.face, min: 256, max: 4096, step: 256 }),
        label3d({ text: bake.status, muted: true }),
        button3d({ label: 'bake cube', handleClick: async () => {
          bake.status = 'baking…'
          const faces = await bakeSkyboxCube(sceneEl.scene, {
            ...defaultBakePose(100, bake.outFraction.valueOf(), bake.offPlane.valueOf()),
            size: bake.face.valueOf(),
            roll: bake.roll.valueOf(),
          })
          // ONE zip, not six downloads — a burst of automatic downloads gets
          // throttled and dropped by the browser (see facesToZip).
          const zip = facesToZip([{ prefix: 'sky', faces }], 'sky-cube.zip')
          const a = document.createElement('a')
          a.href = URL.createObjectURL(zip.blob)
          a.download = zip.name
          a.click()
          setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href), 5000)
          bake.status = `saved ${zip.name} (${faces.length} faces)`
        } }),
        // THE PAIR: a 256 smooth cube for the nebulae plus a 1024 DATA cube
        // the sky shader decodes into points. The right output once the star
        // slider is at 100k — a plain raster at that density is a picture of
        // itself, and it would need 4096 to stop smearing.
        // THE SHIPPED SKY'S RECIPE — sets every slider to what produced
        // static/sky, so a rebake is one tap here and one tap below. (It used
        // to live only in commit messages; reproducing it took archaeology.)
        button3d({ label: 'use shipped recipe', handleClick: () => {
          bake.stars = SHIPPED_SKY.voxel.brightBudget
          bake.particleSize = SHIPPED_SKY.particleSize
          bake.outFraction = SHIPPED_SKY.outFraction
          bake.offPlane = SHIPPED_SKY.offPlane
          bake.roll = SHIPPED_SKY.roll
          bake.status = 'shipped recipe — rebuilding, then bake pair'
        } }),
        button3d({ label: 'bake pair (256 + 1024 data)', handleClick: async () => {
          bake.status = 'baking pair…'
          const eye = defaultBakePose(100, bake.outFraction.valueOf(), bake.offPlane.valueOf())
          // THE POINTS come from the voxel galaxy: every bright star, the dim
          // stars around the eye, the shell — what bin/bake-stars writes too.
          const sky = starsFromVoxelGalaxy(galaxy.galaxy, undefined, eye, {
            radius: 100,
            dimReach: SHIPPED_SKY.voxel.dimReach,
            floor: SHIPPED_SKY.voxel.floor,
          })
          const res = await bakeSkyPair(sceneEl.scene, galaxy, {
            ...eye,
            roll: bake.roll.valueOf(),
            smoothSize: 256,
            dataSize: 1024,
            objects: sky.objects,
          })
          const zip = facesToZip(
            [
              { prefix: 'nebula', faces: res.smooth },
              { prefix: 'stars', faces: res.data },
            ],
            'sky-pair.zip'
          )
          const a = document.createElement('a')
          a.href = URL.createObjectURL(zip.blob)
          a.download = zip.name
          a.click()
          setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href), 5000)
          bake.status = `pair baked: ${res.placed} placed, ${res.lost} lost`
        } }),
      ],
      sceneCreated(el) { sceneEl = el },
    },
    galaxy
  )
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

## Six cameras, and why not a probe

`ReflectionProbe` is the better idea on paper — it renders a correctly-oriented
cube, so the face conventions stay Babylon's problem rather than ours — but its
`cubeTexture.readPixels(face)` returns all zeros here, every face. Six silently
black squares is a worse failure than a little more code, so the faces are
rendered with a camera instead.

The orientation table is therefore written out in full rather than trusted to
memory. The ±Y rows are the ones that bite: they need a different UP vector,
because "up" is undefined when you are looking straight up, and getting it wrong
gives you a sky with one face rotated 90° that nobody notices until a player
stares at the zenith.

## Where to stand

`defaultBakePose` puts you **55% of the way out from the core and slightly above
the plane**, which is roughly where Earth is — the Sun sits about 8 of the disc's
~13 kpc out, a few tens of parsecs up. Each part earns its place:

| choice | what it buys |
| ------ | ------------ |
| 50–60% out | the core is off to one side and bright, the far rim thin behind it. Dead centre is dense in every direction; the rim leaves one half empty |
| slightly off-plane | lets the band read AS a band — and TINY is the word. The disc half-thickness here is ~12, so 1 is plenty; 3 already reads as looking down on the galaxy rather than living in it |
| **tilted** | the band ARCS across the sky instead of lying level — and a level band reads as wallpaper the moment anyone looks up. Applied to the CUBE, not the galaxy: rotating the subject moves it out from under the camera |

The tilt is the one worth insisting on, and it is free: it is a property of the
capture basis, not the galaxy, so it costs one rotation and no geometry. Seed it
per system and no two stars share a sky.

## Framing, then baking

The star count defaults to **10,000 and goes to 100,000**, and the gap is
deliberate: you want the scene responsive while you are deciding where to stand
and how big the stars should be, and dense only for the shot you keep.

Generation is cheap: planets are computed on demand, names come from each
star's own seed, and each star uses a cheap PRNG. Measured, 10k bright stars
(with their interesting dim ones) build in about 0.4 s and 100k in about 2 s,
so the slider is debounced rather than a separate "now bake it" step.

⚠️ **Tune particle size AT 90°.** A cube face is 90° FOV where a typical demo
camera is nearer 46°, so a star covers about half the angular fraction of the
frame once you widen it. Anything dialled in while orbiting the galaxy comes out
small in the bake — 0.7 here against 0.3–0.5 there.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/skybox-baker/

---

# Land and Sky

**THE KITCHEN SINK** — one world that grows with the world-sim layer. Terrain
(with live dials), a sea, weather over both, and the encoded sky behind. As
provinces, weather systems and the simulation land, they land HERE first: this
page is where the pieces meet, so it is also where their disagreements show
first — which is the point.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dMoon, b3dWeatherCell, b3dLightning, b3dAmbient, b3dLightShafts, b3dTerrain, b3dCloudDeck, b3dDecorator, b3dWater, b3dLight, b3dFog, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, select3d, button3d, row3d, volcano, craterField, composeLandforms, mergeProvinces, ROCK_RULES } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { demo } = tosi({
  demo: {
    seed: 111,
    grossScale: 0.01,
    detailScale: 0.09,
    horizScale: 3.31,
    grossAmplitude: 230,
    detailAmplitude: 45,
    // Sea level as a FRACTION of v-size, so the ocean scales with the
    // mountains — the same world at any amplitude keeps the same share of
    // land and sea.
    seaLevel: 0.64,
    volcano: true,
    // CLIMATE, above water. Moisture is the one that matters most: the biome
    // chart's default 0.45 sits between the dry row (dune) and the medium
    // row (steppe), which is why a warm world with a coral reef below the
    // waterline read as barren above it. Land sits on the chart's rows at
    // three quarters of its moisture (the top row is the sea's), so forest
    // wants nearly 1: 0.95, which height and the regions then dry in places.
    // TEMPERATURE: 0 is 0 °C and a unit is 50 °C, so this is 22.5 °C.
    temperature: 0.45,
    moisture: 0.95,
    // Plates sized to THIS volcano (420 m). The plugin's 0.09 was tuned on a
    // 55 m cone, where it gives ~11 m plates; here that is gravel.
    volcanicScale: 0.02,
    // The spring equinox (no temperature offset, so the default look is
    // unchanged), with a temperate swing ready for the 'time of year' slider.
    season: 0,
    seasonality: 0.2,
    // How cratered the ground is (0 = none; a preset sets it: Mars, the Moon).
    craters: 0,
    // A field of volcanoes (Io): how many, 0 = none.
    volcanoes: 0,
    // The ground's palette: 'earth' (the biome chart's own) or 'sulfur' (Io).
    palette: 'earth',
    // The sea's colours: its surface tint and the fog you see from inside it
    // (a methane sea, Titan, is dark amber).
    waterColor: '#0066cc', waterFog: '#00264d', waterTint: 0.1,
    // Is there a sea at all? A dry world (Mars, Venus) has none: no water
    // plane, and no shoreline or seafloor colours.
    sea: true,
    // A SPHERE WORLD: the same ground laid on a planet of this radius, so
    // latitude has a climate (cooler toward the poles, ice at them) and a
    // globe built from the terrain shows the same places. Off, the ground
    // is flat and the climate is the same everywhere but for its regions.
    sphere: false,
    planetRadius: 50, // km
    wireframe: false,
  },
})

// Weather is ONE dial at the top (coverage drives transmission, gloom and
// depth) plus the shaping ones: wind slides the sky, evolve reshapes it,
// cirrus thins it, orographic asks the terrain for its own height sampler so
// the towers build over the mountains that are actually there.
const { sky } = tosi({
  sky: {
    coverage: 0.1, altitude: 280, timeOfDay: 18.5, orographic: 0.8, wind: 10, cirrus: 0.25, evolve: 0.5, eye: 205,
    // What the deck is actually given: the two dials above, thinned by how
    // much air there is (see cloudAir). Not saved in presets.
    cloudCover: 0.1, cloudOrographic: 0.8,
    storm: false,
    // The atmosphere. `atmosphere` is how much air the WORLD has (0 is the
    // Moon: black noon, stars out); the tints colour the scattered light only.
    world: 'Earth', atmosphere: 1, dust: 0, turbidity: 10, rayleigh: 2, mieCoefficient: 0.005, luminance: 1,
    zenithTint: '#ffffff', horizonTint: '#ffffff', tintStrength: 0,
    // The stars: size (1 = the default point), brightness, and the faint floor.
    // Does anything GROW here? Off, the decorator places rocks alone.
    decoLife: true,
    decoBudget: 2000, decoRadius: 900, decoShadows: false, decoClump: 0.85, decoClumpSize: 0,
    starSize: 1, starGain: 0.9, starFloor: 0.4, starSharpness: 3, twinkle: 0.35,
    // Extra (cosmetic) moons: a set, swung round the sky together.
    moons: 'Big moon', moonAz: 0, moonEl: 0,
    // The cloud deck's colours (a Venus deck is sulfur-yellow), and the sun:
    // its apparent size and how bright its light looks.
    deckColor: '#ffffff', deckUnderColor: '#3a4350', sunSize: 1, sunBrightness: 1,
    // The lightning storm: where it forms, how big, the cover it adds and how
    // often it strikes (a multiple of the natural rate). Presets set these.
    stormX: 1600, stormZ: 300, stormRadius: 900, stormCoverage: 1.7, lightningRate: 1, stormRain: 0.9,
    // The world preset in force (see PRESETS below).
    preset: 'Earth',
  },
})

// A world is a few dials at once — the preset writes them, and the sliders
// stay live afterwards so you can walk away from the preset.
// Mars is almost no AIR and a lot of DUST: its sky is bright because of the
// dust, not the gas (under 1% of Earth's). Gas scatters blue; dust scatters a
// bright haze the tint colours.
const WORLDS = {
  Earth: { atmosphere: 1, dust: 0, zenithTint: '#ffffff', horizonTint: '#ffffff', tintStrength: 0 },
  Mars: { atmosphere: 0.15, dust: 0.85, zenithTint: '#c8a070', horizonTint: '#e0b080', tintStrength: 1 },
  Alien: { atmosphere: 1, dust: 0, zenithTint: '#60c080', horizonTint: '#b0e0a0', tintStrength: 0.7 },
  Airless: { atmosphere: 0, dust: 0, zenithTint: '#ffffff', horizonTint: '#ffffff', tintStrength: 0 },
}
// SIZE is the inverse of the shader's sharpness: a gaussian's width goes as
// 1/sqrt(sharpness), so size 2 is twice the width of the default point.
sky.starSize.observe(() => {
  sky.starSharpness.value = 3 / Math.max(0.05, sky.starSize.value) ** 2
})
// COSMETIC MOONS — where, how big, what colour. The phase is not a setting:
// swing them round with the slider and watch it follow from the sun.
const MOONS = {

  Jupiter: [{ frame: 'ground', azimuth: 90, elevation: 13, size: 19, gas: 'jupiter', axisTilt: 8 }],

const skybox = b3dSkybox({
  timeOfDay: sky.timeOfDay,
  realtimeScale: 0,
  starfieldCube: '/sky/nebula',
  starfieldData: '/sky/stars',
  starfieldTilt: '12,25,58',

  sunSize: sky.sunSize,
  sunBrightness: sky.sunBrightness,

const moonEls = []
function placeMoons() {
  const set = MOONS[sky.moons.value] ?? []
  while (moonEls.length > set.length) moonEls.pop().remove()
  set.forEach((m, i) => {
    if (moonEls[i] == null) {
      moonEls[i] = b3dMoon()
      skybox.append(moonEls[i])
    }
    // Every field, so a body left over from another set does not keep its
    // colour or stay a gas giant.
    Object.assign(moonEls[i], { color: '#dddddd', gas: '', axisTilt: 0, frame: 'stars' }, m, {
      azimuth: m.azimuth + sky.moonAz.value,
      elevation: m.elevation + sky.moonEl.value,
    })
  })
}
sky.moons.observe(placeMoons)
sky.moonAz.observe(placeMoons)
sky.moonEl.observe(placeMoons)
placeMoons()
sky.world.observe(() => {
  const w = WORLDS[sky.world.value]
  if (w) for (const k of Object.keys(w)) sky[k].value = w[k]
})

// PRESETS: A WHOLE WORLD AS DATA. Terrain, sea, climate,
// weather, atmosphere, stars, moons, the cloud deck's colour and the sun, as
// one plain object you can pick, save and share. A preset only lists what it
// changes; applying one resets everything else to Earth first, so nothing
// leaks from the last world.
//
// THE SUN'S BRIGHTNESS FOLLOWS THE EYE, not the inverse square. A world
// further from its star gets far less light (Titan about 1/90 of Earth's),
// but vision is logarithmic and adapts, and even from Pluto the sun is some
// 300 times brighter than the full moon. So its disc shrinks for real (1 /
// distance) while its light only dims gently, on a log curve.
const PRESET_KEYS = {
  demo: ['seed', 'grossScale', 'detailScale', 'horizScale', 'grossAmplitude', 'detailAmplitude', 'seaLevel', 'sea', 'waterColor', 'waterFog', 'waterTint', 'palette', 'volcano', 'volcanoes', 'craters', 'temperature', 'moisture', 'volcanicScale', 'season', 'seasonality', 'sphere', 'planetRadius'],
  sky: ['coverage', 'altitude', 'timeOfDay', 'orographic', 'wind', 'cirrus', 'evolve', 'atmosphere', 'dust', 'turbidity', 'rayleigh', 'mieCoefficient', 'luminance', 'zenithTint', 'horizonTint', 'tintStrength', 'starSize', 'starGain', 'starFloor', 'twinkle', 'moons', 'moonAz', 'moonEl', 'deckColor', 'deckUnderColor', 'sunSize', 'sunBrightness', 'decoBudget', 'decoLife', 'stormX', 'stormZ', 'stormRadius', 'stormCoverage', 'lightningRate', 'stormRain',
    // LAST: switching the storm on builds it from the values above.
    'storm'],
}
const STATE = { demo, sky }
// `scale: 2`: temperature is 0 = 0 °C, 1 = 50 °C. A preset without it
// carries the biome chart's 0…1 axis and is converted when read.
function capturePreset(name) {
  const p = { name, scale: 2 }
  for (const [group, keys] of Object.entries(PRESET_KEYS)) {
    p[group] = {}
    for (const k of keys) p[group][k] = STATE[group][k].value
  }
  return p
}
function migratePreset(p) {
  if (p == null || p.scale === 2) return p
  const t = p.demo?.temperature
  return {
    ...p,
    scale: 2,
    demo: typeof t === 'number' ? { ...p.demo, temperature: +((t - 0.36) / 0.8).toFixed(3) } : p.demo,
  }
}
function applyPreset(p) {
  for (const [group, keys] of Object.entries(PRESET_KEYS)) {
    const vals = p[group] ?? {}
    for (const k of keys) if (k in vals) STATE[group][k].value = vals[k]
  }
}
// How bright a sun LOOKS from `au` astronomical units (1 = Earth).
const sunLight = (au) => Math.max(0.35, 1 - 0.3 * Math.log10(au * au))
const EARTH = capturePreset('Earth') // the defaults above
const BUILT_IN = {

    // (No volcano for now: Earth's province, a stand-in until each world

const CUSTOM_KEY = 'land-and-sky:presets'
function loadCustom() {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(CUSTOM_KEY) || '{}') || {}
  } catch {
    return {}
  }
}
function saveCustom(p) {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(CUSTOM_KEY, JSON.stringify({ ...loadCustom(), [p.name]: p }))
  } catch {
    // private window: the preset still applies, it just is not kept
  }
}
const presetNames = () => [...Object.keys(BUILT_IN), ...Object.keys(loadCustom())]
// NO AIR, NO CLOUD. The cloud dials say how cloudy the weather is; how much
// cloud that makes depends on there being air to hold it. Full from about a
// third of Earth's air up, none below a twentieth, so Mars (0.03) has none.
function cloudAir() {
  const k = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (sky.atmosphere.value - 0.05) / 0.25))
  sky.cloudCover.value = sky.coverage.value * k
  sky.cloudOrographic.value = sky.orographic.value * k
}
sky.coverage.observe(cloudAir)
sky.orographic.observe(cloudAir)
sky.atmosphere.observe(cloudAir)
cloudAir()
sky.preset.observe(() => {
  const p = BUILT_IN[sky.preset.value] ?? migratePreset(loadCustom()[sky.preset.value])
  if (p == null) return
  applyPreset(EARTH)
  applyPreset(p)
})

// The volcano is authored ONCE and switched in and out. Applied here as well
// as from the toggle because it is ON by default, and the toggle's handler only
// runs when someone flips it.
// SEMI-ACTIVE: its vent smokes, glows and spits now and then. The
// landform carries that as a vent, and the terrain puts the effect there.
const theVolcano = volcano({ x: 600, z: -400, radius: 420, height: 260, craterRadius: 55, craterDepth: 50, activity: 0.5 })
// Where the sea is: a FRACTION of the terrain's height, or, on a world
// with no sea, far below everything (no water to see).
function seaY() {
  return demo.sea.valueOf() ? demo.seaLevel * demo.grossAmplitude : -10000
}
// The BIOME's datum is separate: it also classifies by altitude above it, so
// on a dry world it sits just under the deepest crater floors (no shore, no
// seafloor colours) rather than kilometres down (which read as bare peaks).
function biomeSea() {
  return demo.sea.valueOf() ? demo.seaLevel * demo.grossAmplitude : -250
}

// Temperature falls with height above the SEA; with no sea there is no
// datum, so a dry world keeps its preset temperature at every height.
function lapse() {
  // (Not 0: the terrain reads 0 as UNSET and falls back to its 0.004, an
  // arctic world. And not 1e-6, which the attribute path rounds to 0.)
  return demo.sea.valueOf() ? 0.5 / demo.grossAmplitude : 0.0002
}

// A FIELD of volcanoes (Io): seeded positions around you, small paterae
// with hot floors. Each is the ordinary volcano landform.
function volcanoField(n, seed) {
  const out = []
  let s = seed * 9301 + 49297
  const rnd = () => ((s = (s * 9301 + 49297) % 233280) / 233280)
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const a = rnd() * Math.PI * 2
    const d = 250 + rnd() * 1600
    out.push(volcano({ x: Math.cos(a) * d, z: Math.sin(a) * d, radius: 160 + rnd() * 220, height: 30 + rnd() * 90, craterRadius: 50 + rnd() * 60, craterDepth: 20 + rnd() * 30 }))
  }
  return out
}

// Landforms COMPOSE: the craters, then the volcanoes on top of them.
function applyVolcano(on) {
  const parts = []
  const provinces = []
  const vents = []
  const density = demo.craters.valueOf()
  if (density > 0) parts.push(craterField({ seed: demo.seed.valueOf(), density, maxRadius: 500 }))
  for (const v of volcanoField(demo.volcanoes.valueOf(), demo.seed.valueOf())) {
    parts.push(v.landform)
    provinces.push(v.province)
    vents.push(...(v.vents ?? []))
  }
  if (on) {
    parts.push(theVolcano.landform)
    provinces.push(theVolcano.province)
    vents.push(...(theVolcano.vents ?? []))
  }
  terrain.vents = vents
  terrain.landform = parts.length === 0 ? null : parts.length === 1 ? parts[0] : composeLandforms(...parts)
  terrain.provinceField = provinces.length === 0 ? null : provinces.length === 1 ? provinces[0] : mergeProvinces(...provinces)
}
demo.volcanoes.observe(() => {
  applyVolcano(demo.volcano.valueOf())
  terrain.regenerate()
})

// THE GROUND'S PALETTE, swapped on the terrain's biome shader (it reads its
// palette every frame). Io's sulfur: frost white, pale and deep yellow,
// orange-red, and black lava for the variation.
const PALETTES = {
  sulfur: {
    a: [[0.92, 0.9, 0.82], [0.9, 0.84, 0.42], [0.86, 0.68, 0.18], [0.74, 0.38, 0.14]],
    b: [[0.8, 0.78, 0.7], [0.14, 0.12, 0.1], [0.7, 0.55, 0.15], [0.3, 0.14, 0.06]],
  },
}
let earthPalette = null
function applyPalette() {
  const plugin = terrain.biomePlugin
  if (plugin == null) return false
  if (earthPalette == null) earthPalette = { a: plugin.palette, b: plugin.paletteB }
  const p = PALETTES[demo.palette.valueOf()]
  // One row of four, repeated for every moisture row (Io has no weather).
  plugin.palette = p ? Array.from({ length: 5 }, () => p.a).flat() : earthPalette.a
  plugin.paletteB = p ? Array.from({ length: 5 }, () => p.b).flat() : earthPalette.b
  return true
}
demo.palette.observe(applyPalette)
demo.craters.observe(() => {
  applyVolcano(demo.volcano.valueOf())
  terrain.regenerate()
})
// A new seed re-rolls the craters too (registered before the terrain's own
// seed observer below, so the landform is current when it regenerates).
demo.seed.observe(() => applyVolcano(demo.volcano.valueOf()))

// 'on'|'off' on the element, a boolean on the toggle — bridged here.
const decorator = b3dDecorator({ budget: sky.decoBudget, radius: sky.decoRadius, clump: sky.decoClump, clumpSize: sky.decoClumpSize })
sky.decoShadows.observe(() => {
  decorator.shadows = sky.decoShadows.value ? 'on' : 'off'
})
// A dead world keeps its rocks: the rules without the plants.
const applyLife = () => {
  decorator.rules = sky.decoLife.value ? null : ROCK_RULES
  decorator.rebuild?.()
}
sky.decoLife.observe(applyLife)
applyLife()

let water
const terrain = b3dTerrain({
  seed: demo.seed,
  biome: 'on',
  surfaceType: demo.sphere.valueOf() ? 'sphere' : 'cylinder',
  radius: demo.sphere.valueOf() ? demo.planetRadius.valueOf() * 1000 : 1000,
  cylinderHeight: 1000,
  tileSize: 128,
  lodLevels: 3,
  splitFactor: 2,
  reach: 5000,
  grossScale: demo.grossScale,
  detailScale: demo.detailScale,
  horizScale: demo.horizScale,
  grossAmplitude: demo.grossAmplitude,
  detailAmplitude: demo.detailAmplitude,
  wireframe: demo.wireframe,
  // The biome classifier's snow line anchors to the SAME sea level as the
  // water plane — keep them equal or the islands between the old and new
  // water line render as snowcaps. The lapse rate MUST scale to the
  // vertical range (0.5 / amplitude gives temperate valleys and cold
  // summits — the element's own attribute note): the 0.004 default assumes
  // a small world, and at v-size 400 every peak would still read as snow.
  biomeSeaLevel: biomeSea(),
  biomeLapseRate: lapse(),
  biomeTemperature: demo.temperature,
  biomeMoisture: demo.moisture,
  biomeVolcanicScale: demo.volcanicScale,
  biomeSeason: demo.season,
  biomeSeasonality: demo.seasonality,
})

applyVolcano(demo.volcano.valueOf())
// Observed rather than handled on the toggle, so a PRESET switching the
// volcano regenerates the terrain too.
demo.volcano.observe(() => {
  applyVolcano(demo.volcano.valueOf())
  terrain.regenerate()
})

// A LIGHTNING STORM, as weather rather than scenery (WEATHER-DESIGN): a cell
// with coverage and storminess, drifting with the wind. It gathers IN FRONT
// of you (the view faces east) over twenty seconds, so switching it on shows
// you a storm, then drifts across the view with the wind. Lightning, thunder, rain and strike
// shadows all come from the cell. Toggling it on again starts a new one.
let storm = null
sky.storm.observe(() => {
  storm?.remove()
  storm = null
  if (sky.storm.value) {
    storm = b3dWeatherCell({ x: sky.stormX.value, z: sky.stormZ.value, radius: sky.stormRadius.value, coverage: sky.stormCoverage.value, storminess: 1, precipitation: sky.stormRain.value, drift: 'wind', grow: 20 })
    scene.append(storm)
  }
})

const scene = b3d(
  {
    // ONE WIND for the clouds, the smoke, spray and storms (the deck follows
    // the scene's). It blows ACROSS the view (toward +Z; the view faces east):
    // blowing straight away from you, cloud and smoke drift would be nearly
    // invisible.
    windSpeed: sky.wind,
    windBearingDeg: 0,
    // Sections as icon TABS (one at a time); 'fold' shows them as headers.
    panelSections: 'tabs',
    // Lightning strikes wherever a weather cell is stormy (the storm toggle).
    // Controls live in the dual-presence scene panel: the owl opens them on flat
    // screens, and the SAME panel opens in VR.
    scenePanel: () => [
      label3d({ text: 'World', icon: 'earth', collapsible: true, open: true }),
      // Pick a world; everything you DO with presets is one menu.
      row3d(
        { weights: [4, 1] },
        select3d({ label: 'preset', value: sky.preset, options: presetNames() }),
        button3d({
          label: '⋯',
          title: 'preset actions',
          menu: [
            {
              label: 'Save as new preset',
              icon: 'plus',
              handleSelect: () => {
                const name = `Custom ${Object.keys(loadCustom()).length + 1}`
                saveCustom(capturePreset(name))
                sky.preset.value = name
                scene.refreshScenePanel?.()
              },
            },
            {
              label: 'Copy preset (JSON)',
              icon: 'uploadCloud',
              handleSelect: () => navigator.clipboard?.writeText(JSON.stringify(capturePreset(sky.preset.value), null, 2)),
            },
            {
              label: 'Paste preset (JSON)',
              icon: 'downloadCloud',
              handleSelect: async () => {
                try {
                  const p = JSON.parse(await navigator.clipboard.readText())
                  p.name = p.name || 'Pasted'
                  saveCustom(p)
                  sky.preset.value = p.name
                  scene.refreshScenePanel?.()
                } catch {
                  // not a preset on the clipboard
                }
              },
            },
          ],
        })
      ),
      // The clocks live with the world: the day, the year, and how much
      // the year matters.
      slider3d({ label: 'time of day', value: sky.timeOfDay, min: 0, max: 24, step: 0.25 }),
      // The year: 0.25 midsummer, 0.5 autumn, 0.75 midwinter. 'season strength'
      // is how hard it swings; at 0 the year does nothing.
      slider3d({ label: 'time of year', value: demo.season, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 }),
      // The swing either side of the yearly mean. Stored in the biome chart's
      // units, where 1 spans 62.5 °C.
      slider3d({ label: 'season strength', value: demo.seasonality, min: 0, max: 0.6, step: 0.01, format: (v) => '±' + Math.round(v * 62.5) + ' °C' }),
      // Flat, or the same ground on a planet: you start at 45° north, and
      // the pole is a quarter of the way round.
      toggle3d({ label: 'sphere world', value: demo.sphere }),
      slider3d({ label: 'planet radius', value: demo.planetRadius, min: 2, max: 6400, scale: 'log', format: (v) => Math.round(v) + ' km' }),
      label3d({ text: 'Terrain', icon: 'terrain', collapsible: true }),
      slider3d({ label: 'gross scale', value: demo.grossScale, min: 0.005, max: 0.3, scale: 'log' }),
      slider3d({ label: 'detail scale', value: demo.detailScale, min: 0.02, max: 1, scale: 'log' }),
      slider3d({ label: 'h size', value: demo.horizScale, min: 0.25, max: 10, scale: 'log2' }),
      slider3d({ label: 'v size', value: demo.grossAmplitude, min: 0, max: 400, step: 1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'sea level', value: demo.seaLevel, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.02 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'v detail', value: demo.detailAmplitude, min: 0, max: 50, step: 0.5 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'seed', value: demo.seed, min: 0, max: 999, step: 1 }),
      // THE FIRST PROVINCE — an authored volcano forced through the live
      // terrain, with the volcanism field that makes it glow. The kitchen
      // sink grows from here.
      toggle3d({ label: 'volcano province', value: demo.volcano }),
      slider3d({ label: 'craters', value: demo.craters, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'volcanoes', value: demo.volcanoes, min: 0, max: 16, step: 1 }),
      select3d({ label: 'ground palette', value: demo.palette, options: ['earth', ...Object.keys(PALETTES)] }),
      // Beside the volcano: the other thing you switch on to watch happen.
      label3d({ text: 'Climate', icon: 'thermometer', collapsible: true }),
      slider3d({ label: 'temperature', value: demo.temperature, min: -1, max: 1, step: 0.02, format: (v) => Math.round(v * 50) + ' °C' }),
      slider3d({ label: 'moisture', value: demo.moisture, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 }),
      // How much one region differs from the next, and how big a region is.
      // Straight onto the shader's settings: the decorator reads the same ones.
      slider3d({ label: 'moisture variation', value: terrain.biomePlugin?.params.mNoiseAmp ?? 0.5, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01, handleChange: (v) => { if (terrain.biomePlugin) terrain.biomePlugin.params.mNoiseAmp = v } }),
      slider3d({ label: 'region size', value: 0.001 / (terrain.biomePlugin?.params.mNoiseScale ?? 0.001), min: 0.1, max: 10, scale: 'log', format: (v) => v.toFixed(1) + ' km', handleChange: (v) => { if (terrain.biomePlugin) terrain.biomePlugin.params.mNoiseScale = 0.001 / v } }),
      slider3d({ label: 'volcanic scale', value: demo.volcanicScale, min: 0.005, max: 0.15, scale: 'log' }),
      label3d({ text: 'Weather', icon: 'cloud', collapsible: true }),
      // With the clouds it is made of.
      toggle3d({ label: 'lightning storm', value: sky.storm }),
      slider3d({ label: 'cloud cover', value: sky.coverage, min: 0, max: 2, step: 0.02 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'cloud base', value: sky.altitude, min: 60, max: 1400, step: 10 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'orographic', value: sky.orographic, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'wind', value: sky.wind, min: 0, max: 40, step: 1 }),
      // Signed: positive streaks ALONG the wind, negative ACROSS it.
      slider3d({ label: 'cirrus', value: sky.cirrus, min: -1, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'evolve', value: sky.evolve, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      label3d({ text: 'Atmosphere', icon: 'sky', collapsible: true }),
      slider3d({ label: 'air', value: sky.atmosphere, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'dust', value: sky.dust, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'tint', value: sky.tintStrength, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'turbidity', value: sky.turbidity, min: 1, max: 40, step: 0.5 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'rayleigh', value: sky.rayleigh, min: 0, max: 4, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'mie', value: sky.mieCoefficient, min: 0, max: 0.05, step: 0.001 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'luminance', value: sky.luminance, min: 0.1, max: 2, step: 0.05 }),
      label3d({ text: 'Stars', icon: 'star', collapsible: true }),
      slider3d({ label: 'star size', value: sky.starSize, min: 0.4, max: 3, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'star brightness', value: sky.starGain, min: 0, max: 3, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'faint stars', value: sky.starFloor, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.02 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'twinkle', value: sky.twinkle, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      label3d({ text: 'Moons', icon: 'moon', collapsible: true }),
      select3d({ label: 'moons', value: sky.moons, options: Object.keys(MOONS) }),
      slider3d({ label: 'moon azimuth', value: sky.moonAz, min: -180, max: 180, step: 1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'moon elevation', value: sky.moonEl, min: -60, max: 60, step: 1 }),
      label3d({ text: 'Vegetation', icon: 'tree', collapsible: true }),
      // THE BUDGET is the performance dial: a count, not a density. Watch the
      // Perf Stats panel's decorator row (placed, draw calls, build ms).
      slider3d({ label: 'rocks & trees', value: sky.decoBudget, min: 0, max: 20000, step: 500 }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'plants (off = rocks only)', value: sky.decoLife }),
      slider3d({ label: 'reach (m)', value: sky.decoRadius, min: 200, max: 3000, step: 100 }),
      // Tighter or looser: how strongly things gather, and how big a clump
      // is (0 = auto, sized from how far apart things are).
      slider3d({ label: 'clumping', value: sky.decoClump, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'clump size (m)', value: sky.decoClumpSize, min: 0, max: 300, step: 10 }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'tree shadows', value: sky.decoShadows }),
      label3d({ text: 'Camera', icon: 'camera', collapsible: true }),
      slider3d({ label: 'eye height', value: sky.eye, min: 5, max: 1500, step: 10 }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'wireframe', value: demo.wireframe }),
      // Ambient occlusion is off here (the heavy scene). Perf Stats has the
      // switch, in every demo and in VR; a second one here drifted out of step
      // with it.
    ],
    sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
      // The terrain's biome shader exists only once it has built: apply the
      // preset's palette as soon as it does.
      const paletteWait = el.scene.onBeforeRenderObservable.add(() => {
        if (applyPalette()) el.scene.onBeforeRenderObservable.remove(paletteWait)
      })
      // A LOOK-AROUND CAMERA: you stand at eye height and turn in place. Not an
      // orbit camera: up-arrow moves an orbit camera UP OVER its target, which
      // points the view DOWN, and left/right swing the eye round the target
      // instead of turning it.
      //
      // So: a FreeCamera at the eye, arrows bound to ROTATION (up = look up;
      // Babylon's keysRotateUp lowers rotation.x, which pitches up) and its
      // move keys cleared so arrows never walk you. Dragging looks around.
      // Facing EAST (+X; +Z is north), just below the horizon.
      const cam = new BABYLON.FreeCamera('look', new BABYLON.Vector3(0, sky.eye.valueOf(), 0), el.scene)
      cam.setTarget(new BABYLON.Vector3(1, sky.eye.valueOf() - 0.08, 0))
      const keys = cam.inputs.attached.keyboard
      keys.keysUp = []
      keys.keysDown = []
      keys.keysLeft = []
      keys.keysRight = []
      keys.keysUpward = []
      keys.keysDownward = []
      keys.keysRotateLeft = [37]
      keys.keysRotateRight = [39]
      keys.keysRotateUp = [38]
      keys.keysRotateDown = [40]
      keys.rotationSpeed = 0.6
      cam.minZ = 0.1
      cam.maxZ = 12000
      cam.attachControl(el.parts.canvas, true)
      el.setActiveCamera(cam)
      // THE EYE IS PINNED: the slider means what it says.
      el.scene.registerBeforeRender(() => {
        cam.position.y = sky.eye.valueOf()
        // In a headset the view is the XR camera on its rig, which took its
        // height from this camera ONCE, on entry: the slider moved nothing.
        // The rig is the floor, so it sits a nominal eye height lower.
        const rig = el.xrFrames?.rig
        if (rig != null) rig.position.y = Math.max(0, sky.eye.valueOf() - 1.6)
      })
    },
  },
  // shadowMaxZ: the cascades must reach the ground from the eye, which starts
  // ~200 m up — at the 100 m default nothing in view casts or receives.
  b3dSun({ activeDistance: 80, shadowMaxZ: 1200 }),
  // THE PAIR: a 256 cube for the nebulae, a data cube the shader decodes into
  // points. Split because they are different KINDS of thing — one is
  // low-frequency and one is not — and the points stay points at any zoom.
  skybox,
  b3dLightning({ seed: 3, rate: sky.lightningRate }),
  // Sunlight breaking through gaps in the deck; strongest in the rain.
  b3dLightShafts({}),
  // Rain and snow come from the WEATHER: nothing falls until a storm is
  // overhead, and it eases in and out as the storm passes.
  b3dAmbient({ preset: 'rain', weather: 'rain', radius: 14 }),
  b3dAmbient({ preset: 'snow', weather: 'snow', radius: 14 }),
  // Bounce from the ground, or every vertical face (a rock's sides) is black.
  b3dLight({ intensity: 0.5, groundColor: '#57523f' }),
  b3dFog({ syncSkybox: true, start: 1000, end: 4000 }),
  terrain,
  // The layer case: a cloud DECK over the peaks, orographic so the towers
  // build over the actual mountains. Blob clouds (b3d-clouds) remain the
  // right tool for cloud you fly BETWEEN.
  // Rocks and trees by climate: pines in the cold, palms on warm shores, cacti
  // in hot dry country, boulders on the steep. See b3d-decorator.
  decorator,
  b3dCloudDeck({
    altitude: sky.altitude,
    coverage: sky.cloudCover,
    orographic: sky.cloudOrographic,
    wind: sky.wind,
    cirrus: sky.cirrus,
    evolve: sky.evolve,
    color: sky.deckColor,
    underColor: sky.deckUnderColor,
  }),
  // The sea follows BOTH dials: seaLevel (a fraction) times v-size, so the
  // ocean scales with the mountains instead of sitting at a fixed height
  // while the world reshapes around it. `follow` keeps it under the camera;
  // the ripples stay anchored in world space.
  water = b3dWater({ y: seaY(), waterSize: 8000, follow: true, twoSided: true, shore: 'on', shoreFine: true, waterColor: demo.waterColor, colorBlendFactor: demo.waterTint, fogColor: demo.waterFog }),
)

preview.append(scene)

// Flat or a sphere: both are generation attributes, so the terrain rebuilds
// itself on its next render.
function applySurface() {
  terrain.surfaceType = demo.sphere.valueOf() ? 'sphere' : 'cylinder'
  terrain.radius = demo.sphere.valueOf() ? demo.planetRadius.valueOf() * 1000 : 1000
}
demo.sphere.observe(applySurface)
demo.planetRadius.observe(applySurface)

// Regenerate the terrain when its dials move, and keep the sea at the same
// FRACTION of the terrain's height.
for (const key of ['seed', 'grossScale', 'detailScale', 'horizScale', 'grossAmplitude', 'detailAmplitude', 'wireframe', 'seaLevel', 'sea']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    // The biome's sea level is a LIVE dial on the terrain — write it BEFORE
    // regenerate() so the adopted generation key is the one the rebuild
    // satisfies (the reverse order costs a second full pool re-cut per step).
    terrain.biomeSeaLevel = biomeSea()
    terrain.biomeLapseRate = lapse()
    terrain.regenerate()
    water.y = seaY()
  })
}
```
```css
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

Drag the terrain dials and the world reshapes under you. Cover the sky, drop
the cloud base into the valleys, scrub to midnight — the encoded galaxy comes
out with the moon riding it, the deck moonlit above.

## The kitchen sink grows from here

- **Provinces** land as toggles like the volcano: a footprint, a falloff, and
  what they do to the terrain and the weather.
- **Weather systems** arrive as province-driven dials (one wind, shared and
  overridable).
- **The simulation** (world-store / world-view) gets a corner of this world
  to populate — the same one a visitor just reshaped.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/land-and-sky/

# City Drive

A city in a landscape. A seeded city of Kenney's kits stands on ground
flattened for it, with traffic, street lights, and lit windows at night. Round
it are hills, woods and a sea under the whole sky: sun and moon, a cloud deck,
the stars. Drive out of town and keep going.

## Demo

```js
import {
  b3d, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dLight, b3dFog, b3dTerrain, b3dCloudDeck, b3dDecorator, b3dWater,
  b3dCity, b3dCar, b3dLibrary, b3dBeacon, inputFocus, cityGround, cityStart, cityLayout,
  slider3d, assetUrl, effectiveTier, headsetDevice,
} from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { cityDrive } = tosi({ cityDrive: { time: 17.5, speed: 64, coverage: 0.45 } })

// A LIGHTER WORLD on a headset or a low-powered device: a smaller town, less
// traffic, a shorter view, fewer trees, no cloud deck. A headset draws
// everything twice, and its browser pays dearly for every draw.
const light = headsetDevice() || effectiveTier() === 'low'

// The city's plan, and where it stands: its ground is flattened at `level`
// under the whole grid and eased back into the hills round it.
const plan = light ? { width: 24, depth: 24, seed: 3 } : { width: 48, depth: 48, seed: 3 }
const level = 12
const ground = cityGround({ ...plan, level })
const start = cityStart(plan)

// A NAMED PLACE: where the street you start on ends, straight ahead. Anything
// named (a beacon, or a car with an id) is a place an agent can go to.
const layout = cityLayout(plan)
const along = start.ry === 0 ? [0, 1] : [1, 0]
let cx = Math.floor(start.x / 12 + plan.width / 2)
let cz = Math.floor(start.z / 12 + plan.depth / 2)
for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
  const nx = cx + along[0], nz = cz + along[1]
  if (!layout.road[nz * plan.width + nx]) break
  cx = nx
  cz = nz
}
const streetEnd = { x: (cx + 0.5 - plan.width / 2) * 12, z: (cz + 0.5 - plan.depth / 2) * 12 }

const terrain = b3dTerrain({
  seed: 7,
  biome: 'on',
  surfaceType: 'cylinder',
  radius: 1000,
  cylinderHeight: 1000,
  tileSize: 128,
  lodLevels: light ? 2 : 3,
  splitFactor: 2,
  reach: light ? 1500 : 4000,
  grossScale: 0.015,
  detailScale: 0.09,
  horizScale: 8,
  grossAmplitude: 160,
  detailAmplitude: 10,
  // Down, so the low ground is under the sea at 0.
  baseHeight: -70,
  // Green country: moist, and cooling slowly enough with height that the
  // hills are not snow-capped.
  biomeMoisture: 0.9,
  biomeLapseRate: 0.0015,
})
terrain.landform = ground.landform
terrain.regenerate()

const woods = b3dDecorator(light ? { budget: 1200, radius: 400 } : { budget: 5000, radius: 900 })
woods.clear = ground.clear

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      style: 'width: 100%; height: 100%',
      gamepad: 'left_stick,right_stick,left_trigger,right_trigger,right_bumper,A,X',
      panelTitle: 'City Drive',
      scenePanel: () => [
        slider3d({ label: 'time of day', value: cityDrive.time, min: 0, max: 24, step: 0.1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'time speed', value: cityDrive.speed, min: 0.25, max: 1024, scale: 'log2', step: 1, zeroStop: true }),
        ...(light ? [] : [slider3d({ label: 'cloud cover', value: cityDrive.coverage, min: 0, max: 1.5, step: 0.05 })]),
      ],
    },
    b3dSun({ shadowTextureSize: 2048 }),
    b3dSkybox({
      timeOfDay: cityDrive.time,
      realtimeScale: cityDrive.speed,
      starfieldCube: '/sky/nebula',
      starfieldData: '/sky/stars',
      starfieldTilt: '12,25,58',
    }),
    b3dLight({ intensity: 0.5, nightIntensity: 0.06, groundColor: '#4b4d52' }),
    b3dFog({ syncSkybox: true, start: light ? 400 : 800, end: light ? 1400 : 3500 }),
    terrain,
    woods,
    ...(light ? [] : [b3dCloudDeck({ altitude: 600, coverage: cityDrive.coverage, orographic: 0.6, wind: 8, skyClock: 'off' })]),
    b3dWater({ y: 0, waterSize: 8000, follow: true, twoSided: true }),
    b3dLibrary({ url: assetUrl('kenney/libraries/car-kit.glb'), type: 'cars' }),
    b3dCity({ ...plan, y: level, traffic: light ? 12 : 32 }),
    // Above the car's wall rays: a beacon's hull is pickable.
    b3dBeacon({ name: 'end of the street', x: streetEnd.x, y: level + 4, z: streetEnd.z }),
    inputFocus(
      b3dCar({ id: 'car', library: 'cars', meshName: 'sedan-sports', scale: 1.7, player: true, ...start, y: level + 0.5 })
    )
  )
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

On a headset or a low-powered device the world is lighter: a town a quarter
the size, a dozen cars, a shorter view, fewer trees and no cloud deck.

You start in the middle of town. The right trigger or **W** drives, the left
trigger, the right bumper or **S** brakes and reverses, and the left stick or
**A** and **D** steer. The right stick or the arrow keys swing the camera round
the car (it springs back behind) and up an arc toward overhead (it stays
there). Time runs
at 60×, so the sun goes down soon after you arrive. The owl's panel sets the
hour, the speed and the cloud.

The beacon at the end of your street is named, so it is a place: with the
scene's [agent tools](/b3d-agent/) open, an agent can drive the car there.

## How it is put together

- [b3d-city](/b3d-city/) builds the town. `cityGround` gives the terrain a
  [landform](/landform/) pad, flat under the grid, and gives the woods a
  `clear` that keeps trees off the streets. `cityStart` is a clear spot in
  the middle to start the car.
- [b3d-terrain](/b3d-terrain/) and [b3d-decorator](/b3d-decorator/) make the
  country, [b3d-cloud-deck](/b3d-cloud-deck/) the weather, and
  [b3d-skybox](/b3d-skybox/) the day and night.
- The traffic ([city-traffic](/city-traffic/)) stays on the town's roads.
  Your car goes anywhere there is ground.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/city-drive/

# Cross Country

A small tank in open country: rolling hills, woods, lakes and the whole sky.
Its tracks are forty links a side, carried round by the model's own animation
at exactly the pace of the ground, so they grip on the spot when it turns in
place; its wheels turn with them, the turret traverses and the gun elevates.
Head for the hills.

## Demo

```js
import {
  b3d, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dLight, b3dFog, b3dTerrain, b3dCloudDeck, b3dDecorator, b3dWater,
  b3dTank, inputFocus, pad, slider3d, assetUrl, effectiveTier, headsetDevice,
} from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { crossCountry } = tosi({ crossCountry: { time: 9, speed: 32, coverage: 0.4 } })

// A LIGHTER WORLD on a headset or a low-powered device: a shorter view, fewer
// trees, no cloud deck.
const light = headsetDevice() || effectiveTier() === 'low'

// A level patch to start on, eased into the hills round it.
const level = 30
const start = pad({ x: 0, z: 0, radius: 12, level, blend: 80 })

const terrain = b3dTerrain({
  seed: 7,
  biome: 'on',
  surfaceType: 'cylinder',
  radius: 1000,
  cylinderHeight: 1000,
  tileSize: 128,
  lodLevels: light ? 2 : 3,
  splitFactor: 2,
  reach: light ? 1500 : 4000,
  grossScale: 0.015,
  detailScale: 0.09,
  horizScale: 8,
  grossAmplitude: 160,
  detailAmplitude: 8,
  // Mostly land, with lakes and sea in the low ground.
  baseHeight: -40,
  // Green country: moist, and cooling slowly enough with height that the
  // hills are not snow-capped.
  biomeMoisture: 0.9,
  biomeLapseRate: 0.0015,
})
terrain.landform = start
terrain.regenerate()

const woods = b3dDecorator(light ? { budget: 1200, radius: 400 } : { budget: 5000, radius: 900 })
// Nothing on the starting patch.
woods.clear = (x, z) => Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (Math.hypot(x, z) - 14) / 20))

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      style: 'width: 100%; height: 100%',
      gamepad: 'left_stick,right_stick,right_stick_click,left_trigger,right_trigger,right_bumper,A',
      panelTitle: 'Cross Country',
      scenePanel: () => [
        slider3d({ label: 'time of day', value: crossCountry.time, min: 0, max: 24, step: 0.1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'time speed', value: crossCountry.speed, min: 0.25, max: 1024, scale: 'log2', step: 1, zeroStop: true }),
        ...(light ? [] : [slider3d({ label: 'cloud cover', value: crossCountry.coverage, min: 0, max: 1.5, step: 0.05 })]),
      ],
    },
    b3dSun({ shadowTextureSize: 2048 }),
    b3dSkybox({
      timeOfDay: crossCountry.time,
      realtimeScale: crossCountry.speed,
      starfieldCube: '/sky/nebula',
      starfieldData: '/sky/stars',
      starfieldTilt: '12,25,58',
    }),
    b3dLight({ intensity: 0.5, nightIntensity: 0.06, groundColor: '#4b4d52' }),
    b3dFog({ syncSkybox: true, start: light ? 400 : 800, end: light ? 1400 : 3500 }),
    terrain,
    woods,
    ...(light ? [] : [b3dCloudDeck({ altitude: 600, coverage: crossCountry.coverage, orographic: 0.6, wind: 8, skyClock: 'off' })]),
    b3dWater({ y: 0, waterSize: 8000, follow: true, twoSided: true }),
    inputFocus(
      b3dTank({ url: assetUrl('tonio/tank/tank2.glb'), player: true, x: 0, z: 0, y: level + 0.5 })
    )
  )
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

On a headset or a low-powered device the world is lighter: a shorter view,
fewer trees and no cloud deck.

The right trigger or **W** drives, the left trigger, the right bumper or **S**
brakes and reverses, and the left stick or **A** and **D** steer: a tank turns
on the spot. The right stick or the arrow keys traverse the turret, and
pulling back raises the gun; clicking the right stick, **V**, or the glass
gamepad's button under the right stick swaps up and down between the gun and the
camera (in a headset a buzz: one for the gun, two for the camera); the view
follows the turret, and the turret holds
its aim while the hull turns under it. The owl's
panel sets the hour, the speed and the cloud.

## How it is put together

- [b3d-tank](/b3d-tank/) drives the model: a body on the pure
  [ground-vehicle](/ground-vehicle/) model, standing on contacts under each
  track. The model is Tonio's (CC BY 4.0), with its track links animated in
  Blender: the tank plays that animation by the distance each track has run,
  one cycle per link.
- [b3d-terrain](/b3d-terrain/) and [b3d-decorator](/b3d-decorator/) make the
  country, with a [landform](/landform/) `pad` to start on;
  [b3d-cloud-deck](/b3d-cloud-deck/) the weather, and
  [b3d-skybox](/b3d-skybox/) the day and night.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/cross-country/

# Core

**The scene itself, and the ways to put things in it.** [b3d](/tosi-b3d/) is the
one element everything else lives inside. After that: a
[box, sphere or ground](/b3d-primitives/) when you need something now, a
[model file](/b3d-loader/) when you have one, and a [library](/b3d-library/)
when you want many copies of the parts in one.
