## A shop

The shop's goods on the left, yours on the right, the deal in the middle.
Put things on the counter from either side; the balance is the price of
what you get less what yours fetch, and **Deal** makes every move and the
payment as one, or none of it. The shop's goods only go to the counter,
and yours only come back to you.

```js
import { ui, createCarry, createInventory, inventoryPanel } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { svgElements } from 'tosijs'
const { svg } = svgElements

const kinds = {
  sword: { id: 'sword', name: 'sword', cost: 40 },
  shield: { id: 'shield', name: 'shield', cost: 30 },
  rope: { id: 'rope', name: 'rope', cost: 2, stack: 20 },
  potion: { id: 'potion', name: 'potion', cost: 12, stack: 9 },
  lamp: { id: 'lamp', name: 'lamp', cost: 8 },
  pelt: { id: 'pelt', name: 'wolf pelt', cost: 10, stack: 10 },
  ring: { id: 'ring', name: 'old ring', cost: 60 },
}
const item = (id, kind, qty = 1) => ({ id, kind, qty })
const list = (...holds) => ({ type: 'list', holds })
const SHOP = { holder: 'shop', container: 'stock' }
const BAG = { holder: 'me', container: 'bag' }
const GET = { holder: 'counter', container: 'you get' }
const GIVE = { holder: 'counter', container: 'you give' }
// Buy at the price, sell at half.
const price = (it, from, to) =>
  (kinds[it.kind].cost ?? 0) * it.qty * (from?.container === 'you give' ? 0.5 : 1)
const inv = createInventory(
  {
    items: {
      sword: item('sword', 'sword'), shield: item('shield', 'shield'), rope: item('rope', 'rope', 12),
      potion: item('potion', 'potion', 6), lamp: item('lamp', 'lamp'),
      pelt: item('pelt', 'pelt', 4), ring: item('ring', 'ring'), mypotion: item('mypotion', 'potion', 1),
    },
    holders: {
      shop: { id: 'shop', containers: { stock: list('sword', 'shield', 'rope', 'potion', 'lamp') }, purse: { gold: 200 } },
      me: { id: 'me', containers: { bag: list('pelt', 'ring', 'mypotion') }, purse: { gold: 50 } },
      counter: { id: 'counter', containers: { 'you get': list(), 'you give': list() } },
    },
  },
  { kinds, price }
)
const carry = createCarry()
const same = (a, b) => a && b && a.holder === b.holder && a.container === b.container
// One at a time from a stack; remember the side it came from.
const moveFor = (id, from, to) => ({ item: id, to, ...(same(from, SHOP) || same(from, BAG) ? { qty: 1 } : {}) })
const refuse = (id, from, to) => {
  if (same(from, SHOP)) return same(to, GET) ? [] : ['put it on the counter to buy it']
  if (same(from, BAG)) return same(to, GIVE) ? [] : ['put it on the counter to sell it']
  if (same(from, GET)) return same(to, SHOP) ? [] : ['buy it first']
  if (same(from, GIVE)) return same(to, BAG) ? [] : ['that is still yours']
  return []
}
const decorations = (it) => ({ badge: it.qty > 1 ? '×' + it.qty : (kinds[it.kind].cost + 'g') })
preview.style.cssText = 'display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:flex-start; overflow:auto; padding:8px'
preview.closest('tosi-example')?.style.setProperty('--tosi-example-height', '420px')
const host = (w, h, style = '') => svg({ width: w, height: h, style: 'touch-action:none;' + style })
const shopHost = host(190, 360)
const middle = document.createElement('div')
middle.style.cssText = 'display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:8px; flex:0 1 210px; min-width:0'
const counterHost = host(210, 280)
const dealHost = host(210, 96, 'width:100%; height:auto')
middle.append(counterHost, dealHost)
const meHost = host(190, 360)
preview.append(shopHost, middle, meHost)
const common = { inv, carry, decorations, moveFor, refuse }
fetch('/item-icons.json').then((r) => r.json()).then((icons) => {
  for (const k of Object.keys(kinds)) kinds[k].icon = icons[k]
  inventoryPanel({ ...common, holder: 'shop', host: shopHost, title: 'shop', height: 360 })
  inventoryPanel({ ...common, holder: 'counter', host: counterHost, title: 'counter', totals: false, height: 280 })
  inventoryPanel({ ...common, holder: 'me', host: meHost, title: 'you', height: 360 })
})

const onCounter = (c) => inv.doc.holders.counter.containers[c].holds
// Sell first, so what yours fetch can pay for what you get.
const dealMoves = () => [
  ...onCounter('you give').map((id) => ({ item: id, to: SHOP, pay: { holder: 'shop', in: 'gold' }, payee: 'me' })),
  ...onCounter('you get').map((id) => ({ item: id, to: BAG, pay: { holder: 'me', in: 'gold' }, payee: 'shop' })),
]
const sum = (c) => onCounter(c).reduce((n, id) => n + price(inv.doc.items[id], { container: c }), 0)
let said = ''
function drawDeal() {
  const balance = sum('you get') - sum('you give')
  const reasons = dealMoves().length ? inv.check(...dealMoves()) : ['nothing on the counter']
  const b = ui.box(
    { width: 210, padding: 10, gap: 6, background: '#1c2230', radius: 10 },
    ui.textBlock(balance >= 0 ? `you pay ${balance} gold` : `you receive ${-balance} gold`, { font: { size: 13, weight: 600 }, color: '#e8e8e8' }),
    ui.textBlock(said || reasons[0] || 'ready', { font: { size: 11 }, color: said === 'done' || !reasons.length ? '#6fd08c' : '#f0907c' }),
    ui.button('Deal', { handleActivate: () => {
      const r = inv.move(...dealMoves())
      said = r.ok ? 'done' : r.reasons[0]
      drawDeal()
    } }),
  )
  dealHost.textContent = ''
  dealHost.append(b.el)
  dealHost.setAttribute('viewBox', `0 0 210 ${dealHost.getAttribute('height')}`)
  dealBox = b
}
let dealBox
inv.subscribe(() => { said = ''; drawDeal() })
drawDeal()
const at = (e) => { const p = ui.svgPoint(dealHost, e.clientX, e.clientY); return [p.x, p.y] }
dealHost.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => dealBox.handlePointer('down', ...at(e)))
dealHost.addEventListener('pointerup', (e) => dealBox.handlePointer('up', ...at(e)))
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

## In 3D

The same loadout in a scene, flat and in a headset, on the scene's SYSTEM
BAR: its button (a standing figure) opens it under the bar, with the bag beside it to
drag to and from; the button again, or the × in its title bar, puts it away.
`inventoryDock` draws both into one SVG, so a drag between them is one panel;
give it no `list` for a craft fitted from a carrier's stock, and it opens to
the schematic alone. A `<tosi-b3d-panel icon title>` takes the dock's
`svg`; the bar asks the dock to open (`panelopen`), and the title bar's ×
puts it away.

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, b3dGround, b3dPanel, createCarry, createInventory, inventoryDock } from 'tosijs-3d'

const kind = (id, tags, mass) => ({ id, name: id, tags, mass })
const kinds = {
  helm: kind('helm', ['helmet'], 2), cuirass: kind('cuirass', ['chest'], 8), pack: kind('pack', ['back'], 1),
  knife: kind('knife', ['side', 'hand'], 1), pistol: kind('pistol', ['side', 'hand'], 1),
  boots: kind('boots', ['feet'], 2), sword: kind('sword', ['hand'], 3),
  rifle: kind('rifle', ['hand', 'two-handed'], 4), shield: kind('shield', ['hand'], 5),
}
const slot = (...accepts) => ({ accepts, holds: null })
const body = {
  type: 'slots',
  slots: {
    helmet: slot('helmet'), face: slot('face'), chest: slot('chest'), shoulder: slot('shoulder'),
    back: slot('back'), waist: slot('waist'), left_side: slot('side'), right_side: slot('side'),
    legs: slot('legs'), feet: slot('feet'), hand_left: slot('hand'), hand_right: slot('hand'),
  },
}
const items = {}
for (const k of Object.keys(kinds)) items[k] = { id: k, kind: k, qty: 1 }
const inv = createInventory(
  { items, holders: { hero: { id: 'hero', containers: { body, bag: { type: 'list', holds: Object.keys(items) } } } } },
  {
    kinds,
    rules: [({ doc, kinds }) => {
      const s = doc.holders.hero.containers.body.slots
      const hands = [s.hand_left.holds, s.hand_right.holds]
      const two = hands.find((id) => id && kinds[doc.items[id].kind].tags.includes('two-handed'))
      return two && hands[0] && hands[1] ? ['two-handed: both hands must be free'] : []
    }],
  }
)
const alsoIn = (item, kind, at) =>
  kind?.tags.includes('two-handed') && at.slot?.startsWith('hand_') ? [at.slot === 'hand_left' ? 'hand_right' : 'hand_left'] : []

// On the system bar: a button (a standing figure) that opens it under the bar.
const loadout = b3dPanel({ title: 'Inventory', icon: 'personStanding' })

preview.closest('tosi-example')?.style.setProperty('--tosi-example-height', '520px')
preview.append(
  b3d(
    {},
    b3dLight({ intensity: 1 }),
    b3dGround({ width: 20, height: 20, texture: 'checker', textureTiles: 10 }),
    loadout,
  )
)

Promise.all([fetch('/person-loadout.svg').then((r) => r.text()), fetch('/item-icons.json').then((r) => r.json())]).then(([art, icons]) => {
  for (const k of Object.keys(kinds)) kinds[k].icon = icons[k]
  const dock = inventoryDock({
    inv, carry: createCarry(), holder: 'hero', title: 'hero', alsoIn,
    schematic: { container: 'body', art }, list: 'bag',
    // A drop target under the bag: here the thing is just gone; a game puts
    // it on the ground (return reasons to refuse instead).
    handleDrop: (item) => console.log('dropped', item.kind),
  })
  // Laid out on the page (text is measured there), out of sight.
  const park = document.createElement('div')
  park.style.cssText = 'position:absolute; left:-10000px; top:0'
  park.append(dock.svg)
  preview.append(park)
  loadout.svg = dock.svg
})
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; position: relative; }
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

## Art and pictures

Colour the art with CSS variables that have defaults, e.g.
`fill: var(--schematic-body, #59647a)`. On the page a panel's host can
restyle it (`host.style.setProperty('--schematic-body', '#7a4a3a')`); drawn
as a texture (where page variables do not reach), it uses the defaults. The
demo art uses `--schematic-body`, `--schematic-socket`,
`--schematic-socket-edge` and `--schematic-label`. (Never write `--` inside
an XML comment in the art: the file stops being XML and will not draw as an
image.)

**Pictures and the info floater.** A kind's `icon` is SVG markup (the demos
load theirs from one JSON file, a kind id to its picture). A row in a list
shows the picture and the name; in a socket the picture fills it, and it is
the picture a drag carries. Point at a thing, or select it with a gamepad,
and a floater says what it is: by default its name, `description`, mass and
what it adds (`info` replaces that).

## Options

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `inv`, `carry` | the model and the carry (share both between panels) |
| `holder` | which holder this panel shows |
| `host` | the `<svg>` it draws into (it listens for the pointer there) |
| `decorations(item, kind)` | what a thing shows: a bar, an outline, a badge |
| `moveFor(item, from, to)` | the move to make for a drop (by default a slot takes one from a stack, with a swap) |
| `refuse(item, from, to)` | reasons this panel will not take a move, on top of the model's rules |
| `schematics` | art per container: `{ body: svgText }`; its sockets are the slots (`data-slot`, or ids in a `Sockets` group) |
| `only`, `hide` | which containers this panel draws (one holder can be split over panels) |
| `height` | a fixed height that scrolls, instead of growing to fit |
| `totals` | show the holder's purse and totals under its title (default on) |
| `handleDrop` | `(item, kind, from)`: adds a **drop** target at the top of the list; return reasons to refuse, else it leaves the inventory (put it in the world yourself) |
| `alsoIn(item, kind, at)` | other slots an item takes up, where it is drawn faded (a two-handed weapon in both hands) |
| `overlay` | draw the drag's ghost in a page overlay above every panel (default); off inside a 3D plane |

`inventoryDock` takes the same model options plus `schematic: { container,
art }`, `list` (the container shown beside it when open, or none), `width`,
`listWidth`, `height` and `handleResize({ width, height, open })`. It returns
`svg` (for the plane), `open`, `setOpen` and `handlePointer`.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/inventory-box/

---

# min-sim-conformance

**One contract, two stores.** The coordinate-free `MinSimApi` ([world-contract](/world-contract/) §8)
is implemented by BOTH Ariosto's reference store and tosijs-3d's [world-store](/world-store/). This
is the shared kit that proves they behave identically — the "conformance" half of the contract
package (the agreement at the seam: *the package is types + conformance kit, not a store*).

It is **framework-agnostic**: it imports no test runner (so it can ship in the library), and takes
the harness (`describe`/`test`/`expect`) as an argument. A `.test.ts` in either repo passes in its
own `bun:test` hooks and a factory for its store:

```javascript
// Subpaths, not the barrel: the barrel defines elements and needs a DOM.
import { runMinSimConformance } from 'tosijs-3d/min-sim-conformance'
import { describe, test, expect } from 'bun:test'
import { WorldStore } from 'tosijs-3d/world-store'
// runMinSimConformance(() => new WorldStore(), { describe, test, expect })
```

What it pins is the **contract behaviour**, not the geometry: place membership, portal routing
(cheapest, bidirectional, locked = impassable), the proximity ladder (a rung in-place, `elsewhere`
across places), the `SchematicView` shape, `traverse` → `placeEntered`, that steering toward an
entity actually *closes the distance*, and the **choice primitive**: a pick emits exactly one
`choiceMade`, an option that is not on the menu emits nothing, a choice is reported once, and the
sim resolves nothing. It never asserts a coordinate — coordinates never cross.

A store handed to the kit needs two simulation-side methods that are not part of `MinSimApi`:
`tick(seconds)` and `chooseOption(choiceId, optionId)` (the player's pick).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/min-sim-conformance/

---

# b3d-spawner

Keeps the world **populated**. Spawns [prefabs](?prefab.ts) — usually *encounters*: a
mothership with escorts, a base with ground defences and air cover — around the player, and
refills them as you destroy them.

An encounter is **not a special kind of thing**. It's a prefab whose members are placed in a
[formation](?formations.ts). That's the whole idea:

```javascript
import { definePrefab, escorts, at, b3dSpawner, b3dDestroyable, b3dRadarBlip } from 'tosijs-3d'

definePrefab('mothership-group', ({ position }) => [
  // The prize. A waypoint blip so the player can FIND it — and it dies with the ship,
  // because the blip follows the mesh and a destroyed mesh reports no position.
  b3dDestroyable(
    { meshName: 'mothership', size: 14, capacity: 400, ...position },
    b3dRadarBlip({ faction: 'hostile', profile: -1 }) // -1 = always detectable
  ),
  // The screen.
  ...at(position, escorts(5, 45, { y: 8 })).map((p) =>
    b3dDestroyable({ meshName: 'escort', size: 3, capacity: 30, ...p })
  ),
])

b3dSpawner({ prefab: 'mothership-group', maxAlive: 1, minDistance: 800, maxDistance: 1600 })
```

## Demo — hunt the mothership

```js
import { b3d, b3dAircraft, b3dRadar, b3dRadarBlip, b3dHud, b3dLibrary, b3dDestroyable, b3dSpawner, b3dDeath, b3dLight, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dGround, definePrefab, escorts, at, gameController, inputFocus } from 'tosijs-3d'

// An ENCOUNTER is just a prefab whose members are placed in a formation.
definePrefab('mothership-group', ({ position }) => [
  b3dDestroyable(
    { meshName: 'mothership', size: 10, color: '#b05050', capacity: 120,
      explode: 'on', explodeForce: 10, ...position, y: position.y + 30 },
    // The prize, and the thing you can FIND: always-detectable waypoint blip.
    b3dRadarBlip({ faction: 'hostile', profile: -1 }),
  ),
  // The screen — no waypoint of their own; radar has to find them.
  ...at({ ...position, y: position.y + 30 }, escorts(5, 55, { y: 6 })).map((p) =>
    b3dDestroyable(
      { meshName: 'escort', size: 3, color: '#d07070', capacity: 20, explode: 'on', ...p },
      b3dRadarBlip({ faction: 'hostile', profile: 1 }),
    )
  ),
])

const plane = () => b3dAircraft(
  { library: 'vehicles', meshName: 'scout', player: true, y: 120, vtolSpeed: 6, maxSpeed: 60 },
  b3dRadar({ range: 900, coneDeg: 90, lockTime: 1.2, maxLocks: 2 }),
)
const focus = inputFocus(gameController(), plane())

const scene = b3d(
  { gamepad: true },
  b3dLight({ y: 1, intensity: 0.5 }),
  b3dSun({ intensity: 0.9 }),
  b3dSkybox({ timeOfDay: 10 }),
  b3dGround({ meshName: 'ground_nocast', width: 6000, height: 6000, color: '#6b7f5e' }),
  b3dLibrary({ url: '/test-3.glb', type: 'vehicles' }),
  b3dHud({}),
  // Two groups at a time, seeded — the same battles in the same places, every run.
  b3dSpawner({
    prefab: 'mothership-group',
    maxAlive: 2, interval: 6,
    minDistance: 700, maxDistance: 1500,
    seed: 42,
  }),
  b3dDeath({ title: 'DOWN', respawn() { focus.appendChild(plane()) } }),
  focus,
)
preview.append(scene)
```
```css
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

Two hostile groups are out there, each a **mothership ringed by escorts**. The motherships
carry a **waypoint blip** (`profile: -1` — always detectable), so the HUD shows you where to
go; the escorts don't, so you only see them when your radar picks them up.

**Kill a mothership and its waypoint vanishes** — not because anything cleans it up, but
because the blip follows that mesh, and a destroyed mesh reports no position. The marker
stops existing because the thing it marked stopped existing.

Clear a group and the spawner puts a fresh one somewhere else.

## The rules it follows

- **`maxAlive` groups, and no more.** A capacity, not a queue — the same discipline as the
  terrain tile pool. It refills as you clear them; it never piles up work behind you.
- **Spawned at a distance you have to fly to** (`minDistance`…`maxDistance`), never on top of
  you and never in your lap. Finding them is the game.
- **Seeded.** The same `seed` gives the same battles in the same places. That's what makes a
  scenario reproducible — and what lets a GM's benchmark mean anything (see
  [world-contract](/world-contract/)).
- **A group is dead when everything in it is dead**, at which point the slot frees and the
  next one can spawn. Kill the escorts and the mothership still counts; kill the lot and a
  new group appears somewhere else.

## Why the prefab is a NAME

Because a **narrative driver can ask for one**. `spawn('mothership-group', at)` is a string,
and a string crosses a worker membrane; a closure does not. So "find and destroy the enemy
mothership" is a GM composing pieces the simulation already has — with no narrative
vocabulary anywhere in the sim.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `prefab` | `''` | Prefab name to spawn (usually an encounter) |
| `maxAlive` | `2` | How many groups may exist at once |
| `interval` | `8` | Seconds between spawn attempts |
| `minDistance` | `600` | Nearest a group may appear (from the player) |
| `maxDistance` | `1400` | Furthest a group may appear |
| `anchor` | `'player'` | `'player'` = a ring around the player (an encounter); `'place'` = exactly at `x`/`y`/`z` (a launchpad) |
| `x` `z` | `0` | Spawn point, when `anchor="place"`. Ignored otherwise |
| `facingDeg` | `0` | Facing for a placed spawn, degrees about Y — reaches the prefab as `rotation` |
| `y` | `0` | Base height for the spawn point (the prefab places its own members) |
| `seed` | `1` | Deterministic placement — same seed, same battles |
| `disabled` | `false` | Stop spawning (a negative, because an HTML boolean attribute cannot default to true) |

## Events

`spawned` — bubbles, `detail: { prefab, position, elements }`.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-spawner/

---

# formations

Pure, deterministic **placement patterns** — where the members of an encounter stand relative
to its centre. A mothership with escorts around it, a base with turrets on its perimeter, a
patrol flying a vee.

No Babylon, no elements, no randomness that isn't seeded: just offsets. That means an
encounter's *shape* is unit-testable without a 3D engine, and the same seed always produces
the same battle — which is what lets a scenario be replayed (and what lets a GM's benchmark
mean anything).

Offsets are `{x, y, z}` in the encounter's local frame: **+y is up, +z is forward**.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dGround, b3dBox, vee } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { orbitCam } from 'tosijs-3d/demo-utils'

// vee(count, opts) → an array of {x, y, z} offsets. The sim just places a mesh at each.
const slots = vee(7, { spacing: 3, sweep: 2.5 })

const scene = b3d(
  {
    sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
      orbitCam(el, { alphaDeg: -90, betaDeg: 60, radius: 30, target: [0, 0, -4] })
    },
  },
  b3dSun(),
  b3dSkybox({ timeOfDay: 10 }),
  b3dGround({ width: 80, height: 80, texture: 'checker', textureTiles: 40 }),
  ...slots.map((o, i) =>
    b3dBox({ meshName: `ship-${i}`, size: i === 0 ? 1.7 : 1.2, x: o.x, y: 0.7, z: o.z, color: i === 0 ? '#c85a3a' : '#5aa0c8' })
  ),
)
preview.append(scene)
```
```css
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

The functions just return offsets — here a crate is dropped at each slot of a **vee** so you can
*see* the shape the pure math produces (the lead ship red, the wings blue). Drag to orbit.

For reference, the raw call — no scene needed, just offsets:

```javascript
import { ring, vee, escorts } from 'tosijs-3d'

// Four escorts in a ring 30 units out, 5 above the leader.
for (const at of ring(4, 30, { y: 5 })) spawnEscort(at)
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/formations/

# prefab

A **prefab** is a named factory that instantiates *a package of stuff* at a pose — the
concept Unity calls a prefab, and one this library needed a name for.

It is not only a death thing. The same idea serves:

- **remains** — what a [destroyable](?b3d-destroyable.ts) leaves behind when it dies:
  wreckage, a burning hull, a crater, scattered loot, a dropped weapon;
- **spawners** — what an enemy wave instantiates (an aircraft *plus* its radar blip *plus*
  its destroyable *plus* its AI);
- **pickups and props** — a crate that is really a mesh, a trigger and a sound.

Because a prefab returns **elements**, and this library is elements, a prefab is just a
function. There is no new object model to learn: whatever you'd have written by hand, write
it in a function and give it a name.

```javascript
import { definePrefab, b3dParticles, b3dSound, b3dDestroyable } from 'tosijs-3d'

definePrefab('fuel-drum-remains', ({ position, velocity }) => [
  b3dSound({ url: '/sfx/explode.mp3', autoplay: true, ...position }),
  b3dParticles({ preset: 'fire', lifetime: 6, ...position }),
  // Loot that inherits the drum's momentum, so it scatters the way it was thrown.
  b3dDestroyable({ meshName: 'canister', capacity: 2, ...position, vx: velocity?.x }),
])

// Then, declaratively:
b3dDestroyable({ meshName: 'drum', remains: 'fuel-drum-remains' })
```

## Why a REGISTRY and not just a callback

Both work: `remains` takes a prefab **name** *or* a factory function. The name matters
because attributes are strings — `remains="fuel-drum-remains"` has to survive being written
in HTML, in a saved level, or in an intent sent across a worker membrane by a narrative
driver (`world-contract.ts`). A driver can ask for "the wreck prefab" without holding a
JavaScript function; a closure cannot cross that boundary, a name can.

## The context a prefab gets

Everything it needs to be *where and how the thing died*: `position`, `rotation`, and the
**`velocity` of what died** — so debris keeps the momentum it had rather than dropping out of
the air like a stone. Plus `source` (what died/spawned it) and `faction`, for prefabs that
care.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/prefab/

---

# b3d-death

**Death needs an exit.** Without one, a crash is a dead end: the input manager stays welded
to the wreck, you go on "flying" a corpse, and the game is stuck.

`<tosi-b3d-death>` is that exit. When the entity you're driving dies — flown into a hill, or
shot down — it:

1. **blows it up** and leaves **burning wreckage** where it happened;
2. **releases input focus** (you stop driving a corpse);
3. swings the camera into a **slow orbit around the wreck** — you watch the mistake you made;
4. after a beat, floats a **panel** with what to do next.

The panel is just widgets, so "what to do next" is entirely yours: `Respawn` is the default,
but a game can offer _Rewind_, _Spectate_, _Eject and walk_, _Quit to menu_ — whatever. It's
an in-scene SVG panel, so it works **flat and in VR** with the same coordinate-based
picking, and needs no DOM overlay. It is the scene's modal (the pause's too), drawn over
everything so terrain cannot bury it: flat in the middle of the screen, in a headset in
front of you.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dAircraft, b3dDeath, b3dLibrary, b3dGround, b3dLight, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, inputFocus } from 'tosijs-3d'

const plane = () => b3dAircraft({
  library: 'vehicles', meshName: 'scout',
  player: true, y: 80, vtolSpeed: 6, maxSpeed: 50,
})

// A respawned aircraft is appended INSIDE the focus manager — it then announces itself
// (adoptIfVacant) once it's ready, and the manager takes it because it's driving nobody.
const focus = inputFocus(plane())

const scene = b3d(
  { gamepad: true },
  b3dLight({ y: 1, intensity: 0.5 }),
  b3dSun({ intensity: 0.9 }),
  b3dSkybox({ timeOfDay: 9 }),
  b3dGround({ meshName: 'ground_nocast', width: 600, height: 600, color: '#6b7f5e' }),
  b3dLibrary({ url: '/test-3.glb', type: 'vehicles' }),
  b3dDeath({
    title: 'DOWN',
    respawn() {
      // A fresh aircraft — NOT a reset of the dead one. The sim really emits a death and
      // really emits a spawn, which is the stream a narrative driver reads.
      //
      // No need to tell the focus manager: a controllable ANNOUNCES itself when it's ready
      // (adoptIfVacant), and the manager takes it because it's driving nobody. Asking the
      // manager to re-scan here would find `player` still false — attributes aren't drained
      // until connectedCallback.
      focus.appendChild(plane())
    },
  }),
  focus,
)
preview.append(scene)
```
```css
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

**Fly it into the ground.** (W/S pitch, A/D bank, R/Q throttle.) Watch it burn, then press
Respawn on the floating panel.

## What it deliberately does NOT do

**It doesn't respawn you.** It calls the `respawn` callback you give it, because only the
game knows what a fresh life means: a new entity at a spawn point, a saved checkpoint, a
different aircraft. Death is a *systemic* fact; what happens next is a *game* decision, and
this component refuses to guess.

Prefer respawning as a **genuinely new entity** rather than teleport-and-reset. A death that
is secretly a reset is a lie the narrative layer would have to un-learn — the simulation
should really emit a death and really emit a spawn, because that's the stream a driver reads
(see [world-contract](/world-contract/)).

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | `'DOWN'` | Heading on the panel |
| `delay` | `1.4` | Seconds between the bang and the panel (let the player watch it burn) |
| `orbitRadius` | `14` | Camera distance from the wreck |
| `orbitHeight` | `6` | Camera height above the wreck |
| `orbitSpeed` | `6` | Degrees/sec — slow. This is a moment, not a ride |
| `spectate` | `'orbit'` | `orbit` circles the wreck; `chase` freezes the third-person shot you died in (static). Flat only |
| `wreckage` | `'on'` | Explode + leave burning wreckage (`'off'` = just the panel) |
| `blastRadius` | `6` | Size of the fireball |

## Callbacks

| Prop | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `respawn` | What "Respawn" does. Without it, the button isn't offered |
| `choices` | `() => Widget3d[]` — replace the whole panel body (Respawn, Spectate, Quit …) |

> **Never name these `onFoo`** — `elementCreator()` binds any `on*` prop as a DOM event
> listener, so `onRespawn` would silently become `addEventListener('respawn')` and never
> fire.

## How wreckage falls

A dead aircraft does not hang where it died, which would leave a solid object in the
sky for the next pilot to hit. It tumbles to the ground, slams in, skids and stops.
The model is pure and deterministic:

- **The spin is derived, never random.** The axis comes from the velocity (a craft
  tumbles end over end across its flight path) and the rate from speed. A fast crash
  windmills, a stall drops flat, and the same crash looks the same twice, which
  matters when you are tuning a scenario.
- **It bounces once, badly.** A small hop and a decaying skid, so it settles quickly
  rather than skating away.
- **It stops for good.** Below a threshold it is grounded and stays there.

The scene raycasts for the ground and hands the model a height, so a floating-origin
rebase is absorbed for free.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-death/

# UI

**One UI that renders twice.** Every control here is a `Widget3d`: it draws to
SVG and takes pointer input as *coordinates*, never as DOM events. That single
choice is what lets the same object be a flat overlay, a texture on a panel in
the scene, and something you poke with a controller in a headset — without a
second implementation, and so without the two drifting apart.

## Kitchen sink

Every family at once, flat and on a plane, bound to the same state. Type in the
field (the ⌨ glyph toggles the on-screen keyboard), drag the curve, pick a tool.

```js
import {
  b3d, b3dLight, panelScene, panel3d, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, select3d,
  button3d, row3d, vector3d, curve3d, iconGrid3d, ui,
} from 'tosijs-3d'
import { elements } from 'tosijs'
const { div, pre } = elements

const out = pre({ style: { margin: '8px 16px', color: '#8ea', font: '12px ui-monospace,monospace' } }, '')
const state = {
  name: 'scout',
  speed: 40,
  lights: true,
  material: 'matte',
  pos: { x: 0, y: 1.8, z: -4 },
  tool: 'move',
}
const show = () => {
  out.textContent =
    `name ${state.name}   speed ${state.speed}   lights ${state.lights}\n` +
    `material ${state.material}   tool ${state.tool}\n` +
    `pos ${state.pos.x}, ${state.pos.y}, ${state.pos.z}`
}

// The field is near the TOP on purpose: the on-screen keyboard opens below it,
// and refuses if there is not room — so a field at the bottom of a panel shows
// an inert glyph.
const nameField = ui.inputField({ value: state.name, handleChange: (v) => { state.name = v; show() } })

const TOOLS = [
  { icon: 'move', label: 'move' },
  { icon: 'rotateCw', label: 'turn' },
  { icon: 'resize', label: 'scale' },
  { icon: 'trash', label: 'delete' },
]

const panel = panel3d(
  { width: 320, height: 460 },
  label3d({ text: 'Kitchen sink', bold: true }),
  label3d({ text: 'name — tap the ⌨ glyph', muted: true, compact: true }),
  nameField,
  slider3d({ label: 'speed', value: state.speed, min: 0, max: 100, showValue: 'always', handleChange: (v) => { state.speed = v; show() } }),
  toggle3d({ label: 'lights', value: state.lights, handleChange: (v) => { state.lights = v; show() } }),
  select3d({
    label: 'material',
    value: state.material,
    options: ['matte', 'gloss', 'metal', 'glass'],
    handleChange: (v) => { state.material = v; show() },
  }),
  label3d({ text: 'position', muted: true, compact: true }),
  vector3d({ value: state.pos, step: 0.25, scrub: 0.02, handleChange: (v) => { state.pos = v; show() } }),
  label3d({ text: 'tool', muted: true, compact: true }),
  iconGrid3d({
    items: TOOLS, mode: 'radio', selected: 0,
    handleSelect: ([i]) => { state.tool = TOOLS[i].label; show() },
  }),
  curve3d({ kind: 'profile', label: 'response curve', aspect: 0.4 }),
  row3d({},
    button3d({ label: 'Reset', handleClick: () => { state.speed = 40; show() } }),
    button3d({ label: 'Apply', handleClick: () => { state.tool = 'applied'; show() } })
  )
)
show()

const { plane, sceneCreated } = panelScene({ svg: panel, target: panel, width: 2.4, camera: { radius: 3.4 } })
const scene = b3d(
  { style: { flex: 1, minWidth: 0, borderRadius: 8, overflow: 'hidden' }, sceneCreated },
  b3dLight({ intensity: 1 }),
  plane
)

// The flat presentation's own popup layer: a positioned sibling ABOVE the panel,
// outside its <svg>, so a keyboard is not cropped by the panel it belongs to.
// `panelScene` adds the scene's layer (a plane) separately — a popup opens in
// both, because the panel is on screen twice.
const flatHost = div({ style: { flex: '0 0 320px', overflow: 'visible' } }, panel)

preview.append(
  div(
    { style: { display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', height: '100%' } },
    div(
      { style: { display: 'flex', gap: 20, flex: 1, minHeight: 0, padding: 14 } },
      flatHost,
      div({ style: { display: 'flex', flex: 1, minWidth: 0 } }, scene)
    ),
    out
  )
)
panel.useDomLayer(flatHost)
```
```css
.preview {
  height: 100%;
}
```

## The pieces

The pieces, roughly outermost first:

- **[widgets3d](/widgets3d/)** — the controls (`panel3d`, `slider3d`, `toggle3d`,
  `select3d`, `button3d`, `list3d`, `row3d`, `label3d`) and the `Widget3d`
  contract they all satisfy.
- **[box](/box/)** and **[surface](/surface/)** — the containers. A box wraps,
  scrolls and traverses; a surface adds an overlay layer for menus and panels.
- **[popup-surface](/popup-surface/)** — a popup is *another surface*, on its own
  plane. Depth replaces z-index, and tearing one off is re-parenting rather than
  new machinery.
- **Editors** — [vector-field](/vector-field/) (a coordinate on one row),
  [curve-field](/curve-field/) and [footprint-field](/footprint-field/) (author a
  terrain province), [icon-grid](/icon-grid/) (segmented select, tool palette and
  mode picker in one), [keyboard](/keyboard/), [table](/table/).
- **[w3d-theme](/w3d-theme/)** — the tokens everything reads, and
  [theme-editor](/theme-editor/) to push them around live.

The pure models underneath (layout maths, key layouts, text editing) are
documented on the page that uses them.

## Callbacks are named `handleX`

Every callback option in the UI is `handleX`: `handleChange`, `handleSelect`,
`handleActivate`, `handleClick`, `handleClose`, `handleKey`. The `onX` spelling is
not read, and passing one logs a warning once per name, naming the replacement. The
reason is the element creator: on a tosijs component it binds any `on*` prop as a DOM
event listener, so an `onChange` callback would never be called and nothing would
say so. `handleX` cannot be mistaken for an event name, and it works the same on every
widget. Components take `whenX` (`whenDestroyed`) or a verb (`drive`) for the same
reason. A widget of your own reads its callbacks the same way:
`handlerOf(config, 'handleChange', 'onChange')?.(value)`.

# widgets3d

A small collection of **SVG-native** UI widgets with element-creator ergonomics
(built on tosijs's `svgElements` proxy, the same way [[virtual-gamepad|gamepadSvg]] is). They
render to SVG — not HTML — so the *same* widget works both as a DOM overlay on a
flat screen and inside a 3D scene on a `b3dSvgPlane` (where the panel is
serialized to a texture; HTML-in-`<foreignObject>` doesn't rasterize reliably).

## Layout protocol

You build a `panel3d` container and hand it widgets. The container gives each
widget its content **width**; each widget lays itself out and returns the
**height** it needs. The container stacks them and, if the stack overflows,
becomes scrollable (wheel + drag). Every widget defaults to ~40px tall.

## Binding

A widget's `value` may be a plain value *or* a tosijs reactive proxy (e.g.
`sky.timeOfDay`). When it's a proxy the widget reads/writes it and re-renders on
external change, so a `slider3d` and a native bound `<input>` stay in sync.

The example below has a **Test** tab: those assertions run in the doc system's
in-browser harness (real DOM + real pointer events) — coverage `bun test` can't
reach, since tosijs needs a DOM.

```js
import { tosi, elements } from 'tosijs'
import {
  panel3d, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, button3d, text3d, list3d, colorPicker3d,
} from 'tosijs-3d'

const { ui } = tosi({ ui: { time: 8, fog: true, tint: '#4a6a9c99' } })
const { div, label, input } = elements

const panel = panel3d(
  { width: 340, height: 320 },
  label3d({ text: 'Scene settings' }),
  slider3d({ label: 'time of day', value: ui.time, min: 0, max: 24, step: 0.5 }),
  toggle3d({ label: 'fog', value: ui.fog }),
  // A colour WITH alpha: tap the swatch for the picker and its swatches.
  colorPicker3d({ label: 'fog tint', value: ui.tint }),
  button3d({ label: 'Reset', handleClick: () => { ui.time.value = 8; ui.fog.value = true } }),
  text3d({ text: 'Drag the slider — the native control below is bound to the same value.' }),
  list3d({
    items: [{ label: 'Talk' }, { label: 'Trade' }, { label: 'Leave' }],
    // Reports on the PAGE, not to the console: a demo you must open devtools to
    // read is one most people never see the output of — and it spams the console
    // of every page that embeds it.
    handleSelect: (item) => (readout.textContent = `picked: ${item.label}`),
  })
)

const readout = div({ style: { padding: '0 16px 12px', font: '13px system-ui', opacity: '0.75' } }, 'Pick a list item.')
// The tint laid over stripes, so its alpha is something you can see.
const chip = div({ style: { width: '120px', height: '60px', borderRadius: '8px', background: 'repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, #222 0 8px, #ddd 8px 16px)' } },
  div({ style: { width: '100%', height: '100%', borderRadius: '8px' } }))
const showTint = () => { chip.firstChild.style.background = ui.tint.value }
ui.tint.observe(showTint)
showTint()

preview.append(
  div(
    { style: {
      display: 'flex',
      gap: 24,
      padding: 16,
      alignItems: 'flex-start'
    } },
    panel,
    div({ style: { display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 12 } },
      label('native, same binding ', input({ type: 'range', min: 0, max: 24, step: 0.5, bindValue: ui.time })),
      chip),
  ),
  readout
)
```
```test
import { tosi, updates } from 'tosijs'
import { panel3d, slider3d, toggle3d, button3d, iconBar3d, list3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
const { s } = tosi({ s: { v: 0, on: false } })

test('slider reflects an external bound change', async () => {
  s.v = 0
  const panel = panel3d({ width: 300, height: 100 }, slider3d({ value: s.v, min: 0, max: 100 }))
  preview.append(panel)
  const knob = panel.querySelector('[data-w3d="slider"] circle')
  const before = Number(knob.getAttribute('cx'))
  s.v = 100 // a tosijs leaf is a boxed proxy — write through .value
  await updates() // let tosijs flush its update queue before asserting
  expect(Number(knob.getAttribute('cx'))).toBeGreaterThan(before)
})

// Widgets are coordinate-routed (no DOM events), so drive panel.handlePointer
// with viewBox coords — the same entry point the overlay and the in-scene/VR
// host both call. A down+up at a point = a click there.
test('toggle flips its bound value when the switch is clicked', async () => {
  s.on = false
  const panel = panel3d({ width: 300, height: 100 }, toggle3d({ label: 'sound', value: s.on }))
  preview.append(panel)
  // The switch is right-aligned (only it is interactive — the label area is
  // scroll surface), so click near the right edge, not the row centre.
  panel.handlePointer('down', 255, 30)
  panel.handlePointer('up', 255, 30)
  await updates()
  expect(s.on.value).toBe(true)
})

test('button fires handleClick on release', () => {
  let clicked = false
  const panel = panel3d({ width: 300, height: 100 }, button3d({ label: 'Go', handleClick: () => { clicked = true } }))
  preview.append(panel)
  panel.handlePointer('down', 150, 30)
  panel.handlePointer('up', 150, 30)
  expect(clicked).toBe(true)
})

test('iconBar toggles the icon under the pointer on release', () => {
  const hits = []
  const panel = panel3d({ width: 300, height: 100 }, iconBar3d({
    items: [
      { icon: 'barChart2', handleClick: () => hits.push('perf') },
      { icon: 'bug', handleClick: () => hits.push('bug') },
    ],
  }))
  preview.append(panel)
  // Buttons are 32px wide from the left padding, 6px gap → 2nd button ~x=50.
  // padding(12) + button0 spans ~12..44, button1 ~50..82. Click the 2nd.
  panel.handlePointer('down', 62, 30)
  panel.handlePointer('up', 62, 30)
  expect(hits).toEqual(['bug'])
})

test('list selects the clicked row', () => {
  const picks = []
  const panel = panel3d({ width: 300, height: 200 }, list3d({
    items: [{ label: 'A' }, { label: 'B' }],
    handleSelect: (item) => picks.push(item.label),
  }))
  preview.append(panel)
  // The second 40px row: viewBox y = padding(12) + ~58 lands in row B.
  panel.handlePointer('down', 150, 70)
  panel.handlePointer('up', 150, 70)
  expect(picks).toEqual(['B'])
})

test('panel clips when its content overflows', () => {
  const rows = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) => button3d({ label: 'row ' + i }))
  const panel = panel3d({ width: 300, height: 120 }, ...rows)
  preview.append(panel)
  expect(panel.querySelector('g[clip-path]')).toBeTruthy()
})
```

## In a 3D scene

The same panel rendered onto a `b3dSvgPlane`, interactive **the way VR needs
it**. Because the panel exposes `handlePointer`, `b3dSvgPlane` routes each pick's
texture UV → the panel's viewBox coords and lets the panel hit-test and capture
in its own SVG coordinate space — no DOM events, no `elementFromPoint`, no
`clientX`. That same path is fed by mouse, touch, **and XR controllers** (through
the scene's pointer observable), so the identical panel works as a DOM overlay,
on a flat canvas, and in immersive VR. Press **Enter VR** on a headset to drive
this exact panel with controllers.

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, panelScene, panel3d, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, list3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

// distinct namespace — tosi() is a singleton keyed by path, so reusing `ui`
// here would collide with the first example's `ui`.
const { hud } = tosi({ hud: { hue: 200, glow: true } })

const HUES = { Warm: 30, Cool: 210, Lime: 90, Magenta: 320, Gold: 50 }
const panel = panel3d(
  // sized so the list overflows — scrolling is always part of the demo.
  { width: 280, height: 260 },
  label3d({ text: 'In-scene panel' }),
  slider3d({ label: 'hue', value: hud.hue, min: 0, max: 360, step: 1 }),
  toggle3d({ label: 'glow', value: hud.glow }),
  // logs which row was picked.
  list3d({ items: Object.keys(HUES).map((label) => ({ label })), handleSelect: (i) => console.log('list picked:', i.label) })
)
// Show it as a DOM overlay too (top-right) — the SAME panel object, so you can
// compare the in-DOM and on-plane surfaces side by side. It's also the texture
// source for the plane (b3dSvgPlane clones it each frame).
panel.style.position = 'absolute'
panel.style.top = '8px'
panel.style.right = '8px'
panel.style.zIndex = '1'
preview.append(panel)

// panelScene packages the plane, camera and pick routing (uv → viewBox
// coords → the panel's handlePointer, mouse AND XR controllers) with
// camera-yield and capture semantics.
const { plane, sceneCreated } = panelScene({ svg: panel, target: panel, resolution: 512, camera: { beta: Math.PI / 2.4, radius: 4 } })

const sceneEl = b3d({ sceneCreated }, b3dLight(), plane)
preview.append(sceneEl)
// No manual Enter-VR button needed — b3d offers one automatically whenever an
// immersive-vr session is supported (suppress it with the `no-xr` attribute).
```

## Dual-presence scene panel

The same widgets, authored once, drive a panel that has a presence **both in the
flat view and in a headset**. Pass `b3d` a `scenePanel` hook returning the
widgets: the **owl** on the system bar (top left, flat; up ahead in a headset)
opens them as a panel drawn in the scene, under the bar. In VR the bar also
carries **Exit VR** (you can't click a DOM button inside a headset).
`flat-ui="dom"` puts the flat panel back in an HTML overlay. Both presentations
bind to the same reactive values, so they stay in sync.

Click the owl to raise/lower and spin the cube — then try it in VR.

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, b3dBox, label3d, toggle3d, slider3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { cfg } = tosi({ cfg: { spin: true, height: 1 } })

const cube = b3dBox({ meshName: 'cube', size: 1, y: 1, color: '#39c5ff' })

// b3dBox is an AbstractMesh: it drives mesh.rotationQuaternion from its rx/ry/rz,
// and a mesh WITH a rotationQuaternion ignores its euler `rotation`. So nudging
// cube.mesh.rotation does nothing — set the quaternion directly. Tumble on two
// axes so a single-colour cube under flat lighting clearly reads as spinning.
let spin = 0
const sceneEl = b3d(
  {
    panelTitle: 'Scene settings',
    scenePanel: () => [
      toggle3d({ label: 'spin', value: cfg.spin }),
      slider3d({ label: 'height', value: cfg.height, min: 0, max: 3, step: 0.1 }),
    ],
    update(el, BABYLON) {
      if (!cube.mesh) return
      cube.mesh.position.y = cfg.height.value
      if (cfg.spin.value) {
        spin += 0.02
        cube.mesh.rotationQuaternion = BABYLON.Quaternion.RotationYawPitchRoll(spin, spin * 0.6, 0)
      }
    },
  },
  b3dLight(),
  cube
)
preview.append(sceneEl)
```

## Widget reference

Every widget's options in one place. Note `slider3d`'s `step`: it quantises the
drag *and* the reported value, so a slider can be discrete without becoming a
`select3d`.

| widget | option | default | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `panel3d` | `width` | `360` | |
| | `height` | `'fit'` | a number to fix it; `'fit'` sizes to content |
| | `maxHeight` | — | cap for `'fit'`; past it the panel scrolls |
| | `padding` / `paddingTop` / `gap` | `12`/`padding`/`4` | gap is half the theme spacing |
| | `background` | theme `panelBg` | |
| `label3d` | **`collapsible`** | `false` | a SECTION header: tap to fold everything below it, up to the next collapsible label. A `<tosi-b3d>` `scenePanel` folds them itself; for a `panel3d` of your own, run the rows through `foldSections(rows, { key, mode, repaint })` and rebuild on `repaint` |
| | `open` | first section only | whether a collapsible section starts open |
| `row3d` | `weights` | equal | proportional shares of the post-gap width |
| | `align` | `'middle'` | `top` / `middle` / `bottom` |
| | `gap` | `8` | |
| `slider3d` | `min` / `max` | `0` / `1` | |
| | **`scale`** | `'linear'` | `'log'` / `'log2'` — equal travel per decade / octave |
| | **`snap`** | `0` | quantise the VALUE (e.g. `1` for whole grid sizes) |
| | **`zeroStop`** | `false` | an explicit `0` at the bottom of a log track; `min` becomes the log floor |
| | **`step`** | `0` | **quantises the drag and the value**; `0` is continuous |
| | **`notches`** | | values a press BESIDE the handle steps to, the next one that way (`textureScaleNotches`: 1/3 → 1/2 → 1 → 2); dragging the handle stays continuous |
| | `showValue` | `'peek'` | `peek` (on touch/drag) / `always` / `never` |
| | `format` | step-derived | `(v) => string` — units, precision |
| `toggle3d` | `label` / `value` | | |
| `select3d` | `options` | | opens a list (downward chevron); steps only with no host |
| | `stayOpen` | `false` | keeps the list open after a pick, until closed or pressed behind: for trying options one after another |
| `inputField` | **`type`** | `'text'` | `text`/`number`/`integer`/`email`/`url`/`tel` |
| | `placeholder` / `value` / `height` / `fontSize` | | |
| `list3d` | `items` / `handleSelect` | | items may carry `icon` and `disabled` |
| `button3d` | `label` / `handleClick` | | |
| | `menu` | — | makes it a MENU button — opens actions instead of firing `handleClick` |
| `menu3d` | `items` / `handleSelect` | | rows of `MenuAction`; usually via `openMenu3d` |
| `iconBar3d` | `items` / `inTabs` | | `{icon, title, handleClick}`; `{ spacer: true }` is an elastic gap, so what follows sits at the right end. `inTabs`: in a tabbed panel, a bar before the first section goes on the tab strip's right end (undo, redo) |
| `foldSections` | `key` / `mode` / `repaint` | `'fold'` | the rows to show for collapsible sections: folded one open at a time (`'fold'`, an accordion), folded with several open (`'folds'`), or as `tabs3d` (`'tabs'`); rebuild your panel on `repaint` |
| `tabs3d` | `tabs` / `active` / `handleSelect` | `0` | file tabs; a tab is a caption or `{ icon, title }`; at most half the strip each, overlapping around the active one when they don't fit; `tools` (an `iconBar3d`) sits at the strip's right end |
| `spinner3d` | `label` / `size` | | INDETERMINATE busy — call `dispose()` when done |
| `progress3d` | `label` / `value` / `showValue` | | determinate `0..1`; `setValue(f)` |

## Menus are for ACTIONS; a select is for a VALUE

`select3d` keeps and displays what you chose. A menu item **happens** and leaves
nothing behind — so using a picker for a one-shot reads wrong, showing a
lingering "value" for something that was an event.

`openMenu3d(host, anchor, items)` is the whole API. Any widget handed a
`WidgetHost` via `setHost` can open one, so an icon in a tool palette can open
a menu as readily as `select3d` opens its list.

```javascript
// Declared ONCE — `disabled` is a predicate, so this constant never goes stale.
const FILE_MENU = [
  { label: 'Recent scene', icon: 'star', handleSelect: loadRecent },
  { label: 'From file…', icon: 'uploadCloud', handleSelect: pickFile },
  { label: 'Revert', icon: 'rotateCcw', disabled: () => !doc.dirty, handleSelect: revert },
]
openMenu3d(host, cellRect, FILE_MENU)
```

**`disabled` takes a predicate, and usually should.** A boolean captures the
state at construction, so the only way to keep it honest is to rebuild the
array — which means the menu cannot be a constant, and every consumer reinvents
rebuild-on-change plumbing. A predicate is asked each time it matters, so one
array stays correct forever. (A plain boolean still works, for something
genuinely constant.) Same for `IconGridItem.disabled`, so a tool palette can be
a constant for the same reason.

Three rules it enforces, each of which is a bug if you get it wrong:

- **A disabled item is present, greyed, and inert.** Not hidden — a menu whose
  items come and go reflows under you, so the same command is at a different
  place depending on state and muscle memory never forms. It is also checked at
  activation rather than at hover, so an item that becomes unavailable
  mid-gesture cannot fire — which only means anything *because* `disabled` can
  be a predicate that changed while the menu was open.
- **The menu closes before any handler runs.** An action that opens something of
  its own — a confirm, a file picker, another menu — would otherwise be torn
  down a moment later by its parent closing on top of it.
- **A menu cell in an `iconGrid3d` never joins the selection**, whatever the
  grid's mode. Otherwise opening "Load ▾" in a radio palette silently deselects
  your active tool, and dismissing without choosing leaves the palette lying
  about which tool is live.

**On a panel** (not options — methods on the returned element):
`measure()` → `{content, viewport, overflow, fits}`, `openPopup(config, …widgets)`,
`handlePointer(kind, x, y)`, `scrollBy(dy)`, `scrollable`, `scrollTop` (read and
set: carry it across a rebuild) and `reveal(widget, band?)` (scroll a row into
view, in a headset too).

**On a field**: `type`, `keyboardMode`, `isValid()`, `commit()`, plus the edit
protocol (`insert`, `action`, `setValue`, `moveCaret`). `fieldGroup` manages
several of them — exclusivity, commit-on-leave and keyboard layout.

## Tabs

`tabs3d` is a strip of FILE TABS: pick one of several pages. Each tab is at
most half the strip wide, its caption ellipsized. When they fit, they sit
side by side; when they don't, they OVERLAP around the active tab, those to
its left sharing the space before it and those to its right the space after,
stacked toward it, so every tab stays reachable. Pick one on the left and one
on the right and watch the strip re-spread. A tab can be an icon instead
(`{ icon, title }`); icons are narrow, so an icon strip rarely overlaps.

In a `<tosi-b3d>` scene panel you do not build the strip yourself:
`panelSections="tabs"` turns `label3d({ collapsible: true })` sections into
tabs, and a section's `icon` becomes its tab.

```js
import { elements } from 'tosijs'
import { panel3d, tabs3d, label3d } from 'tosijs-3d'

const { div } = elements
const readout = div({ style: { padding: '0 16px 12px', font: '13px system-ui', opacity: '0.75' } }, 'Pick a tab.')
const say = (strip) => (i) => (readout.textContent = `${strip}: ${i}`)

const SECTIONS = ['World', 'Terrain', 'Climate', 'Weather', 'Atmosphere', 'Stars', 'Moons', 'Vegetation', 'Camera']
const FEW = ['General', 'Graphics', 'Audio']
const ICONS = [
  { icon: 'earth', title: 'World' },
  { icon: 'terrain', title: 'Terrain' },
  { icon: 'thermometer', title: 'Climate' },
  { icon: 'cloud', title: 'Weather' },
  { icon: 'moon', title: 'Moons' },
  { icon: 'tree', title: 'Vegetation' },
]

preview.append(
  div(
    { style: { display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 16, padding: 16 } },
    panel3d({ width: 320 }, label3d({ text: 'Nine captions: they overlap', muted: true }),
      tabs3d({ tabs: SECTIONS, active: 3, handleSelect: (i) => say('captions')(SECTIONS[i]) })),
    panel3d({ width: 320 }, label3d({ text: 'Three captions: side by side', muted: true }),
      tabs3d({ tabs: FEW, handleSelect: (i) => say('few')(FEW[i]) })),
    panel3d({ width: 320 }, label3d({ text: 'Icons', muted: true }),
      tabs3d({ tabs: ICONS, active: 3, handleSelect: (i) => say('icons')(ICONS[i].title) })),
    readout
  )
)
```

## Saying that something is HAPPENING

`spinner3d` for "working, duration unknown"; `progress3d(fraction)` when the
total is genuinely known. Both are `Widget3d`s, so the thing that is loading is
one ROW of a panel rather than a mode the whole panel enters — which is usually
the truth.

**The spinner animates as geometry, not CSS**, and that is the reason it lives
here rather than in each consumer. Flat, a keyframe animation works. Rasterised
to an in-scene texture it does not run at all: `SvgTexture` serialises the SVG
into its own document, where no stylesheet and no animation clock follow it. A
consumer would ship a spinner that looks right on a desktop and silently freezes
in a headset.

One shared ticker drives every spinner, so N spinners are not N timers, and the
timer stops when the last one goes. **Call `dispose()` when the work ends** —
a forgotten spinner keeps that ticker alive and keeps painting something that is
no longer true.

If you find yourself faking a fraction, you wanted `spinner3d`: a determinate
bar that is not determinate is a lie with a progress percentage on it.

## Callbacks are `handleX`, not `onX`

`handleChange`, `handleClick`, `handleSelect`. An `onX` option is ignored, and
passing one warns once.

Not a style preference. If a factory becomes a tosijs COMPONENT, the element
creator binds an `on*` prop as a DOM event **listener** and the class field is
silently never called: no error, no warning, a callback that never fires.
`handleX` cannot be mistaken for an event name, so the name removes the trap
rather than documenting it.

## Log sliders — for anything spanning orders of magnitude

`scale: 'log'` gives every DECADE equal travel; `scale: 'log2'` every octave.
Reach for one whenever the useful values are multiplicative rather than
additive — a light's intensity, a **noise scale**, a grid or texture size, a
frequency, a zoom factor.

The tell is a linear slider where everything you want lives in the first few
percent of the track: an intensity slider from 0 to 1000 leaves almost no
travel for 0 to 1.

```javascript
slider3d({ label: 'intensity', value: 2, min: 0.01, max: 1000, scale: 'log' })
// A rate that can also be OFF — 0 is the default and must stay reachable.
slider3d({ label: 'sky speed', value: 0, min: 0.1, max: 3600, scale: 'log', zeroStop: true })
slider3d({ label: 'noise scale', value: 0.05, min: 0.001, max: 10, scale: 'log' })
slider3d({ label: 'grid', value: 16, min: 1, max: 256, scale: 'log2', step: 1 })
```

**`step` and `snap` answer different questions**, and both are useful:

- `step` is how far one notch moves you, in the SCALE's units — octaves on
  `log2`, so `step: 1` walks 1, 2, 4, 8.
- `snap` is which values are legal at all, in plain units — `snap: 1` keeps a
  grid size a whole number however it was reached.

`log` and `log2` place the handle identically (the base cancels in the mapping);
they differ only in what a step means. A range including zero falls back to
linear rather than producing NaN, because a slider that silently stops working
is worse than one that is merely the wrong shape.

**`zeroStop` when the quantity has an explicit OFF.** A log scale cannot
represent zero, but plenty of decade-spanning values can be switched off — a
sky's `realtimeScale` (0 is a still sky, and it is the default), fog density,
wind speed, any rate. Without it the default becomes unreachable the moment you
touch the control. With it, the bottom slice of the track IS zero and `min`
means the log floor; the handle catches at off rather than approaching it
asymptotically.

## Theming

Widget colours, font, and weights are driven by `--w3d-*` CSS variables with
sensible defaults. Set them on `:root` **before the bundle loads**, or call
`setW3dTheme` and rebuild; they are resolved once, for the reason given on
[w3d-theme](/w3d-theme/), which also has a live theme editor. Per-widget
options (`label3d`'s `color` / `bold`) override the variables.

| Variable | Default | Controls |
|----------|---------|----------|
| `--w3d-text` | `#f0f0f0` | Primary text/label colour |
| `--w3d-muted` | `#9aa0a6` | Muted/secondary text |
| `--w3d-heading-weight` | `700` | Weight of `bold` labels/headings |
| `--w3d-text-weight` | `400` | Weight of normal text |
| `--w3d-font-size` | `16` | Base font size (px) |
| `--w3d-font-family` | `system-ui, sans-serif` | Font family |
| `--w3d-accent` | `#39c5ff` | Slider fill / active accent |
| `--w3d-track` | `#3a3f4a` | Slider/toggle track |
| `--w3d-panel-bg` | `rgba(20,22,28,0.94)` | Panel background |
| `--w3d-button-bg` / `--w3d-button-hover` / `--w3d-button-active` | greys | Button states |
| `--w3d-row-bg` / `--w3d-row-hover` | subtle whites | Row background / hover |

## Layout helpers

The maths behind the layout protocol is pure (no DOM, no Babylon) and exported,
for a consumer laying out SVG of its own:

- `stackLayout(heights, gap)` → `{ offsets, total }`: a column, top to bottom.
- `panelFit(content, viewport)` → whether a stack overflows, so must scroll.
- `measureTextWrap(text, width, font)` breaks a paragraph into lines by real
  glyph measurement (canvas `measureText`), not a guessed character count, so a
  panel wraps where the text actually overflows. `cssFont(spec)` builds the
  font string; `measureTextWidth` measures one line.
- `valueToFraction` / `fractionToValue` map a slider value to its track
  position and back, for the `linear`, `log` and `log2` scales.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/widgets3d/

# Playback

**A clip's transport on ONE row**: play or pause, a scrub bar you can drag to
any moment, and the playback speed. A [[widgets3d|Widget3d]], so it sits in a
`panel3d` beside the rest of a panel and works the same flat, in a scene and in
a headset.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, panelScene, panel3d, label3d, playback3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { elements } from 'tosijs'
const { div, pre } = elements

// A pretend clip, four seconds long, run by the page.
const clip = { time: 0, duration: 4, playing: true, speed: 1 }
const readout = pre({ style: 'margin:8px 16px;color:#8ea;font:12px ui-monospace,monospace' }, '')
setInterval(() => {
  if (clip.playing) clip.time = (clip.time + 0.05 * clip.speed) % clip.duration
  readout.textContent = `${clip.time.toFixed(2)} s of ${clip.duration} s  ·  ${clip.playing ? 'playing' : 'paused'}  ·  ×${clip.speed}`
}, 50)

const panel = panel3d(
  { width: 320 },
  label3d({ text: 'Walk_Loop', muted: true, compact: true }),
  playback3d({
    read: () => clip,
    handlePlay: (on) => { clip.playing = on },
    handleSeek: (t) => { clip.time = t },
    handleSpeed: (s) => { clip.speed = s },
  })
)

const { plane, sceneCreated } = panelScene({ svg: panel, target: panel, width: 2.4, camera: { radius: 3.2 } })
const scene = b3d({ style: 'border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden', sceneCreated }, b3dLight({ intensity: 1 }), plane)

preview.append(
  div(
    { style: 'display:flex;flex-direction:column;height:100%;background:#0c0e14' },
    div(
      { style: 'display:flex;gap:24px;flex:1;min-height:0;padding:16px 16px 4px' },
      div({ style: 'color:#9ab;font:12px system-ui;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;flex:1;min-width:0' }, 'DOM', panel),
      div({ style: 'color:#9ab;font:12px system-ui;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;flex:1;min-width:0' }, '3D texture', scene)
    ),
    readout
  )
)
```
```css
.preview {
  height: 100%;
}
```

Press the button to pause, drag the bar to any moment (it pauses there, so
you can look), and pick a speed from the menu.

## The clip is the host's

The widget holds no clock. It asks `read()` what the clip is doing (its
`time` and `duration` in seconds, whether it is `playing`, its `speed`) a few
times a second while it is on screen, and reports what a hand does through
`handlePlay`, `handleSeek` and `handleSpeed`. So it follows a clip however
the clip is driven, and a pause in the scene shows in the button.

Scrubbing pauses the clip, since a moment you drag to is one you want to see
held. Press play to carry on from there.

`speeds` sets the menu (default 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5 and 2).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/playback-field/

---

# widget-box

The seam between the two SVG UI systems, so they **compose instead of competing**.

- [[widgets3d]] has the *controls* — `slider3d`, `toggle3d`, `select3d`, `list3d` —
  and they're what every `scenePanel` hook in this library is written against.
- [[box]] / [[surface]] have the *container*: text that re-wraps, scrolling, focus
  traversal, and (via `surface`) cascade menus plus persistent draggable, closable
  panels.

`widgetBox` puts the first inside the second. A `Widget3d` becomes a `BoxChild`, so
an existing panel's rows can be dropped into a floating panel — or a popup, or a
scrolling region — without rewriting them, and without `box` having to grow its own
slider.

## Demo

```js
import {
  b3d,
  b3dLight,
  panelScene,
  slider3d,
  toggle3d,
  button3d,
  label3d,
  ui,
} from 'tosijs-3d'
const { surface, widgetBox, box, textBlock, svgPoint } = ui
import { tosi, elements } from 'tosijs'
import { svgElements } from 'tosijs'

const { svg } = svgElements
const { div } = elements
const { wb } = tosi({ wb: { time: 14, fog: true } })

const W = 360
const H = 280

const readout = div({ style: 'margin:8px 4px;color:#8ea;font:13px system-ui' }, 'time 14.0 · fog on')
const update = () => {
  readout.textContent = `time ${Number(wb.time.value).toFixed(1)} · fog ${wb.fog.value ? 'on' : 'off'}`
}
wb.time.observe(update)
wb.fog.observe(update)

const s = surface({ width: W, height: H })
s.setContent(
  box(
    { width: W, height: H, padding: 12, gap: 8, background: '#12151c' },
    textBlock('widgets3d inside a surface panel', { font: { size: 14, weight: 600 }, color: '#e6e6e6' }),
    textBlock('The panel is draggable and closable; the controls are ordinary widgets3d.', { font: { size: 12 }, color: '#9fb0c3' })
  )
)
s.openPanel(
  { x: 14, y: 78 },
  widgetBox({ width: 300, padding: 10, gap: 4, background: '#0e1116' }, [
    label3d({ text: 'Scene', bold: true, compact: true }),
    slider3d({ label: 'time of day', value: wb.time, min: 0, max: 24, step: 0.5 }),
    toggle3d({ label: 'fog', value: wb.fog }),
    button3d({ label: 'Reset', handleClick: () => { wb.time.value = 14; wb.fog.value = true } }),
  ]),
  { title: 'Scene', draggable: true }
)

const svgEl = svg({ viewBox: `0 0 ${W} ${H}`, width: W, height: H, style: 'max-width:100%;touch-action:none' }, s.el)
const at = (e) => {
  // svgPoint, not rect arithmetic: the viewBox is letterboxed when the
  // container's aspect ratio differs, and a linear map drifts as it's resized.
  const p = svgPoint(svgEl, e.clientX, e.clientY)
  return [p.x, p.y]
}
svgEl.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => { s.handlePointer('down', ...at(e)); svgEl.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId) })
svgEl.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => s.handlePointer('move', ...at(e)))
svgEl.addEventListener('pointerup', (e) => s.handlePointer('up', ...at(e)))

// 3D side — panelScene routes scene picks to the SAME surface, so the slider
// drags and toggles work identically on the plane (the path a VR ray takes).
const { plane, sceneCreated } = panelScene({ svg: svgEl, target: s })
const scene = b3d({ style: 'border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden', sceneCreated }, b3dLight({ intensity: 1 }), plane)

preview.append(
  div({ style: 'display:flex;flex-direction:column;height:100%;background:#0c0e14' },
    div({ style: 'display:flex;gap:20px;flex:1;min-height:0;padding:14px' },
      div({ style: 'color:#9ab;font:12px system-ui;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;flex:1;min-width:0' }, 'DOM', svgEl),
      div({ style: 'color:#9ab;font:12px system-ui;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;flex:1;min-width:0' }, '3D texture', scene)),
    readout)
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

widgets3d controls living inside a `surface` panel — **drag the title bar** to move it,
× to close. The slider drags properly because `BoxChild.handlePointer` captures: the
gesture survives the pointer leaving the track.

> Drag the sliders in either pane — same panel, same drags. A drag that leaves
> the track keeps working, which is the whole reason `BoxChild.handlePointer`
> captures: on a texture there is no pointer capture to inherit.

## Why an adapter rather than a port

Porting the controls to `box` would mean rewriting `slider3d` and friends, and every
`scenePanel` written against them, to end up with the same widgets. The two protocols
differ only in activation: a `BoxChild` is activated *semantically*, which cannot
express a drag, while a slider needs `down → move* → up` with **capture**, so the drag
survives the pointer slipping off the track. `BoxChild.handlePointer` (raw, capturing)
covers that: `box` hands a raw child the whole gesture and keeps routing to it until
`up`, and `widgetBox` is the translation.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/widget-box/

---

# widget semantics

**What a panel control IS, as well as how it draws.** Every `Widget3d` may
say what it is through `semantics()`: a role (button, toggle, slider,
select, text box, …), its accessible NAME, its value, and how to set or
press it through its own path, exactly as a hand on it would. A panel's
widgets then read as a tree of named controls, which is what an agent's
tools, a screen reader's mirror and the panel name test all read.

```javascript
import { controlTree, findControl, nameProblems } from 'tosijs-3d/widget-semantics'
const tree = panel.controls()               // a Panel3d's rows, header and open popups
findControl(tree, 'Sky/time of day').node.set(18)
findControl(tree, 'Character/save…').node.activate()
nameProblems(tree)                          // [] when every control has a unique name
```

A control is addressed by its PATH: the names of the sections and groups
above it and its own, joined by `/`. Sections (`label3d({ collapsible })`)
are levels, and a closed section still lists its name (activate it to open
it, then read the tree again). A popup that is open is a level named after
the control that opened it.

**Names.** A control's own label first. A control with none (an input field)
takes the label beside it in the same row, then its placeholder, then the
label or text just above it. An interactive control with no name, one named
only by a glyph (`⋯`), or two with the same path, is what `nameProblems` reports: icons first, but never
nameless.

Pure: no DOM, no Babylon. The widgets implement `semantics()`; this module
only reads it.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/widget-semantics/

---

# aria mirror

**A panel a screen reader can use.** A panel draws in SVG, flat or on a plane
in the scene, and a screen reader sees none of it. The mirror is the same
panel as real HTML controls (buttons, checkboxes, range inputs, selects, text
fields), visually hidden, built from the panel's control tree (see
[widget semantics](/widget-semantics/)). Sections are headings with an
expand button, popups are dialogs. Using a mirrored control sets or presses
the panel's own widget through its own path, exactly as an agent's tool or a
hand on it would, so there is one definition of what each control does.

**Placed over what it mirrors.** With `place`, each copy is a real target
laid exactly over its drawn control: unpainted (no background, no text
colour) but fully opaque and, where the main pointer is a finger, taking
touches (with a mouse every press goes through to the drawn panel), because iOS VoiceOver finds what
a finger is on by hit-testing, and skipped transparent, untouchable copies
for the canvas under them. So a person exploring by touch finds "Continue"
where Continue is drawn, and a double-tap presses the copy. A copy with
keyboard focus shows a ring over the drawn control. Without `place` the
copies are hidden in a corner and reached by swiping or Tab.

**Built only when someone uses it.** `<tosi-b3d>` builds nothing for a
screen reader until focus first lands in the scene (Tab, or VoiceOver moving
onto the owl or the scene); from then it mirrors its settings panel and any
modal (a pause: focus moves to Continue), describes the scene and names the
glass gamepad's controls. Values are read again when a copy takes focus;
nothing runs on a timer. Its system bar's buttons are real HTML buttons
already, laid exactly over the drawn bar.

```javascript
import { ariaMirror } from 'tosijs-3d/aria-mirror'
const mirror = ariaMirror(hostElement, () => panel.controls(), { label: 'Settings' })
mirror.update()   // after the panel rebuilds; values patch in place, focus stays
mirror.dispose()
```

What it cannot do yet: a big editor (a curve, a footprint) is read out by name
and value only, unless its value is a few numbers, which become number fields.
In a headset there is no DOM to mirror into.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/aria-mirror/

---

# carry

**Picking a thing up and putting it somewhere**, as a model with no surface
in it: what is being carried, where it came from, which target the pointer
is over, whether that target will take it and, if not, WHY. Drag and drop,
and its two-tap twin, on every surface (a page, a panel in a flat scene, a
panel in a headset, a socket on a model in the world) is this model with a
view on top.

Why it is its own thing: a drag that crosses from one panel to another
cannot belong to either. Each panel only sees its own pointer events (a page
listener, or the ray that hits its plane), so they report to one carry, and
the carry decides.

```javascript
import { createCarry } from 'tosijs-3d'

const carry = createCarry()
const holster = {
  id: 'holster',
  accepts: (thing) => (thing.kind === 'pistol' ? [] : ['only a pistol fits']),
  receive: (thing, from) => console.log('holstered', thing, 'from', from),
}

carry.pickUp({ kind: 'pistol' }, 'hand')
carry.over(holster)            // carry.verdict → { ok: true, reasons: [] }
carry.drop()                   // holstered { kind: 'pistol' } from hand
```

## Two ways, one model

- **Drag:** `pickUp` when the press has moved far enough to be a drag
  (`DRAG_THRESHOLD` in the surface's units decides that, in the view), `over`
  as the pointer moves, `drop` on release (on nothing: the carry is cancelled
  and the thing stays where it was).
- **Two taps:** `pickUp` on the first tap, `drop` on the tap on a target.
  Tapping the thing again, or anything that is not a target, puts it down.
  This is the path for a gamepad and the kinder one in a headset, where
  holding a trigger while you aim at arm's length is tiring.

## Targets say why

A target's `accepts(thing, from)` returns REASONS, an empty list meaning yes.
A view lights the targets that would take what is held and dims the rest,
and shows the reason on the one the pointer is over: "two-handed: both hands
must be free" is an answer, a red outline is not.

`drop` is all or nothing: it asks the target again (the world may have
changed since the pointer arrived) and only then calls `receive`. If
`receive` throws or returns reasons, the thing stays where it was.

## Watching it

`carry.subscribe(fn)` calls `fn` with the state after every change: what is
held, the target under the pointer and its verdict. Every view of every
surface draws from that one state, so they cannot disagree.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/carry/

---

# carry-box

**Drag and drop on a panel**: [carry](/carry/)'s model with a view. Tiles you
can pick up, sockets that take them, a ghost that follows the pointer, and
the two-tap path, as children of a [box](/box/), so they work wherever a box
does: on a page, on a panel in a flat scene, on a panel in a headset.

## Demo

```js
import { ui, createCarry, carryTile, carrySocket, carryPanel } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { svgElements } from 'tosijs'
const { svg } = svgElements

const carry = createCarry()
const bag = new Set(['sword', 'shield', 'rifle', 'lamp'])
const hands = { left: null, right: null }
const LOOK = {
  sword: {},
  shield: { outline: 'damaged' },
  rifle: { badge: '2H' },
  lamp: { bar: 0.25, barColor: '#e0b040' },
}

const handTarget = (side) => ({
  id: side,
  accepts: (thing) => {
    if (hands[side]) return ['this hand is full']
    if (thing === 'rifle' && (hands.left || hands.right)) return ['two-handed: both hands must be free']
    return []
  },
  receive: (thing, from) => {
    bag.delete(thing)
    if (from === 'left' || from === 'right') hands[from] = null
    hands[side] = thing
    build()
  },
})
const bagTarget = {
  id: 'bag',
  accepts: (thing, from) => (from === 'bag' ? ['already in the bag'] : []),
  receive: (thing, from) => {
    hands[from] = null
    bag.add(thing)
    build()
  },
}

// TWO panels, one carry: the bag and the hands are separate surfaces, and a
// drag goes from one to the other.
const bagHost = svg({ viewBox: '0 0 300 190', width: 300, height: 190, style: 'touch-action:none' })
const handHost = svg({ viewBox: '0 0 220 250', width: 220, height: 250, style: 'touch-action:none' })
preview.append(bagHost, handHost)
const tileOf = (t, from) => carryTile({ carry, thing: t, from, label: t, decorations: () => LOOK[t] })
const panels = new Map()
function mount(host, children) {
  host.textContent = ''
  const b = ui.box({ width: Number(host.getAttribute('width')), padding: 12, gap: 10, background: '#1c2230', radius: 10 }, ...children)
  host.append(b.el)
  panels.set(host, carryPanel(b, carry))
}
function build() {
  mount(bagHost, [
    ui.textBlock('Bag', { font: { size: 14, weight: 600 }, color: '#ddd' }),
    ...[...bag].map((t) => tileOf(t, 'bag')),
    carrySocket({ carry, target: bagTarget, label: 'put back in the bag', width: 270, height: 30 }),
  ])
  mount(handHost, [
    ui.textBlock('Hands', { font: { size: 14, weight: 600 }, color: '#ddd' }),
    ...['left', 'right'].map((side) =>
      carrySocket({ carry, target: handTarget(side), label: side + ' hand', width: 190, holding: hands[side] ? tileOf(hands[side], side) : null })
    ),
  ])
}
build()
for (const host of [bagHost, handHost]) {
  const at = (e) => { const p = ui.svgPoint(host, e.clientX, e.clientY); return [p.x, p.y] }
  host.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => panels.get(host).handlePointer('down', ...at(e)))
  host.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => panels.get(host).handlePointer('move', ...at(e)))
  host.addEventListener('pointerup', (e) => panels.get(host).handlePointer('up', ...at(e)))
  host.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => panels.get(host).handlePointer('leave', 0, 0))
}
// Let go of a DRAG anywhere else: it goes back where it was. (A panel's own
// release has already dropped it by the time this runs, so this only catches
// misses.) Only a drag: a two-tap pick-up happens ON a release, and cancelling
// every release would put it straight back. (A page using `carryOverlay`
// gets this built in.)
window.addEventListener('pointerup', () => {
  if (carry.state.mode === 'drag') carry.cancel()
})
```

A bag and a pair of hands. Drag a thing to a hand, or tap it and then tap
the hand. While something is held, the hands that would take it light up
and the others dim; point at a dim one to see why. The rifle needs both
hands free; the shield is cracked (its outline) and the lamp is running low
(its bar).

## How it fits together

- **`carryTile`** is a thing you can pick up: a label and its DECORATIONS,
  which the consumer supplies per thing: a small status `bar` (durability,
  charge, ammo; 0…1), an `outline` (`'damaged'`, `'broken'`, or any
  colour), a `badge` (a count, a mark). While it is being carried it fades
  where it was.
- **`carrySocket`** is a place it can go: it lights when what is held would
  fit, dims when it would not, and shows the reason when the pointer is on
  it. `holding` draws what is in it now.
- **`carryPanel(box, carry)`** goes between the host's pointer events and the
  box: a press on a tile that moves `DRAG_THRESHOLD` becomes a drag, a
  ghost follows the pointer, and letting go drops it on the socket under the
  pointer. A drop that is refused, lands on nothing or is cancelled
  outside every panel springs back: the ghost returns to where it was picked
  up, carrying the reason it was refused. A tap on a tile and then a tap on a
  socket does the same without carrying it.

Several panels share one `carry`, which is how a drag goes from one to
another (the demo's bag and hands are two): each reports what its own
sockets see, and whichever panel the pointer is let go over drops it. Let go
outside every panel and the host cancels (the demo listens on `window`).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/carry-box/
