# b3d-galaxy

Procedural galaxy renderer — the [voxel galaxy](/voxel-galaxy/), the one galaxy
implementation, drawn: thousands of stars in a spiral arm distribution, each
coloured by spectral class. All generation is seeded — same seed, same galaxy.
`el.galaxy` is the galaxy itself; every star carries its address in `id`, and
`getStar(id)` finds it again (an index only means a position in what is loaded).

Stars and nebulae are billboarded **in the vertex shader**: each is a static
quad whose corners the shader turns to face the viewpoint, so a galaxy costs
nothing per frame on the CPU however many stars it holds.

Stars use a custom shader: white-hot center fading to spectral color at edges.
A procedural black hole with accretion disk sits at the galaxy center.

Stars are pickable with `pickStar(x, y)` — click one to zoom in and see its star system rendered
in detail. Use `getStarAt(index)` to retrieve star data and
`getStarSystem(index)` to get full planet detail for any star.
Use `hideStarAt(index)` to hide a star (e.g. when replacing it with a
rendered star system) and `showStarAt(index)` to restore it.

Filter stars by habitability index and/or name using `filterStars({ maxHI, nameSearch })` —
non-matching stars are dimmed.
The galaxy holds every BRIGHT star and every INTERESTING one: a dim star whose
system has a planet with HI ≤ 2 (see **Interesting stars** below).
So the filter sees every habitable system there is, with its HI already known.
The boring dim stars (the other ~95%) are only generated locally, as sky
texture.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, b3dGalaxy, b3dStarSystem, label3d, slider3d, select3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi, elements } from 'tosijs'
const { div, label, input, button, span } = elements

const { demo } = tosi({
  demo: {
    seed: 1234,
    starCount: 5000,
    radius: 100,
    spiralArms: 4,
    particleSize: 2.5,
    coreSize: 0.12,
    habitability: 5,
    nameSearch: '',
    selectedStar: '',
  },
})

const galaxy = b3dGalaxy({
  seed: demo.seed,
  starCount: demo.starCount,
  radius: demo.radius,
  spiralArms: demo.spiralArms,
  particleSize: demo.particleSize,
  coreSize: demo.coreSize,
})

// Star system state
let activeStarSystem = null
let activeStarIndex = -1
let sceneEl = null
// Transition: 'galaxy' | 'zooming-in' | 'star-system' | 'zooming-out'
let viewState = 'galaxy'
let transition = { t: 0, savedAlpha: 0, savedBeta: 0, savedRadius: 0, savedTarget: null }

function lerp(a, b, t) { return a + (b - a) * t }
function smoothstep(t) { return t * t * (3 - 2 * t) }

const scene = b3d(
  {
    frameRate: 60,
    // Generation settings live in the dual-presence settings panel (works in VR); the
    // free-text star search + selection readout stay a flat overlay (typing needs
    // a keyboard). All widgets bind the same demo.* leaves the observers watch.
    panelTitle: 'Galaxy',
    scenePanel: () => [
      select3d({ label: 'habitability', value: demo.habitability, options: [
        { label: 'All', value: 5 },
        { label: 'Robot+', value: 4 },
        { label: 'EVA+', value: 3 },
        { label: 'Survivable+', value: 2 },
        { label: 'Earthlike', value: 1 },
      ] }),
      // 50k, because the interesting use of this demo is to stand INSIDE a
      // galaxy and photograph the sky from it — and a naked-eye sky wants tens
      // of thousands of stars, not five.
      slider3d({ label: 'stars', value: demo.starCount, min: 1000, max: 50000, step: 1000 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'radius', value: demo.radius, min: 50, max: 300, step: 10 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'spiral arms', value: demo.spiralArms, min: 1, max: 8, step: 1 }),
      // Down to 0.1: a dense field wants a small particle.
      slider3d({ label: 'particle size', value: demo.particleSize, min: 0.1, max: 3, step: 0.1 }),
      // The core is scenery at galaxy scale and an obstruction from inside one.
      slider3d({ label: 'core size', value: demo.coreSize, min: 0, max: 4, step: 0.1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'seed', value: demo.seed, min: 0, max: 65535, step: 1 }),
    ],
    sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
      sceneEl = el
      el.scene.clearColor = new BABYLON.Color4(0.012, 0.008, 0.024, 1)
      const camera = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera(
        'orbit-cam',
        -Math.PI / 2,
        Math.PI / 4,
        200,
        BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(),
        el.scene
      )
      camera.lowerRadiusLimit = 2
      camera.upperRadiusLimit = 500
      camera.minZ = 0.1
      camera.maxZ = 2000
      camera.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
      el.setActiveCamera(camera)

      // Transition animation
      el.scene.registerBeforeRender(() => {
        if (viewState === 'zooming-in') {
          transition.t = Math.min(1, transition.t + 0.02)
          const t = smoothstep(transition.t)
          // Fade galaxy out
          galaxy.setVisibility(1 - t)
          // Fade star system in
          if (activeStarSystem) activeStarSystem.setVisibility(t)
          // Zoom camera toward star, then reset to origin for star system view
          const starPos = transition.savedTarget
          camera.target.x = lerp(starPos.x, 0, t)
          camera.target.y = lerp(starPos.y, 0, t)
          camera.target.z = lerp(starPos.z, 0, t)
          camera.radius = lerp(transition.savedRadius, 100, t)
          if (transition.t >= 1) {
            viewState = 'star-system'
            galaxy.setVisibility(0)
            camera.target.set(0, 0, 0)
            camera.radius = 100
          }
        } else if (viewState === 'zooming-out') {
          transition.t = Math.min(1, transition.t + 0.02)
          const t = smoothstep(transition.t)
          // Fade star system out
          if (activeStarSystem) activeStarSystem.setVisibility(1 - t)
          // Fade galaxy in
          galaxy.setVisibility(t)
          camera.radius = lerp(100, transition.savedRadius, t)
          camera.target.x = lerp(0, transition.savedTarget.x, t)
          camera.target.y = lerp(0, transition.savedTarget.y, t)
          camera.target.z = lerp(0, transition.savedTarget.z, t)
          if (transition.t >= 1) {
            viewState = 'galaxy'
            if (activeStarSystem) {
              activeStarSystem.remove()
              activeStarSystem = null
            }
            galaxy.showStarAt(activeStarIndex)
            galaxy.setVisibility(1)
            activeStarIndex = -1
            demo.selectedStar.value = ''
            camera.alpha = transition.savedAlpha
            camera.beta = transition.savedBeta
            camera.radius = transition.savedRadius
            camera.target.set(transition.savedTarget.x, transition.savedTarget.y, transition.savedTarget.z)
          }
        }
      })

      // Star picking — click = mousedown + mouseup within 5px
      let downX = 0, downY = 0
      el.scene.onPointerDown = (evt) => {
        if (evt.button !== 0) return
        downX = evt.offsetX
        downY = evt.offsetY
      }
      el.scene.onPointerUp = (evt) => {
        if (evt.button !== 0 || viewState !== 'galaxy') return
        const dx = evt.offsetX - downX
        const dy = evt.offsetY - downY
        if (dx * dx + dy * dy > 25) return // dragged — not a click

        const idx = galaxy.pickStar(evt.offsetX, evt.offsetY)
        if (idx >= 0) zoomToStar(idx, camera, el)
      }
    },
  },
  b3dLight({ intensity: 0.1 }),
  galaxy,
)

function zoomToStar(idx, camera, el) {
  if (activeStarSystem) {
    activeStarSystem.remove()
    galaxy.showStarAt(activeStarIndex)
  }

  activeStarIndex = idx
  const star = galaxy.getStarAt(idx)
  const pos = galaxy.getStarPosition(idx)
  if (!star || !pos) return

  const system = galaxy.getStarSystem(idx)
  const hi = system && system.planets.length > 0
    ? Math.min(...system.planets.map((p) => p.HI))
    : star.bestHI
  demo.selectedStar.value = star.name + ' (' + star.spectralType + ', HI ' + hi + ')'
  galaxy.hideStarAt(idx)

  // Save camera state for return trip
  transition = {
    t: 0,
    savedAlpha: camera.alpha,
    savedBeta: camera.beta,
    savedRadius: camera.radius,
    savedTarget: { x: camera.target.x, y: camera.target.y, z: camera.target.z },
  }

  // Create star system at origin, full scale, initially invisible
  // By ADDRESS — the star itself, not its position in a list.
  activeStarSystem = b3dStarSystem({
    galaxySeed: demo.seed.value,
    starCount: demo.starCount.value,
    star: star.id,
    scale: 5,
    orbitScale: 3,
    animate: 'on',
    showOrbits: 'on',
  })
  el.appendChild(activeStarSystem)
  activeStarSystem.setVisibility(0)

  viewState = 'zooming-in'
}

function returnToGalaxy() {
  if (viewState !== 'star-system') return
  transition.t = 0
  viewState = 'zooming-out'
}

// Escape key returns to galaxy view
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if (e.key === 'Escape' && activeStarIndex >= 0) returnToGalaxy()
})

const backBtn = button(
  {
    style: 'display:none; margin-top:4px; cursor:pointer; background:#444; color:white; border:1px solid #888; border-radius:3px; padding:2px 8px; font:12px monospace',
    onclick() { returnToGalaxy() },
  },
  'Back to galaxy'
)
const starLabel = span({ style: 'color:#8cf' })
demo.selectedStar.observe((v) => {
  starLabel.textContent = v
  backBtn.style.display = v ? 'block' : 'none'
})

// Flat overlay keeps only the star search + selection readout; the generation
// settings all live in the settings panel (and in VR).
preview.append(
  scene,
  div(
    { class: 'debug-panel' },
    starLabel,
    backBtn,
    label(
      'search ',
      input({ type: 'text', placeholder: 'star name', style: 'width:8em; color:white; background:transparent; border:1px solid #666; padding:1px 4px; font:12px monospace', bindValue: demo.nameSearch }),
    ),
  )
)

for (const key of ['seed', 'starCount', 'radius', 'spiralArms', 'particleSize', 'coreSize']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    if (activeStarSystem) {
      activeStarSystem.remove()
      activeStarSystem = null
      activeStarIndex = -1
      demo.selectedStar.value = ''
      viewState = 'galaxy'
    }
    galaxy.setVisibility(1)
    galaxy.regenerate()
  })
}

function applyFilter() {
  galaxy.filterStars({
    maxHI: Number(demo.habitability.value),
    nameSearch: demo.nameSearch.value,
  })
}
demo.habitability.observe(applyFilter)
demo.nameSearch.observe(applyFilter)
```
```css
.preview { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100%; }
tosi-b3d { flex: 1; min-height: 0; width: 100%; }
.debug-panel {
  background: rgba(0,0,0,0.6);
  color: white;
  padding: 8px 12px;
  border-radius: 6px;
  font: 12px monospace;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 2px;
}
```

Click a star to zoom in to it, and press Esc to come back. The generation settings are in the scene panel (the owl), in VR too.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | `1234` | Galaxy seed |
| `dimBudget` | `95000` | The DIM population's budget. Its interesting share (~5%, HI ≤ 2) is drawn globally; the boring rest only near a point (the baker's eye) |
| `starCount` | `10000` | The galaxy's BRIGHT budget — the stars visible across it (±noise; counts round per voxel). The dim population is local and not loaded here yet |
| `radius` | `100` | Galaxy radius in scene units |
| `spiralArms` | `4` | Number of spiral arms |
| `spiralAngle` | `240` | Spiral arm sweep in degrees |
| `thickness` | `0.06` | Disk thickness (fraction of radius) |
| `particleSize` | `1.0` | Base star particle diameter |
| `maxStarApparentSize` | `0.01` | Cap on a star's apparent size as a fraction of its distance. `0` = off. Only affects the near end |
| `distantGalaxies` | `500` | External galaxies scattered isotropically outside the disc — what keeps the off-band sky from reading as empty |
| `distantStars` | `3000` | Dim far-out stars scattered isotropically outside the disc — the same emptiness budget, but for POINTS. They carry no name or system; they exist so the sky outside the band has texture |
| `coreSize` | `0.12` | Central black hole radius. Disk radii are multiples of it, so this scales the whole assembly |

## Star data

The galaxy's data is pure (no Babylon) and seeded: same seed, same galaxy. Each
star has a spectral class, luminosity, mass, and a deterministic set of planets
with radius, density, atmosphere, temperature and habitability index (HI).

```js
import { voxelGalaxy, generateStarSystem } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { elements } from 'tosijs'
const { div, p, pre, table, tr, td, th, thead, tbody } = elements

const galaxy = voxelGalaxy({ seed: 1234, brightBudget: 100, dimBudget: 0 }).view()

let output = `Galaxy: ${galaxy.stars.length} stars\n\n`
output += 'First 10 stars:\n'
for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
  const s = galaxy.stars[i]
  output += `  ${s.name.padEnd(20)} ${s.spectralType.padEnd(4)} `
  output += `L=${s.luminosity.toFixed(2).padStart(10)} `
  output += `planets=${s.numberOfPlanets}\n`
}

output += '\nStar system for star 0 (' + galaxy.stars[0].name + '):\n'
const system = generateStarSystem(galaxy.stars[0])
for (const planet of system.planets) {
  output += `  ${planet.name.padEnd(25)} ${planet.classification.padEnd(12)} `
  output += `${planet.description.padEnd(16)} `
  output += `${planet.atmosphere.padEnd(12)} `
  output += `${planet.tempC}°C\n`
}

preview.append(pre(output))
```

### `voxelGalaxy({ seed, brightBudget }).view()`

The galaxy itself is [voxel-galaxy](/voxel-galaxy/); its `view()` returns
`GalaxyData` (`{ stars, nebulae, distantStars }`). Each star has position,
spectral type, luminosity, mass, planet count, and a deterministic seed for
system generation.

### `generateStarSystem(star)`

Returns `{ star: StarData, planets: PlanetData[] }` with full planet detail.

| Type | Key Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `StarData` | name, seed, position, spectralType, luminosity, mass, numberOfPlanets, rgb |
| `PlanetData` | name, classification, orbitalRadius, radius, density, atmosphere, tempC, HI, description |
| `GalaxyOptions` | spiralArms, spiralAngleDegrees, minRadius, maxRadius, thickness, distantGalaxies, generatePlanets |

## Interesting stars

The dim stars split in two:

- **interesting**: a system with a planet of **HI ≤ 2**, meaning a breathable
  or filterable atmosphere, under 2 g, not an extreme temperature. Generated
  GLOBALLY, so a habitability search sees all of them.
- **boring**: everything else, generated only LOCALLY as sky texture.

HI 3 is not interesting on purpose. It has no atmosphere requirement (the Moon
and Mars are HI 3), and nearly every system with planets has a ball of rock
someone could plant a flag on.

Spectral class sets the odds, but within a class whether a system scores well
is the system's own draw, so no mix can guarantee a pass. So a harness
(`bin/tune-populations.ts`) scores a corpus per spectral cell with the real
rules and writes the pass rates to a generated table; `interestingMix` and
`boringMix` weight each cell by its pass and failure rate, so candidates are
drawn where they are likely to succeed; and the galaxy VERIFIES each candidate
with `bestHIOf` and keeps the first that passes, so the populations are exact.

When planet generation or HI changes, rerun `bun bin/tune-populations.ts`. A
test fingerprints HI on a fixed probe set and fails until you do. Interesting
addresses may then point at different stars, which is expected: different
rules make a different galaxy.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-galaxy/

---

# voxel-galaxy

**A galaxy as a grid of voxels, each with two derived seeds** — one for its
BRIGHT stars, one for its DIM stars. The bright pass is global (the stars you
can see across the galaxy); the dim pass is local, generated only for the
voxels near something that is looking — above all, the skybox baker's camera.
Design and reasoning: [GALAXY-DESIGN.md](https://github.com/tonioloewald/tosijs-3d/blob/main/GALAXY-DESIGN.md).

Pure: no Babylon, no DOM, deterministic. Positions are in the same frame as
the galaxy's [star data](/b3d-galaxy/) (z-up, the disc's radius ≈ 0.9), so a consumer
applies the transform it always has.

```javascript
import { voxelGalaxy } from 'tosijs-3d/voxel-galaxy'

const galaxy = voxelGalaxy({ seed: 1234 })
const bright = galaxy.brightStars()                     // ~5k, the whole galaxy
const local = galaxy.dimStarsNear({ x: 0.5, y: 0, z: 0.01 }, 0.08)
// Same query, any time, any order: the same stars, with the same addresses.
```

## What it guarantees

- **Identity is an address**, `seed:population:voxel:n` (galaxy seed,
  bright/dim, voxel, sequence number), and a star's seed is derived from it —
  never drawn from a shared range. Star n never depends on the budget, so an
  address resolves in a galaxy computed with a SMALLER one (`galaxy.star(id)`).
  Seeds drawn from a shared range would collide: at 100k stars, a range of
  100,000 gives 63% of them a shared seed.
- **Determinism and locality.** A voxel's stars depend only on the galaxy seed
  and the voxel. Generating one voxel never requires another, and loading them
  in any order gives the same stars.
- **Every voxel has a non-zero budget.** Density is sampled from the current
  spiral generator, lightly smoothed, and extended to every empty voxel by a
  distance falloff with a PINNED share — so the fringe is a dial, not a side
  effect, and the arms keep their contrast.
- **The grid does not show.** Stars are placed by rejection against the density
  interpolated between voxel centres, not uniformly within their voxel.

## Options

| option | default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | — | Galaxy seed: shapes the density AND derives every voxel's seeds |
| `brightBudget` | `5000` | Stars in the global pass |
| `dimBudget` | `95000` | Stars across all voxels' dim passes — most are never generated |
| `samples` | `100000` | Positions drawn from the spiral model (`sampleSpiral`) to impute the density |
| `galaxyOptions` | `{}` | Passed to the sampler (`spiralArms`, `thickness`, …) |
| `nx` | `64` | Grid resolution across the disc (x) |
| `ny` | `64` | Grid resolution across the disc (y) |
| `nz` | `60` | Grid resolution through the disc (z). Must resolve the disc's thickness: at 20 a layer (0.03) is as thick as the disc itself, so stars sit in flat slabs with hard edges that read as columns at 1M stars |
| `halfXY` | `1.05` | Grid half-extent across the disc |
| `halfZ` | `0.3` | Grid half-extent through the disc — room for a halo |
| `smoothPasses` | `1` | Blur passes over the sampled histogram (calms sparse voxels) |
| `fringeShare` | `0.02` | Share of the budget spread across EMPTY voxels |
| `fringeFalloff` | `3` | Falloff length for the fringe, in voxels |
| `brightMix` | O–G5 | The bright population's spectral mix — the bright/dim cut is here |
| `dimMix` | G6–M | The dim population's spectral mix — underweight late M freely |

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/voxel-galaxy/

# b3d-star-system

Renders an individual star system with a procedural star and its planets.
Given a galaxy seed and a star's ADDRESS (`star`, stable) or index
(`starIndex`) in the [voxel galaxy](/voxel-galaxy/), it creates `b3d-star` and `b3d-planet` child components with
deterministic seeds.

Every body is a real [planet](/b3d-planet/): giants banded and ringed, rocky
worlds picked from what the generator says about each one (airless rock,
seas, a toxic hot sky, or dust; see [rocky-world](/rocky-world/)'s
`rockyWorldFor`), moons locked to their planets, and an asteroid belt where
there is room for one. Where they go is worked out by a layout (see **Layout**
below): distances on a log scale and sizes on a square root, so the system fits
on a screen without being empty.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, b3dStarSystem, spaceBackdrop, voxelGalaxy, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, select3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi, elements } from 'tosijs'
const { div, pre } = elements

const galaxy = voxelGalaxy({ seed: 1234, brightBudget: 1000 }).view({ generatePlanets: true })

const { demo } = tosi({
  demo: {
    starIndex: 130,
    scale: 5,
    orbitScale: 3,
    animate: true,
    showOrbits: true,
    time: 3600,
    // Which body the camera follows ('' = the whole system).
    focus: '',
  },
})

const starSystem = b3dStarSystem({
  galaxySeed: 1234,
  starCount: 1000,
  starIndex: demo.starIndex,
  scale: demo.scale,
  orbitScale: demo.orbitScale,
  // 'on'|'off' attributes, driven from the toggles' booleans below — a
  // boolean written straight into them warns (and means nothing).
  animate: 'on',
  showOrbits: 'on',
  timeScale: demo.time,
})
demo.animate.observe(() => (starSystem.animate = demo.animate.value ? 'on' : 'off'))
demo.showOrbits.observe(() => (starSystem.showOrbits = demo.showOrbits.value ? 'on' : 'off'))

// Simulated time per real second, in the unit that reads best.
const perSecond = (v) =>
  v < 60 ? `${v.toPrecision(2)} s/s`
  : v < 3600 ? `${(v / 60).toPrecision(2)} min/s`
  : v < 86400 ? `${(v / 3600).toPrecision(2)} h/s`
  : `${(v / 86400).toPrecision(3)} days/s`

const scene = b3d(
  {
    frameRate: 60,
    clearColor: '#000011',
    panelTitle: 'Star system',
    scenePanel: () => [
      slider3d({ label: 'star index', value: demo.starIndex, min: 0, max: 999, step: 1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'scale', value: demo.scale, min: 1, max: 20, step: 0.5 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'orbit scale', value: demo.orbitScale, min: 1, max: 10, step: 0.5 }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'animate', value: demo.animate }),
      slider3d({ label: 'time', value: demo.time, min: 1, max: 3.16e6, scale: 'log', format: perSecond }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'show orbits', value: demo.showOrbits }),
      // Look at one body: the camera follows it round its orbit.
      select3d({ label: 'look at', value: demo.focus, options: ['', ...starSystem.bodies.map((b) => b.name)] }),
    ],
    sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
      const camera = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera(
        'orbit-cam',
        -Math.PI / 2,
        Math.PI / 3,
        100,
        BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(),
        el.scene
      )
      camera.lowerRadiusLimit = 1
      camera.upperRadiusLimit = 600
      camera.minZ = 0.1
      camera.maxZ = 5000
      camera.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
      el.setActiveCamera(camera)
      // FOLLOW THE CHOSEN BODY: ease the camera's target onto it each frame,
      // and on choosing, pull in to a few of its radii.
      let following = ''
      el.scene.onBeforeRenderObservable.add(() => {
        const body = starSystem.bodies.find((b) => b.name === demo.focus.value)
        const to = body ? body.node.getAbsolutePosition() : BABYLON.Vector3.Zero()
        // In place: assigning an orbit camera's target moves its distance.
        BABYLON.Vector3.LerpToRef(camera.target, to, 0.15, camera.target)
        if (demo.focus.value !== following) {
          following = demo.focus.value
          camera.radius = body ? Math.max(3, body.radius * 7) : 100
        }
      })
    },
  },
  b3dLight({ intensity: 0.2 }),
  // The star sky, without a sun: the system's own star lights it.
  ...spaceBackdrop({ sky: '/sky', sun: false }),
  starSystem,
)

const infoEl = pre({ style: 'margin:0; font-size:10px; max-height:120px; overflow-y:auto' })

preview.append(
  scene,
  div(
    { class: 'debug-panel' },
    infoEl,
  )
)
function updateInfo() {
  const sys = starSystem.getSystemData()
  if (!sys) { infoEl.textContent = ''; return }
  const lines = [sys.star.name + ' (' + sys.star.spectralType + ') HI:' + sys.star.bestHI]
  sys.planets.forEach(p => {
    let info = p.name + ' ' + p.classification + ' HI:' + p.HI
    if (p.rings > 0) info += ' rings:' + p.rings.toFixed(2)
    if (p.HI <= 2) info += ' ' + p.atmosphere
    lines.push('  ' + info)
  })
  infoEl.textContent = lines.join('\n')
}

for (const key of ['starIndex', 'scale', 'orbitScale']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    starSystem.regenerate()
    demo.focus.value = ''
    updateInfo()
    // The 'look at' list is this system's bodies.
    scene.refreshScenePanel?.()
  })
}
for (const key of ['animate', 'showOrbits']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    starSystem.updateOptions()
  })
}
updateInfo()
```
```css
.preview { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100%; }
tosi-b3d { flex: 1; min-height: 0; width: 100%; }
.debug-panel {
  background: rgba(0,0,0,0.6);
  color: white;
  padding: 8px 12px;
  border-radius: 6px;
  font: 12px monospace;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 2px;
}
.debug-panel pre {
  background: none;
  border: none;
  color: inherit;
  padding: 0;
  margin: 0;
}
```

Scroll to zoom, drag to orbit.

> The panel's readout opts out of the doc system's `<pre>` styling. A `<pre>`
> is rendered as a CODE BLOCK there (light background, its own colour), and
> inside a panel that sets `color: white` it would be white on white.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `galaxySeed` | `1234` | Galaxy seed for deterministic generation |
| `starCount` | `10000` | The galaxy's bright budget (needed to regenerate the same galaxy) |
| `star` | `''` | A star's ADDRESS (`1234:bright:5021:0`, the `id` on every star). Stable, and wins over `starIndex` |
| `starIndex` | `0` | Which star to render, by position in the galaxy's view (moves if `starCount` does) |
| `scale` | `5` | Visual scale factor for star/planet sizes |
| `orbitScale` | `3` | Multiplier for orbital distances |
| `animate` | `'on'` | Animate planet orbital motion |
| `showOrbits` | `'on'` | Show orbital path lines |
| `maps` | `'off'` | `'on'`: bodies with real maps in a `system` (our own Earth, Moon and Mars, see **Our solar system** below) are drawn from them |
| `timeScale` | `3600` | Simulated seconds per real second. Every period is real (a day, a month, a year), so this is how fast the system runs: `1` is real time, `3600` an hour a second, `3.16e6` a year in ten seconds. On top of the scene's own `timeScale` |
| `beltCount` | `1500` | Rocks drawn in the asteroid belt, when the system has one (it sits in a wide gap between the rocky planets and the first giant) |

## Our solar system

`SOL` is our own solar system as data: the Sun, the eight planets in order,
the moons worth drawing and the asteroid belt's four biggest bodies, each with
its true radius and the look that draws it. Set `system.system = SOL` and it is
laid out like any other.

Every body has a generated look ([rocky-world](/rocky-world/) and
[gas-giant](/gas-giant/)). The Earth, the Moon and Mars also have `maps`:
NASA's and NOAA's own height and colour maps (see [planet-map](/planet-map/)),
which `maps="on"` uses instead. Phobos and Deimos are too small to have pulled
themselves round, so they are drawn as rocks.

## Layout

A real system is almost all empty space: drawn to scale, the planets are specks
a long way apart and there is nothing to look at. So the layout (pure, from
`system-layout`) lies, in documented ways:

- **Distances are logarithmic.** Each doubling of distance from the star adds
  the same step, so an inner system of rocks and an outer one of giants both
  fit on screen. The order is kept, and so is "much further out".
- **Sizes are compressed by a square root.** A giant is still visibly bigger
  than a rock, but not so big that the rock vanishes beside it.
- **Planets never crowd.** Each takes as much room as its moons need, and the
  next planet out starts beyond that.
- **The belt is wildly overpopulated.** A real asteroid belt is so sparse that
  you would see nothing from inside it; this one is a band of rock you can see,
  with its few large bodies picked out as bodies of their own.
- **Time is not squeezed.** Every period is the real one, in seconds: an Earth
  year is 365.26 days, Jupiter's day under ten hours, the Moon's month 27.3
  days. A planet's year follows Kepler from its true distance; a moon's month
  follows Kepler from its true distance in planet radii (`moonPeriod`). How
  fast it all runs is `timeScale`.

Everything follows from each body's seed, so the same system lays out the same
way every time.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-star-system/

# b3d-star

Procedural star: a sphere with a shader surface. What makes it read as a ball
rather than a white disc is **limb darkening**: toward the edge you look
through cooler, higher layers, so it dims and reddens. Under that, a seething
granulation and a few sunspots. Spectral class sets the colour temperature.
It is unlit, because it is the light.

An optional corona (a glow shell) surrounds it, and `activity` adds a few
**active regions**, turning with the star: over the edge each is a prominence
(a glowing loop arching out of the limb, drawn in the corona), and now and then
one flares, its loop swelling while a bright patch flashes on the disc. The
same material draws the star in a [star system](/b3d-star-system/).

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dLight, b3dStar, b3dSphere, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, select3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { demo } = tosi({
  demo: {
    spectralClass: 'G',
    radius: 20,
    surfaceDetail: 0.5,
    coronaSize: 0.3,
    glowIntensity: 1.1,
    rotationSpeed: 0.02,
    wireframe: false,
    pointLight: true,
    lightIntensity: 1.0,
  },
})

const star = b3dStar({
  seed: 42,
  radius: demo.radius,
  subdivisions: 32,
  spectralClass: demo.spectralClass,
  surfaceDetail: demo.surfaceDetail,
  coronaSize: demo.coronaSize,
  glowIntensity: demo.glowIntensity,
  rotationSpeed: demo.rotationSpeed,
  wireframe: demo.wireframe,
  pointLight: demo.pointLight,
  lightIntensity: demo.lightIntensity,
})

const scene = b3d(
  {
    frameRate: 60,
    clearColor: '#000000',
    panelTitle: 'Star',
    scenePanel: () => [
      select3d({ label: 'spectral class', value: demo.spectralClass, options: ['O', 'B', 'A', 'F', 'G', 'K', 'M'] }),
      slider3d({ label: 'radius', value: demo.radius, min: 5, max: 50, step: 1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'surface detail', value: demo.surfaceDetail, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'corona size', value: demo.coronaSize, min: 0, max: 0.5, step: 0.01 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'glow', value: demo.glowIntensity, min: 0, max: 3, step: 0.1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'rotation', value: demo.rotationSpeed, min: 0, max: 0.2, step: 0.005 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'light intensity', value: demo.lightIntensity, min: 0, max: 5, step: 0.1 }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'wireframe', value: demo.wireframe }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'point light', value: demo.pointLight }),
    ],
    sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
      const camera = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera(
        'orbit-cam',
        -Math.PI / 2,
        Math.PI / 3,
        80,
        BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(),
        el.scene
      )
      camera.lowerRadiusLimit = 30
      camera.upperRadiusLimit = 300
      camera.minZ = 0.5
      camera.maxZ = 2000
      camera.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
      el.setActiveCamera(camera)
    },
  },
  b3dLight({ intensity: 0.1 }),
  star,
  b3dSphere({ radius: 5, x: 40, y: 0, z: 0, color: '#888888' }),
  b3dSphere({ radius: 5, x: -40, y: 0, z: 0, color: '#888888' }),
)

preview.append(
  scene,
)

for (const key of ['radius', 'surfaceDetail']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    star.regenerate()
  })
}
for (const key of ['spectralClass', 'coronaSize', 'glowIntensity', 'wireframe', 'rotationSpeed', 'pointLight', 'lightIntensity']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    star.updateOptions()
  })
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | `12345` | Noise seed for surface features |
| `radius` | `20` | Star radius |
| `subdivisions` | `32` | Grid subdivisions per cube face |
| `spectralClass` | `'G'` | Spectral class: O, B, A, F, G, K, M |
| `surfaceDetail` | `0.5` | Surface noise intensity (0=uniform, 1=strong spots) |
| `coronaSize` | `0.15` | Corona thickness as fraction of radius (0=none). Prominences live in it, so they are as tall as it allows |
| `activity` | `0.6` | Prominences over the edge and flares on the disc, 0 to 1 (0 none) |
| `rotationSpeed` | `0.02` | Auto-rotation (radians/sec) |
| `wireframe` | `false` | Debug wireframe |
| `glowIntensity` | `2.0` | Emissive brightness multiplier |
| `pointLight` | `false` | Create a point light at star center |
| `lightIntensity` | `1.0` | Point light intensity |
| `lightRange` | `500` | Point light range |

# b3d-planet

Procedural planet mesh using a subdivided cube projected onto a sphere.
Height displacement from 3D Perlin noise (gross + detail layers) with
gradient filters for terrain shaping. Same noise system as `b3d-terrain`
so ground-level and orbital views are consistent.

Optional atmosphere (glow shell) and sea: land and sea are one mesh and one shader, told apart per pixel by height (there is no separate sea sphere).

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, spaceBackdrop, b3dLight, b3dPlanet, ROCKY_WORLDS, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, select3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { demo } = tosi({
  demo: {
    grossScale: 0.005,
    detailScale: 0.02,
    grossAmplitude: 5,
    detailAmplitude: 1,
    atmosphere: 0.08,
    clouds: 0.45,
    ocean: 0.6,
    wireframe: false,
    rotationSpeed: 0.05,
    // A rocky world's look ('' = these dials): see rocky-world.
    world: '',
  },
})

const planet = b3dPlanet({
  seed: 42,
  radius: 50,
  subdivisions: 64,
  biome: 'on', // the biome shader's planetary front-end — radial altitude, insolation
  world: demo.world,

  grossScale: demo.grossScale,
  detailScale: demo.detailScale,
  grossAmplitude: demo.grossAmplitude,
  detailAmplitude: demo.detailAmplitude,
  atmosphere: demo.atmosphere,
  clouds: demo.clouds,
  ocean: demo.ocean,
  wireframe: demo.wireframe,
  rotationSpeed: demo.rotationSpeed,
})

const scene = b3d(
  {
    frameRate: 60,
    panelTitle: 'Planet',
    scenePanel: () => [
      select3d({ label: 'world', value: demo.world, options: ['', ...Object.keys(ROCKY_WORLDS)] }),
      slider3d({ label: 'gross scale', value: demo.grossScale, min: 0.001, max: 0.1, scale: 'log' }),
      slider3d({ label: 'detail scale', value: demo.detailScale, min: 0.005, max: 0.1, scale: 'log' }),
      slider3d({ label: 'gross amp', value: demo.grossAmplitude, min: 0, max: 20, step: 0.5 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'detail amp', value: demo.detailAmplitude, min: 0, max: 5, step: 0.1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'rotation', value: demo.rotationSpeed, min: 0, max: 0.5, step: 0.01 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'atmosphere', value: demo.atmosphere, min: 0, max: 0.2, step: 0.01 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'clouds', value: demo.clouds, min: 0, max: 3, step: 0.05 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'ocean', value: demo.ocean, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'wireframe', value: demo.wireframe }),
      // The biome climate, in the terms you think in: temperature at the
      // equator, the temperate zone, and the pole — plus moisture and the
      // rain-shadow strength. All live (bindForSubMesh reads each frame).
      label3d({ text: 'Climate' }),
      ...(planet.biomePlugin
        ? (() => {
            const p = planet.biomePlugin.params
            const bind = (label, key, min, max, step) =>
              slider3d({ label, value: p[key], min, max, step, handleChange: (v) => { p[key] = v } })
            return [
              bind('equator temp', 'equatorTemp', 0, 1, 0.01),
              bind('temperate temp', 'temperateTemp', 0, 1, 0.01),
              bind('pole temp', 'poleTemp', 0, 1, 0.01),
              bind('moisture', 'mapMoisture', 0, 1, 0.01),
              bind('moisture variation', 'mNoiseAmp', 0, 1, 0.01),
              bind('rain shadow', 'rainShadow', 0, 0.6, 0.01),
              bind('volcanism', 'volcanism', 0, 1, 0.01),
            ]
          })()
        : []),
    ],
    sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
      const camera = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera(
        'orbit-cam',
        -Math.PI / 2,
        Math.PI / 3,
        150,
        BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(),
        el.scene
      )
      camera.lowerRadiusLimit = 60
      camera.upperRadiusLimit = 500
      camera.minZ = 0.5
      camera.maxZ = 2000
      camera.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
      el.setActiveCamera(camera)
    },
  },
  ...spaceBackdrop({ sky: '/sky' }),
  // A little fill, so the night side is not a hole in the stars.
  b3dLight({ intensity: 0.15 }),
  planet,
)

preview.append(
  scene,
)

// Choosing a world sets the dials to its numbers (the planet writes the
// same ones into itself), and they are yours to move from there.
demo.world.observe(() => {
  const look = ROCKY_WORLDS[demo.world.value]
  if (look) Object.assign(demo, { grossAmplitude: look.grossAmplitude, detailAmplitude: look.detailAmplitude, atmosphere: look.atmosphere, clouds: look.clouds, ocean: look.ocean })
  // Written straight away: a bound attribute arrives a frame later, after
  // this rebuild.
  planet.world = demo.world.value
  planet.regenerate()
})
for (const key of ['grossScale', 'detailScale', 'grossAmplitude', 'detailAmplitude']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    planet.regenerate()
  })
}
for (const key of ['atmosphere', 'clouds', 'ocean', 'wireframe', 'rotationSpeed']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    planet.updateOptions()
  })
}
```

```css
tosi-b3d { flex: 1; min-height: 0; width: 100%; }
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | `12345` | Noise seed |
| `biome` | `'off'` | `'on'` shades the land with the procedural biome shader, planetary version: altitude is radial, latitude sets the temperature, and the sea level follows `ocean` (see [biome-chart](/biome-chart/)) |
| `radius` | `50` | Base sphere radius |
| `heightMap` | `''` | A real world's HEIGHTS: a 16-bit greyscale PNG, 2:1, `metres = value − 32768` (see [planet-map](/planet-map/)). A full URL, or a path resolved by `assetUrl`: call `setAssetBase('https://cdn.tosijs.net')` once and `nasa/moon/height-2k.png`, `nasa/mars/…` and `noaa/earth/…` are there. Sets `surface` when it has loaded. Those maps are NASA's and NOAA's and free to use with credit, which is yours to show |
| `bodyRadiusKm` | `0` | The real body's radius in km, which is what the heights are a fraction of (Moon 1737.4, Mars 3389.5, Earth 6371). `0` reads the height map's `body-radius-km` header, which a browser only shows to a page on the same origin unless the server exposes it: set this for a map from another host |
| `colorMap` | `''` | A real world's COLOUR: a 2:1 image, longitude −180° to 180° left to right. `nasa/moon/color-2k.jpg` and so on. Replaces the biome shading (and the drawn sea) |
| `flatSea` | `'off'` | `'on'` says the world has a SEA at 0 m: everything below is drawn as level water (and its depth still colours it), for a world whose map shows water (the Earth) |
| `seaGlint` | `1` | The sun's glint on the sea, `0…1`: a patch of sparkle, broken up by fine wave texture, that slides over the water as you move |
| `seaIce` | `0` | Sea ice toward the poles, `0…1` |
| `inlandWater` | `'off'` | `'on'` guesses LAKES from a `colorMap`: where the picture is blue, or nearly black (how NASA's Blue Marble paints deep lakes), it is drawn as water: the map's colour, with the glint. The height map only knows the sea, and a lake is above it. A guess: blue ice or black lava can pass for a lake |
| `terrain` | `''` | A selector for the sphere `<tosi-b3d-terrain>` this is a GLOBE OF (`'#moon-ground'`): drawn from that ground's own height function, and again whenever its shape changes, so a place on the globe is the place on the ground. (The other way round, a terrain's `planet` gives the ground this planet's shape) |
| `relief` | `1` | With a `heightMap` or a `surface` set: how much its true relief is exaggerated. `1` is to scale, which on a globe is flat to the eye; 20 to 60 reads as a relief map |
| `world` | `''` | A ROCKY WORLD preset: `'moon'`, `'mercury'`, `'mars'`, `'venus'`, `'io'`, `'titan'` or `'earth'` (see [rocky-world](/rocky-world/)). Choosing one writes its sea, air, clouds, relief, craters and climate into this planet's own settings, which stay yours to tune; `worldOverrides` (a property) changes the preset for this planet |
| `craters` | `0` | How cratered, `0…1` (see landform's `sphereCraters`) |
| `seaShallow` / `seaDeep` | `''` | The sea's colour in the shallows and the deep, `#rrggbb` (both, or neither: blank is an Earth's) |
| `craterSize` | `0.15` | The largest crater's radius, a fraction of the planet's |
| `craterWear` | `0.6` | How worn the old craters are, `0…1` |
| `craterAsymmetry` | `0` | More craters on the planet's local +Z side, `-1…1` (a locked moon's leading side) |
| `gas` | `''` | Make it a GAS GIANT: `'jupiter'`, `'saturn'`, `'uranus'` or `'neptune'`. A smooth banded sphere with winds and a storm in place of terrain, sea and air shell; `seed` gives a different planet of the same kind and `rings` still applies. See [gas-giant](/gas-giant/) |
| `bands` | `0` | Gas giant: stripes from pole to pole. `0` = the preset's |
| `turbulence` | `-1` | Gas giant: how torn the band edges are, `0…1`. `-1` = the preset's |
| `storm` | `-1` | Gas giant: size of the great storm, `0` = none. `-1` = the preset's |
| `bandColors` | `''` | Gas giant: up to three `#rrggbb`, comma separated (zones, belts, accent). Blank = the preset's |
| `rings` | `0` | A ring, `0` = none. The value is its strength: it widens the default ring and multiplies `ringOpacity`, reaching full strength at about 0.85 |
| `ringInner` | `0` | Inner edge of the ring, in planet radii from the centre. `0` = the gas giant preset's, else 45% of the outer edge |
| `ringOuter` | `0` | Outer edge of the ring, in planet radii. `0` = the gas giant preset's, else 1.5 to 3 by `rings` |
| `ringOpacity` | `-1` | `0…1`, always multiplied by `rings` (which reaches full strength at about 0.85). `-1` = the gas giant preset's |
| `ringColor` | `''` | `#rrggbb`. Blank = the gas giant preset's, else a pale tan |
| `subdivisions` | `64` | Grid subdivisions per cube face |
| `grossScale` | `0.005` | Gross noise frequency |
| `detailScale` | `0.02` | Detail noise frequency |
| `grossAmplitude` | `5` | Gross height multiplier |
| `detailAmplitude` | `1` | Detail height multiplier |
| `atmosphere` | `0.08` | Atmosphere thickness (fraction of radius, 0=none). The clouds ride half way up it |
| `atmosphereColor` | `'rgba(77,128,230,0.15)'` | The glow shell's colour; its alpha is the shell's opacity |
| `atmosphereTurbulence` | `0.5` | How much the glow shell shimmers |
| `clouds` | `0` | (Provisional: this is the weather from ORBIT only. It is its own field, and does not yet agree with the cloud deck or the weather cells on that world's ground.) Weather seen from orbit: how much of the sky is cloud: `1` is mostly cloud with breaks, and on to `3`, a solid deck (Venus). A shell inside the air, with winds that reverse with latitude, more cloud along the equator and the storm tracks, and a shadow on the ground beneath. `0` = none |
| `cloudColor` | `'#ffffff'` | The cloud's colour where lit |
| `storms` (property) | `[]` | Storms placed on the weather, up to four: `planet.storms = [{ lat: 22, lon: -60, size: 8, intensity: 1, lightning: 1 }]`. Each is a cyclone with an eye, turning the right way for its hemisphere, with lightning inside; `cyclone: 0` makes it a thunderstorm complex that sits and flashes. Needs `clouds` above 0. Provisional: a storm here is not yet a weather cell on the ground, and the shape of this may change when it is |
| `cloudSpeed` | `1` | How fast the weather moves. `0` holds it still |
| `ocean` | `0.6` | Ocean coverage (0=none, 0.6=60% of surface underwater) |
| `wireframe` | `false` | Debug: render as wireframe |
| `tilt` | `0` | Axial tilt in degrees: the axis leans and stays fixed in space while the planet spins about it. Rings tilt with it, which is what lets their shadow fall across the planet (Saturn 26.7). A star system tilts its own planets from its spec |
| `rotationSpeed` | `0` | Auto-rotation speed (radians/sec), west to east as planets turn. Negative turns it the other way |

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-planet/

---

# gas-giant

**The cloud tops of a gas giant, as one shader function.** Banded, sheared by
winds that alternate direction from belt to belt, with a long-lived storm.
It colours a point on a sphere, so the same code draws a giant hanging in a
moon's sky ([`<tosi-b3d-moon gas="jupiter">`](/b3d-moon/)) and one you orbit.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dPlanet, spaceBackdrop, GAS_GIANTS, select3d, slider3d, label3d, colorPicker3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const start = GAS_GIANTS.saturn
const { orbit } = tosi({ orbit: {
  kind: 'saturn', seed: 7, spin: 0.03,
  bands: start.bands, turbulence: start.turbulence, storm: start.storm,
  zones: start.colors[0], belts: start.colors[1], accent: start.colors[2],
  rings: 1, ringInner: start.rings.inner, ringOuter: start.rings.outer, ringOpacity: start.rings.opacity, ringColor: start.rings.color,
} })
const planet = b3dPlanet({ gas: orbit.kind, seed: orbit.seed, rotationSpeed: orbit.spin, radius: 50 })

// Everything that changes the planet's look rebuilds it (a sphere: cheap).
const rebuild = () => {
  Object.assign(planet, {
    bands: orbit.bands.value, turbulence: orbit.turbulence.value, storm: orbit.storm.value,
    bandColors: [orbit.zones.value, orbit.belts.value, orbit.accent.value].join(','),
    rings: orbit.rings.value, ringInner: orbit.ringInner.value, ringOuter: orbit.ringOuter.value,
    ringOpacity: orbit.ringOpacity.value, ringColor: orbit.ringColor.value,
  })
  planet.regenerate()
}
// Choosing a planet sets every dial to that planet's own numbers.
orbit.kind.observe(() => {
  const look = GAS_GIANTS[orbit.kind.value]
  Object.assign(orbit, {
    bands: look.bands, turbulence: look.turbulence, storm: look.storm,
    zones: look.colors[0], belts: look.colors[1], accent: look.colors[2],
    ringInner: look.rings.inner, ringOuter: look.rings.outer, ringOpacity: look.rings.opacity, ringColor: look.rings.color,
  })
})
for (const key of Object.keys(orbit.valueOf())) if (key !== 'spin') orbit[key].observe(rebuild)

const planetColours = Object.values(GAS_GIANTS).flatMap((look) => look.colors)
preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      scenePanelOpen: true,
      panelTitle: 'From space',
      scenePanel: () => [
        select3d({ label: 'planet', value: orbit.kind, options: Object.keys(GAS_GIANTS) }),
        slider3d({ label: 'bands', value: orbit.bands, min: 1, max: 30, step: 1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'turbulence', value: orbit.turbulence, min: 0, max: 1.5, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'storm', value: orbit.storm, min: 0, max: 2, step: 0.05 }),
        colorPicker3d({ label: 'zones', value: orbit.zones, alpha: false, presets: planetColours }),
        colorPicker3d({ label: 'belts', value: orbit.belts, alpha: false, presets: planetColours }),
        colorPicker3d({ label: 'accent', value: orbit.accent, alpha: false, presets: planetColours }),
        label3d({ text: 'Rings' }),
        slider3d({ label: 'amount', value: orbit.rings, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'inner edge (radii)', value: orbit.ringInner, min: 1.05, max: 3, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'outer edge (radii)', value: orbit.ringOuter, min: 1.1, max: 4, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'opacity', value: orbit.ringOpacity, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 }),
        colorPicker3d({ label: 'ring colour', value: orbit.ringColor, alpha: false }),
        label3d({ text: 'Motion' }),
        slider3d({ label: 'seed', value: orbit.seed, min: 1, max: 96, step: 1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'rotation', value: orbit.spin, min: 0, max: 0.3, step: 0.01 }),
      ],
      sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
        const camera = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera('orbit', -Math.PI / 3, Math.PI / 2.4, 220, BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(), el.scene)
        camera.lowerRadiusLimit = 70
        camera.upperRadiusLimit = 700
        camera.maxZ = 3000
        camera.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
        el.setActiveCamera(camera)
      },
    },
    ...spaceBackdrop({ sky: '/sky' }),
    planet,
  )
)
rebuild()
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

A giant as a body you can fly round:
[`<tosi-b3d-planet gas="saturn">`](/b3d-planet/). Drag to orbit it. The sun
is where the scene's sun is, so swing round to the night side. The bands'
three colours and the ring are yours to set: pick another planet and note how
thin and faint every ring but Saturn's is.

## In a moon's sky

The same planet hanging over the horizon of one of its moons,
[`<tosi-b3d-moon gas="jupiter">`](/b3d-moon/). Pick a planet, then pull it
about: the dials start at the preset's own values.

```js
import { b3d, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dMoon, b3dGround, GAS_GIANTS, slider3d, select3d, label3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { gg } = tosi({ gg: { kind: 'jupiter', size: 28, time: 16, tilt: 10, ...GAS_GIANTS.jupiter } })
const planet = b3dMoon({
  frame: 'ground', azimuth: 22, elevation: 22,
  gas: gg.kind, size: gg.size, axisTilt: gg.tilt,
  bands: gg.bands, turbulence: gg.turbulence, storm: gg.storm,
})
// Choosing a planet resets the dials to that planet's numbers.
gg.kind.observe(() => {
  const look = GAS_GIANTS[gg.kind.value]
  gg.bands.value = look.bands
  gg.turbulence.value = look.turbulence
  gg.storm.value = look.storm
})

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      scenePanelOpen: true,
      panelTitle: 'Gas giant',
      scenePanel: () => [
        select3d({ label: 'planet', value: gg.kind, options: Object.keys(GAS_GIANTS) }),
        slider3d({ label: 'bands', value: gg.bands, min: 1, max: 30, step: 1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'turbulence', value: gg.turbulence, min: 0, max: 1.5, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'storm', value: gg.storm, min: 0, max: 2, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'tilt', value: gg.tilt, min: -45, max: 45, step: 1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'size (degrees)', value: gg.size, min: 2, max: 80, step: 1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'time of day (its phase)', value: gg.time, min: 0, max: 24, step: 0.25 }),
      ],
      sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
        const cam = new BABYLON.FreeCamera('c', new BABYLON.Vector3(0, 2, 0), el.scene)
        cam.setTarget(new BABYLON.Vector3(0, 6, 10))
        cam.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
        el.setActiveCamera(cam)
      },
    },
    b3dSun({}),
    b3dSkybox(
      { timeOfDay: gg.time, realtimeScale: 0, atmosphere: 0, starfieldCube: '/sky/nebula', starfieldData: '/sky/stars', starfieldTilt: '12,25,58' },
      planet,
    ),
    b3dGround({ width: 80, height: 80, color: '#6a6250' }),
  )
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

## How it works

It is the [cloud deck](/b3d-cloud-deck/)'s idea turned on its side: a noise
field advected by wind. There the wind blows across a plane; here each
latitude has its own wind, which is what draws the bands out into streaks.

## What the numbers mean

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `bands` | How many light and dark stripes from pole to pole, counting both. Jupiter is about 14, Neptune 6. Those near the equator are the broadest |
| `turbulence` | How far the edges of the bands are torn, `0…1`. 0 is ruled lines; 1 is Jupiter |
| `storm` | Size of the great storm, `0…1` of a band's width. 0 is none |
| `colors` | Three: the bright zones, the dark belts, and the accent (the storm, the poles) |
| `seed` | A different planet with the same look |
| `rings` | The preset's ring: `inner` and `outer` edge in planet radii, `opacity` and `color`. Saturn's is broad and bright; the others are thin and nearly invisible, which is true to life |

## Presets

`GAS_GIANTS` has `jupiter`, `saturn`, `uranus` and `neptune`. `resolveGasGiant`
takes a preset name and any overrides and returns the numbers the shader
wants.

## The shader

`GAS_GIANT_GLSL` defines

```glsl
vec3 b3dGasGiant(vec3 n, vec4 k, vec3 c0, vec3 c1, vec3 c2, float t)
```

`n` is the unit normal in the planet's own frame (Y is the spin axis), `k` is
`(bands, turbulence, storm, seed)`, the colours are linear RGB and `t` is
seconds. It returns the unlit colour. No textures and no other functions are
needed: it carries its own noise.

```glsl
vec3 b3dGasGiantLit(vec3 albedo, float nDotL, float nDotV, vec3 haze)
```

lights it as a ball of gas: brightness falls away from the point under the
sun and again toward the limb, and a thin rim of `haze` shows on the day
side. A flat disc with a hard terminator reads as a coin; this is what makes
it a sphere.

## On a mesh

`createGasGiantMaterial(scene, look)` wraps both for a sphere you can fly
round. [`<tosi-b3d-planet gas="saturn">`](/b3d-planet/) uses it, and so does
the [star system](/b3d-star-system/) for its giants. It lights itself: a soft
terminator, a darkening limb and the day side's haze rim. The light is the
first point or directional light in the scene unless you pass `light`.

```javascript
import { createGasGiantMaterial, resolveGasGiant } from 'tosijs-3d'

sphere.material = createGasGiantMaterial(scene, resolveGasGiant('neptune'))
```

The bands follow the sphere's own Y axis, so turning the mesh turns the
planet, and tilting it tilts the bands.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/gas-giant/

# rocky-world

**What kind of rock a planet is**, as data: the Moon, Mercury, Mars, Venus,
Io, Titan, an ice moon and an Earth, each a sea, an air, clouds, relief, craters and a climate.
[`<tosi-b3d-planet world="moon">`](/b3d-planet/) draws one; the
[star system](/b3d-star-system/) picks one for each rocky planet it makes.
To see them, use the `world` menu in [b3d-planet](/b3d-planet/)'s demo.

It is the rocky half of [gas-giant](/gas-giant/)'s `GAS_GIANTS`, and works the
same way: a preset is a starting point, and the planet's `seed` makes another
world of the same kind.

The colours come from the biome shader, not from a palette here. A world with
no water at all sits on the chart's DEAD row, where a warm world is red rock
and dust (Mars) and a cold one grey regolith (the Moon); the temperature is
what picks between them. So Mars is "warm" here, which it is not: read the
temperatures as the chart's way of choosing a colour (Land and Sky's Mars
preset does the same). A world with its own `palette` is not bound by this.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `ocean` | How much of the surface is under water, `0…1` |
| `atmosphere` | The air's thickness, a fraction of the radius; `0` is none |
| `atmosphereColor` | The air's colour and strength, `rgba(…)` |
| `clouds` | How much of the sky is cloud: `1` mostly cloud with breaks, `3` a solid deck |
| `grossAmplitude`, `detailAmplitude` | Relief, in the planet's own units (its radius is 50 in the demos) |
| `craters` | `density` `0…1`, `size` (the largest, a fraction of the radius), `wear` `0…1`, and `asymmetry` `-1…1`: more craters on one side (see [landform](/landform/)'s `sphereCraters`) |
| `sea` | The sea's colour, `{ shallow, deep }` (Titan's methane is nearly black); absent, an Earth's |
| `palette` | The ground's own colours in place of the chart's, `{ a, b }`: four cold-to-hot (Io's sulfur) |
| `climate` | The biome shader's planetary climate: `equatorTemp`, `temperateTemp`, `poleTemp` (chart units, freezing at 0.36), `mapMoisture`, and `slopeExaggeration` (how steep must read as rock: about 6 for an Earth, 1.5 on cratered ground) |

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/rocky-world/

---

# b3d-black-hole

Procedural black hole with accretion disk, gravitational lensing effect,
and photon ring. Inspired by the Interstellar visualization — not physically
accurate but visually striking.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, b3dBlackHole, b3dSphere, label3d, slider3d, toggle3d, select3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const { demo } = tosi({
  demo: {
    radius: 10,
    diskInnerRadius: 1.05,
    diskOuterRadius: 3.0,
    diskBrightness: 1.5,
    rotationSpeed: 0.3,
    lensing: 'on',
    photonRing: 'on',
    photonRingBrightness: 2.0,
    wireframe: false,
  },
})

const hole = b3dBlackHole({
  radius: demo.radius,
  diskInnerRadius: demo.diskInnerRadius,
  diskOuterRadius: demo.diskOuterRadius,
  diskBrightness: demo.diskBrightness,
  rotationSpeed: demo.rotationSpeed,
  lensing: demo.lensing,
  photonRing: demo.photonRing,
  photonRingBrightness: demo.photonRingBrightness,
  wireframe: demo.wireframe,
})

const scene = b3d(
  {
    frameRate: 60,
    clearColor: '#000000',
    panelTitle: 'Black hole',
    scenePanel: () => [
      slider3d({ label: 'radius', value: demo.radius, min: 3, max: 20, step: 0.5 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'disk inner', value: demo.diskInnerRadius, min: 1.01, max: 2, step: 0.01 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'disk outer', value: demo.diskOuterRadius, min: 2, max: 8, step: 0.1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'disk brightness', value: demo.diskBrightness, min: 0.5, max: 3, step: 0.1 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'rotation', value: demo.rotationSpeed, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01 }),
      slider3d({ label: 'photon ring bright', value: demo.photonRingBrightness, min: 0.5, max: 5, step: 0.1 }),
      select3d({ label: 'lensing', value: demo.lensing, options: ['on', 'off'] }),
      select3d({ label: 'photon ring', value: demo.photonRing, options: ['on', 'off'] }),
      toggle3d({ label: 'wireframe', value: demo.wireframe }),
    ],
    sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
      const camera = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera(
        'orbit-cam',
        -Math.PI / 2,
        Math.PI / 3,
        80,
        BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(),
        el.scene
      )
      camera.lowerRadiusLimit = 20
      camera.upperRadiusLimit = 300
      camera.minZ = 0.5
      camera.maxZ = 2000
      camera.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
      el.setActiveCamera(camera)
    },
  },
  b3dLight({ intensity: 0.05 }),
  hole,
  b3dSphere({ radius: 3, x: 50, y: 0, z: 0, color: '#888888' }),
)

preview.append(
  scene,
)

for (const key of ['radius', 'diskInnerRadius', 'diskOuterRadius']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    hole.regenerate()
  })
}
for (const key of ['diskBrightness', 'rotationSpeed', 'lensing', 'photonRing', 'photonRingBrightness', 'wireframe']) {
  demo[key].observe(() => {
    hole.updateOptions()
  })
}
```
```css
.preview { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100%; }
tosi-b3d { flex: 1; min-height: 0; width: 100%; }
```

Scroll to zoom, drag to orbit. The settings are in the scene panel (the owl).

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | `10` | Event horizon radius |
| `diskInnerRadius` | `1.5` | Inner edge of accretion disk (multiple of radius) |
| `diskOuterRadius` | `4.0` | Outer edge of accretion disk (multiple of radius) |
| `diskBrightness` | `1.5` | Accretion disk emissive brightness |
| `rotationSpeed` | `0.3` | Disk rotation speed (rad/sec) |
| `lensing` | `'on'` | Show gravitational lensing ring |
| `photonRing` | `'on'` | Show photon ring at event horizon |
| `photonRingBrightness` | `2.0` | Photon ring glow intensity |
| `wireframe` | `false` | Debug wireframe |
| `seed` | `12345` | Noise seed for disk turbulence |
| `subdivisions` | `64` | Mesh detail level (lower = faster) |

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-black-hole/

# sphere-map

**Where a place on the ground is on the globe, and back.** A terrain in
`surfaceType="sphere"` is a flat sheet wrapped round a planet: walk far enough
east and you come back. This is the arithmetic of that wrapping, as pure
functions, so that a planet seen from orbit and the ground you land on can
agree about where things are.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dTerrain, b3dPlanet, b3dWater, b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dLight, latLonToDirection } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { elements } from 'tosijs'

const { div } = elements
const readout = div({ class: 'readout' }, 'finding the ground…')

// A whole planet 4 km in radius, so that a globe of it shows real relief.
const terrain = b3dTerrain({
  id: 'sphere-map-ground',
  seed: 11, biome: 'on', surfaceType: 'sphere', radius: 4000,
  tileSize: 128, lodLevels: 3, splitFactor: 2, reach: 4000,
  grossScale: 0.0016, detailScale: 0.012, grossAmplitude: 320, detailAmplitude: 24,
  center: true,
})
// biome: 'on' so the globe shades with the ground's own climate and colours;
// flatSea because this world has a sea at 0 m (the water below).
// `terrain` makes it a globe OF that ground: drawn from it, and again
// whenever the ground's shape changes.
const globe = b3dPlanet({ terrain: '#sphere-map-ground', radius: 40, relief: 2, flatSea: 'on', atmosphere: 0.05, subdivisions: 96, biome: 'on' })

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
        const scene = el.scene
        const cam = new BABYLON.FreeCamera('fly', new BABYLON.Vector3(0, 420, -260), scene)
        cam.setTarget(new BABYLON.Vector3(0, 380, 200))
        cam.speed = 12
        cam.maxZ = 12000
        cam.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
        el.setActiveCamera(cam)

        const pin = BABYLON.MeshBuilder.CreateSphere('pin', { diameter: 3 }, scene)
        const red = new BABYLON.StandardMaterial('pin', scene)
        red.emissiveColor = new BABYLON.Color3(1, 0.15, 0.1)
        red.disableLighting = true
        pin.material = red

        scene.onBeforeRenderObservable.add(() => {
          const root = globe.rootNode
          if (root == null || typeof terrain.latLonAt !== 'function') return
          // The globe rides ahead of the camera, like a map on a stand.
          root.position.set(cam.position.x + 60, cam.position.y + 10, cam.position.z + 190)
          // The camera's place in the world: scene position plus the
          // terrain's floating origin.
          const off = terrain.originOffset
          const here = terrain.latLonAt(cam.position.x + off.x, cam.position.z + off.z)
          if (here == null) return
          const d = latLonToDirection(here.lat, here.lon)
          // The pin sits ON the globe, and the globe turns to show you the
          // side you are on (yaw only, so north stays up).
          pin.parent = root
          pin.position.set(d.x * 43, d.y * 43, d.z * 43)
          const toCam = cam.position.subtract(root.position)
          root.rotation.y = Math.atan2(toCam.x, toCam.z) - Math.atan2(d.x, d.z)
          readout.textContent = `${Math.abs(here.lat).toFixed(2)}° ${here.lat >= 0 ? 'N' : 'S'}   ${Math.abs(here.lon).toFixed(2)}° ${here.lon >= 0 ? 'E' : 'W'}`
        })
      },
    },
    b3dSun({}),
    b3dSkybox({ timeOfDay: 10, realtimeScale: 0 }),
    b3dLight({ intensity: 0.5 }),
    terrain,
    b3dWater({ y: 0, waterSize: 9000, follow: true }),
    globe,
  ),
  readout,
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; position: relative; }
.readout { position: absolute; left: 12px; bottom: 12px; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 6px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.6); color: #fff; font: 13px ui-monospace, monospace; }
```

A small world, and the same world as a globe hung in its own sky. The globe
is not a picture of the terrain: it is built from the terrain's own height
function (`terrain.planetSurface()`), so its coasts are the coasts below. The
red pin is where the camera is, and the globe turns to keep your side of the
world facing you. Fly about (arrow keys, drag to look) and the land under the
pin changes; the readout is your latitude and longitude.

## Three names for one place

Three ways of naming one place:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **direction** | a unit vector from the planet's centre. What a globe is made of |
| **latitude, longitude** | degrees. What a person writes down. North is +Y |
| **ground** | metres east (+x) and north (+z) of the terrain's origin, in the terrain's own unshifting coordinates: a scene position plus `terrain.originOffset`. What the terrain uses |

`frame` says how the sheet is laid on the sphere: the planet's `radius` and
the `worldU`, `worldV` the terrain's origin sits at.

```javascript
import { groundToLatLon, latLonToGround, latLonToDirection } from 'tosijs-3d/sphere-map'

const frame = { radius: 6000, worldU: 0, worldV: 0.25 }
const pin = { lat: 12, lon: 40 }
latLonToGround(pin.lat, pin.lon, frame) // where to stand: { x, z } in metres
latLonToDirection(pin.lat, pin.lon)     // where to put the marker on the globe
```

The wrapping is the plain latitude and longitude one, so a metre east is the
same number of degrees at every latitude and the ground is squeezed
east-to-west toward the poles. It is exact at the equator and good across the
middle latitudes; a pole is a line, not a point.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/sphere-map/

---

# planet-map

**A real world from its maps.** NASA and NOAA publish the height of the Moon,
Mars and the Earth as flat images, one pixel per patch of latitude and
longitude. This turns such an image into a [`PlanetSurface`](/sphere-map/):
the thing a [`<tosi-b3d-planet>`](/b3d-planet/) draws a globe from. Set the
planet's `heightMap` and `colorMap` and it is that world.

## Demo

```js
import { b3d, b3dPlanet, spaceBackdrop, select3d, slider3d, label3d } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { tosi } from 'tosijs'

const WORLDS = {
  Moon: { heightMap: 'nasa/moon/height-2k.png', colorMap: 'nasa/moon/color-2k.jpg', bodyRadiusKm: 1737.4, flatSea: 'off', inlandWater: 'off', clouds: 0, atmosphere: 0, atmosphereColor: 'rgba(77,128,230,0.15)', relief: 12 },
  Mars: { heightMap: 'nasa/mars/height-2k.png', colorMap: 'nasa/mars/color-2k.jpg', bodyRadiusKm: 3389.5, flatSea: 'off', inlandWater: 'off', clouds: 0, atmosphere: 0.006, atmosphereColor: 'rgba(225,165,115,0.04)', relief: 14 },
  // NOAA's heights include the sea floor; `flatSea` fills the oceans level.
  Earth: { heightMap: 'noaa/earth/height-2k.png', colorMap: 'nasa/earth/color-2k.jpg', bodyRadiusKm: 6371, flatSea: 'on', inlandWater: 'on', clouds: 0.45, atmosphere: 0.03, atmosphereColor: 'rgba(77,128,230,0.15)', relief: 30 },
}
const { real } = tosi({ real: { world: 'Earth', relief: WORLDS.Earth.relief, spin: 0.03, clouds: WORLDS.Earth.clouds, storms: 3, stormIntensity: 1 } })
const planet = b3dPlanet({ radius: 50, subdivisions: 160, ocean: 0, rotationSpeed: real.spin, ...WORLDS.Earth })

// Storms on the Earth: a hurricane off the Caribbean, a cyclone in the
// south-west Pacific and a typhoon in the Philippine Sea (the fourth, and
// four is as many as a planet takes), each turning the right way for its
// hemisphere. And one
// that is real: the Catatumbo lightning over Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela,
// a thunderstorm that stands in the same place most nights of the year
// (`cyclone: 0`: it does not turn). Swing round to the night side to see
// them flicker.
const STORMS = {
  Earth: [
    { lat: 24, lon: -62, size: 6, intensity: 1, lightning: 1.5 },
    { lat: -17, lon: 160, size: 5, intensity: 0.9, lightning: 1 },
    { lat: 9.5, lon: -71.5, size: 2.2, intensity: 0.8, lightning: 4, cyclone: 0 },
    { lat: 17, lon: 133, size: 7, intensity: 1, lightning: 1.2 },
  ],
}
// None of the weather is a picture: the cloud cover and the storms are
// computed as you watch, so all of it is dials. A stronger storm winds
// harder, flashes more and is wider.
const setStorms = () => {
  const k = real.stormIntensity.value
  const wide = 0.6 + 0.4 * k
  planet.storms = k <= 0 ? [] : (STORMS[real.world.value] ?? []).slice(0, real.storms.value).map((s) => ({ ...s, size: s.size * wide, intensity: s.intensity * k, lightning: s.lightning * k }))
}
setStorms()
real.storms.observe(setStorms)
real.stormIntensity.observe(setStorms)
real.clouds.observe(() => {
  planet.clouds = real.clouds.value
  planet.updateOptions()
})

real.world.observe(() => {
  const w = WORLDS[real.world.value]
  setStorms()
  Object.assign(planet, w)
  real.relief.value = w.relief
  real.clouds.value = w.clouds
  planet.regenerate()
})
real.relief.observe(() => {
  planet.relief = real.relief.value
  planet.regenerate()
})

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      scenePanelOpen: true,
      panelTitle: 'Real worlds',
      scenePanel: () => [
        select3d({ label: 'world', value: real.world, options: Object.keys(WORLDS) }),
        slider3d({ label: 'relief (× true)', value: real.relief, min: 1, max: 60, step: 1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'rotation', value: real.spin, min: 0, max: 0.3, step: 0.01 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'clouds', value: real.clouds, min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.05 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'storms', value: real.storms, min: 0, max: 4, step: 1 }),
        slider3d({ label: 'storm intensity', value: real.stormIntensity, min: 0, max: 2, step: 0.05 }),
      ],
      sceneCreated(el, BABYLON) {
        const camera = new BABYLON.ArcRotateCamera('orbit', -Math.PI / 2.4, Math.PI / 2.3, 150, BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(), el.scene)
        camera.lowerRadiusLimit = 65
        camera.upperRadiusLimit = 500
        camera.maxZ = 3000
        camera.attachControl(el.querySelector('canvas'), true)
        el.setActiveCamera(camera)
      },
    },
    ...spaceBackdrop({ sky: '/sky' }),
    planet,
  )
)
```
```css
.preview { height: 100%; }
```

The Moon, Mars and the Earth from NASA's and NOAA's own measurements. Drag to
turn them. `relief` exaggerates the heights: at 1 a planet is as smooth as a
billiard ball, which is the truth, and somewhere past 10 it becomes a relief
map.

The Earth's weather is not part of the picture: `clouds`, `storms` (how
many) and `storm intensity` are dials, and the cover and the cyclones are
worked out as you watch.

Credits: Moon and Mars from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (LRO LOLA
and LROC; MGS MOLA and Viking); the Earth's colour from NASA's Blue Marble and
its heights from NOAA's ETOPO 2022. Each file names its source and licence in
its response headers.

## From code

```javascript
import { loadPlanetMap, assetUrl } from 'tosijs-3d'

const moon = await loadPlanetMap(assetUrl('nasa/moon/height-2k.png'))
moon.radius            // 1737400, read from the file's own headers
moon.heightAt({ x: 1, y: 0, z: 0 }) // metres above the datum at 0°N 0°E
```

## What the image has to be

- **A 16-bit greyscale PNG**, where `metres = value − 32768`. Sixteen bits
  because eight cannot hold a planet: Everest and the Mariana Trench are
  twenty kilometres apart and a byte has 256 steps. A browser's own image
  decoding gives eight bits a channel, so this module reads the PNG itself.
- **Equirectangular, 2:1**: longitude −180° to +180° left to right, latitude
  +90° to −90° top to bottom. It is what the public data comes in.

The maps on `cdn.tosijs.net` (`nasa/moon`, `nasa/mars`, `nasa/earth`,
`noaa/earth`, each at `1k`, `2k` and `4k`) are in this form, and say so in
their response headers along with the body's radius, the credit and the
licence. `loadPlanetMap` reads the radius from there.

## Options

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `radius` | The body's radius in metres. Unset, the file's `body-radius-km` header, which a browser shows only to a page on the same origin unless the server exposes it; from another host, pass it |
| `seaLevel` | Height of the datum or sea, metres. Default `0` |
| `floor` | Nothing is reported lower than this. `0` on the Earth fills the oceans level, which is what a globe with a blue sea wants; unset, the sea floor is ground |

## The pieces

`decodeGray16Png(bytes)` is the decoder (any 16-bit greyscale,
non-interlaced PNG) and `mapSurface(map, options)` wraps decoded heights as a
surface, sampling between pixels and wrapping at the date line. Both are pure:
no DOM, no engine.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/planet-map/

# space-backdrop

**Space, set up once**: a sun and the encoded star sky with no air, the
galaxy's band tipped off the scene's horizontal plane. Every demo that hangs
a body in space uses it ([planet](/b3d-planet/), [gas giant](/gas-giant/),
[planet-map](/planet-map/), the [star system](/b3d-star-system/)), so they
share one sky and one sun.

```javascript
import { b3d, b3dPlanet, spaceBackdrop } from 'tosijs-3d'

preview.append(b3d({}, ...spaceBackdrop(), b3dPlanet({ world: 'mars' })))
```

**Why the tilt matters.** The galaxy's disc is baked level in the sky's own
frame. Untilted, its band lies along the scene's horizontal plane, which is a
planet's equator and its ring's plane, so the Milky Way would run exactly
along Saturn's rings: tidy, and obviously staged. The default is the tilt the sky
was framed for (`SHIPPED_SKY.tilt`), the one the rest of the library uses.

**Which sky.** By default the versioned sky on `3d.tosijs.net`, which is
never rewritten, so a page keeps the sky it was made with. `sky: '/sky'` is the
doc site's latest (what its demos load). Anything else in `skybox` or `sun`
is passed through.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/space-backdrop/

# Performance

**One scene, a phone and a workstation.** The [probe](/b3d-probe/) measures the
device once and sorts it into a tier; components then resolve any setting left
on `auto` against that tier's budget. The pages beneath it are the model and
the place to force a tier.
