# b3d-probe

`<tosi-b3d-probe>` — a device-capability probe. Drop it anywhere (a landing page is
ideal): it benchmarks the device once, and every `<tosi-b3d>` on the origin reads
the result to pick sensible defaults.

## Demo

```js
import { elements } from 'tosijs'
import { b3dProbe } from 'tosijs-3d'

const output = elements.pre()

preview.append(
  b3dProbe({
    // tosijs binds on<Event> props via addEventListener — onProfile → 'profile'.
    onProfile(e) {
      const { tier, xrTier, budgets, xrBudgets, cached } = e.detail
      output.textContent = [
        `flat tier: ${tier}  (${cached ? 'cached' : 'measured'})`,
        JSON.stringify(budgets, null, 2),
        ``,
        `xr tier: ${xrTier}  (what a headset scene reads)`,
        JSON.stringify(xrBudgets, null, 2),
      ].join('\n')
    },
  }),
  output
)
```

## How it works

On connect it times a short battery of real GPU/CPU work on a hidden canvas,
classifies the device into a quality tier + concrete budgets (via the pure
[perf-probe](?perf-probe.ts) core), and caches the result in `localStorage`. That
drops detail on a Quest-class device without user-agent voodoo.

It **skips the benchmark** and returns the cached budgets instantly when a recent
result exists for this device + probe version (see `perf-probe`'s re-run rules; TTL
is 30 days). A cached result — even a stale one — is dispatched immediately so
consumers never wait; a fresh measurement follows if a re-run is due.

The probe measures the FLAT pipeline (you can't open an immersive session without a
gesture); the XR tier is derived by biasing down one notch for stereo fill. This is
the *starting* tier — pair it with a runtime FPS-driven loop to handle thermal
throttling.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-probe/

---

# perf-probe

Pure, Babylon-free core for the device-capability probe (see
[b3d-probe](?b3d-probe.ts) for the component that actually runs the benchmark).

The philosophy is **measure, don't guess**: rather than sniffing user-agents, the
probe times a small battery of real GPU/CPU work, maps the raw milliseconds to a
quality *tier* and concrete *budgets* (terrain detail, shadow map size, render
scaling…), and caches the result in `localStorage`. This module owns everything
that doesn't touch the GPU — the classifier, the budget table, the storage schema,
the device signature, and the "should I re-run?" decision — so it's all unit
testable without a canvas (feed it synthetic numbers, assert the tier).

Re-run only when the benchmark itself changed (`PROBE_VERSION`), the device changed
(`signature`), or the cache is stale (`DEFAULT_TTL_MS`, 30 days — devices don't get
faster; the TTL is just a backstop for browser/driver updates and a bad cold read).

## Example

The pure classifier. [b3d-probe](?b3d-probe.ts) runs the benchmark and stores the result; this core
just turns measurements into a tier and its budgets:

```javascript
import { classify, budgetsForTier } from 'tosijs-3d'

// milliseconds from the four benchmark passes → 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'
const tier = classify({ fillMs: 4, vertexMs: 3, drawCallMs: 2, cpuMs: 5 })
const flat = budgetsForTier(tier)     // what a flat scene resolves `auto` against
const xr = budgetsForTier(tier, true) // the same tier, scaled down for stereo
console.log(tier, flat.shadowTextureSize, xr.hardwareScaling)
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/perf-probe/

---

# b3d-quality

The **system quality proxy** — the single place that vends device-appropriate
defaults. The [probe](?b3d-probe.ts) measures the device and feeds a
[`PerfProfile`](?perf-probe.ts) in here; components then resolve any attribute left
at its `auto` sentinel against the current budgets. A global override (`setQuality`)
lets a settings menu force a tier.

This module is deliberately DOM-free (plain state + an observer list, no tosijs
import) so all of its logic is unit-testable headless — the pure-module ethos the
rest of the framework follows.

## The `auto` default convention

Components declare performance-sensitive attributes with an **`auto` sentinel**
(`0` for numbers) instead of a hard-wired number, and resolve them here:

```typescript
// in a component's setup:
const subs = resolveBudget(this.hiResSubdivisions, 'hiResSubdivisions', { xr })
//           explicit author value wins; 0 (auto) → the tier's budget
```

So an author who sets a value gets exactly that; everything left unset adapts to
the measured device. **This is the pattern to reach for wherever you find a
hard-wired default that affects performance** (terrain detail, shadow map size,
reflection resolution, render scaling…): make the default `auto` and resolve it,
rather than baking one number that's wrong for both a phone and a workstation.

## Global override

```javascript
import { setQuality, getQuality } from 'tosijs-3d'

setQuality('low')            // force low everywhere
setQuality('auto')           // back to the measured profile (default)
// a settings <select> calls setQuality(e.target.value) and reads getQuality()
```

## Budgets that are sized once: `headsetDevice()`

A scene is built flat, before any session starts, so a budget that is read
once at build (terrain detail, a pool size, a shadow map) is resolved for the
flat tier and then drawn twice in stereo. On a standalone headset that is the
wrong tier for the whole session. For those, pass `headsetDevice()` as `xr`:

```javascript
import { resolveBudget, headsetDevice } from 'tosijs-3d'

const subs = resolveBudget(this.subdivisions, 'hiResSubdivisions', {
  xr: headsetDevice(),
})
```

It is true on a standalone headset (a Quest), false on a PC driving one. A
budget re-read every frame does not need it: pass the live `xr` state there.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-quality/

---

# Cost sweep

Where a frame goes, **measured on the device it runs on**. The sweep switches
one thing off at a time (a group of meshes, the render targets, the shadows),
or turns a resolution lever (hardware scaling flat; in a headset it puts the
viewport scale and the foveation back to full, so the row is what each is
saving), holds it for a couple of seconds, and records the frame
time. What comes back is a ranked list: the things whose absence bought the
most.

It exists because a headset has no GPU timer and no profiler, and guesses about
its fill cost made on a desktop are wrong in both directions. It is a button in
the Perf Stats panel (**Cost sweep**), so it runs inside the session.

```javascript
const rows = await document.querySelector('tosi-b3d').costSweep()
// [{ name: 'baseline', ms: 71.4, p95: 83.3, saved: 0 }, { name: '- water', ms: 55.6, saved: 15.8 }, …]
```

## Reading it

- **`ms`** is the median interval between frames; **`saved`** is the baseline
  minus that.
- **A headset's frame time moves in steps.** The compositor shows a frame on a
  refresh or the one after, so at 72 Hz the readings are 13.9, 27.8, 41.7,
  55.6 ms and so on. A saving smaller than a step can read as zero, and two
  small savings can add up to a step that neither shows alone.
- **`- everything`** is the floor: what the session costs with nothing drawn.
  If it is close to the baseline, the scene is not the problem.
- **`baseline again`** is the first measurement repeated at the end. If it
  differs from the first, the device drifted during the sweep (heat, a
  background task) and the rows are that much in doubt: run it again.
- Groups are meshes sharing a material, named after it. The sweep takes the
  twelve that could cover most of the view and lumps the rest as `other`.

Each experiment is restored before the next. A sweep changes nothing for good.

**Shader sweep**, the button beside it, measures the ground shader's other
forms (`costSweep(2, 'shaders')`). It is separate because each row recompiles
every ground and decoration shader twice, which is the heaviest thing either
sweep does.

## If it hangs the device

A sweep can hang a headset. So it writes what it has measured, and the
name of the experiment it is about to start, to `localStorage` before each
one, once as it switches the experiment on and once as it starts measuring.
Reload the page and Perf Stats shows the rows it got and **STOPPED** with the
experiment that never finished. Runs are numbered and the last four are kept:
a run that hangs at once does not replace the rows of the one before it. The two headset levers run last for that
reason: they are the part no emulator can exercise.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/cost-sweep/

---

# Draw order

Babylon draws opaque meshes in the order they were created. Nothing looks wrong
that way, because the depth buffer sorts out who is in front, but every pixel
of a far thing is shaded before a near thing covers it. A sky made first is
shaded across the whole view and then painted over by the land.

`<tosi-b3d>` draws opaque meshes **nearest first, and the sky last**, so a
covered pixel is rejected by depth before its shader runs. The picture is the
same; the saving is whatever was hidden. On a phone or headset GPU that is a
large part of a frame, and on a desktop tile renderer it is close to nothing.

Blended meshes are untouched: they are still drawn after the opaque ones, far
to near.

To put Babylon's own order back (by material), call
`scene.setRenderingOrder(0)` after the scene is ready. A sky of your own that
is pinned to the camera must set `infiniteDistance`, or it sorts as the
nearest thing and is drawn first.

```javascript
import { nearFirst } from 'tosijs-3d'
// A render target of your own does not inherit the scene's order.
target.setRenderingOrder(0, nearFirst(scene), nearFirst(scene))
```

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/draw-order/

---

# debug-sink

Somewhere for a page to send what it would otherwise print: a headset has no
console, so its readings have to go somewhere you can read them afterwards.

Off until a URL is set. With one, `sendDebug(tag, event)` posts a line of JSON
to it, and `<tosi-b3d>` reports the things that are worth having afterwards:
every step of a cost sweep, the Perf Stats lines while that popup is open, a
lost WebGL context, any event passed to `logDebug`, and every uncaught error
or promise rejection on the page, with its stack.

```javascript
import { debugSink } from 'tosijs-3d'

debugSink.url = '/__debug-sink'
```

`/__debug-sink` is the endpoint a tosijs-ui dev server opens when its site
config has `debugSink: true`: it appends each post as one line of a file
outside the project, and prints that file's path at startup. Any endpoint that
accepts a POST works.

Sent with `navigator.sendBeacon`, which does not wait for an answer and still
goes out when the page is about to die. That is the case it is for: the last
line before a hang is the one you want.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/debug-sink/

# clock

**Game code does not read the wall clock.** Time in a simulation comes from
the simulation: `sceneDelta(scene)` for a frame's step and `sceneSeconds(scene)`
for animation, both of which stop when the world is paused, slow with its
`timeScale`, and run the same way in a test or a replay. Code that reads the
system clock instead keeps going through a pause, ignores the time scale, and
behaves differently every run.

This module is the ONE place the system clock may be read, so every use is a
named call a review can find (`clock.test.ts` fails on a read anywhere else).
What is left to it is time that really is real:

- `realNow()`: monotonic milliseconds, for measuring how long work took
  (profiling, budgets), spacing out work that is not part of the world
  (debounces, retries), and UI that must move in a pause menu
- `wallMs()` / `wallDate()`: the calendar, for timestamps on logs, files and
  caches

If you are about to call one of these from something that lives in the world
(a projectile, an animation, an AI's patience), you want the scene's clock.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/clock/

---

# undo history

A list of states and a place in it: the one undo model behind the character
builder and the rig tool. A tool records its whole state after each change that
settles (a slider drag ends, a marker is dropped, a grip is placed); undo and
redo step back and forth through what was recorded, and recording after an undo
drops the steps that were undone, as every editor does.

States are snapshots, not commands. A tool that can already save itself (a
character, a rig recipe) can therefore undo with no more code than saving takes,
and nothing has to describe how each change is reversed.

```javascript
import { undoHistory } from 'tosijs-3d'

const history = undoHistory({ limit: 100 })
history.record(state())           // the state it opened in
// … after each change settles:
history.record(state())
// Undo:
const before = history.undo()
if (before) restore(before)
```

`record` ignores a state equal to the current one (compared as JSON unless you
pass `same`), so a tool may record whenever something might have changed, and
restoring a state and then recording it does nothing. Past `limit` the oldest
steps are forgotten.

Pure: no DOM, no Babylon.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/undo-history/

# Migration

What to change when upgrading. Only breaking changes are listed — everything
else is additive. The full detail for each is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://3d.tosijs.net/CHANGELOG/).

This file ships **inside the package**, because a migration table you can only
read on GitHub does not exist for someone who has already installed the thing
and is staring at an error.

## 0.12.x → 0.13.0

The peer ranges are unchanged. Four things change under you:

1. **`riggedBodyGlb` no longer recolours garment pictures by default.** Its
   `bake` option is now the baker itself: pass `bake: bakeClothLook` (from
   `tosijs-3d/cloth-bake`) to keep the baked look. Without it the pictures
   are written as they are, and it warns once. `bake: false` still means no
   bake; `bake: true` no longer means anything. `exportBody` passes the baker
   for you.
2. **The settings panel's Slow motion button is gone.** Set `timeScale` on
   the `<tosi-b3d>` from your own control if you want one.
3. **`barMenu` submenus cascade** beside the list, all on one surface,
   instead of replacing it with a way back. A press opens one; a press on its
   row again closes it.
4. **`viewMenu` leaves the system bar during a headset session**, since in VR
   the camera is your head. It comes back when the session ends.

## 0.11.x → 0.12.0

The peer ranges are unchanged. Four things change under you:

1. **`<tosi-b3d-car>` is rebuilt on the vehicle model.** `turnRate` and
   `friction` are gone (setting either now warns once and does nothing): use
   `steerDeg` (degrees of full lock) and `grip` (a tyre friction coefficient).
   `acceleration` and `braking` are now m/s². The default mapping is GTA V's:
   the right trigger drives, the left brakes and reverses, the left stick
   steers.
2. **Models are no longer drawn mirrored.** Everything loaded through
   `canonicalize` or a `<tosi-b3d-library>` (vehicles, aircraft, lamp
   fixtures, library instances) now looks as authored, where 0.11 drew each as
   its mirror image. An asymmetric model now faces the other way from before;
   anything you measured or placed against the mirrored picture (a marker's
   side, a kit's road turns) needs checking. Skinned models are unchanged.
3. **`KENNEY_CITY`'s road turns changed** with that: `bend` is `turns: 0`
   (it joins north and east) and `end` is `turns: 3` (it opens west). A kit
   manifest of your own measured against 0.11's picture needs the same check.
4. **`RiggedBody.surfaces[].material` is typed `SurfaceMaterial`** (a name),
   not Babylon's `Material`, so the character core carries no engine in its
   types. On the Babylon side, cast it back: `surface.material as
   BABYLON.Material`.

## 0.10.x → 0.11.0

Nothing was removed, and the peer ranges are unchanged. 0.11 collects the
0.10.x line's new features (retargeting, auto-rig, spring bones, effects, the
rig and effect tools); see [0.11.0](/v0.11.0/)'s summary. A few behaviours
changed that you may see without touching your code:

1. **Retargeting no longer lines up the body's axis.** The hips, spine, chest,
   neck and head now take the clip's turn as it is; only limbs are lined up
   with the source's rest pose. A character whose neck or torso leans at rest
   (a weasel's neck forward to its snout) keeps that lean in every clip
   instead of being pulled upright, which tipped its head back by about 14°.
   Nothing to do, unless you had corrected for the old tilt in your own code.
2. **A biped sprints.** Near full speed it plays the rig's `sprint` state
   (UAL's `Sprint_Loop`, already in `ualAnimationStates()`) instead of the
   jog sped up. A rig with no sprint clip jogs as before. To keep the jog,
   leave `sprint` out of your animation states.
3. **Effects release their shared parts with the last player.** The per-scene
   driver observer, pooled lights and sprite textures go when a scene's last
   `EffectPlayer` is disposed, and are made again by the next effect. Code that
   held on to a sprite texture from `effectSprite()` past that point holds a
   disposed texture.
4. **`InspectStage.light` can be null** (new in 0.10.19): `inspectStage(scene,
   { light: false })` adds no key light, for a scene with a sun of its own.

## 0.9.0 → 0.10.0

### 1. The deprecated callback names are gone: `onX` → `handleX`

**What changed.** The `onX` callback options were deprecated in 0.8.0 and kept
working, with a warning, through 0.9.x. They are removed. An `onX` option is
no longer called.

**Who is affected.** Anyone who saw the console warning
"`onChange` is deprecated — use `handleChange`" and has not renamed yet.

**How you will notice.** TypeScript reports the old name as an unknown
property. At runtime the callback does not fire, and the console says so once
per name: "`onChange` was removed in 0.10 and is IGNORED — use `handleChange`".
Demo code in doc comments and plain JavaScript is not type-checked, so search
for the names rather than relying on the compiler.

**What to do.** Rename. Every pair:

| where | removed | use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toggle3d` `slider3d` `select3d` `color3d` `vector3d` `euler3d` `angle3d` `arc3d` `picker3d` `curve3d` `footprint3d` `themeEditor` `terrainEditor3d` | `onChange` | `handleChange` |
| `button3d`, menu actions, `addDebugSource` actions | `onClick` | `handleClick` |
| `list3d`, `surface` `MenuItem`, `table` | `onSelect` | `handleSelect` |
| `table`, `box` `button` / `BoxChild` | `onActivate` | `handleActivate` |
| `showPopup` / `openPopup` / `openMenu3d` / `surface.openPanel` | `onClose` | `handleClose` |
| `inputField` | `onChange` / `onEnter` / `onFocus` | `handleChange` / `handleEnter` / `handleFocus` |
| `keyboard` | `onKey` / `onAction` / `onCaretMove` | `handleKey` / `handleAction` / `handleCaretMove` |
| `curve3d` / `footprint3d` result (`field.onChange = …`) | `onChange` | `handleChange` |

Components take `when*`:

| component | removed | use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<tosi-b3d-trigger>` | `onEnter` / `onExit` properties | `whenEnter` / `whenExit` |
| `<tosi-b3d-manipulator>` | `handleChange` / `handleCommit` | `whenChange` / `whenCommit` |

`b3dTrigger({ onEnter })` through the element creator is unchanged: it was
never the property, it is a listener for the `'enter'` event and receives an
`Event`.

`handlerOf(config, 'handleX', 'onX')` keeps its signature. It now returns only
`handleX`, and warns once if it finds a function under the old name.

### 2. `generateGalaxy` and `galaxy.getStarSPS()` are removed

`generateGalaxy(seed, count, options)` was an adapter over the voxel galaxy.
Call that directly:

```javascript
// before
const galaxy = generateGalaxy(1234, 10000, options)
// after
const galaxy = voxelGalaxy({
  seed: 1234,
  brightBudget: 10000,
  dimBudget: 0,
  galaxyOptions: options,
}).view({ generatePlanets: options.generatePlanets === true })
```

The result is identical. `getStarSPS()` on `<tosi-b3d-galaxy>` returned `null`
since the stars moved to a vertex shader; use `galaxy.pickStar(x, y)`.

### 3. `new MersenneTwister()` needs a seed

It used to seed from `Date.now()` when you left the argument out. It now
throws. Pass a seed, or `new MersenneTwister(Date.now())` if you want a
different sequence each run. (`PRNG` always required one.)

### 4. `WorldStore` queries return copies

`getState()`, `getEntity()` and `query()` used to return the store's live
objects, so writing to a result changed the simulation. They return copies
now. If you were moving something by writing to a query result, call the
command for it. Engine-side code that needs the live state every frame reads
`store.liveState` and must not write to it. A store passed to the conformance
kit must also implement `chooseOption(choiceId, optionId)`.

### 5. Some defaults changed: a scene can look different

Nothing to rename, but four things change what you see without a line of
yours changing. The changelog's **Changed defaults** block has all of them.

- **Decoration layouts differ again.** Plants thin out in drier country, things
  gather into clumps more strongly, and a low-tier device (a Quest in a
  session) places 60% of the budget as fewer clumps. `budgetScale: 1` places
  the whole budget; `clump: 0.85` on the decorator is the old gathering.
- **Opaque meshes are drawn nearest first.** Same picture for ordinary meshes.
  `scene.setRenderingOrder(0)` puts Babylon's order back; a camera-pinned sky
  of your own needs `infiniteDistance`.
- **A headset on the low tier renders at reduced scale with foveation.**
  `xrRenderScale: 1` and `xrFoveation: 0` are full resolution.
- **Water receives sun and cloud shadows.**

## 0.8.15 → 0.9.0

### 1. `biomeTemperature` is in degrees now: 0 is 0 °C, 1 is 50 °C

**What changed.** `<tosi-b3d-terrain biomeTemperature>` used to be the biome
chart's own axis: `0…1`, cold to warm, with `-1` meaning "use the default".
It is now a temperature: `0` is 0 °C and each unit is 50 °C, so `-1` is
-50 °C, and the value is not limited to any range. The default is `0.45`
(22.5 °C), which is the same climate as before.

**Who is affected.** Anyone who sets `biomeTemperature`. An old value is read
on the new scale and comes out much warmer: `0.3` used to be about -4 °C and
is now 15 °C. `-1` used to mean the default and is now -50 °C.

**What to do.** Convert each value: `new = (old - 0.36) / 0.8`. Replace `-1`
with `0.45`, or delete the attribute.

| Old | New | Climate |
|-----|-----|---------|
| `-1` (auto) | `0.45` | 22.5 °C |
| `1` | `0.8` | 40 °C |
| `0.72` | `0.45` | 22.5 °C |
| `0.36` | `0` | 0 °C |
| `0` | `-0.45` | -22.5 °C |

`chartTemperature` and `planetTemperature` (from `biome-chart`) do the
conversion in code. Only this attribute moved. `BiomePlugin.params`, the
province climate curves and the decorator's rule bands are still in chart
units.

### 2. Nothing else is removed, including what was promised

The deprecated `onX` callback names (and the other names announced as
"removed in 0.9") still work in 0.9.x and warn once. They are removed in
0.10. Rename when convenient.

## 0.8.14 → 0.8.15

**Nothing breaks at compile time. Three defaults change what you see.**

### 1. The decorator's default library is Quaternius', not Kenney's

**What changed.** `<tosi-b3d-decorator>` with no `url` loads
`quaternius/libraries/nature.glb` and uses `NATURE_RULES`. It used to load
Kenney's Nature Kit and use `NATURE_KIT_RULES`.

**Who is affected.**
- You set no `url` and no `rules`: you get the new trees. Nothing to do unless
  you want the old ones.
- You set custom `rules` that use Kenney's model names (`tree_oak`,
  `rock_largeA`) and no `url`: none of those names exist in the new library.
  The decorator now warns in the console and places nothing for them.
- You self-host only the Kenney kit: the default URL is a file you do not have.

**What to do.** To stay on Kenney's kit, name it:

```javascript
b3dDecorator({ url: assetUrl('kenney/libraries/nature-kit.glb') })
```

With a `url` set and no `rules`, the decorator uses `NATURE_KIT_RULES`.

### 2. Layouts are different, and things clump

**What changed.** Every scatter rule now gathers into clumps by default, the
candidate grid changed, and the budget became a ceiling (a small radius or a
mostly-sea map places fewer than the budget). The same seed gives a different
layout than 0.8.14 did. `NATURE_KIT_RULES`' rocks are now procedural
(`rock:boulder:1` …) at a different scale, and no rocks are placed on a
volcanic province.

**Who is affected.** Anyone who stored placements, compared them in a test, or
tuned a scene around where things stood.

**What to do.** There is no switch that restores 0.8.14's exact layout. For an
even spread again, set `clump="0"` on the element (or `clump: 0` on a rule).

### 3. Water reflections follow the device tier

**What changed.** `<tosi-b3d-water>`'s `textureSize` defaults to auto (1024,
512 or 256 by device tier; it was 1024 everywhere) and a new
`reflectionRefresh` redraws the reflection every frame, every second or every
third by tier on a flat screen.

**What to do.** Top-tier devices see no change. To keep the old behaviour on
every device:

```javascript
b3dWater({ textureSize: 1024, reflectionRefresh: 1 })
```

## 0.8.0 → 0.8.1

**Nothing breaks at compile time, and one behaviour changes.** The
`activationVeto` signature grew a second parameter and it is OPTIONAL — a
required one would have been a hard TypeScript break for every caller, and the
default is chosen so that a veto reading it gets a conservative answer rather
than a permissive one.

### 1. Aircraft guns are direct-hit, not area-effect

**What changed.** `<tosi-b3d-aircraft>`'s cannon damages the thing its shell
passes through. It used to detonate a small AOE warhead at the impact point.

**Why.** Blast damage resolves by distance to a destroyable's registered point —
one point, at the model's origin. Scale a fighter up and its wing sits outside
the blast, so point-blank fire does nothing, silently. Direct-hit damage has no
length scale in it, so it cannot break that way. Reported by an adopter who hit
it by making their world four times larger (#23).

**If you relied on the old behaviour**, say so explicitly:

<!--
`xml`, NOT `html` — the doc system RUNS a ```html fence as a live example, and
this one is illustrative markup in a reference document with no scene to mount
into. `xml` highlights the same and stays inert. See `doc-examples.test.ts`,
which now fails on any live-language fence in a published markdown file.
-->

```xml
<tosi-b3d-aircraft
  gun-mode="blast"
  gun-blast-radius="1.5"
  gun-full-radius="0.5"
></tosi-b3d-aircraft>
```

Both radii are attributes now; they used to be hardcoded. Missiles and bombs are
unchanged — AOE is right for those.

### 2. `activationVeto`'s second parameter (optional)

`blocks(info)` now receives a description of the activation — who, how, how far.
A veto that ignores its argument is unaffected, which is every veto written
before this existed:

```javascript
use.vetoes.push({ name: 'locked', blocks: () => !hasKey }) // unchanged
```

Calling `activationVeto(vetoes)` directly still compiles. When you omit the
info, vetoes are told `distance: Infinity` — "we do not know that you are near"
— so a **reach veto refuses** rather than waving the activation through. If you
call it yourself and want a reach veto to pass, supply the distance:

```javascript
activationVeto(vetoes, { source: 'near', distance: 0.4 })
```

### 3. `select3d` no longer draws ‹ › stepper arrows

Tapping the control opens a popup list, which it already did — the arrows were
a second way to do the same thing and made the popup undiscoverable. Nothing to
change; the control is the same size and the same tap.

## 0.7.8 → 0.8.0

**Nothing breaks at runtime.** Both items below keep working in 0.8.x; one is an
install-time floor, the other is a deprecation with a removal date.

### 1. Peer floor: `tosijs` `^1.7.8` → `^1.9.2`

Upgrade `tosijs` alongside this. npm will refuse to install otherwise
(`ERESOLVE`); bun and pnpm warn and proceed, which is the case worth reading on.

One behaviour changed with it, and it is silent. A wrong-typed write to an
`initAttributes` prop used to be **discarded**; since tosijs 1.9 it **warns and
applies the value as given**. So on an `'on' | 'off'` attribute, `foo: false`
used to mean `'on'` and now genuinely sets `false` — anything comparing against
the string breaks instead of quietly defaulting.

Use **`isOff()`** from `tosijs-3d`, which accepts `'off'`, `false` and
`'false'`, rather than comparing to a string yourself.

### 2. Callback options: `onX` → `handleX`

Every callback option in the library now takes `handleX`. The old `onX` spelling
kept working through 0.9.x, warning **once per name**, and was **removed in
0.10** (see the top of this file).

| widget                                   | old                                  | new                                              |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `inputField`                             | `onChange` / `onEnter` / `onFocus`   | `handleChange` / `handleEnter` / `handleFocus`   |
| `keyboard`                               | `onKey` / `onAction` / `onCaretMove` | `handleKey` / `handleAction` / `handleCaretMove` |
| `table`                                  | `onSelect` / `onActivate`            | `handleSelect` / `handleActivate`                |
| `box` `button` / `BoxChild`              | `onActivate`                         | `handleActivate`                                 |
| `surface` `MenuItem`                     | `onSelect`                           | `handleSelect`                                   |
| `showPopup` / `openPopup` / `openMenu3d` | `onClose`                            | `handleClose`                                    |
| `addDebugSource` actions                 | `onClick`                            | `handleClick`                                    |
| `themeEditor`                            | `onChange`                           | `handleChange`                                   |

**Why, in one sentence:** these are plain factories today, but the moment one
becomes a tosijs component the element creator binds an `on*` prop as a DOM
event **listener**, so the callback is never called and nothing errors — which
is not hypothetical, it shipped three times in this codebase.

**Components use `when*`, not `handleX`** — `b3d-trigger` gains
`whenEnter`/`whenExit` (`onEnter`/`onExit` still work). Passing `onEnter` to the
element creator never set the field at all; it added a listener for the `'enter'`
CustomEvent, so your callback received an `Event` instead of the trigger.

If you write your own widgets, `handlerOf(config, 'handleX', 'onX')` is exported
so you can follow the same rule.

## 0.6.2 → 0.7.0

> # ⚠️ READ THIS FIRST: library rotation
>
> **If you place library models with `rx`/`ry`/`rz`, your scenes will MOVE.**
>
> Everything else in this release either errors or looks obviously wrong. This
> one changes a scene that previously looked **correct**, which is why it is at
> the top instead of in the table.
>
> Two things happened to the same option at once:
>
> 1. It **never worked** on the default path. `instantiate()` wrote
>    `result.rotation`, but Babylon's glTF loader always assigns a
>    `rotationQuaternion`, and a `TransformNode` ignores `.rotation` while one is
>    present. Measured on a real model: `ry: 0`, `ry: 140` and `ry: -90` all
>    produced **bit-identical** orientations — you got the GLB's own baked
>    rotation whatever you asked for. Position worked, which is exactly what made
>    it look wired up.
> 2. It is now **degrees**, not radians.
>
> So a value that did nothing now does something, in a unit that also changed.
>
> **What to do:**
>
> - **If you passed rotation and it appeared to work** — it was not your value
>   doing it. Something else was: baked rotation in the model, a parent
>   transform, or a compensating tweak downstream. That compensation is now
>   **doubled up**. Look at every placement before assuming a regression.
> - **If you passed rotation and gave up because it did nothing** — it works now.
>   Your values are in radians; multiply by `180 / Math.PI`.
> - **If you never passed rotation** — nothing changes. `canonical: true` was
>   unaffected throughout.
>
> Quickest way to tell: search for `instantiate(` and `make.` with an `r[xyz]`
> key. If there are none, skip this entirely.

> ## ⚠️ AND THIS: models placed away from the origin in their file
>
> **If a `.glb` has its object sitting somewhere other than (0,0,0) in the source
> scene, `canonicalize` now discards that placement** — as its contract always
> claimed it did. It previously zeroed only the glTF loader's `__root__`
> wrapper, leaving the authored object's scene transform intact.
>
> **The tell is a vehicle that pivots or collides oddly**, because the control
> node used to sit a fixed distance from the model it steers (1.7 m for our own
> scout). A `_centerOfGravity` marker measured against that node folded the
> offset into the pivot, so a marker authored **correctly on the centreline**
> produced a pivot 1.75 m out, while a hand-tuned offset came out right. Ours
> was re-exported to the documented convention and immediately began crashing on
> every bank.
>
> **What to do:** author in the model's LOCAL frame and delete compensating
> offsets. Before treating a changed vehicle as a regression, check whether a
> marker or placement was tuned against the old behaviour. **Models authored at
> the origin — the common case — are unaffected.**

| What                                            | Before                                               | After                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `landform.gulley` / `landform.cover` `heading`  | radians                                              | **degrees** — `heading * 180 / Math.PI`                                                                                                                   |
| `library.instantiate()` / `lib.make.*` rotation | radians **and silently ignored** — see the box above | **degrees, and actually applied**                                                                                                                         |
| `b3d-aircraft` chase HUD                        | `hudChase: true` / `hudChase: false`                 | delete it (now default) / `hudChaseOff: true`                                                                                                             |
| Right stick                                     | aux roll                                             | **camera**. `strafe` still sums into roll, so a custom mapping can restore a roll axis                                                                    |
| Glass gamepad                                   | always visible                                       | **auto-hides** once a keyboard or hardware gamepad is used. `fade="off"` pins it                                                                          |
| `carve` exports                                 | 13 bare names (`sphere`, `tube`, …)                  | the **`carve.*` namespace** (`carve.sphere`, `carve.tube`)                                                                                                |
| `b3dPatch` / `B3dPatch`                         | experimental element                                 | **removed** — the pure modules it used (`carve.*`, `sdf-lattice`, `patch-field`) are kept                                                                 |
| `library.getNames()`                            | raw node names                                       | **public names** — `.model`, behaviour suffixes and the glTF loader's `_primitiveN` removed, so `building_collideCylinder_primitive0` lists as `building` |
| Model scene transform                           | kept on the content node under `__root__`            | **dropped** — see the box above; affects models not authored at the origin                                                                                |
| `spawnProjectile` / `spawnMissile` impact       | `onImpact(point)`                                    | `whenImpact({ point, normal, mesh })`. The old name still fires, with a one-shot warning                                                                  |

### The two that fail SILENTLY

Most of the above errors, or is obvious the first time you look. These two do
not, so check them by hand:

- **Angles.** A bare number is valid in either unit, so a value meant as radians
  now produces a different orientation rather than an error.
- **`hudChase`.** tosijs props end in an index signature, so a stale `hudChase`
  **compiles and is silently ignored**. Nothing will tell you.

### A note on library rotation

See the box at the top of this section. It is the one change here that can move a
scene which previously looked correct, so it is not buried down here.

### Prerelease users

If you pinned `0.7.0-rc.1` or any `0.7.0-beta.*`, move to `0.7.0`. The
prerelease channel was inverted — `rc.1` was published before `beta.1…6`, and
semver sorts beta below rc, so `@next` resolved _backwards_ to the older build.
`0.7.0` sorts above all of them.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/Migration/

# Changelog

All notable changes to **tosijs-3d**, one page per version: each lives in
`changelog/v<version>.md` (on the site at `/v<version>/`), and this page is the
index: the latest release below, then every version, newest first (that list is
generated from each page's `parent`). This project is pre-1.0 (`0.x`), so minor
versions may carry breaking peer-dependency changes. Each is called out in a
**⚠️ Breaking** block on its version's page, with what a consumer must do.
Upgrading across a minor? Start with [Migration](/Migration/).

## Unreleased

## 0.13.1

The latest release. Retargeted legs that hold still and walk cleanly, a foot-turn dial for splay-footed bodies, fingertip handles in the rig tool, and a character builder whose rig panel follows the bar's menus. See [0.13.1](/v0.13.1/).

# 0.13.1

Retargeted legs that hold still and walk cleanly, a foot-turn dial for splay-footed bodies, fingertip handles in the rig tool, and a character builder whose rig panel follows the bar's menus.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1708.6 KB raw / 594.3 KB gz, up 1.0 KB / 0.3 KB gz (+0.06%) on 0.13.0.

### Added

- `footTurnDeg` in a rig recipe (the rig tool's **foot turn** slider, under Motion): both feet turn in (negative) or out (positive) in every clip, for a body modelled with its feet turned out. Retargeting, `bakeClip`, `retargetClip` / `retargetSourceClip`, the biped, the builder and exports all pass it.
- Rig tool fingertips (orange, with `move joints` on): dragging one turns and stretches its whole finger or thumb about the finger's first joint, keeping the curl, its mirror following with symmetry on.

### Changed

- Foot IK sets only a grounded foot's HEIGHT; its place across the floor is the clip's. Pulling it to where the source's foot was dragged a body that stands wider than UAL's mannequin (MakeHuman, by 8 cm) toward the mannequin's stance and hitched every step of a walk. Crouches still plant.
- In the character builder, the Rig panel has no animate, clip or View rows: the Animation menu plays and picks the clip on the rig, and the View menu has **Mannequin** and **Bones** as checked items while rigging. `mountRigTool`'s `hostMenus` option does this for any host, which drives it through the new `api.clip`, `api.mannequin` and `api.bones`; `viewMenu` takes `items` for extra rows.
- The builder opens meshes from one place, the Character menu's **Open mesh…** (into the rig tool while rigging; otherwise a GLB is the body and an OBJ opens the rig tool). With `hostMenus` the rig tool drops its Model section, and **use its own skeleton** comes first. Its Motion section (offsets and spacing: floor, arm space, foot turn) wears the move icon, Springs the link icon.

### Fixed

- A retargeted leg that is nearly straight no longer twitches (MakeHuman's right thigh in UAL's idle). Foot IK bends a straight leg's knee toward the leg's front instead of the way a knee a few millimetres off the line happens to point.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.13.1/

# 0.13.0

Biped gunplay that aims where you look, crowds you can move figure by figure, cascading system-bar menus that work flat and in a headset (the character builder's Animation menu among them), and a round of headset fixes: panels that keep their place under the bar, presses from either hand, a chase camera that keeps its seat. Garment exports bake their cloth look only when given the baker.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1707.6 KB raw / 594.0 KB gz, up 9.2 KB / 3.0 KB gz (+0.5%) on 0.12.6.

### ⚠️ Breaking

- `riggedBodyGlb` bakes a garment's cloth look only when given the baker: pass `bake: bakeClothLook` (from `tosijs-3d/cloth-bake`). Without it the pictures are written as they are, and a bundle that imports `tosijs-3d/rigged-body-glb` alone no longer carries an image decoder (about 11 KiB gzip less; the barrel still exports both). It warns once when a garment has a look and no baker. `exportBody` passes it. `bake: false` still means no bake.

See [Migration](/Migration/) for the other changes that need attention (Slow motion removed, cascading `barMenu` submenus, `viewMenu` in a headset).

### Added

- `<tosi-b3d-crowd>`: `setFigure(i, { x, y, z, yaw, clip, speed })` moves, turns or re-clips a figure; changes are uploaded once per frame however many figures moved. `clipNames` lists the clips. The doc page has a demo of walkers crossing a field.
- `aimSpine(chain, held, target)` turns a spine after the clips have posed it so a held item points along an aim.
- `<tosi-b3d-cloud-deck sky-clock="off">`: the deck drifts in world time, not the sky's, so a fast day passes under clouds that move at their own pace. City Drive and Cross Country use it.
- `<tosi-b3d-panel bar-button="off">`: a system panel with no button of its own on the bar, for one something else opens (`el.show()` from a menu entry).

### Changed

- `<tosi-b3d-biped>` holding a weapon in `gunplay` points it along its aim: the spine is turned after the animations. Crouched, the gun used to point about 45° low, and standing 11° low.
- `viewMenu` leaves the system bar during a headset session; in VR the camera is your head.
- A trackpad pinch on an orbit camera zooms three times as far (`PINCH_GAIN`), and pinching works in Safari, which sends gesture events rather than a ctrl-wheel.
- The character builder has an **Animation** menu on the system bar (play/pause and the clip); its **Playback controls** entry opens a small panel for scrubbing and speed. The page is titled **Character Builder**. While rigging, Play goes to the perspective view and Pause back to the face view last held.
- `barMenu` submenus open beside the list (cascading, all on one surface) instead of replacing it with a way back. A submenu opens on a press, and a press on its row again closes it.
- A system panel's button on the system bar stays lit while its panel is open (its HTML button carries `aria-pressed`).
- Nothing is heard before the scene is shown: the effect voices (traffic, street lights, effects) and Babylon's own sounds stay silent until the loading spinner gives way. `holdEffectAudio()` (from `tosijs-3d/effect-audio`) holds them for a page's own reasons.
- The settings panel no longer has a Slow motion button. Set `timeScale` from a page that wants one.

### Fixed

- In a headset, a system panel whose content grows after it opens (the rig tool once a body is rigged, the tailor) grows downward from under the system bar. It used to grow about its centre, up over the bar. `attachFramePanel` takes `keepTop: true` for this.
- A trackpad pinch sent as ctrl-wheel notches (many Windows trackpad drivers) zooms one wheel step a notch; each notch used to move the camera about twenty times as far.
- `<tosi-b3d-launcher>`'s `reloadModel()` no longer disposes the library's materials with the old model: after the first weapon swap, every weapon from that library was drawn white (the Biped Playground's loadout). `<tosi-b3d-crowd>`'s actors had the same fault when removed.
- `<tosi-b3d-hud>`: changing `size` resizes the HUD straight away; it used to wait for the next window resize. Any `handleResize()` call made after setting it can go.
- `<tosi-b3d-sound>` removed while its file loads no longer throws an unhandled rejection ("No volume subnode"); it is disposed once Babylon has finished loading it, and never starts playing.
- Removing a `<tosi-b3d>` no longer warns "WebGL context LOST": the teardown loses the context on purpose. An unexpected loss still warns.
- A skybox with its own `<tosi-b3d-moon>`s takes its night light from the brightest moon above the horizon. A moon that has set no longer lights the ground from below, and with every moon set the night has only ambient light.
- In a headset, a press on the hand that is not pointing now counts on every way into VR (`enterXR` and the biped's own XR camera), not only `<tosi-b3d>`'s.
- A popup whose content changes shape after it opens follows the new shape. It used to be drawn stretched or squashed until it was closed and opened again.
- The tailor: an outline that lies past the outline field (one carried over from another body) is clipped to the field, and its points are drawn at the field's edge so you can drag them back. It used to draw over the panel's buttons.
- In a headset, the system bar follows its panels during the session: a menu that leaves the bar (`viewMenu`) or a panel added late now does so in VR too. It used to keep the buttons it had when you entered.
- A select (or other popup) in a system panel opens on its own surface in front of the panel instead of being cropped inside it.
- The biped's aim reticle and the shadow blob under characters and vehicles are never culled. They used to vanish when the spot where they were created went out of view (in a headset, sometimes from one eye only).
- In a headset, the vehicle chase camera keeps its seat through a brief moment with nothing piloted. It used to take wherever you were looking as forward again, a re-seat you did not ask for.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.13.0/

# 0.12.6

For the character builder and the rig tool: clips from motion capture (BVH) kept in the browser and carried in character files, exports of MakeHuman's body in its clothes, hair, skin, eyes and lashes, a tailor's garment that fits any body, and retargeted feet that stay on the ground. Rigs from markers place the pelvis, neck and the AI cast's knees as UAL's mannequins have them.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1698.6 KB raw / 591.0 KB gz, up 43.5 KB / 17.5 KB gz (+2.6%) on 0.12.5.

### Added

- Rig tool: drag a marker forward or back in a side view to set its joint's depth (the fit puts each at the middle of the body's thickness, and the mannequin's pelvis is well behind it). Kept in the rig recipe as `binding.depths`, an offset per marker from the fit's depth; `fitSkeleton`'s `depths`, `bodyFromMarkers`'s `depths` and `rigFromMarkers`'s sixth argument take it too.
- Rig tool: a **floor** slider (Motion) moves the body up or down from where its soles stand, for one that floats or sinks; kept in the rig recipe as `floor` (metres), and the character builder stands the body the same way. At rest the soles, not the mesh's lowest point, are put on the floor.
- Character builder: exporting MakeHuman's body writes the clothes it wears (MakeHuman's own and garments of your own made on it), fitted as drawn, with their pictures and looks. `character.exportGarments()` gives them for `riggedBodyGlb`'s `garments` on either kind of body; `onSkin` (`garment-proxy`) binds a piece made for MakeHuman's pack to the skin a body draws, and `packGarmentMaterial` gives a pack piece's material as data.
- The export of MakeHuman's body carries its eyelashes, drawn and faded as in the builder, following the head. The fade is a small ramp picture, so it needs no vertex alpha (`shortenLashes`, `lashAlpha`, `lashUvs`, `lashPicture` in `eye-art`).
- The export of MakeHuman's body carries its hair, beard, moustache and brows: Quaternius' pieces placed as the builder places them (scalp hair following the head, tucked under a hat), MakeHuman's own hair and brows bound like clothes, each picture coloured as the builder colours hair (`recolourHair`, `cloth-bake`). A garment may `follow` one joint wholly; `riggedBodyGlb` tucks the skin under clothes only. `readHairLibrary` now gives each part's uvs and material, and `readHairMaterials` the library's pictures.
- The export of MakeHuman's body carries its skin (its tone as the material, lips and stubble as vertex colours: `skinSurface`, `skin-paint`) and its eyes with Tonio's eye art in its iris colour (`riggedBodyGlb`'s `eyeTexture`, laid on by `gltfEyeUvs`). `character.exportCharacter()` gives the body, garments and eye picture together.
- Export (rig tool, character builder): **animation** puts the clip playing in the GLB, retargeted onto the skeleton as written, whether it is UAL's, a GLB of your own or a BVH capture. A host passes it as `clip` on the export target (`ExportClip`: the file and the clip's name); `exportClip` reads one into `riggedBodyGlb`'s `clips`.
- A character file carries the clip it plays when that is one of your own (`clips`: the BVH or GLB file, by name), so it plays on a page that has never seen the file; the builder reads and keeps it on load. `characterStore` keeps the bytes once, as it does garments.
- A garment's look goes out in its picture: `riggedBodyGlb` writes a recoloured cloth's texture recoloured, so any engine shows what the builder does (`bake: false` keeps the pictures as they came). `bakeClothLook(picture, look)` (`cloth-bake`) is the step on its own.
- `jpegDecode` and `decodeImage` (`tosijs-3d/jpeg`): JPEGs read with no engine or canvas (baseline and progressive, grey or colour, any chroma subsampling), as `pngDecode`'s `RgbaImage`; `decodeImage` reads either. `pngDecode` now reads grey PNGs too.
- Character builder: **clips from a file…** takes BVH motion captures as well as GLBs, and keeps them in this browser (`clipStore`, IndexedDB `tosijs-clips`), so they come back next visit; **forget** drops one. `retargetSourceClip` plays a clip held as data (a BVH, or a GLB read with `readGlbClips`) on a loaded skeleton, as `retargetClip` does a loaded one.
- `readBvh` and `writeBvh` (`tosijs-3d/bvh`): BVH motion capture files read as clips (any skeleton, any Euler order, units guessed or given) that `bakeClip` and `retargetClip` play on any body, and any clip written out as BVH.
- A tailor's garment fits any body (`tailor-recipe`): a cut records the joints of the body it was drawn on (`TailorCut.on`), and `recutGarment(body, cut)` makes it on another rigged body, its outlines carried by the joints so a hem drawn at the knee stays at the knee. In the tailor, outlines now follow the body when it is reshaped. `fitCut`, `warpOutline`, `outlineLandmarks` and `tailorBody` are the parts.
- `heldParts(joints, held, bases)` (`tosijs-3d/rigged-body-glb`): a held item for any skeleton at rest, as `riggedBodyGlb` writes one: the socket joint under the hand (local transform and inverse bind), and the item's mesh skinned to it with its materials and pictures. For a GLB writer whose skeleton `riggedBodyGlb` did not make; `riggedBodyGlb` now uses the same code.
- `loftGarment` (`body-sweep`): a garment lofted along a chain of bones, as rings round the hull of the body's slice plus thickness and an `ease` curve, with mitred or rounded (`steps`) bends and open, sealed or capped ends. It returns a `GarmentCut` binding, so it fits and bends like a tailor's cut. The first piece of the sweep core; no tool uses it yet.

### Changed

- Rigs bound from markers put the pelvis behind the thigh joints by 0.028 of the body's height and below them by 0.008, as UAL's mannequins have it, not above them at the middle of the hips' thickness (a seat, a belly or armour moved it). Every marker rig changes, saved ones too: look at yours in a crouch. `fitSkeleton`'s `pelvis: 'middle'` gives the old placement.
- Rigs bound from markers put the neck joint at the top of the shoulders, an eighth of the way down from the head joint to the pelvis as on UAL's mannequins; on a body with its arms down it sat in the upper chest (5 to 9 cm low on the AI cast), so the head turned from there.
- Tailor: a new garment, or one with nothing drawn yet, is cut from the body's own triangles (**cloth mesh: as the body**), not draped: the cheapest and surest way. Saved garments keep how they were made.
- `loadCharacterAssets` no longer fetches Quaternius' hair library (13.9 MB) at start: a character fetches it the first time it wears one of its pieces, and offers the pieces by name before then (`QUATERNIUS_HAIR`). `CharacterAssets.hair` is null until then; `assets.loadHair()` loads it, and `loadCharacterAssets(scene, { hair: 'now' })` keeps the old behaviour.
- Character builder: the panel runs from the most basic, least changeable choices to the most: tabs Body, Skin, Eyes, Face, Hair, Clothes, Hold, Motion, Export; in the Body tab, shape (gender, age, height) then ancestry then figure (weight, muscle and the rest); in Hair, brows and the style before beard, moustache and stubble. Control paths that moved: `Body/figure/weight`, `Body/figure/muscle`.

### Fixed

- Retargeted clips keep the feet on the ground on bodies whose thigh and shin are proportioned differently from the clip's (the rig tool's AI characters crouched with one foot in the air): a foot near the ground goes where the source's went and the leg bends to reach it; a foot in the air keeps the copied angles. On by default in `retargeter`, `retargetClip` and `bakeClip`; `footIk: false` turns it off.
- Rig tool: a recipe handed over through `api.recipe` with new markers now binds the mesh again (it kept the old binding).
- The African American female's and Eurasian male's knee joints sit higher (2.5 and 4.4 cm), at the hollow behind the knee rather than below it.
- Tailor: switching to a slot that wears something the body shown cannot (MakeHuman's shoes while another body is on show) opened as "(new garment)" but said there was no outline; it now starts a new garment.
- Tailor: undo and redo work while an outline is being clicked out, a point at a time (they did nothing until it was closed). `outlineField3d` gains `undoPoint`/`redoPoint`. A panel's tooltips stay inside its padding, so the undo button's is no longer cut off at the edge.
- `riggedBodyGlb` wrote a garment's uvs upside down (ours run up the image, glTF's down), so a textured garment's picture landed flipped on it in other engines.
- The tailor could not cut a large garment ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"): a big cut's triangle list was spread into a call. The same pattern is gone from `remesh` and `loadRigTriangles`.
- A body opened from the builder's own export GLB (`riggedBodyGlb`) is its skin and eyes only: `glbRigTriangles`, `loadRigTriangles` and `loadSkinnedBody` leave out the garments and the held item it also carries, which were merged into the body.
- A menu opened from a scene panel (a select's list) closes on a press anywhere else: outside it, or on its panel anywhere but the control that opened it, which still toggles it. `showLayer` takes `dismissOutside`, and `showPopup` (every menu) asks for it.
- A popup dropped with its title band off screen comes back on release until the band is reachable (its top on screen, 48 px of it across), as a frame panel's screen drag already does. It may still be slid partly off to see past it.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.12.6/

# 0.12.5

For Dramatis and the character builder: an exported body now carries clips, garments and what the hand holds, the cast's rigs are engine-free data, and the Babylon peers are optional, so a three.js app can take the character core without installing Babylon. The builder gets a Character menu on the system bar, a manipulator for placing hair, and sub-sections in its panels.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1655.1 KB raw / 573.5 KB gz, up 11.3 KB / 4.5 KB gz (+0.7%) on 0.12.4.

> **⚠️ Breaking (install only):** `@babylonjs/core`, `@babylonjs/gui`, `@babylonjs/loaders` and `@babylonjs/materials` are now *optional* peers, so npm no longer installs them for you. A Babylon app that was relying on that installs them itself: `npm i @babylonjs/core @babylonjs/gui @babylonjs/loaders @babylonjs/materials`. The version ranges are unchanged.

### Added

- **`lockMove`** on `<tosi-b3d-manipulator>` (`'x'`, `'xz'`…): the object's axes a move may not go along. The widget shows only what is left (an arrow per free axis, a pad where both its axes are free) and a drag never moves along a locked axis. The character builder's hair handle locks x: up and forward, one pad.
- **Menus of actions on the system bar**: `barMenu` options can be actions (`handleSelect`, `checked`), submenus (`items`), rules (`separator`) and `disabled`, `options` may be a function read on each opening, and `layout: 'list'` shows each option's icon beside its caption. `viewMenu` is a list now (each view named).
- **`panelIcon`** on `<tosi-b3d>`: the settings button's icon in place of the owl, named by `panelTitle`, for a page whose panel is its main tool.
- **Character builder**: the character (select, delete, save, save as, rename, export and load JSON, go to the playground) is a **Character** menu on the system bar instead of a tab; the panel's button is the body. A library hairstyle is placed with a move-only manipulator on the head (up and forward) and a **scale** slider, in place of the up, forward and size sliders (the settings are unchanged, so saved characters keep their hair). The Body tab carries the mesh icon, and a mesh body's surfaces are a sub-section under its source. `makeCharacter(...).hairAnchor()` is the Head node and the skull's middle the adjustment is measured from.
- **Sub-sections**: `label3d({ collapsible: true, level: 2 })` folds inside the section or tab it is in (one open at a time, except with `panelSections: 'folds'`), drawn indented, and is a level under its section in the control tree (`Body/shape/gender`). The character builder's Body tab folds into shape, figure and ancestry.
- **`tailorPanel(el, options)`**: the character builder's always-on tailor as a piece any page with a character mounts (slot and garment pickers, keep on switch or close, forget, export, import), with the host's draft, slots and garment store passed in; `garmentStore()` is the browser's IndexedDB store the builder uses. The builder now runs on it.
- **Clips in an exported body**: `tosijs-3d/glb-clips` (engine-free) reads any skinned GLB's animations and the skeleton they were made on (`readGlbClips`) and bakes one onto another skeleton through the retargeter (`bakeClip`); `riggedBodyGlb(body, { clips: [{ from, clip, extras }] })` writes them as glTF animations, each with its licence in its `extras`. `writeSkinnedGlb` takes `animations`.
- **Garments in an exported body**: `riggedBodyGlb(body, { garments })` writes garments bound to that body (`garmentProxy`: the tailor's cuts and draped cloth on a file body, or Blender's) as meshes skinned on the same skeleton with weights from the body's own, their materials as glTF, and tucks the skin they cover (`cover: false` leaves it). A character's `wornGarments()` hands over what it wears; the character builder's export GLB includes them.
- **`tosijs-3d/garment-proxy`** (engine-free): `garmentProxy(content, body)` binds a garment file to the body it was made on as a `HumanProxy`, its material as data (pictures as bytes, `twoSided`, the saved `look`, and `gltf`, that look as glTF factors where it has a plain reading), so an exporter writes own garments through the same path as MakeHuman's clothes; `garmentMadeOn`, `garmentLook`, `lookGltf`. The character wears own garments through it. `clothRecipe` moved to `material-recipe` (still exported from `cloth-shading`).
- **Held items in an exported body**: `riggedBodyGlb(body, { held: { grip, item, gripPoint, extras } })` writes a `weapon_r` joint (or `weapon_l`, or `held.name`) under the hand where the character builder holds the grip, and with `item` (a mesh read by `glbRigTriangles(bytes, { pick })`) the item itself, skinned to that joint with its materials and its licence in the mesh's `extras`. `glbNodePosition` reads an item's `_grip` node with no engine. The socket arithmetic is the engine-free `tosijs-3d/hand-socket`, which the launcher's `handSocket` now runs too. `writeSkinnedGlb` meshes take `extras`. The character builder's export GLB carries what the right hand holds (`BodyExportTarget.held`).
- **`tosijs-3d/character-sources`** (engine-free): `CHARACTER_SOURCES` and `AI_CHARACTER_SOURCES` with Tonio's hand-placed rigs for the AI cast, and `rigFromMarkers`, so an exporter rigs the cast as the builder does (`glbRigTriangles`, `bodyFromMarkers` with the source's `recipe.binding`, `riggedBodyGlb`). Still exported from `character` and the barrel. `riggedBodyGlb`'s `recipe` may be partial.

### Changed

- **The `@babylonjs/*` peers are optional**, so a consumer of the engine-free subpaths (a three.js app taking the character core) installs no Babylon. A Babylon app that relied on npm installing the peers for it installs them itself: `npm i @babylonjs/core @babylonjs/gui @babylonjs/loaders @babylonjs/materials`.

### Fixed

- **Manipulator plane pads** can be grabbed again: the hairline arrow shafts, drawn in front of them from most angles, took the press first.
- Character builder: loading a saved character (or the autosaved one on opening the page) stopped before restoring its name and its tailor outline (a call left behind when the clothes "edit" picker went, in 0.12.4).
- A system panel with no title bar (a bar menu) keeps its size in step with its content when the content is swapped (a submenu was drawn at the full menu's height).
- A select's list is one at a time: tapping the select again closes it, and a panel rebuilt while the list was open (an in-place refresh) closes it with the old content. Before, the list stayed in the scene at its old offset (off screen once the panel's height changed) and the next tap opened a second.
- The character builder keeps a held item's grip point on the grip when the grip's scale is not 1 (the item slid off it).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.12.5/

# 0.12.4

Tabbed settings panels and undo across the character builder, rig tool and tailor; pictures in materials (Poly Haven's fabric scans as cloth presets, a picture or a flat colour or grey for any input); the tailor always on the bar; grips per class of held item; Tonio's textured weapons and melee in the biped.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1643.8 KB raw / 569.0 KB gz, up 47.8 KB / 14.0 KB gz (+3.0%) on 0.12.3: the material pictures and fabric presets, the drape's sliced runner, undo history, playback and hold grips are in the barrel.

## Added

- **Tabbed settings panels with icons**: `panelSections: 'tabs'` with an `icon` on each collapsible `label3d`. The character builder and the rig tool use it.
- **`panelActions(el)`** on `<tosi-b3d>`: a page's own buttons on the settings panel's icon bar, at its right end. Icon bars take `{ spacer: true }` (an elastic gap); `tabs3d` takes `tools`, and in a tabbed panel `iconBar3d({ inTabs: true })` goes on the tab strip.
- **Undo and redo** in the character builder and the rig tool (⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z). `undoHistory` is the pure history behind them.
- **Panels rebuild once a resize settles.** The scene dispatches `resizeend`; `panelRoom(panelEl)` gives a system panel its room.
- **Pictures in materials**: a material picker's colour, opacity, glow and bumps (and a cloth's colour, roughness and normal) can take a picture, kept by `material-pictures` and saved in a character file (`pictures`). Cloth and PBR take `tile` (metres per repeat).
- **Photographed fabrics**: eleven of Poly Haven's CC0 fabric scans as cloth presets (`textiles`, `textiles-full`; `fabricTexturePresets`).
- **Material previews** are drawn on Tonio's material test ball, on grey (a cube until it loads).
- **Export a rigged body as a GLB** from the rig tool and the character builder (joint names, rest pose, height; the model's materials and springs).
- **Character builder**: Hold uses Tonio's textured weapons with a manipulator on the grip; clips come from a smaller builder pack (`UAL_builder.glb`); `playback3d` (play, scrub, speed) in Motion; all four AI characters open on hand-placed rigs.
- **Rig tool**: spread fingers, and hand modes (full, mitten, none); opened from the builder it shows the body it already wears.
- **Biped melee**: `holdingWeapon` stands on guard in Sword_Idle and the right trigger swings (Sword_Attack). The biped playground carries Tonio's weapons.
- **Material inputs that take a picture** are a heading and a row: choose a picture, clear it, a flat colour or grey instead (`colorPicker` icon), and a swatch of what it is now. `colorPicker3d` and `color3d` take `grey: true` (a black-to-white ramp and a ladder of greys).
- **`slider3d` `notches`**: a press beside the handle steps to the next notch that way; dragging stays continuous. A material's `tile` is now **scale textures**, 1/32 to 4 on a log scale, notched at 1/n and whole numbers (`textureScaleNotches`), where pictures repeat whole.
- **The tailor has undo and redo** on a bar pinned to the top of its panel (⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z in the builder while it is open), with cancel and done unless it is `persistent`.
- **Grips per class of item** (`hold-grip`: `holdGrip`, `holdClassOf`, `HOLD_CLASSES`): pistols, rifles, heavy weapons, one- and two-handed blades, bows, shields. The character builder keeps an adjusted grip per class (placing one sword places every one-handed blade; per-item grips saved before are read as their class's), and the biped playground holds by class.
- **The character builder's tailor is always on the bar** (scissors): pick a slot and a garment, and one you cut opens on its outline to edit, or start a new one; no done or cancel, it keeps the garment when you switch or close, and undo covers the edits. Export, import and forget moved into it; the Tailor tab is gone. `mountTailorTool` takes `panel`, `persistent` and `rows`; characters take `hideSlot` (one slot's garment off for a moment).
- **Character builder clothes**: each slot is one row, the garment and its material swatch beside it; the "edit" picker is gone. `materialPicker3d` takes `name` (a title with no caption).
- **Tailor drape**: edits no longer lock the page (debounced, sliced, interruptible: `drapeGarmentAsync`, `runSliced`, `drapeSteps`, `remeshSteps`); cloth goes over arms, shoulders and hips; anchored points are drawn in the new `--w3d-anchored` colour.

## Changed

- **Stroked-and-filled icons fill with `--w3d-icon-fill`** (a mid blue) instead of the button colour behind them. Pass `knockout` to `iconGlyph`, or set `--tosi-icon-knockout`, for the old look.
- The rig tool's hosted "start over" is an icon beside undo and redo.
- Material inputs are labelled **diffuse** (albedo), **normal map** (was bumps) and **colorize** (a cloth's recolour); the recipe keys are unchanged.
- A material's `tile` input's range is now 1/32 to 4 (was 0.02 to 4), so a smaller saved value is clamped.
- Cloth material previews show a colour the recipe names wholly (the preview has no texture for a recolour to keep).
- The tailor's "export glTF" button reads "export GLB".

## Fixed

- Arrow keys and Space no longer scroll the page while you play a demo.
- Tailor, cut from the skin: tidy, smoothed cut edges (no spikes or notches along a neckline).
- Drape: edges well clear of the body are no longer pinned to it (rigid hems).
- A held item's grip is measured on fresh world matrices (the pistol no longer circles the hand metres away); the launcher reads its `_grip` the same way.
- Auto-rig: glove bumps are not read as fingers, and a knotted thumb is placed by proportion.
- The rig tool casts shadows when hosted, and done on a body from a file no longer leaves it invisible.
- Undoing a placed grip in the character builder moves the held item back (the numbers were restored, the item was not).
- A stroked-and-filled icon's part drawn with `stroke:none` stays unstroked (tosijs-ui#251 worked round by `bin/icon-no-stroke.ts`).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.12.4/
