# 0.12.3

Characters out to other engines and any mesh rigged well: a GLB read with no engine, any rigged body written as a skinned GLB that plays UAL's clips by name in three.js, Unity, Godot and Blender, and its springs as `VRMC_springBone`; the rig tool's fixes for AI-made meshes; draped cloth in the tailor; and scenes as agent tools and for a screen reader.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1596.0 KB raw / 555.0 KB gz, up 85.6 KB / 31.3 KB gz (+5.7%): scenes as agent tools, widget semantics, the screen-reader mirror and the scene description, and the drape and remesh are in the barrel; `glb-rig`, `rigged-body-glb`, `ual-rest` and `spring-vrm` are subpaths.

## Added

- **`tosijs-3d/glb-rig`**: `glbRigTriangles(bytes, { pick })` reads a mesh file's triangles for rigging with no engine: the file's frame, a skinned mesh at rest, one surface per material carrying its glTF material and its pictures as bytes, eyes split out. It agrees with `loadRigTriangles`, and `bodyFromMarkers` on it rigs a body with no scene (the same bytes and markers give the same weights).
- **`tosijs-3d/rigged-body-glb`**: `riggedBodyGlb(body, { naming, restPose, height, recipe, extras })` writes any rigged body (from the rig tool, a file's own skin, MakeHuman) as a skinned GLB in Dramatis's export profile: UAL's 65 joints with UAL's rest frames, so UAL's clips play on it by name; a T-pose by default (or the body as rigged); the soles at y = 0 under the origin; `body` and `eyes` meshes; the file's own materials and pictures; UE or Mixamo joint names. `tosijs-3d/ual-rest` is UAL's rest pose as data (`bin/ual-rest.ts` regenerates it).
- **`tosijs-3d/spring-vrm`**: a rig recipe's springs (a tail, strands hung from a bone, with colliders) go out as `VRMC_springBone`, which three-vrm, UniVRM and Godot's VRM importer read with no setup, and as `TOSIJS_spring_chains` with our own settings (`springChainsSchema()`). The page says where VRM's spring model differs from ours.
- `writeSkinnedGlb` writes emissive materials and root-level `extensions`.
- **Draped cloth in the tailor** (`tosijs-3d/cloth-drape`, `drapeGarment`): an outline becomes a front and a back piece laid over the body, sewn up its steep sides, bridged over hollows and settled under gravity. Pick it as "made by: drape". The tailor cuts from an even surface laid over the body at a density you pick, finer where the body is thin.
- **Character builder**: Tonio's AI-made characters (Keisha and Kevin, in underwear and in spacesuits) are bodies, one picked at random on a first visit; a **View** menu on the system bar, shared with the hosted rig tool, with a right-hand view that follows the palm through the clip; **clips from a file** (any skinned GLB's animations, Mixamo's or Meshy's, retargeted onto the body shown); every clip in the library; **hold** an item in the right hand, placed by its grip and saved with the character (`handSocket`, `deriveGrip`, `heldGrip`); **body detail** draws MakeHuman's own lighter body proxies; revert, delete, and the selector shows the character on screen.
- **Rig tool**: markers colour-coded with a reference mannequin; a dragged wrist or knee carries its hand or foot, a dragged shoulder or elbow the markers below it; joints mode shows every joint.
- **Scenes as agent tools** (`b3d-agent`): each `<tosi-b3d>` offers tools on WebMCP (`registerTool` only) and on `window.b3dAgent`: `b3d_<scene>_scene` and `_places` (named things and beacons, in world metres, with distance and bearing), `_snapshot`, `_control_go` (drives the vehicle in focus to a named place with its own controls; the player's input cancels it), `_control_hold`, `_control_status`, `_control_stop`, and the settings panel (`_panel`, `_panel_set`, `_panel_activate`). Closed by default: `enableSceneAgents({ expose: 'all' | 'read' })` opens the page, and a scene's new `agent` attribute (`read`, `on`, `off`) overrides it. `b3d.originOffset` is how far the floating origin has moved. Changing a scene's `agent` (or its name) after it is on the page updates its tools (#3699).
- **`bun run xr --flat --script`** now runs the script (it was ignored without VR), and a script that throws fails the run.
- **`semantics()` on every panel widget** (`tosijs-3d/widget-semantics`): a control says what it is (role, name, value) and can be set or pressed through its own path, as a hand would. `panel.controls()` reads a panel as a tree of named controls, including an open popup's form; `findControl` and `nameProblems` (unnamed or duplicate controls) work on it. `inputField` and `vector3d` take a `name`; `tabs3d` a `name`. This is the base the WebMCP tools and the screen-reader mirror are built on (#3699).
- **A screen reader can use the settings panel** (`tosijs-3d/aria-mirror`): an open flat panel is mirrored as visually hidden HTML controls (buttons, switches, range inputs, selects, text and number fields; sections as headings), which set or press the panel's own widgets. The system bar's HTML buttons now stay in the accessibility tree in scene mode (they were `visibility: hidden`) and appear while one has keyboard focus, so Tab goes from the owl into the settings. `ariaMirror(host, read)` mirrors any panel (#3699).
- **Every demo's settings panel passes the name test** (63 pages, about 1000 controls). The big editors describe themselves too: `curve3d` and `footprint3d` are editors whose value is their points and whose options are their presets (set either), and `curveProgram3d`, `lightEditor3d` and `terrainEditor3d` list their rows. A `list3d` item may carry a `title`, its accessible name when the label is not unique; an indented label is trimmed (#3699).
- **A keyboard and screen-reader pass over the panels** (`bun run screen-reader <page> --steps …`, a driver that reads only Chrome's accessibility tree and presses real keys). Fixes from it: the owl says whether its panel is open (`aria-expanded`); a slider announces its formatted value (`semantics().valueText`, `aria-valuetext`: "50 km", "±13 °C"); a log-scale slider is stepped along its track, not in equal steps of its value; focus stays in place when the control it was on is renamed (Pause becoming Resume); a toolbar with no name is "tools". `button3d` takes a `title` (its name and tooltip when the label is a glyph), and the name test now reports a control named only by a glyph such as `⋯` (#3699).
- **The 3D view for a screen reader**: the canvas is an image named "<title>, 3D scene", described in words (`describeScene`, `tosijs-3d/scene-description`: what you are in, which way you face, the time of day, the named things nearby with distance and direction). Built only when asked for: once when the scene appears, when the canvas takes focus, and by a visually hidden "Describe the scene" button that speaks it; never on a timer (#3699).
- **Assistive features cost nothing until used, and sit where things are drawn**: a scene builds no mirror, description or pad labels until focus first lands in it (not focus from a mouse or finger press: clicking the scene focuses its canvas) or one of its hidden buttons is pressed for real (iOS VoiceOver presses without focusing) (`b3d.assistive`), and runs no timer even then (values are re-read when a control takes focus). The mirrored controls are placed exactly over the drawn panel, modal and system bar (`ariaMirror`'s `place`; `ControlNode.box`, `WidgetSemantics.box` / `childBoxes`), so VoiceOver's touch exploration on a phone finds "Continue" where it is drawn and a double-tap lands on it (#3699).
- **Modals for a screen reader**: a modal (`showModal`: the pause, a respawn panel) is mirrored as a hidden dialog that takes focus on its first control (Continue) and gives focus back when it closes, so a pause can be dismissed with no pointer. It is always mirrored, not only once a scene is in use, because a modal blocks the page; its title ("Paused") is also announced. `ariaMirror` takes `role: 'dialog'`. Pressing a mirrored copy no longer counts as a press outside the settings panel (that closed the panel before the copy's click). Placed copies are real touch targets over the drawn controls, unpainted but opaque and, where the main pointer is a finger, touchable (`UNPAINTED`; with a mouse every press goes through to the drawn panel): iOS VoiceOver finds what a finger is on by hit-testing and passed transparent, untouchable copies over for the canvas. In use, the system bar's real buttons are touch targets the same way, and a copy with keyboard focus shows a ring over the drawn control. While a modal is open the system bar's buttons and the panel's copies are inert, so a reader cannot open the settings from behind a pause (#3699).
- **The glass gamepad says where its controls are and what they do**: each control is named for a screen reader ("A button, bottom right: handbrake"), from the driven entity's new `inputLabels` (car, tank, aircraft and biped carry their mapping's labels), updated when you change what you control. The pad also stays hidden while the scene is loading.
- **A weapon in a hand holds the same way on any rig**: a launcher with `socket: 'right-hand'` or `'left-hand'` rides a node under the hand oriented by the hand's anatomy at rest (forearm, thumb side), calibrated so UAL's hand is unchanged. A character from the character builder held the playground's pistol at a wrong angle and mirrored, because its hand bone's axes and mirror differ from UAL's.
- **Character builder ↔ Biped Playground**: the builder is under Demos, and **play in Biped Playground** takes the figure you are working on straight there (`/playground/?character=…`). The playground lists that figure as "from the character builder", loads the character it shows (the last one picked, remembered in this browser), and links back with **make your own character…**.
- **A sideways trackpad drag over a scene no longer swipes the page back or forward**: a scene cancels the default of a mostly horizontal wheel over it (the camera and panels still get the event).
- **Input trace in development**: with the debug sink on (the dev server), a scene posts each press it receives (touch, pointer, click, focus: real target, position, whether genuine) to the sink as `input`, so how a phone's screen reader presses things can be read rather than guessed (#3699).
- **Clouds drift on the sky's clock**: a cloud deck under a sky sped up with `realtimeScale` drifts and evolves that much faster, so a time-lapse carries its clouds; a stopped sky leaves them in real time (`skyRate(owner)`).

## Changed

- **Bone heat with visibility**: a bone heats only the skin it can see, radiating along its whole length.
- **Arm space follows the clip**: how far a clip hangs the arm decides how much arm space applies.
- A biped's character loads out of sight and appears standing where it belongs.

## Fixed

- **The rig tool stands a model on the floor when its file's origin is its middle** (Meshy's are), not its feet: on 0.12.2 these stood half under the floor.
- **Auto-rig**: a body with its arms held out keeps the arm bones off its ribcage and the collarbones off the chest; a held-out arm's shoulder clears the body; the thighs stay out of the belly, so a walk no longer squashes the torso; the elbow is found on arms held steeply down.
- **Done in the rig tool no longer makes the character vanish.**
- The tailor cuts a file's body as one surface (seams split for UVs are welded first).
- A character in the Biped Playground wears its clothes' saved colours, not white; a reload of the builder remembers which saved character you were editing.
- Panels fold their own sections, and the rig tool wears a mesh's own materials.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.12.3/

# 0.12.2

More of the character, engine-free: eyes from Tonio's art, hair placed with no engine, lips and stubble as vertex colours, cloth recoloured into its texture, and the extremes sweep, all moved here from Dramatis. The character builder's save and rename ask in a popup.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1516.6 KB raw / 526.0 KB gz, up 6.2 KB / 2.3 KB gz (+0.4%): the eye art painter, `pngDecode` and the save popup are in the barrel; the rest are subpaths.

## Added

- **Eyes from a picture**: `eyeTexture({ style: 'basic' | 'anime' })` paints Tonio's CC0 eye art with its iris recoloured, and a character's new `eyeStyle` setting picks it (`basic` by default; `drawn` keeps the eye drawn in code, which also shows while the art loads). `tosijs-3d/eye-art` is the engine-free half: the art's URLs, `recolourEyePng`, and `gltfEyeUvs` for an export. `pngDecode` joins `pngEncode`.
- **`tosijs-3d/hair-place`**: hair placed on a body's head with no engine (`headScalp`, `placeHair`, and the hair library read from its GLB with `readHairLibrary`). `human-hair` uses it and re-exports what it exported before.
- **Baked materials**: `tosijs-3d/skin-paint` (`lipTint`, `stubbleTint`, `stubbleMask`) gives the lips and stubble as per-vertex colours over the skin's albedo, and `writeSkinnedGlb` writes them as `COLOR_0` (a primitive's new `colors`), which glTF multiplies into the base colour, so no texture is needed. `tosijs-3d/cloth-bake` (`recolourCloth`, `textureMean`, `clothSheenColour`) bakes a garment's recolour into its texture as cloth-shading draws it. `lipTint` and `stubbleTint` moved from character-builder and are still exported from the barrel.
- **`tosijs-3d/fit-extremes`** and **`bun run extremes`**: every MakeHuman garment and Quaternius hairstyle on 133 bodies at the sliders' corners, measured for penetration (raw, and visible past the skin's tuck) and bone sanity, with a markdown/JSON report and a headless contact sheet of the worst cases.
- **`tosijs-3d/mesh-sdf`**: signed distance to a triangle mesh.
- **`coverDepths`** (proxy-cover): how deep each skin vertex goes under what is worn, the rule `coverSkin` applies before its fade.
- **`button3d({ popup })`**: a button that opens a small form (controls, flat and in a headset) in a popup anchored to it; the controls get a handle to close it or show the next step.
- All the new modules are in the engine-free [character core](/character-core/).

## Changed

- **Character builder**: `save…` asks for the name in a popup (filled in with the current one), refuses a blank name or the working figure's with a reason, and asks before replacing another saved character; `rename…` renames the picked one. Both work in a headset. `nameCharacter` (character-store) is the rule.

## Fixed

- Stubble no longer darkens the lower lip.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.12.2/

# 0.12.0

**0.12 in one paragraph.** Vehicles you drive: a pure model of wheeled and
tracked vehicles (no physics engine), `<tosi-b3d-car>` rebuilt on it and a new
`<tosi-b3d-tank>`, with a chase camera that orbits, booms up to overhead and
climbs over what is in its way, flat and in a headset. A procedural city to
drive them in (`cityLayout`, `<tosi-b3d-city>`: Kenney's kits, traffic, street
lights, lit windows, sound, light pollution), and two demos, City Drive and
Cross Country. Models are no longer drawn mirrored. The character creator's
working parts are promised as twenty engine-free subpaths, for other engines.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1510.4 KB raw / 523.7 KB gz, +6.16% gz on 0.11.6 (vehicles, the city, traffic, its sound and lights, the character core split out).

## ⚠️ Breaking

Each is in [Migration](/Migration/) with what to do.

- **`<tosi-b3d-car>`'s `turnRate` and `friction` are gone** (setting either warns once): use `steerDeg` and `grip`. `acceleration` and `braking` are now m/s².
- **Models are no longer drawn mirrored.** Anything loaded through `canonicalize` or a `<tosi-b3d-library>` now looks as authored; 0.11 drew it as its mirror image. Check anything you placed or measured against the mirrored picture. Skinned models are unchanged.
- **`KENNEY_CITY`'s `bend` is `turns: 0` and its `end` `turns: 3`**, measured on the unmirrored models.
- **`RiggedBody.surfaces[].material` is `SurfaceMaterial`** (a name), not Babylon's `Material`; cast it back on the Babylon side.

## Added

- **Vehicles you can drive.** `ground-vehicle` is a pure model of wheeled and tracked vehicles (springs, tyre grip that slides past its limit, Ackermann steering, skid steer), no physics engine. `<tosi-b3d-car>` is rebuilt on it: give it a model whose wheels have `wheel` in their names (Tonio Loewald's cars on the CDN, `tonio/vehicles/cars.glb`, work at `scale: 2`; so does Kenney's Car Kit at `1.7`), and it measures them. `<tosi-b3d-tank>` is new: tracks, a pivot turn, and a plain tank when given no model. The car mapping is GTA V's: right trigger accelerates, left trigger brakes and reverses, the left stick only steers, the right stick looks around, A is the handbrake, and one step from GTA, the right bumper also brakes and reverses so the right thumb has both pedals on the on-screen pad (W/S still drive on a keyboard, through the new `keyboard` hook on an `InputMapping`). Vehicles bring their own chase camera, high and aimed ahead of the car (`chaseRigFor`, `chasePose`). Off the throttle a car coasts down (`coast`, m/s²); steering at speed is held to what the tyres grip, so turns keep their speed. A tank keeps turning at top speed and goes where it points. The tank's right stick (arrow keys) aims its turret: traverse and gun elevation, held in the world while the hull turns, and the camera looks where it aims; a model's `turret` and `gun`/`barrel`/`cannon` nodes are found by name. A tank climbs a step about as high as its tracks (a `TrackSpec` may carry `climb` points, which carry nothing on the flat). Vehicles stop at walls with rays from their own body instead of a swept ellipsoid, which stepped over anything under half its height.
- **Chase camera and Cross Country.** A vehicle's chase camera pivots round a point above it: the right stick orbits (springing back on release) and up/down moves it along an arc from close behind to nearly overhead, where it stays (`CHASE_BOOM`; `chasePose` takes the boom and a lift). It climbs over walls, traffic and hillsides before it pulls in, and keeps clear of the ground. In a headset it orbits too and looks down from the top. A tank's view follows its turret. `ControlInput.lookMode` is the right-stick click (R3; **V** on a keyboard, `right_stick_click` on the glass gamepad): on a tank it swaps the stick's up/down between the gun and the camera, with a buzz in a headset (`b3d.haptic()`). The track links of a model that animates them (Tonio's tank) run at ground speed. **Cross Country** (Demos): that tank in open country.
- **A city to drive in**: `<tosi-b3d-city>` builds roads, buildings, street lights and parked cars from a seed with Kenney's city kits (any kit, through its `kit` manifest), drawn as thin instances at 12 m a cell (9.6 m kerb to kerb: a lane each way and a parked car; the kit's `roadway` says how wide its road is), each building on as many cells as its model covers; `cityStart(options)` is a clear spot in the middle to start a car. Street lights are spots pointing down from their poles (`lampAngle`, reaching twice their height), and some flicker (`flicker`, `lampFlicker`). **Traffic** (`traffic`, default 24): cars drive round on their own in the right-hand lane, turn at junctions, keep their distance and stop for your car. Each is a body on the same model as your car (`TRAFFIC_CAR`), steering after a plan that drives the lane: cars that touch push and spin each other, and ramming one knocks both cars about (momentum is exchanged; your car is no longer stopped dead), kerbs keep them out of buildings, and two cars jammed into each other sort it out by one backing away. The count is a GTA-style budget (`recycleTraffic`): cars far away or out of view go and come back out of view, driving toward you. Head, tail and brake lamps, and a headlight beam at night. The model is pure (`createTraffic`, `stepTraffic`). **Lit windows** (`windowLights`, `roomLit`): a material plugin lights rooms' windows at night (warm lamps, the odd blue screen). Every room has a habit it keeps (always dark, night owl, early riser, evening, bathroom), each with its own hours: most lit around ten, rare after midnight, more from five. **Lamps** (`lightPool`): street lights and headlights are virtual lights, and the few that matter most to the view get real lights (`lampLights`, a new device budget; ranked by `poolScore`, lamps ahead first), falling off linearly to their range on PBR materials too. Where the device supports clustered lighting, every lamp is a real light (a `ClusteredLightContainer`): a city's hundred street lights and the traffic's headlights all light the street. A `VirtualLight` may carry a ranking `weight`. The sky reports `daylight`, so street lights come on at dusk and a driven vehicle's `headlights` at night.
- **City Drive** (Demos): a 48 × 48 city on ground flattened for it, in green hills by the sea under the full sky (day and night, cloud deck, stars), with woods round it; drive out of town and keep going. `cityGround({ width, depth, level, x, z })` gives a terrain `landform` (a pad flat under the grid) and a decorator `clear`; `<tosi-b3d-decorator>` takes `clear`, ground kept clear of trees and rocks.
- **Sound in the city** (positional, synthesised): the nearest traffic's engines (the note rises with speed, opens on the throttle), a horn from a driver you block (and, after a long wait, from one stuck behind a stuck car; `car.honk` in the pure model), the hum of the nearest street lights and a sputtering buzz from the failing ones. Your own vehicle's engine plays while you drive it (`sound="off"` to silence; a tank's is lower). New effect voices: `engine`, `hum`, `horn`. `<tosi-b3d-city sound="off">` for silence.
- **A city's plan**: `cityLayout({ width, depth, seed })` lays out roads, blocks and lots on a grid of cells (every road connected, every lot on a street), with each road cell's piece and rotation; it knows no kit or metres, so any kit on any grid can dress it.
- **Light pollution.** A lit town washes the faint stars out of its own sky and lays a warm glow along the horizon; out in the country they come back. Anything that lights the night registers a source (`lightPollutionSource(scene, { centre, radius, strength })`, `<tosi-b3d-city>` does, following its street lights), and `<tosi-b3d-skybox>` reads them at the camera every frame; its `lightPollution` attribute is the base for the whole sky (0, a dark sky).
- **The scene waits until it is built.** `el.holdLoading(label)` keeps a `<tosi-b3d>` behind its spinner until the returned release is called (at most 20 s); the first showing also waits for a streaming terrain. `<tosi-b3d-city>` and `<tosi-b3d-library>` hold it, so a city is never shown without its buildings.
- **The character core is engine-free, and promised.** Twenty modules that make a character with no Babylon and no DOM (human-pack, human-morph, human-rig, rigged-body, rig-fit, bone-heat, rig-recipe, retarget, spatial-transform, proxy-fit, proxy-rigid, hair-fit, garment-cut, garment-file, uv-unwrap, skin-tone, character-file, and the new character-settings, proxy-cover and asset-url) are subpaths (`tosijs-3d/human-morph`, …) a three.js app or a server can import; a test fails if any of them reaches Babylon, types included, and the packed tarball imports each under plain Node. `RiggedBody.surfaces[].material` is typed `SurfaceMaterial` (a name) instead of Babylon's `Material`: cast it back on the Babylon side. New: `character-settings` holds `DEFAULT_CHARACTER`, `CHARACTER_SLOTS`, `HAIR_COLOURS` and `hm08PackUrl()` (with `HM08_PACK_PATH`, `HM08_PACK_VERSION`); `proxy-cover` is the engine-free half of `coverBody` (`coverSkin`, `BODY_WRAPPING_SLOTS`). The barrel exports everything it did. See the `character-core` page.
- `b3dLight` takes `nightIntensity`: under a day/night `b3dSkybox` the ambient fill eases to it as the daylight goes (the sun is already the moon), so night no longer looks like an overcast noon.

## Changed

- **Faster on a headset**: a vehicle's physics takes at most 0.1 s a frame, so a stall cannot pile up steps; the vehicle model steps at 1/60 s (was 1/120), and a vehicle casts each wheel's ground ray once a frame, its later steps meeting the plane that ray found; `pickWorld(scene, ray, predicate)` and `rayProxies(scene)` let something that knows its own shape answer rays (a `RayProxy`), and `<tosi-b3d-city>` does (flat ground, a box per building, parked car and pole, filed by cell), so a vehicle's ray in the city costs a quarter of what it did. City models are one mesh each, and only buildings and moving traffic cast shadows. Fixed: cars with their wheels as instances (half Kenney's) were drawn without wheels; your own headlights flickered as you looked round (the lamp pool gave their light away; the one you drive now keeps it, and a lamp holding a light keeps it unless another is clearly better). Effect audio that cannot start (an iPhone's audio device) no longer retries every frame or throws an unhandled rejection; it tries once a second. In a headset the lamp pool uses its ranked lights, not clustered lighting: Babylon's container bins lamps for one camera a frame, so the second eye flickered and lost the street lights.

## Fixed

- **Fixed: models were drawn mirrored.** Everything loaded through `canonicalize` or a `<tosi-b3d-library>` (vehicles, aircraft, lamp fixtures, the city's kits, any library instance) was its own mirror image: text backwards, left and right swapped. Babylon's glTF loader converts handedness with one mirror on `__root__`, which both paths dropped. `unmirrorGltf` / `unmirrorContainer` now move that mirror into the content node by node (transforms, vertices with their winding, animation keys), so every frame stays proper and the model looks as authored. ⚠️ An asymmetric model now appears the other way round from 0.11, and anything measured off the mirrored picture needs checking: `KENNEY_CITY`'s bend is now `turns: 0` and its end `turns: 3`. Skinned models are left as they were.
- Fixed: a car's headlight beam trailed the car by a frame or two (visible from above at speed). The lamp pool now places its lights after everything else has moved that frame, and a vehicle aims its beam from where it is now.
- Fixed: building a scene after the page's only one was removed (a route change) lost skin, hair and cloth shading, caustics, the biome ground, cloud shadows and projected occlusion; skin shading threw 'plugin not registered'. Babylon clears material plugins when its last engine goes; ours now register again (`registerMaterialPlugin`).
- iPhone: the page no longer zooms from inside a scene (`<tosi-b3d>` is `touch-action: none` and cancels Safari's pinch), and a zoomed page is reset when the scene goes full screen, where nothing was left to pinch out on.
- Fixed: getting into a car during a VR session no longer blanks the headset (the car's camera waits until you leave VR), and leaving VR in a vehicle shows the scene behind it, not a frame from inside the ground; the Enter VR button is no longer left lit.
- Fixed: setting a vehicle's removed `turnRate` or `friction` warns once instead of doing nothing silently.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.12.0/

# 0.11.6

The character leaves the builder. Any body (MakeHuman's, Blender's, Quaternius', or a mesh of your own) is rigged, dressed and tailored the same way; a character is a file that carries its body, `makeCharacter` builds it anywhere, and `<tosi-b3d-biped character>` walks it in a game. The biped playground plays as a character you saved. Materials get a picker of their own.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1430.1 KB raw / 493.3 KB gz, +5.74% on 0.11.5 (rigged bodies, characters, the tailor and rig tools as tools, the material picker).

## Added

- **`RiggedBody`** (rigged-body): one shape for a character's body whoever made it: the rest mesh, UAL's joints, skin weights, regions, and how it was made. Three producers: `bodyFromMarkers` (any mesh plus eight markers, guessed if absent), `humanBodyMaker(pack)` (MakeHuman's sliders) and `loadSkinnedBody` (a file already skinned to UAL's skeleton, as Quaternius' characters are, taken with its own joints and weights). `buildBody` makes a Babylon skeleton from any of them; `autoRig` and `loadRigTriangles` (rig-build) are the whole path in two calls. A body from a file carries its `uvs`, `colors` and `surfaces` (its materials), and its eyeballs (`body.eyes`, objects named as eyes), which take the iris dial and the gaze.
- **`lidBlink(positions, eye)`**: a blink made from a body's shape, for bodies with eyeballs and no blink targets (Blender's Human Base Meshes). Bodies rigged from markers blink with it.
- **`makeCharacter(scene, assets, { settings, garments, gaze })`** (character): the character builder's character from its settings, outside the builder. `set(changes)` applies only what changed; `skeleton`, `recipe` and `groundFor(clip)` are what playing clips on it needs. `loadCharacterAssets` loads MakeHuman's pack and the hair once per scene.
- **Character files** (character-file): a character as one versioned JSON document: every setting, each slot's look and material, the tailor's outlines, its own garments and its body (`bodies`: a URL, or the file itself) embedded, so a file is whole on another machine. `readCharacter` reads it against the page's defaults (unknown settings listed in `warnings`, missing ones defaulted, older versions migrated, newer refused).
- **`<tosi-b3d-biped character="…json">`** (or `characterDoc`): a biped made from a character file, with the clips its states name retargeted onto it (UAL1 by default), so `ualAnimationStates()` drives it. MakeHuman is imported only when a biped has a character.
- **`characterStore()`** (character-store): the characters this browser keeps (IndexedDB), shared by the builder and any page. A mesh or garment shared by several saves is stored once. The biped playground's settings panel has a **character** menu: the mannequin or any saved character, swapped in where the hero stands.
- **`mountTailorTool(b3d, { body, built, handleDone })`** (tailor-tool): the tailor as a tool, cutting a garment from any `RiggedBody`. Garments cut or imported on a mesh's body are bound to that body. `mountRigTool` takes `handleDone` / `handleCancel` and a host `panel`, and hands back `{ recipe, body }`.
- **The rig tool's markers are on the body**, dragged onto the joints they place; every joint can be moved by hand (kept in the recipe as `binding.joints`), and a tail has markers at its base and tip.
- **`materialPicker3d`** (material-picker): a material as one row, edited in a popup with rendered previews. `material-recipe` is the data (`{ type, inputs }`, schema, validator, collections such as the fabrics), `applyMaterial` puts it on a Babylon material. The character builder's garments use it.
- `barMenu` options take an `icon`; when every option has one the menu is a row of icon buttons. A new icon kind, `stroked filled`. Icons: `svgIcons.biped`, the rig and the tailor's scissors.
- `chooseFile(accept)`: the file picker as a promise, which keeps its input in the page until it answers.
- An [Acknowledgements](/acknowledgements/) page: every source used, with its licence.

## Changed

- The character builder has a body **source**: MakeHuman's, Blender's realistic Human Base Meshes, Quaternius' superheroes, or a GLB/glTF you open. A body from a file wears its own materials (each "as made" or "skin"), gets clothes and the Tailor, and its rig recipe is saved with the character. Characters save and restore (autosaved as you work, named saves beside it, JSON export and import).
- Feet and toes take the clip's turn by heading only, so feet stand flat on bodies whose ankle sits higher or lower than UAL's.
- The rig tool grounds a clip on the body's soles, so a body whose legs differ from the mannequin's no longer floats or sinks.

## Fixed

- Every file picker (the builder, the rig tool, the effect tool) delivers the file picked; a detached input could lose it, silently on Safari.
- The builder's Blender and Quaternius bodies load on a page that sets the asset base after import.
- Auto-rig on A-posed bodies: shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands and feet are found on the body.
- Turning a tail on brings its spring; its tip starts at the end of the mesh.
- Cloth eased onto a coarse body stays on its skin.
- A `b3d-launcher` moved to another holder shows its model, not the placeholder box.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.11.6/

# 0.11.5

The character creator gets dressed. Clothes (MakeHuman's CC0 garments, fitted to any body shape, with fabrics and recolouring), the Tailor (cut a garment out of the body by drawing its outline, or a skirt, kilt or robe in skirt mode; save it, or take it to Blender and back, rigid armour parts included), faces that move (MakeHuman's face units: blinking, talking, expressions), hair and skin shading, stubble, and new body controls (waist, chest, bust).

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1352.5 KB raw / 465.5 KB gz, +7.28% on 0.11.4 (clothing, the Tailor, expressions, shading).

## Added

- `skirtGarment(positions, triangles, { front, side?, thickness })` (garment-cut): a skirt, kilt or robe from the same outlines as `cutGarment`. At each height the cloth goes round the convex outline of the body inside the cut, hangs straight below its widest ring, and is an open tube (no top or bottom) to draw two-sided; each point is bound between the nearest skin left and right, so it moves with both legs; `anchor` says which skin it may go round (the builder leaves out the arms, which a skirt cannot follow without cloth simulation; sleeves are a cut garment). The builder's Tailor has a `skirt` toggle, saved with the garment. A two-sided proxy material (`humanProxy`) lights its inside as an inside (`twoSidedLighting`).
- `smoothUnder`'s `bridge` (0..1) lets thicker cloth flatten the curve under a bump too, and `cutGarment`'s `fitOn` keeps a garment cut on one body in that shape when it is fitted on another. The builder's Tailor bridges more of the chest the thicker the cloth.
- A popup opened with `side: 'right'` or `'left'` in a scene panel's layer (`showLayer`) hangs beside the panel, level with its anchor, and may be up to twice the panel's width; it was always centred over the panel and no wider than it. The character builder's Tailor draws its outline in one (**draw the outline…**), with delete point and clear.
- A `waist` macro (human-morph, 0.5 neutral) on MakeHuman's waist-circumference targets, and a **waist** slider in the character builder: the weight macros barely narrow a woman's waist (about 1 cm from average to least). Needs the human pack from 2026-10-27 or later (`hm08.json?v=16`); an older pack lacks the targets and the slider does nothing. Below 0.5 it also pinches the waist toward the centre line (`pinchWaist`, `WAIST_NARROW` in the weights map), because MakeHuman's waist target mostly takes depth off: at 0 a woman's waist is about 4.5 cm narrower from the front, with the chest and hips unchanged.
- `unwrapUvs(positions, triangles, options?)` (uv-unwrap): UVs from a mesh's shape. It is cut along the plane between left and right and the one between front and back (vertices near a plane are used as the seam, triangles crossing it are cut), each piece is flattened by least-squares conformal maps at its true area with the mesh's up as +v, and the pieces are packed into the unit square (`fit: false` keeps metres; `metresPerUnit` gives the scale). A ball falls into four pieces, trousers into a front and back per leg. `carryUnwrapped` takes normals or any per-vertex data over to the cut mesh. `unwrapGarment` (garment-file) unwraps a garment with its normals carried across the seams, and the character builder's Tailor now exports and saves a cut unwrapped, so a pattern runs across it in Blender and a map can be painted on it.
- `readGarment` returns the garment's `material` from a GLB, which is what Blender's Principled BSDF exports: a base colour map (its alpha is the garment's alpha), a normal map, a roughness and metalness map, their factors, the alpha mode and double-sidedness, with the images copied out of the file (`materialCount` says how many the parts used; the first part's is read). `writeGarmentGlb` takes a `material` and writes the images into the GLB. A proxy's `material` takes the same (`metallicRoughness`, `roughness`, `metallic`, `baseColor`, `blend`, `alphaCutoff`, `normalScale`) and `proxyMaterial` draws them. The builder's Tailor draws an imported garment with its own maps, has a **recolour** slider, and the fabric **as made**, which leaves a garment's surface alone.
- The builder's Tailor can **hide other clothes**, and **save as an option**: a named garment, cut or imported, is kept in the browser (IndexedDB) and becomes a choice in its slot with the fabric and colour it was saved with; a saved cut can be edited again from its outline, and **forget** removes it. `GarmentMeta` carries `cut` and `look` for this.
- `cutGarment(positions, triangles, { front, side?, thickness, ease, hem })` (garment-cut): a garment cut out of the body by polygons drawn in the front view (and optionally the side view), cut along the outline, pushed out, eased across creases and hemmed. It returns an ordinary proxy binding, so it fits every body shape and bends with every clip; `humanProxy` draws it and `delete` lists the skin it covers. A rectangle from the waist to the ankles is a pair of trousers.
- `outlineField3d` (outline-field): a scene-panel control for drawing those outlines over the body's front view. Click out points and click the first to close; drag a point; press an edge to add one; `removeSelected()` and `clear()` for buttons. With symmetry on (the default) you draw one side and `mirrorOutline` (garment-cut) makes it whole: a half with an edge on the centre line becomes one garment across the body, any other a mirrored pair. The character builder has it as **Tailor**, with thickness, fabric and colour.
- A garment out to Blender and back. `writeGarmentGlb` / `writeGarmentObj` (garment-file) save a garment with, optionally, the body it was made on as a translucent `body-reference` marked as a helper; the base, pack version and body sliders travel as glTF `extras` (in Blender, export with Include → Custom Properties). `readGarment` reads either format back, skipping the helper, and `bindGarment` (garment-bind) binds any mesh to the body by its nearest skin, so a hand-made collar or a garment with its own UV unwrap fits every body. The builder's Tailor has export glTF, export OBJ, include the body, and import.
- Rigid parts in a bound garment (`proxy-rigid`): an armour plate, a visor and its ring, a buckle keep their shape. A binding's `rigid` groups are placed on a new body shape by the best rotation, uniform scale and shift of their flexible fit, share one set of skin weights so a clip carries them without bending, and move as one with an expression; rigidity is a 0 to 1 dial per vertex, so a part can stiffen gradually. `fitProxy`, `proxyWeights` and `proxyDelta` honour it. From Blender, a `rigid` custom property on an object says how (`1`, a fraction, `parts` for each loose island, `paint` for vertex colour, or a group name shared by objects that move together), a `_rigid` float attribute sets it per vertex, and a name ending `_rigid` or `_rigidParts` works without custom properties. `garmentRigidity(garment)` resolves it for `bindGarment`.
- Export the body alone, to model a garment from nothing: `writeGarmentGlb` / `writeGarmentObj` take no `garment`, and the builder's Tailor has **export the body alone**. Everything modelled beside it comes back as the garment. The body helper now carries the metadata too, and `readGarment` reads it from there when no garment node has it.
- The body helper's name carries the body, for files that lose the metadata (an OBJ through Blender, a glTF exported without custom properties): `body-reference_hm08_p15_weight72_muscle100` is the base, the pack version and each non-default slider as a whole percentage. `readGarment` reads it when nothing better is there; `referenceName` / `metaFromName` (garment-file) write and read it. Keep the name when editing.
- `<tosi-b3d-aircraft dropShadow="on">` (off by default): a soft blob shadow straight below the craft, darkest on the ground and fading and spreading as it climbs, so its height reads at a glance. Meant for scenes without real shadows; beside a sun's shadow it contradicts it.
- The rig tool imports animations made on another rig (`load animations…`, `rig.loadClips(file | url)`): a GLB's clips (Mixamo, mocap, another library) are retargeted onto the character and the comparison mannequin. Mixamo's FBX needs converting to GLB first.
- A slow-motion button beside Pause in the settings panel's icon bar: world time at a quarter speed (`timeScale` 0.25) and back.
- The rig tool binds a model with no skeleton itself (`load model file…` takes a GLB or OBJ): eight markers on its outline, guessed and then dragged onto the joints, place a skeleton, and bone heat binds the mesh to it. `bind from markers` does the same for a model that has a skeleton, ignoring it. The markers are saved in the recipe as `binding` (`RigBinding`).
- `skinShading` (`skin-shading`), a PBR material plugin for skin: a reddened, softened terminator (scatter), a grazing rim, and back-light through thin parts (ears, nose, fingers) from `skinThinness`, a per-vertex thinness carried in the vertex colour's alpha (`lipTint` takes it). `skinMaterial` turns it on (`shading: false` for plain PBR) and is a little glossier (roughness 0.42).
- Hair shading (a highlight band along the strands from PBR anisotropy, a sheen rim) and dye: `hairDye(natural, hue, saturation)` and `HairMaterial.setHair(light, red, { hue, saturation })` turn the natural colour toward a hue at the hair's own lightness (blue over dark hair is blue-black, pink over bleached hair pastel). The builder has dye hue and strength sliders.
- CLOTHING. `proxy-fit` is MakeHuman's `.mhclo` binding (three base vertices, weights and an axis-scaled offset per vertex), so a garment follows every body shape with no per-body fitting: `fitProxy`, `drawnPositions`, `proxyWeights` (skin weights from the vertices it is bound to), `nearestWeights` (for the helper vertices clothes bind to), `coveredTriangles`. `human-proxy` puts one on a built body, skinned to its skeleton: `humanProxy`, `proxyMaterial`, `coverBody` (hides covered skin). The human pack (`?v=5`) carries MakeHuman's CC0 system assets as proxies: 20 suits and shoes, a fedora, 10 hairstyles and 12 brows (`pack.proxy(name)`). The builder has outfit, shoes and hat menus, MakeHuman's hair and brows beside Quaternius', and beard nudges.
- `underCover(hat, hair, triangles)` hides the hair a hat covers (above its brim, within its reach, followed around a tilted brim), so hair no longer pokes through hats; MakeHuman's CC0 beards and moustaches (Bodyparts 05) in the pack (`?v=6`), bound to the body like clothes, so they sit on any face. The builder's sun takes `shadowNormalBias: 0.008`: the default thinned a body's shadow.
- `hairShading` (`hair-shading`): hair coloured by a BASE and a HIGHLIGHT colour, the way a colourist describes it: a material plugin tints the texture with the base and leans its brighter strands to the highlight (and the strand sheen takes it), with `desaturate` for libraries whose hair textures are already coloured (MakeHuman's), so one pair of colours works on every library. `HAIR_COLOURS` are paired presets, natural and dyed. The builder's hair colour is a preset menu and two colour pickers, replacing the light, red and dye sliders.
- Clothing materials. `clothShading` (`cloth-shading`) puts a fabric on a garment (`FABRICS`: cotton, denim, wool, linen, velvet, silk, satin, synthetic, leather, rubber, as roughness and PBR sheen) and a recolour over its texture (read as grey, tinted, blended by `amount`; 0 keeps the texture's colours). `proxyMaterial(scene, proxy, look)` draws one of a garment's alternate textures; the pack (`?v=7`) carries MakeHuman's CC0 colourways for the elegant and casual suits. The builder has look, fabric, colour and recolour per outfit, shoes and hat.
- Separate garments and accessories in the human pack (`?v=8`), each with a `slot` (outfit, top, bottom, shoes, hat, glasses, gloves; one of each worn at a time): MakeHuman's CC0 shirts, pants, skirts, suits, shoes, hats, glasses and gloves. The builder wears one per slot (an outfit replaces a top and bottom) and edits whichever is chosen. `inflate` pushes a proxy out from a point: the builder's hats sit 12 mm out from the skull, over the hair, and `underCover` drops only hair wholly under a hat (dropping any triangle across the brim left bare scalp below it).
- `studioEnvironment(scene)`, a procedural studio (sky, horizon, floor) as the scene's environment, so gloss and metal have something to reflect; metal and gloss finishes in `FABRICS` (vinyl, foil, chrome, brushed steel, gold, copper, silver lamé; `metallic`, and a `tint` for finishes that are a colour); a `mask` slot and MakeHuman's CC0 sci-fi suits, helmets and masks in the pack (`?v=9`).
- FACES THAT MOVE (`human-expression`). MakeHuman's 59 CC0 face pose units (lids, jaw, lips, mouth corners, brows, cheeks, tongue) are baked into the human pack (`?v=12`) as shape targets (`expression/<Unit>`): its face rig posed per unit and the base skinned with its own weights, offline. At runtime they are morph targets on the body, the eyelashes, the teeth and tongue and whatever is bound to the face (a beard follows the jaw): `faceDeltas`, `humanExpressions` (weights in named LAYERS, summed per unit), `blinker` (a person's rhythm, sometimes twice), `lidsFollow` (upper lids follow the eyes up and down), `lipSync` (any Web Audio source: loudness opens the jaw, bright sound widens, dark rounds), `babble` (talking with no audio), `VISEMES`. `proxyDelta` moves a bound proxy with the face. The pack also carries MakeHuman's teeth and tongue, and the builder wears them. The builder has a Face section: blink, talk, mic (lip sync from your microphone), smile, brows, frown.
- `select3d({ stayOpen: true })` keeps its list open after a pick, until it is closed or something behind it is pressed, for trying options one after another; the character builder's style, clothes and clip menus use it.
- Stubble. `stubbleTint(colours, mask, amount, skinRgb, hairRgb)` darkens the skin toward the hair colour where a mask says the beard grows; the character builder makes the mask from MakeHuman's full beard fitted to the body (below the cheekbones, faded) and has a stubble slider.
- Chest and bust controls in `MacroBody` (all optional, 0.5 neutral): `chestDepth`, `pecs`, and `bustSize` / `bustFirmness`, which blend MakeHuman's breast targets across gender, age, muscle and weight like the macros and apply in proportion to how female the body is. The human pack (`?v=15`) carries the targets; the character builder has the four sliders.

## Changed

- A neckline drawn level (`cutGarment`, the builder's Tailor) is cut 15° lower in front than behind, as most are: hm08's neck leans forward, so a ring level in the world rose toward the front. A V or a scoop is cut as drawn.
- `skinAlbedo` (skin-tone) is paler and whiter at the fair end, and `redness` is stronger toward both ends of its dial (subtle near 0.5): 0 is a drained grey-white, 1 is flushed. A recipe at a fair tone or an extreme redness looks different.
- Collapsible sections in the settings panel (and `foldSections`) open one at a time, as an accordion: opening one closes the others, and all may be closed. Of several declared `open: true`, the first wins. `panelSections="folds"` (`mode: 'folds'`) keeps the old behaviour, several open at once; the rig tool and effect tool use it.
- `touchOrbit` makes the wheel and a trackpad pinch zoom by a share of the camera's distance (`WHEEL_SHARE`, 1%, as Babylon's `wheelDeltaPercentage`) instead of Babylon's fixed step, which moved about 0.8 m a notch and went from the default view to far too close in one or two. It applies to `<tosi-b3d>`'s default camera, `orbitCam` and any orbit camera given to it; a page that set `wheelPrecision` or `wheelDeltaPercentage` keeps its own. The character builder's camera stays between 0.3 m and 10 m.
- `readGarment` reads every mesh in the file except the body helper as the garment (an object added in Blender, a collar or a plate, was dropped), and returns them as `parts`; `writeGarmentGlb` / `writeGarmentObj` write a garment's parts as separate objects.
- `clothShading` colours an untextured garment (one cut from the body) by its albedo; it only recoloured a texture before.
- In a headset's chase view, `b3d-aircraft`'s HUD is an overlay like the flat one: face on, centred on the aircraft and at its distance, so both eyes see it where they see the craft, drawn over the scene, covering the angle the flat overlay covers, with no horizon. It used to hang ahead of the craft level with its heading and ring it in the world. `b3d-hud`'s `attachInScene` takes `onTop` for this.
- `stubbleTint` is about twice as dark at full: a shadow going most of the way to a darkened, slightly cool hair colour (it was barely visible, worst on light-brown hair).
- The character builder's hair colours are two `colorPicker3d` rows (a swatch that opens a picker with named presets); a base preset brings its usual highlight.
- The character builder: beards and moustaches are separate choices and MakeHuman's (Quaternius' facial hair, drawn for its own stylised mouth, drooped and tilted on ours); MakeHuman's hair and brows are the defaults and listed first; hair, brows and beards keep their texture's alpha (pack `?v=10`).
- Clothes TUCK the skin they cover rather than cutting it: `coverBody` drops only triangles wholly under a garment and draws the covered skin 6 mm in (`tuck`), so a neckline no longer shows holes where a garment's edge and its listed vertices disagree (`coveredTriangles` takes `mode: 'all'`). `underCover` likewise tucks hair in under a hat (`tuck`).
- Hair colour is normalised by each texture's own measured brightness (`HairShadingPlugin.mean`), so a preset is the same colour on every library's hair; MakeHuman's hair is rougher and reflects its surroundings less (it shone like wet plastic); highlights are subtler. Skin reflects the environment faintly (`environmentIntensity` 0.3, roughness 0.5): very dark skin looked polished.
- Clothes are categorised by where they sit on the body, not by the pack they came in (pack `?v=14`): hoods are hats, the viking boots, pants and tunic are separate, shorts and miniskirts are bottoms. Two new slots: `bodysuit` (a base layer) and `armour` (an overlay, worn over anything; `humanProxy`'s `lift` sets it 5 mm out along its surface so it does not fight what is beneath).
- No wall clock in game code. The system clock is read only in `clock` (`realNow`, `wallMs`, `wallDate`), and a test fails on a read anywhere else. The exploder's debris, the biome shader's drift and the stars' twinkle now run on the scene's clock (`sceneSeconds`), so they stop in a pause and follow `timeScale`.
- Physics is repeatable. `JoltPlugin` steps Jolt by a fixed step (1/60 s, `setTimeStep`) as many times as WORLD time covers (`sceneDelta`: zero while paused, scaled by `timeScale`), carrying the remainder; it used to step by however much real time had passed, so no run repeated and physics carried on through a pause. Kinematic bodies are given their target before each step. The sky's day cycle (`realtimeScale`) runs on world time too: it stops in a pause and follows `timeScale`.
- Controllables (bipeds, vehicles, aircraft) step by world time (`sceneDelta`), so slow motion slows them too; input stays real-time. While the world is not running, a controllable still reads its input and discards it, so nothing accumulated during a pause (a wheel's scroll) arrives on resume.
- The character builder has a gridded floor that takes the sun's shadow, and an eye colour slider under its own heading.
- Hair is carried from the head it was modelled on, skin to skin (`headScalp` now warps the library's own heads, carried in the hairstyles library as of `?v=2`; `shellWarp`, `applyWarp`, `headRegion`), instead of fitting a buzz cut to the scalp, which sank every style by its own thickness. Women's styles use Quaternius' female head, brows are placed from the eyes, moustaches above the lip, and `nudge` adjusts a style by hand. `headScalp`'s arguments and `HeadScalp` changed; `humanHair` and `placeHair` take the piece's `head` (`library.headFor(name)`).

## Fixed

- A garment cut (`cutGarment`, the builder's Tailor) that goes round a limb is now square to the limb: a sleeve ending on the forearm was cut along the outline's line, which crosses hm08's forward-reaching forearms at a long slant. Cuts round the body and the neck, and round a limb already within 30° of square to the line (a leg under a level hem), still follow the line.
- Clothes in the character builder no longer show nipples: they are fitted over the body with its nipples smoothed (`smoothUnder` in proxy-fit, with the pack's new `nipples` region; pack `?v=17`). The skin keeps them.
- Closing a popup from the settings panel (its ×, or a press on its title bar) no longer closes the panel too. The press was never marked as taken by a panel, so the panel's close-on-a-background-press saw it.
- A popup hung from a panel whose plane had been stretched to new content (the flat settings panel, after a section opened) took the stretch: it came out up to half again too tall. It now keeps its opener's size and its own shape.
- The Tailor's outline view showed the body the page loaded with, not the one you shaped, so on a different body (a woman's, a shorter one) an outline drawn at the neck cut through the face. It now shows the current body each time it opens.
- Skin's back-light (skin-shading) lit the whole body when seen against the sun, not just the thin parts: Babylon drops a vertex colour's alpha, where the thinness rides, unless the mesh blends by vertex alpha. The plugin now carries it in its own varying, so only ears, fingers and toes glow. It is also narrower: it shows only when looking nearly into the sun (a power of 8, was 3), and `skinThinness` counts up to 2.2 cm as thin (was 3.5), so a fist, a palm or the sole of a foot no longer glows; ears and finger edges still do, at about half the old strength (`backlight` 1.2, was 2.5).
- A trackpad pinch zoomed far too little after the wheel became proportional: it arrives as many small ctrl-wheel steps, which the wheel's 1% share per notch barely moved. `touchOrbit` now scales the distance by the pinch (`PINCH_SHARE`: doubling the fingers' spread about halves it); a mouse wheel is unchanged.
- The character builder's body stood 1 to 4 cm into the floor: it was grounded at rest, but a retargeted clip carries the feet lower (Idle by about 4 cm). The clip is now sampled over a cycle when it starts and whenever the clothes change, and the body stands on its lowest point.
- `outlineField3d` leaves 4 cm of room around the body, so an outline can reach past it. Points were held to the silhouette's own edges, so socks could not be drawn below the soles: the sole was left out of the cut and showed through an open bottom.
- `mirrorOutline` keeps a shape that already crosses the centre line (by more than 2 cm each side) as it is. Mirrored, it lay on itself, and the cut ragged its edges.
- `readGarment` fails on a broken OBJ with the line and what is wrong (a vertex that is not three numbers, a face index that is 0, not a number or past the end, a face with fewer than three corners) instead of returning NaN positions. A `.gltf` JSON file, a binary file that is not a GLB (an FBX) and a file with only the body each say so. The builder's Tailor shows the message under **import…**.
- `writeGarmentGlb` always writes normals (smooth ones when the garment has none), and `writeGarmentObj` marks each object smooth. Without them Blender imported the garment flat-shaded, split every face, and sent it back faceted with six times the vertices.
- A headset no longer hangs mid-flight when it switches to hand tracking. Babylon parents the topmost ancestor of the hand mesh beneath the XR rig, and with the rig riding an aircraft that ancestor was the aircraft (or its chase anchor), which was then its own ancestor. Every node the rig hangs from now refuses such a parent. `refuseOwnAncestors(node)` (b3d-utils) guards a node and everything above it.
- In a headset, the death and pause modals sit at your own eye height, a little below and facing you. They assumed a standing 1.6 m, so seated they came up above you, tilted towards a point over your head.
- `b3d-aircraft` puts its HUD away when it crashes in a scene with `<tosi-b3d-death>`. A wreck stops updating the HUD, so in a headset's chase view it went on hanging over the wreck as it fell.
- `<tosi-b3d>`'s `timeScale` slows Babylon's own clocks too: animation groups (`scene.animationTimeScale`) and particle ageing (each system's `updateSpeed`) are the app's value times `timeScale`, and particles stop in a pause. A consumer that multiplied `speedRatio` by `timeScale` to work around it should drop that, or slow motion compounds.
- In a headset, the `body` frame takes the piloting recenter as the `eye` frame does, so panels on it (the death and pause modals among them) come up ahead of you. Sat in a cockpit facing away from the headset's own forward, they appeared that far to one side, which read as no respawn panel at all. The chase view also waits for a real head pose before taking its forward, as the cockpit already did.
- In a headset, a controller press on a moving vehicle reaches the system bar and other `ui`/`modal` panels. A press carried the previous frame's ray, which stopped short of a panel that had moved on with the vehicle (the button lit, the click was lost); it is now aimed from the controller's current pose.
- `b3d-hud` tracks a radar contact only inside its ring. A contact in the corners of the HUD's square was drawn there, outside the circle; it is now pinned to the outer ring along its bearing, like any other contact off the HUD. `hudPointFromUV` takes an optional `radius` for this.
- In a headset, panels on the `ui` and `modal` layers (the system bar among them) no longer trail a moving vehicle by a frame. They were placed before the vehicle moved, which left them most of a metre behind at flying speed, so they jumped around. They are now placed again just before drawing. `freshWorldMatrix(node)` (b3d-utils) gives a node's world matrix with its ancestors updated first.
- The character builder's stubble covers the upper lip (the moustache's coverage is added to the full beard's, which has none) and the throat and sides of the neck (carried 5 cm down from the beard's edge, fading), and leaves the lips bare.
- The owl shows on the flat system bar whenever its panel has anything in it, including only the icon bar (Pause). A scene with no settings rows of its own (the Biped Playground) had no owl flat, though it had one in a headset.
- Auto-rig: fingers a mesh does not show lie on the nearest one it does, so a mitten hand is aimed along the mitten (omnidude's hands curled into hooks).
- `<tosi-b3d-light>` applies its attributes when its light is made. Before, a light whose element rendered before the scene was ready kept Babylon's defaults (intensity 1, a black ground colour) whatever it was given, so a page that hit it (the character builder did) now gets the fill it asked for. The demos that set a very dim fill (colour picker, beacon, solar system, planet) render exactly as before: they were not hit.
- Hair is matched to the head it was modelled on by how closely it hugs that head (the crown rule put Balding on the wrong one), and every vertex keeps its height above the skin (`skinGaps`, `keepHeight`), so beards are as thick on the chin as on their own head; a face is fitted with one scale (`fitToScalp`'s `scaling: 'uniform'`), since a stylised face's flatter depth squashed beards back.
- Every orbit camera given to `setActiveCamera` gets `touchOrbit`'s view controls, so shift-drag (and a trackpad's two-finger drag) pans in demos that build their own camera (the character builder, auto-rig, spring bones and others could not pan on a laptop); `touchOrbit` is once per camera.
- An orbit camera's zoom stops short of its target (`touchOrbit` sets `lowerRadiusLimit` to twice the near plane when a page has not set one): a two-finger scroll could zoom through zero and flip the view.
- The human pack publishes its textures (they 404'd on the CDN, and clothes drew Babylon's missing-texture checkerboard).
- A character builder body stands on its soles: `humanRig(…, { triangles })` puts the floor at the skin's lowest point (the foot's joint cubes are inside the foot, and the body sank by an ankle's height), and worn shoes lift it by their sole.
- The face moves with the head (`stiffenHead`: skin above the head joint weighted wholly to it, blended over 4 cm), so the eyelids no longer slide over the eyeballs when a clip moves the neck; a moustache's lower edge sits 4 mm above the lip.
- Faces no longer shear when a clip turns the neck: `stiffenHead` now makes the whole face rigid with the head (the jaw, chin and mouth, in front of the head joint, which sits at about nose height on hm08), not only the skin above the joint. Idle's look-around showed it most.
- Skin no longer shows through trousers and skirts at the knees and thighs: `coverBody({ drawn })` finds skin a garment covers by geometry (`coveredBy`: garment surface just outside it along its normal), not only its listed vertices, and tucks lower garments' skin deeper. Hair colours tint only hair, brows and beards (the teeth came out brown).
- Closing a popup no longer sometimes closes the panel behind it: a press on a popup's close is claimed, so the parent never sees it (only the close: claiming a drag's press broke dragging and dismissed everything). A `select3d`'s menu is as wide as its longest option (at least 220, at most 420), and a long value is ellipsized instead of running into the row's caption.
- The lower chest no longer narrows when a clip lowers the arms: `armsOffTorso` moves arm and collarbone weight off the ribcage below the armpit to the spine (bone heat let the arms claim the ribcage's sides, since MakeHuman's rest pose holds them close; Idle lost 5 to 6 cm of width there). The builder's clothes editor shows `look` only for items that have colourways.
- Tucking under clothes is gentler: only body garments tuck skin they cover by geometry (not glasses, hats or masks, which pulled the eyelids in), at most 10 mm, faded in over 3 cm from the covered skin's edge (`coverBody`'s `fade`), so a cuff no longer pinches the wrist. Glasses' lenses are blended glass (pack `?v=13`). Eyes look together or not at all (past the limit, both look ahead) and follow the active camera, so in a headset they find you. The palest skin tone is paler. `EyeTexture.setIrisColour`; the builder's eye colour is a colour picker with presets.
- `<tosi-b3d-manipulator>`'s handles follow a move drag instead of staying where the drag began until release; they still ignore a target's parent animation while you drag.
- In flat view, a popup opened partly off the screen is moved back on (its corners projected, the overshoot turned into a move at its depth), or centred when it is too big to fit; a headset is left alone.
- A panel's popups on a page (its DOM layer) are mounted in the document body, not beside the panel, so a clipping container (a doc page's demo frame, a scrolling sidebar) no longer cuts them off; they still scroll with the page and close when their panel leaves it. `useDomLayer(container)` still mounts in the container given.
- Retargeting drives the middle of a three-bone spine (new role `midSpine`; UAL's `spine_02`). Without it a clip's mid-back bend was dropped and the bones either side bent harder, creasing the lower back in a crouch.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.11.5/

# 0.11.4

## Added

- **A character creator, on MakeHuman's CC0 body** (CHARACTER-DESIGN.md). Try it on the [character builder](/character-builder/) page: a person walking while you reshape them. The data is a **human pack** on the CDN (`makehuman/hm08/`), loaded with `loadHumanPack`.
  - **Body**: `macroWeights` / `morphHuman` turn gender, age, muscle, weight, height, proportions and an ancestry mix into a body, in about a millisecond.
  - **Skeleton**: `humanRig` places UAL's 65 joints from the body's own joint cubes, and bone heat binds the skin once per base, so UAL's clips play on any body shape (`buildRig`, `retargetClip`). `humanBody` draws a body unrigged.
  - **Skin**: one dial from very fair to very dark through the Monk Skin Tone Scale, plus redness (`skinMaterial`, `skinAlbedo`); lips tinted from it over the pack's `lips` region, no UVs needed (`lipTint`, `lipAlbedo`).
  - **Eyes**: `humanFace` adds eyes and eyelashes that fit every body (they are the base mesh's own helper vertices); the iris is drawn in code with a colour dial (`eyeTexture`, `irisColor`); `eyeGaze` aims the eyes at a world point with small saccades.
  - **Hair**: Quaternius' CC0 hairstyles, beards and eyebrows, modelled for another head, fitted to any body (`loadHairLibrary`, `headScalp`, `humanHair`); tinted by `hairColor` (black to platinum, plus red). The pure fit is `fitToScalp` / `conformOutside`.

## Fixed

- **Retargeting no longer lines a character's collarbones up with the clip's.** A collarbone's rest direction is the body's shape, like the spine's; where two rigs differed (UAL's runs back to the shoulder, MakeHuman's lies flat), every clip shrugged the shoulders.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1266.7 KB raw / 433.9 KB gz, +1.67% on 0.11.3 (the character creator).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.11.4/

# 0.11.3

## Added

- **`blendSeconds` on `<tosi-b3d-biped>`** (default 0.25): how long each animation change eases over. `0` cuts.
- The panel page's system-bar demo has a "New journal entry" button that blinks the Journal button (`attention()`).

## Changed

- **The biped eases every animation change** instead of cutting: walk to run, standing to crouch, the gun coming up and going down, aim up/level/down. The blend is timed, so it lasts the same at any frame rate. A crouch at rest plays a transition clip if the states name one (`sneakEnter` / `sneakExit`, e.g. UAL's `Crouch_Enter` / `Crouch_Exit`); the defaults have none, so it blends.
- **The sun's shadow bias defaults are now `shadowBias` 0.002 and `shadowNormalBias` 0.04**, which clears the fine acne stripes on plain lit surfaces. If a small caster's shadow detaches, set them lower on your `<tosi-b3d-sun>`.
- **In the biped mapping, clicking the right stick (R3) toggles the weapon**, as the right bumper does. The playground's glass pad shows both stick clicks.

## Fixed

- **XR thumbsticks have the hardware pad's 0.15 per-axis deadzone**, so a stick pushed sideways to turn no longer drifts the biped's look pitch (its aim). Raising the weapon now levels the aim in a headset too.
- In the glass gamepad demo, the cube moves away from you on left stick up, and the readout sits top centre, clear of the system bar.

# 0.11.2

## Added

- **A new glass gamepad**, laid out like a pair of VR controllers held flat: on each side a trigger, bumper, stick and two face buttons (X and Y on the left, A and B on the right, in Xbox colours), with view and menu between them at the bottom. It is one SVG sheet (`static/glass-gamepad.svg`) that the pad cuts into three clusters along the bottom; on a narrow screen the centre cluster tucks in between the others when it fits and sits above them when it does not.
- **Stick clicks (L3, R3)**: `leftStickPress` and `rightStickPress` on `VirtualGamepad`. The glass pad has a button under each stick, a hardware pad's buttons 10 and 11 feed them, and so does clicking a thumbstick in a headset. On the biped, a left-stick click sneaks (as L3 does in GTA V).
- **View and menu on the headset's system bar**, when the glass pad's `controls` name them. `pad.pulse('view' | 'menu')` presses one from code.

## Changed

- **The glass gamepad hides its d-pad unless you name it** (`controls="…,dpad"`). View and menu are still shown by default, but will become opt-in in a future release: name them if you use them.
- **In a headset, clicking a thumbstick is a stick press**, not view (right) or menu (left). Y still toggles the camera view, and the system bar carries view and menu when a scene asks for them.
- **A hardware pad's view and menu buttons (8 and 9) now reach `view` and `menu`**; they were read but dropped.
- The glass pad's `clusters.top` is now `clusters.center` (`top` still works).

## Fixed

- **The full-screen button on an iPhone.** iPhone Safari has no Fullscreen API for anything but video, so the button hid itself. It now maximises the scene instead: in the top layer as a popover (iOS 17+, so a doc page's card cannot trap it), filling what is visible.
- **The glass gamepad demo goes full screen with its pad**, which is now inside the scene as `gamepad: true` mounts it; beside the scene it was left behind.

# 0.11.1

## Fixed

- **The glass gamepad draws on your site** (0.11.0 docs review). Its default art was fetched from `/gamepad-left.svg`, `/gamepad-right.svg` and `/gamepad-top.svg`, which our doc site serves from `static/` and the package does not ship, so on an adopter's site the fetches 404'd and `gamepad` mounted nothing. Attribute tables are complete for `<tosi-b3d>` (35), the biped (33), water, skybox, planet, clouds, lamp, launcher, turret, radar, glass gamepad and others. The changelog is one page per version, and it and Migration are under [Upgrading](/upgrading/). No code changed.

# 0.11.0

**0.11 in one paragraph.** Any character plays the Universal Animation
Library: `retarget` reads which bone is which across UE, Mixamo, Kenney and
Blender names and transfers clips across A- and T-poses; a mesh with no
skeleton is auto-rigged from eight markers (`fitSkeleton`, fingers, mittens
and tails found from its shape, `boneHeat` binding, `buildRig`); hair and
tails hang on spring bones; the rig tool does it all in the browser and saves
a recipe (`applyRigRecipe`), and mounts in a host's scene (`mountRigTool`).
Effects are particles, light and sound as layers on one clock
(`<tosi-b3d-effect>`, presets from volcano to sparks, procedural sprites and
voices), edited in the effect tool (`mountEffectTool`). Around them:
`inspectView` (held orthographic views), `seamMaterial`, `barMenu`, slider
stops, landform schemas, the biped's sprint. Nothing was removed; see
Migration.md for the behaviours that changed. Size over the 0.10 line: see
the release's Size line.

## Added

- **System panels from code, and a button that asks to be looked at** (#3436, Manta's objectives list): `<tosi-b3d-panel>` has `show()`, `hide()`, `toggle()` and `isOpen`, and fires `paneltoggle` (`detail.open`) whenever it opens or closes, by code or by its button, so a list can put itself away after a while. `attention(ms?)` blinks its button on the system bar, flat and in a headset (and on the HTML lozenge with `flat-ui="dom"`). Before the scene is up, `show()` means open at start.
- **`systempanels` on `<tosi-b3d>`** (#3436): fires (bubbling) on every system panel opened or closed, with `detail.panel`, `detail.shown`, `detail.byUser` (opened by its button, not by code) and `detail.open` (every open one, `{ panel, byUser }`), so the game decides what it means: `e.detail.open.some((p) => p.byUser)` pauses while the person has one up. A headset session starting or ending is reported once, after it, with `panel` null. `paneltoggle` also carries `byUser`.

## Changed

- **The glass gamepad stands aside only for system panels the person opened** (#3436). One opened by its button hides the pad as before; one opened by code (`show()`, `open` at start) leaves it up, because it is up while they play and on a phone hiding the pad took the controls away. Give one that stays open a `screenAnchor` clear of the pad.

## Fixed

- **The effect tool's `listen from` works in a headset** (Tonio). Flat it pulls the camera back; in a headset you are the camera, so it did nothing. There the effect now moves along the ground, on the line from you to it, to that distance (on entering the session too, so the sound's lateness on the status line is true), and goes back when the session ends.
- **A tool's settings panel shows its changes in a headset** (Tonio, the rig tool in VR: picking a face stopped the clip, but the animate toggle still showed it on, so turning it off and on again was needed to play). `refreshScenePanel()` rebuilt only the flat panel; it now rebuilds the headset's too. The rig tool's doc says what `view` means in a headset (you are the camera: it switches between still and playing) and names the faces it takes.
- **The system bar keeps working after the glass pad** (Tonio, in a headset's flat browser: open and close the inventory, drag the pad's stick twice, and the bar stopped answering until a click elsewhere on the page). Babylon keeps one canvas slot per touch (`navigator.maxTouchPoints`, else 2) and gives a touch it sees move without a press a slot retroactively; when that touch was released on the pad (which captures its own pointer), the canvas never heard it, and with every slot held Babylon ignored new presses ("Max number of touches exceeded"). A touch or pen released anywhere off the canvas is now cancelled on the canvas too, which frees its slot.
- **Effect sounds stop when you leave** (Tonio, in the headset: leaving the effect tool page left its sound playing). A voice lives in the page's audio context, not the scene, and a scene that went away never stopped its voices, so they looped on. Now a disposed scene stops every effect voice it was playing, and the effect audio is suspended while the tab is hidden (a hidden tab draws no frames, so nothing would fade a voice out).
- **The pause panel says "Continue in VR" only where there is VR** (#3431, Manta): with `enterXrOnResume="on"` it said so on an iPhone and a laptop too, where resuming just continues. It now needs the headset helper as well, which is built only when `immersive-vr` is supported.
- **A biped's sprint ends when it stops** (0.11.0 gate): the sprint is held down to 70% of full speed so a trigger near the line does not flicker, but the flag was only updated while running forward, so a stop, swim or sidestep left it set and the next run went straight into the sprint at 75%. The choice is now the pure `forwardGait` (`tosijs-3d/gait`), tested for entering, holding, leaving and a rig with no sprint clip.
- **An effect voice that yielded to the budget stays quiet** (0.11.0 gate): over `effectVoices`, the quietest voice was stopped and then started again on the next frame, as loud as before and so stopped again: a new WebAudio graph every frame for each voice over budget, and for a `url` voice a fetch. It now comes back when the pool has room or when it would clearly outrank the quietest voice playing; turning its layer off and on starts it fresh. A NullEngine test counts the starts (21 where 9 belong, before the fix).
- **`seamOverlay`'s twin casts wherever the mesh did** (0.11.0 gate): the mesh is hidden while its twin is drawn, so it stopped casting and the twin never started. The twin now takes the mesh's place in every shadow map it was in (and receives as it did), and gives it back on dispose; the rig tool's own workaround for the twin is gone.
- **`<tosi-b3d-effect>` builds its player once on mount** (0.11.0 gate): `sceneReady` started it and then `render()`, which starts any effect whose key is new, built it again. Releasing a scene's effect pool also removes its scene-dispose observer, and a frame with no effect lights skips ranking them.
- **The water readiness report stays quiet in a hidden tab** (nothing draws there, so nothing is ready) and says how many frames had drawn and whether a headset session was on.
- **`strandPoints`, `strandPath`, `setStrandPath`, `pathLength`, `quadDiagonals` and `viewSpanAt` are in the barrel**, as this changelog's entries for them implied.
- **The README names the 0.11 features** (0.11.0 gate): retargeting, auto-rig, spring bones and the rig tool; effects and the effect tool. Migration.md has a 0.10 → 0.11 section (nothing removed; the behaviours that changed).
- **A water that is not ready says so** (#3335): eight seconds after its scene is up, a water surface that is missing, disposed, out of the scene, not ready to draw or failing to compile posts what it found to the debug sink (`water-not-ready`), so the next first-visit sighting of missing water can be read rather than guessed at.
- **A sun's shadows follow the camera, whatever order things happen in** (#3420, Tonio: "I'd really like shadows to just work"). Babylon's cascaded shadow generator works out its cascade splits from the camera's near and far planes once, and again only when its own settings change; a camera change never told it, and its `shadowMaxZ` setter ignores a value the camera of the moment does not admit. So a sun made while the camera was unusual kept that camera's splits for good: made during an orthographic face view (whose near plane sits behind the camera), the splits were NaN and the whole scene rendered black, in perspective too. Switching cameras or entering a headset left stale splits the same way. `<tosi-b3d-sun>` now checks, just before its shadow map renders, whether the camera, its near or far plane or its projection changed, and if so splits again and re-applies `shadowMaxZ`; a near plane at or behind the camera is never split from (a small positive one stands in, and the camera gets its own back before anything draws). `cascadesFollowCamera(generator, shadowMaxZ)` does the same for a generator of your own. Reproduced headless in a minimal scene (a late sun, a face view, back to perspective: black before, a shadow after); unit-tested against a stand-in generator.
- **The rig tool casts shadows** (#3420): the standalone page declares a sun in its scene, as the playground does, and hands the character (and, in a face view, its seam twin) to the sun's shadow generator. `inspectStage({ light: false })` leaves out the stage's key light for a scene with a sun of its own; `seamOverlay` returns its twin as `mesh`. Hosted, the figure is in the host's lighting. The failures behind #3420 turned out to be the camera, not the order (see the entry above).

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1230.0 KB raw / 421.9 KB gz, +0.41% on 0.10.20 (system panels from code, attention, the per-change systempanels event, and the gate's fixes).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.11.0/

# 0.10.20

## Fixed

- **An effect's SVG picture that finishes loading after its scene let it go no longer throws** (regression in 0.10.19, found by ensemble): releasing a scene's sprites with its last effect (new in 0.10.19) could dispose a picture texture before its image loaded, and the late `onload` drew on it ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'clearRect')", uncaught). It now draws nothing; a sprite with no 2D canvas is likewise undrawn rather than a throw. A test releases the sprites before the load. A hotfix from v0.10.19: this is the only change.
