# 0.10.19

## Added

- **Auto-rig finds the fingers a mesh has** (Tonio: the skinny weasel has three fingers and a thumb, and they were not rigged). Palm down in a T-pose, fingers are separate only from above, so `fitSkeleton` looks down on each hand (`MeshQuery.fromAbove()`): slices across the hand from the tips back find the fingers as separate runs, where they join is the knuckle, and a prong that reaches forward near the wrist is the thumb. Each joint sits along the real finger at the middle of its thickness, and found fingers take the skin (the hand then runs to the knuckles). `rig.fingers` says which were found; the rest are placed by proportion as before and take none. The skinny weasel gets index, middle, ring and thumb; omnidude's mitten an index and a thumb; the chunky weasel's paws none.
- **A strand is laid along a path** (Tonio: map out the tail or the ponytail, not one stub, and choose how many links). `StrandSpringRecipe.path` is the line it follows at rest, root first; its `segments` links are spaced evenly along it (`strandPoints`). In the rig tool every point is an orange handle you drag, `+ point` adds one beyond the tip, `− point` takes one away, `links` sets the count, and the chosen strand marks where each link falls. A straight strand still reads as before, and `setStrandPath` keeps `offset`, `length`, `yawDeg` and `pitchDeg` true to a path for a reader that knows nothing of paths.
- **The rig tool snaps its view** to a face of the character (see `inspectView` below), and its API gains `view` and `play(clip)`. A bone chain spring shows every link, not only its first bone, and an auto-rigged tail has a `tail links` slider.
- **`inspectView(camera)`: front, back, side, top and bottom views, orthographic and held** (Tonio, #3419). It turns an `ArcRotateCamera` orthographic and pins it to a face, so a drag no longer orbits and is free for what is under the pointer; pan and zoom still work. The camera's own `radius` is the zoom: each frame the orthographic box is what a perspective camera at that radius would show, so leaving the view leaves the scene the same size. The near plane moves behind the camera, so zooming in close never cuts the subject open.
- **Panels and the system bar work under an orthographic camera.** They were placed from the camera's field of view, so they shrank to a stamp. `viewSpanAt(camera, d, w, h)` in frame-panel answers both kinds of camera.
- **`barMenu(...)`: a system-bar button that is a menu**: one press opens a short list under the bar, a choice closes it, flat and in a headset. `viewMenu(inspect, scene, options)` is the camera one: it picks the face or `perspective`, and its faces, labels and whether it stays in the perspective view can all be configured.
- **`seamMaterial` / `withBarycentrics`: a mesh drawn as its polygons**: a flat fill (desaturated pink by default) with soft white edges, drawn in the fragment shader from barycentric coordinates, so the edges are smooth and the same width in pixels at any zoom; they fade where triangles shrink to a few pixels. `seamOverlay(mesh)` draws a twin in the mesh's place (its own unshared geometry, the same skeleton), so the mesh itself is untouched.
- **The rig tool's view is its pose** (Tonio): standing at rest it is orthographic (front by default) and drawn as its polygons; `perspective` plays the clip. The camera on the system bar picks either, and the animate toggle moves the view the other way. Seen from a side, the mannequin stands beside the character rather than in front of it.
- **Auto-rig: a hand with no fingers apart gets a mitten and a thumb** (Tonio, the space marine's claws). Seen from above such a hand is one blob, so no finger was found and four were placed by proportion, in the air past a claw that hooks down. Now its middle line is followed slice by slice from the wrist (the middle of the flesh in height and depth across each slice), so one chain (the index, as Mixamo's mittens have) runs down the hook to its tip. A thumb that grows straight out of the palm's edge, with no gap, is found as a bump on the palm's front edge. The chunky weasel's paws get a mitten each, so a paw curls on a grip.
- **The seam material hides the diagonals that split quads** (Tonio): `quadDiagonals` finds the quads again (two triangles sharing the longest edge of both, nearly flat together) and that edge is not drawn. `withBarycentrics(mesh, { quads: false })` draws every edge.
- **The biped sprints**: near full speed it plays the rig's `sprint` state (UAL's `Sprint_Loop`, already mapped by `ualAnimationStates()` but never played) instead of the jog sped up, held until the speed drops back a little so an analog trigger does not flicker between them. A rig without a sprint clip jogs as before (Tonio).
- **`inspectStage(scene)`**: a neutral floor to look at a model on (light grey, ruled every metre and faintly every quarter) and a key light. The rig tool stands on it. Shadows are not on yet (see #3420).
- **The rig tool's mannequin is a ghost** (translucent, so it compares without competing), and its toggle is called `mannequin` (it was `compare`). The glTF loader marks materials opaque, which `visibility` alone cannot override, so they are set to blend. The clip picker lists loops first.
- **The seam material can receive shadows**: `seamOverlay`'s twin receives them, and `shade` (now 0.45 by default) is the part of the fill that light, and so shadow, reaches. Fill and line colours are options.
- **The effect tool mounts in a host's scene** on the same contract (tosijs-3d#122, for ensemble's `effect` piece): `mountEffectTool(b3d, { recipe, target, files, stage, camera })`, `change` and `commit` with the recipe, a system panel when hosted, `unmount()` that returns every count. `effectTool()` is the same tool in a scene of its own.
- **A scene's last effect player takes the shared parts with it**: the per-scene driver observer, pooled lights and sprite textures are released when the last `EffectPlayer` in a scene is disposed (they used to stay until the scene went), and made again by the next effect.
- **The rig tool mounts in a host's scene** (tosijs-3d#122, for ensemble's `figure` piece): `mountRigTool(b3d, { models, recipe, files, stage, camera })` returns a handle firing `change` (every edit) and `commit` (one per finished gesture) with a copy of the recipe, its `api`, and `unmount()`. `files: false` drops save, load, copy and the browser's working copy; `stage: false` adds no floor or light; a given camera is driven and restored exactly (angles, distance, target, projection, limits). Hosted, its panel is a system panel. Unmount (safe twice, and mid-load) returns the scene's mesh, material, texture, node, skeleton, animation, observer and panel counts to where they were, checked headless. `rigTool()` is now the same tool mounted in a scene of its own, with `change` and `commit` dispatched on the element.

## Changed

- **A character's head is no longer tipped back by its own neck** (Tonio: the weasels looked up). Retargeting lined every bone up with the source's rest direction, which is right for a limb (an A-pose against a T-pose) and wrong for the body's axis: the weasel's neck leans forward to a chin under its snout, and pulled upright to match the mannequin's, it tipped the head up by about 14° through every clip. The hips, spine, chest, neck and head now take the clip's turn as it is.
- **A tap on the body no longer reassigns a bone on its own** in the rig tool (Tonio: on an iPhone the weasels' heads sank into their chests and a tail pointed forward). The chosen role starts as the head, and any press that did not travel set the head's bone to whatever was under it. On a phone that was every attempt to orbit, and the tool remembered it. Now a tap sets a bone only right after a dot, the role or `clicking sets` was chosen, and only once. `start over` clears a recipe that was already changed.
- **The weasels' tails are stiffer** in the rig tool (Tonio: too floppy): stiffness 0.6 and damping 0.85, down from 0.25 and 0.6, which cuts the tail tip's sway on a walk to about 40%. A recipe the tool remembered keeps its own values; `start over` takes the new ones. Stiffness is the knob for floppiness: damping only trims the swing a little.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.10.19/

# 0.10.18

## Added

- **`landformSchemas`**: the options of `volcano`, `impactCrater`, `pad`, `gulley` and `cover` as JSON Schema (asked for by ensemble, tosijs-3d#119, for landform pieces linked to a terrain). `x` and `z` carry `x-position`, so a host can take them from the piece's position. A default worked out from another option (a volcano's `craterRadius` is `radius × 0.22`) is marked `x-derived: { from, scale }` and has no frozen `default`, so it keeps following its source; `landformDerived()` works one out. A volcano's `activity` names its stops (extinct, dormant, semi-active, erupting). The schemas are typed against the options interfaces, and a test checks that spelling out every default draws the same ground as leaving it out.
- **`slider3d({ stops })`**: named values on a slider's track (tosijs-3d#121): a tick at each, a detent that catches the handle within a few pixels, and the name beside the number while the value is on it. The landing spot for a schema's `x-stops`.

## Changed

- **`effectRecipeSchema()` says which strings are fetched** (tosijs-3d#120): a sound layer's `url` is `format: 'uri-reference'`, and a particle layer's `texture` is `anyOf` a URI (not starting with `<`) or inline SVG markup (`contentMediaType: 'image/svg+xml'`, `x-inline: 'svg'`), told apart by the leading `<` exactly as the player does. Markup is drawn as an image, so nothing it links to is loaded.

# 0.10.16

## Added

- **Effects: particles, light and sound on one clock** (EFFECTS-DESIGN.md, step 1; Tonio). `<tosi-b3d-effect preset="…">` plays a volcano (one preset, dormant to erupting by its `activity` dial: 0.15, 0.5, 1), a geyser, a splash, an explosion, a fireball or electrical sparks; `recipe` plays one of your own. An effect is LAYERS (particles, a light, a sound) with a start, a duration and curves over its life, written as data (`EffectRecipe`, `validateEffectRecipe`). It reacts to where it is: smoke and ash drift with the wind there, lava bombs and sparks land on what is below them, sound arrives `distance / 343` seconds late and duller with distance, and effect lights share one pool with the scene's lamps, ranked by strength and nearness (`rankLights`). Sprites and sounds are made in code, no files; budgets per device tier (`effectParticles`, `effectLights`, `effectVoices`). `scale` makes a vent a crater (Froude scaling: sizes ×scale, speeds and lives ×√scale, gravity unchanged, so arcs keep their shape and the wind still bends a mountain's plume); `ground="on"` sits it on the terrain.
- **A landform says where it is active** (Tonio: is the effect part of the province?). `volcano({ activity })` returns `vents` beside its landform and province: where the vent is (the crater's centre), how big (from the crater) and how busy (0, the default, is extinct). `terrain.vents = …` puts a grounded `<tosi-b3d-effect>` on each, kept in step as they change, so a field of volcanoes smokes without placing anything by hand. Land and Sky's volcano is now one of these.
- **Underwater effects**: `bubbles` (a vent or leak: bubbles rising in a zigzag, growing as they rise, ending at the water's surface, with a bubbling voice) and `black smoker` (a hydrothermal vent: a dark mineral plume, bubbles, a dull glow, a roar). Particle layers gain `surface` (end at the water) and `wobble` (a sideways zigzag).
- **Your own pictures and sounds in effects**: a particle layer's `texture` is an image URL, an SVG URL or SVG markup (SVG is drawn through a canvas, which keeps its transparency); a sound layer's `url` is a sample. The effect tool's `picture` button embeds an image in the recipe.
- **The effect tool** (`/effect-tool/`, `tosijs-3d/effect-tool`): pick a preset, edit any layer live (particles, light, sound, timing, colours), the activity dial, mute, `listen from` to hear the sound delay, save, load and copy the recipe.
- **Stars have prominences and flares** (Tonio). A few active regions, fixed on the star in the sunspot latitudes and turning with it: over the edge of the disc each is a glowing loop of drifting filaments standing on the limb (most low, the odd one tall), and now and then one flares, its loop swelling and a bright patch flashing on the disc. Drawn in the corona shell's shader, so no meshes or textures. On by default in `<tosi-b3d-star>` (`activity`, 0 to 1) and the star system's star (the Solar System demo's Sun). The two copies of the corona shader are now one (`createCoronaMaterial`).
- **Land and Sky's volcano is semi-active**: steam, a thin ash column on the wind, a glowing vent, a rumble, and now and then a burst of spatter and cinders (the volcano preset's new `spatter` and `cinders` layers, between dormant and erupting).

- **`effectRecipeSchema()`**: an effect recipe as JSON Schema (every layer kind, ranges, units as `x-unit`, defaults, the sprite and voice enums), for ensemble's editors, beside `rigRecipeSchema()`. A test checks every preset against it, so a field added to a layer and not to the schema fails.
- **The effect tool's backdrop is a neutral grid** (Tonio): grey sky, a grid in metres (lines every metre, heavier every ten), so an effect's colours and size read as they are. `backdrop: sky` brings back the sunset and its time of day.
- **`rigRecipeSchema()`**: a rig recipe as JSON Schema (ranges, units as `x-unit`, defaults), for a host that builds its editors from schemas or keeps recipes in its own documents (asked for by ensemble). A test holds it to `validateRigRecipe` and the tool's strand defaults.

## Fixed

- **Effect smoke starts at the vent and fades in** (Tonio: it popped into being too high). A `cone` emitter used Babylon's, which spawns anywhere up the cone's height (radius ÷ tan(angle): 68 m for the volcano's ash); every vent shape now starts on the ground and leaves within its angle, and covering (`alpha`) particles come up from nothing over their first moments.
- **The cloud deck drifts with the scene's wind** when the scene has one (`<tosi-b3d wind-speed>`), as smoke, spray and storms already did; its own `wind` and `windHeadingDeg` are the fallback (Tonio: the clouds and the volcano's smoke did not seem to share a wind). Its drift is integrated frame by frame, so a change of speed no longer jumps the clouds. Land and Sky's wind now blows across the view instead of straight away from it, where neither the clouds' nor the smoke's drift could be seen.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1205.7 KB raw / 412.8 KB gz, +3.3% on 0.10.15 (effects: the recipe, player, procedural sprites and voices, presets and `<tosi-b3d-effect>`; star activity; landform vents; the effect tool is a subpath, outside the barrel).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.10.16/

# 0.10.15

## Added

- **The rig tool** (`/rig-tool/`, `tosijs-3d/rig-tool`; Tonio). Load a demo character (the weasels and the space marine are rigged from markers on the spot, as the auto-rig page does, and a weasel's tail is a spring from the start) or your own GLB, check which bone plays each role (fingers included), set the arm space, hang spring chains on it (a new strand with a tube, such as a ponytail, or bones the model already has, such as a tail), and try any UAL clip beside the mannequin, scaled to the character. It opens in the rest pose with a dot on each role's bone: tap a dot, then the body, to give the role a bone (or hang a spring chain there); drag a strand's root and tip to place it. Save the result as a **rig recipe** (JSON), load it back, or copy it; the working recipe is kept per model in the browser. The element's `.rig` (`recipe`, `applied`, `load`) lets a page or an editor drive it.
- **Rig recipes**: `RigRecipe`, `validateRigRecipe` (headless, says what is wrong and where) and `strandDirection` in `rig-recipe`, and `applyRigRecipe(scene, root, skeleton, recipe)`, which puts a saved recipe on the same model in a game: the skeleton read with the recipe's roles, ready for `retargetClip`, and the springs live.

- **Panning in the default view controls** (Tonio). Shift-drag pans with a mouse, a trackpad's two-finger drag pans (a pinch still zooms), and right-drag and ctrl-drag pan by the same rule as touch: the point you grabbed follows the pointer, at any zoom. `touchOrbit(camera, { trackpadPan: false })` leaves the wheel to Babylon. A trackpad and a mouse wheel send the same event, so `wheelClassifier` (in `touch-gesture`) tells them apart by heuristic: a pinch carries `ctrlKey`, a mouse notch is big, a trackpad moves sideways or starts small. A wheel over a panel is still the panel's.

## Fixed

- **Panels no longer blink when they rebuild.** A frame panel is an SVG drawn into its texture asynchronously, so a new plane is blank until that draw lands; on a headset (and a 4× throttled laptop: seven blank frames per rebuild) every refresh flashed. A rebuild now puts the new element into the SAME plane, and the texture keeps its old picture until the new one is drawn. This applies to the settings panel in a headset, the flat in-scene settings panel, and system panels (`frame-panel`'s new `setSvg`, `SvgTexture.setElement`).
- **The system bar and pinned flat panels are reconciled, not all rebuilt**, when the set of panels changes: the unchanged ones keep their mesh.
- **A rebuilt settings panel keeps its scroll position**: flat in the scene, in the HTML overlay, and in a headset.
- **Retargeted characters keep their heads and hands** (Tonio). Where a bone with no joint below it points (a head, a hand) was measured through the mesh's world matrix, which is wrong under a scaled armature: omnidude's (Mixamo, 0.01) all landed by the origin, so every clip played his head upside down and twisted his hands. It is now measured through each bone's inverse bind matrix and up the rest chain, as the bones are.
- **Fingers and thumbs are retargeted.** `humanoidRoles` finds each finger's three joints across UE, Mixamo and Rigify spellings (never the tip's end bone or a metacarpal), so a clip's grip comes across instead of the fingers staying splayed at rest. A hand is aimed along a finger both rigs have, so the wrist's twist comes across too.
- **A settings-panel rebuild waits for the press to end**, so `refreshScenePanel()` during a slider drag no longer cuts the drag off (`panel3d`'s new read-only `pressing`).

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1167.3 KB raw / 399.6 KB gz, +0.8% on 0.10.14 (the rig recipe and retarget's finger roles; the rig tool is a subpath, outside the barrel).

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.10.15/

# 0.10.14

## Fixed

- **A press during a system panel's content swap is no longer lost** (#111 follow-up, ensemble). Setting `el.svg = next` on an open panel closed and reopened it, which left a moment with no plane: a click landing then went nowhere (ensemble's host-actions test failed one run in four after a store refresh swapped every panel's content), and `contentToClient` returned null. A framed panel (the default title bar) now swaps the content under the same frame, so the plane, texture, spot and focus stay. `panelopen` still goes to the old content (close) and the new (open). A press already down in the old content ends there rather than releasing onto the new. `chrome="none"` panels still close and reopen.
- **The docs a consumer reads describe what the code does** (#116, ensemble). `select3d`'s JSDoc called it "a compact cycler, no dropdown" five releases after it became a select that opens a list (it steps only with no host). A sweep of every behaviour change in this CHANGELOG against the shipped docs found 33 more, fixed against the code:
  - The settings panel is the owl's in-scene panel, not a gear and an HTML overlay (about 20 pages, and the `scenePanel` property).
  - `gameController`'s key map: the wheel zooms (the d-pad axis), the arrows look, the mouse buttons are listed, `mouseLook` defaults to `'off'`.
  - `b3dBiped`: the camera defaults in its table, `invertLookY` is off by default, `jumpSpeed` has no wind-up, `wadeDepth`'s swim thresholds (in at 1.3 ×, out at 1 ×).
  - SSAO runs in a headset with `on` and the default `projected` method (three type docs and a console warning said never).
  - `slider3d`'s peek readout sits beside the label; `panel3d`'s gap is 4.
  - Frame-panel presets are angular, and frame panels can show flat; `b3d-moon` lights the night; planets have no separate sea sphere; the loadout is on the system bar; `lookX`/`lookY` persist on foot; `gamepadFade` ignores the pointer; the aircraft's `maxSpeed` is full lever; `GulleyOptions.heading` is degrees; `iconGlyph` takes composed and mirrored names; `biomeLapseRate`'s auto value is a fixed 0.004.
  - Two doc comments had come loose from their declarations (`iconGlyph`'s sat on a private constant, `wadeDepth`'s on the wrong attribute), so the `.d.ts` documented the wrong thing.

## Added

- **`titled3d(…).setContent(next)`**: other content under the same title bar, in place (the old content goes back where it came from).

# 0.10.13

## Fixed

- **Overlapping screen panels: the one drawn on top is the one you press** (#115, from ensemble). Every screen-pinned panel sat at the same distance, and on a tie Babylon draws the later mesh on top but picks the first, so a press in an overlap went to the panel underneath. It showed up as a system panel whose content was swapped for something taller: reopened, it was drawn over its neighbour, and every row over the neighbour ignored the pointer. Screen panels in a layer now stack: newest on top, and a press or a title-bar grab brings a panel to the front, with drawing and picking taken from the same order.
- **The wheel over an in-scene panel scrolls the panel** (#114, from ensemble), instead of zooming the camera behind it; trackpad two-finger scroll too. A panel that cannot scroll still takes the wheel, so the scene does not zoom under a pointer that is on the UI. `titled3d` passes `scrollBy`, `scrollTop` and `scrollable` through to its content.
- `iconGrid3d` hovers inside a panel. It listened for `move`, and a panel reports an unpressed pointer as `hover`, so its cells never lit.

## Added

- **Tooltips for icon-only controls, wherever the panel is drawn** (#112, from ensemble): `IconGridItem` takes a `title`, shown on hover (a mouse, or a controller ray in a headset) and on D-pad focus. The panel draws it over its body, so a bottom row's tip is not clipped, flipped above the control when there is no room below. `iconBar3d` uses the same tip. A custom widget gets one through `WidgetHost.showTip`/`hideTip`.
- **A test can click a system panel's content where a person would** (#113, from ensemble): `el.contentToClient(x, y)` gives the client pixel of a point of the content (its viewBox units), through the drawn plane, so a drag, a scale and the title bar are accounted for; `el.clientRect()` is the content's box. Null unless open and flat.
- **A host can re-stack its system panels**: until someone drags a system panel, its spot is its current `screenAnchor`, so setting a new one moves an open panel (a column re-stacked as the panel above it grows). A dragged panel keeps its spot until its button is held. `screenAnchorDragged(anchor)` is exported.

# 0.10.12

## Added

- **A system panel's content can be rebuilt in place** (#111, from ensemble): system panels are now identified by their `<tosi-b3d-panel>` element, not by the SVG it shows. Setting `el.svg = next` on an open one shows the new content where it was, with the same system-bar button, the same dragged spot (flat and in a headset) and its open state, refitted to the new height. A closed one shows it when next opened. Before, a host that rebuilt its `panel3d` got a second button, lost the spot, and the open panel kept the old content. The setter fires a bubbling `panelcontent` event; disposing the dropped content stays the host's job.
- **`stretch` on a destroyable: a per-axis scale applied when the library piece arrives** (#105, the rest of it): `stretch="2 1 3"` multiplies `scale` per axis. A stretch written on the node by hand before the instance existed was lost when it loaded (ensemble measured 6.036 wide where 18.108 is right); as an attribute it is applied on adoption, like `scale`. A hand-set scaling still survives renders until `scale` or `stretch` changes.

# 0.10.11

## Added

- **A table can show its selection as the row** (#109, from ensemble): `selectionMarker: 'row'` fills the selected row and drops the radio/checkbox column, for rows that carry a leading control of their own (two circles side by side read as one toggle that did not work). Coordinate-based, so it works in a headset, where the host has no DOM to measure.

# 0.10.10

## Fixed

- **`panel3d`'s return type says what it carries** (#104): the exported `Panel3d` type lists `handlePointer`, `scrollBy`, `scrollable`, `gripHeight`, `gripHit`, `measure`, `addLayerHost`, `useDomLayer` and `dispose`. The declaration was a bare `SVGSVGElement`, so calling `dispose()` (new in 0.10.8) did not typecheck. Existing casts to a subset of those methods still compile.
- **A per-axis scale set on a library destroyable's node survives moves and turns** (#105): the uniform `scale` attribute was rewritten onto the node on every render, so a consumer's `[2, 1, 3]` stretch was lost at the next unrelated attribute write. It is now written only when `scale` (or the node) changes, and the attribute still wins whenever it is set.
- **Projected AO darkens library pieces** (#107, from ensemble): it hooked only the materials in `scene.materials` and those created after it started, but a library's instances share its container's materials, which are in neither. So pieces placed from a `<tosi-b3d-library>` were left out of the depth picture and never occluded, while the plugin count said AO was running. It now also finds materials through the scene's meshes, at start and as meshes are added. On twelve pirate-kit pieces, the pixels it changes went from 0% to 5.8% at strength 1, and from 0.1% to 16.5% at strength 3 (screen AO: 13%).
- **A key is delivered once even when a handler re-renders its field group mid-keystroke** (#94, from ensemble): a `handleChange` that rebuilt its panel inside the keydown detached the focused field's group, so the window listener, deciding afterwards, typed the key a second time (`flagXXship`). Every route now marks the event it consumed and skips one already marked.
- **The Moon with NASA's maps is a globe again**: its height map was exaggerated 12×, which put its relief at 14% of the radius ("ridiculous"). It is 3× now, about 3.5%: basins still show at the limb.
- **A planet's golden hour peaks with the sun at the horizon, not well above it.** The gold at the limb was strongest with the sun about 50° from behind the planet and still bright at 70°: daylight over most of the limb. It now needs the sun close behind (full within about 15°, gone by about 50°) and keeps its breadth. A first attempt that narrowed the band itself was rejected ("a very thin effect which isn't what I wanted"); Tonio, on this one: "pretty perfect".
- **A star system's rocky worlds have continents, not one blob.** A planet reads its noise at `grossScale × radius`, and its presets' relief is tuned for radius 50, both in drawn units. A system draws a world a few units across, so the synthetic Earth read a fiftieth of one noise wave and came out as a single smooth landmass ("very Fisher Price Pangaea"). Its noise is now set per world (about 1.6 waves across it for continents, 6 for coastlines), and the preset's relief is scaled by drawn radius over 50, for planets and moons alike. A look that sets its own scales or relief still wins.

## Added

- **Retargeting: one humanoid's animation on another's body.** The Universal Animation Library's clips now play on characters that weren't built for them. The demo (`/retarget/`) shows one clip on four bodies: UAL's mannequin, a Quaternius superhero, omnidude (Mixamo's bones) and a Kenney chibi (seven bones).
  - **Roles:** `humanoidRoles` says which bone is which across UE, Mixamo, Kenney and Blender names.
  - **Rotations:** `retargeter(source, target)` transfers each bone's world-space rotation since rest, so a clip made on an A-pose rig plays as shown on a T-pose one.
    - The hips move in proportion to hip height.
    - A target bone that stands for several source bones (a chibi's whole leg) aims along the source's chain.
  - **The Babylon side:** `readSkeleton` reads a loaded character; `retargetClip`/`retargetClips` turn a clip into an AnimationGroup for it. All pure except the Babylon side, and tested on the real UAL, Mixamo and Kenney skeletons.
- **Auto-rig: a mesh with no skeleton, walking** (#3349). Eight markers on a front view, as on Mixamo's auto-rigger, are enough to rig a mesh for UAL's clips. The auto-rig page (`/rig-build/`) rigs Tonio's omnidude, two weasels and a space marine in the browser (CC BY 4.0, on the CDN under `tonio/rigging/`) and plays clips on them side by side.
  - **Fitting:** `fitSkeleton(markers, meshQuery(positions, indices))` places UAL's 65 joints, each at the middle of the mesh's thickness. An optional tail tip grows a tail chain.
  - **Binding:** `boneHeat` binds the mesh by bone heat (Baran & Popović), in about 0.1–0.3 s.
  - **Building:** `buildRig` makes a Babylon skeleton of the result the way the glTF loader would, so `readSkeleton` and `retargetClip` work on it.
  - **Reading files:** `objTriangles` reads an OBJ.
- **Spring bones: secondary motion for hair, tails and capes.**
  - **Model:** `spring-chain` is the pure model: Verlet at a fixed 120 Hz step, stiffness toward the rest shape, damping, sphere colliders, and a correction that keeps the tip from whipping.
  - **Babylon side:** `springBones` hangs a simulated chain from any node, after the animation has posed the body, and `skinTube` skins a tube to it. `springNodes` runs an existing chain, which is how the weasels' tails swing.
  - **Demo:** a mannequin running in circles with a ponytail.

- **The auto-rig's marker step** (#3349). `markerField3d` shows a mesh's front silhouette with Mixamo's eight markers on it, to be dragged onto the joints, plus a side view for a tail tip. It is an ordinary panel control, so it works on a page, in the scene and in a headset. Symmetry is on by default, hovering names a marker, `handleChange` fires as a marker moves and `handleCommit` when it is let go. The pure half is in `rig-fit`:
  - `rigSilhouette(positions, indices, view)` is a mesh's front or side view as runs on a grid (a few ms).
  - `guessMarkers(silhouette)` gives a first placement read off the outline: the crotch, the arms' row, the neck and the legs. On Tonio's three OBJ meshes it lands within 10% of body height of the hand-placed markers, mostly within 3%.
  - The auto-rig page (`/rig-build/`) now rigs a character from the panel: pick one, drag its markers, and on release it is fitted, bound and walking again (about 0.15 s). **guess** re-places the markers from the silhouette alone.
- **Arm space for retargeting** (Mixamo's "Character Arm-Space"): `retargeter(source, target, { armSpaceDeg })` and `retargetClip(..., { armSpaceDeg })` turn the upper arms out from the body after retargeting, and the forearm and hand follow. A Kenney chibi's arms are long for its height, so hanging where UAL's hang put its hands half a metre through the floor, and in the retarget demo it looked as if it were kneeling. At 55° it walks like Kenney's own walk for that character, compared side by side: the arms are held out at about 45° and the lowest point is −0.13 m against Kenney's −0.15 m. The retarget page's panel no longer opens over the characters.
- **System panels for an app's main chrome** (#106, from ensemble). Three new `<tosi-b3d-panel>` controls for a panel with an `icon`:
  - **`exclusive="off"`** lets it stay open beside other system panels. Opening it closes nothing, and the settings panel or an exclusive panel (an inventory) opens and closes over it without closing it. The default is unchanged: one at a time.
  - **`open`** opens it when the scene starts.
  - **Its `screenAnchor` is where it first opens**, so a right-hand column can be declared. A drag still moves it and it reopens there; holding its button still puts it back.
  - **In a headset** the non-exclusive panels that were open follow you in and back out. A left-pinned panel sits left of centre and a right-pinned one right, lower for a lower pixel `top`.
  - A focused `inputField` in one takes typing as it does anywhere: keys come from a window listener, not the DOM (checked).
- **Screenshot from the scene panel.** A download icon on every scene's standard panel opens a popup with two buttons: **With panels** and **Scene only**. Each saves the canvas as a PNG. Scene only hides the `ui` and `modal` layers and world-layer panels (the system bar included) for the frame and puts them back. The popup closes itself first, so it is never in the picture. It is `b3d.saveScreenshot({ ui, name })` in code, and returns the Blob. `setPanelsHidden(scene)` (frame-panel) is the hide, and returns its undo. Feather's `download` icon is added.
- **Axial tilt.** Planets lean, with the axis fixed in space as they orbit, so seasons and a ring's shadow on its planet come and go with the year.
  - **Moons orbit their own plane:** `inclination` on a moon (degrees from the ecliptic), by default its planet's equator, as regular moons do. Our Moon takes 5.1°; with the tilt on its holder it had dropped 23° below the ecliptic.
  - **`SOL` carries the real tilts** (Earth 23.4°, Saturn 26.7°, Uranus 82.2°, Venus 2.6°; a negative `day` already makes Venus and Uranus turn backwards). A star system tilts each planet (and its rings).
  - **`tilt` on `<tosi-b3d-planet>`** does the same for a standalone planet; the spin runs about the tilted axis.
  - **What it fixes:** Saturn's rings shadowed nothing in the Solar System demo, because they lay in the plane of the orbit, edge-on to the Sun, and their shadow was a hairline on the equator. The sun's elevation above the rings now runs from −26.7° to +26.7° round Saturn's year: two equinoxes (the demo's clock starts at one) and two solstices.

# 0.10.9

## Added

- **A compass and a watch** (`import … from 'tosijs-3d/dials'`, not in the barrel: the artwork is 36 KB). Both are drawn by Tonio, and the code only moves their named parts. The compass needle points north as you turn (`sceneCompass(b3d)` follows the active camera, flat or in a headset; north is +Z). On the watch, a dot on the ring is the time of day (noon at the top, midnight at the bottom) and a dot on the bar is how fast it passes, from still to an hour a second. Drag either: `skyWatch(skybox)` reads and writes the sky's `timeOfDay` and `realtimeScale`. Each goes on the system bar as a `<tosi-b3d-panel icon title>`. Feather's `clock` icon is added. `bun run dial-art` re-embeds the SVGs after they are redrawn.
- **A planet and its sphere terrain are one world** (#3344). Tonio: "if you pick a point in the middle of what looks like the ocean, coast, mountain range on a planet you end up with corresponding terrain in the sphere terrain and vice versa." Either can be the source, stated by one attribute:
  - **`<tosi-b3d-terrain planet="#p">`**: the ground takes its large shape (sea, coasts, mountain ranges) from the planet, scaled to its `radius` with the sea at 0. Its own detail layer and landforms ride on top, and it rebuilds when the planet changes (`planet.shapeKey`). Measured at 200 random places: the ground sits within the detail layer of the globe's height (mean 2.5 m, worst 3.9 m with 5 m of detail), and sea or land agrees except at the waterline.
  - **`<tosi-b3d-planet terrain="#t">`**: the globe is drawn from the ground's own height function, and again whenever the ground's shape changes. This replaces the hand-written `planet.surface = terrain.planetSurface()` loop, and the sphere-map demo now uses it.

  Linked, not automatic: a gas giant in a moon's sky, or every body of a star system, must not become the ground you stand on. `planet.relativeHeightAt(direction)` is the globe's height above its sea as a fraction of its radius. Both attributes are in the schemas.
- **Planetary rings catch shadows** (#3320). Both are worked out in the shaders for a sphere and a flat ring lit by one star, with no shadow maps. **The planet's shadow falls across its rings** (the dark wedge behind Saturn): each ring fragment asks whether the ray toward the star passes through the planet, softened slightly at the edge. This applies to any `<tosi-b3d-planet>` with `rings`. **The rings' shadow bands a gas giant**: each fragment finds where the ray toward the star crosses the ring plane and dims by how much ring is there, so the shadow has the ring's own gaps (a lighter stripe where the Cassini gap lets light through). The ring is now one GLSL function (`RING_GLSL` in `gas-giant`) that the ring draws itself from and the planet reads, and `createGasGiantMaterial` takes `ring: () => RingShadow | null` for a planet built by hand. Not yet: the rings' shadow on a ROCKY planet's surface.

# 0.10.8

## Added

- **`planetSchema()`** (`sceneSchemas.planet`): `<tosi-b3d-planet>` described like the other scene primitives, with sections (World, Surface, Sea, Air, Clouds, Craters, Rings, Gas giant, Maps), `heightMap`/`colorMap` marked as fetched, and the `world`/`gas` lists taken from the preset tables so they cannot drift. **`x-preset-written`** names the attributes a `world` preset writes into the planet. A consumer that applies schema defaults on bind should show them but not write them back over the preset (#103, ensemble).
- **`lat` / `lon` on `<tosi-b3d-terrain>`**: where this ground is on its planet, the latitude and longitude of the terrain's origin in degrees, so "this ground is at 12° N, 40° E" is one attribute pair, in markup and in `terrainSchema()`. `worldU`/`worldV` are now JS properties over them (`worldU = lon / 360`, `worldV = (lat + 90) / 180`). Before, they were plain properties that markup could not set and that needed a `regenerate()`. Changing `lat`/`lon` (or either view of them) rebuilds the ground. The defaults (-45, 0) are the old 0.25 / 0, so nothing moves (#103).
- **`seamBlend` / `seamWeight`** (`sphere-map`): make a layer laid out in flat metres periodic round a world, mixed with its copy one circumference away near the far meridian and untouched elsewhere.

## Fixed

- **A widget bound to a tosijs box lets go of it** (#100). `toggle3d`, `slider3d` and `select3d` subscribed to a bound box and threw the unsubscribe away. Every bound row left a listener in tosijs's module-level list that held the row, its panel and its host, so ensemble's editor grew by 125 listeners and 5,360 nodes per round of panel rebuilds. Each now unsubscribes in its `dispose()`. `B3d` already disposes the widget lists it rebuilds, and **`panel3d(…)` has a `dispose()`** that disposes its rows, for a consumer that drops its own panels. Not reaped by `isConnected`: an in-scene panel's SVG is never in the document.
- **Removing the last instance of a library model no longer turns every later one white** (#102). `disposeMeshTree` disposed a material when no mesh in the scene used it, but a library's source meshes live in its AssetContainer, out of that list, so the guard could not see that the library still needed the material. Ensemble's editor lost the colour of a whole kit on its first rebuild, and a game would see it when the last enemy of a type despawned and the next one spawned white. It now disposes only materials the scene owns (`scene.materials`); a container's are the container's.
- **A frozen or paused scene builds its system bar** (#3342). The bar and flat panels were built only on running frames, so a scene that started frozen (Manta freezes on every menu) showed the HTML lozenge, and a `<tosi-b3d-panel icon title>` got no button until it unfroze. Stopped frames keep the scene's chrome current now, as they already did its fog.
- **A sphere terrain joins at the far meridian** (#3318). Its noise is read on the sphere and always repeated; its profile fields (`blendProfiles`, `profileField`) and landforms (`craterField`, …) read flat metres and did not. The ground opposite the terrain's origin (longitude 180 at the default `worldU`) was two different places: a 116 m step on Manta's cratered moon, 19.5 m without the craters. Within 5% of a turn of that meridian they are now mixed with their copy one turn away, so the two sides meet. Elsewhere the ground is exactly as before, and a place one whole turn round is the same place. Spheres only: a cylinder is used as a big flat world with things placed in metres.
- **A globe of a world with no sea is drawn at its size** (#3319). A planet drawn from a `PlanetSurface` measured every height from `seaLevel`, so a dry world that says "no sea" with a sea level far below its ground (Manta's -10000 m) gained that depth as ground. A globe meant to be 40 units across came out at 2476. The globe now measures from the higher of the sea and the lowest ground. A world with a real sea is unchanged, and on a dry world the lowest ground sits on the base radius. The convention for "no sea" is a `seaLevel` below all of the ground.

# 0.10.7

**What you will see on upgrading** (nothing exported in 0.10.6 is removed or renamed, but a `^0.10` range picks this up unasked):

- Every `panel3d` is tighter (shorter rows, half the space between them), and icon-bar captions are tooltips.
- Flat, the corner buttons, settings panel and pause are drawn in the scene; `::part(...)` styling of them no longer shows. `<tosi-b3d flat-ui="dom">` keeps the HTML.
- The settings panel has a title bar (move, name, ×); in a headset it opens from the system bar ahead of you, and Exit VR is on that bar.
- Popups are alpha-blended with the panels' light outline, where they were opaque with a grey rim.
- The placeholder Inventory, Journal, Quick Access and Menu rig panels no longer ship; declare your own `<tosi-b3d-panel>`s.

## Changed

- **The scene's corner controls, settings panel and pause are drawn in the scene by default** (flat), not as HTML over the canvas (#3307). If you styled them through `::part(sceneToolbar)`, `::part(scenePanelGear)`, `::part(enterVrButton)` or the pause host, that styling no longer shows: the HTML is still there but hidden. A button you hide with `display: none` (on `::part(...)` or otherwise) is still left off the in-scene toolbar, which mirrors what shows. The toolbar now has a third button (full screen) and covers about 150 x 56 px at the top left, so anything of yours pinned there needs moving (the demo loadouts moved to 64 px down). `<tosi-b3d flat-ui="dom">` restores the HTML presentation.
- **The system bar** (`systemBar`, was `sceneToolbar` earlier in this cycle): the scene's one row of buttons, flat in the top-left corner and, in a headset, up ahead where the settings panel used to hang for the whole session (twice the flat bar's size there). The owl opens the settings panel under it (now with a ×, flat and in VR alike); in a headset Exit VR is on the bar and no longer on the settings panel. **System panels**: a `<tosi-b3d-panel preset="system-bar" icon="personStanding">` is not pinned to the rig but gets a button on the bar and opens under it, flat and in a headset (and from the HTML lozenge with `flat-ui="dom"`). One is open at a time, the settings panel included. The content is asked with a cancelable `panelopen`, so content that opens itself (`inventoryDock`) does, and its own close puts the panel away. `FramePanelSpec.focusable: false` keeps a panel where it is placed (#3307).
- **Placeholder cards wear the outline too** (the pins demo's plaques, a system panel with no `svg`): `placeholderPanelSvg` draws the shared `panelRim`, and the card now fills its viewBox.
- **A panel on the system bar is an icon, a title and what it shows.** `<tosi-b3d-panel icon="map" title="Map">` with an `<svg>` inside it (in HTML, or `b3dPanel({ icon, title }, panel3d(...))`) gets a button on the bar and opens under it; nothing else to wire. An `icon` with no `preset` now means the system bar (`preset="system-bar"` still works), and an `<svg>` child is the content (the `svg` property, when set, wins). A panel with neither shows a card with its title.
- **Frame panels can be dragged by their title bar in space**, not only on the screen: in a headset the panel slides over its sphere to where the controller points, keeping the offset you grabbed it by (a point along the ray, not its direction from your eyes: `orbitFromAim`). For a panel whose anchor is its own angles (not a preset, not a `position`). A system panel reopens where you left it in a headset too; holding its button resets both.
- **A list's "put in" target stays in view**: with the heading and the drop target, at the top of a fixed-height list, and the things scroll in the space left. It was the list's last row, below the bottom of a list taller than its panel.
- **Polish, from a headset pass.** The system bar's buttons are 3 apart with the same 3 between them and its outline (`BAR_GAP`, `BAR_PAD`, `BAR_HEIGHT` exported), so it reads as one even strip. Panels and popups have no dark fringe at their rounded corners: their textures are premultiplied (`SvgTexture` `premultiplied`) and blended `SRC + DST(1 - a)`. A box's clip is rounded as the box is, so a pinned heading no longer squares off its top corners. The inventory dock: the bag sits half as far from the loadout, has no "bag" caption, and its two targets sit side by side as **unequip** (Lucide's backpack, new icon `lucideBackpack`) and **drop** (`trash`) (`inventoryPanel` `headings`, `putLabel`, `putIcon`, `dropIcon`; `carrySocket` `inline`, `icon`); a list that scrolls leaves room for its scrollbar, so rows breathe evenly either side; a one-line target centres its label, and a refusal's reason takes its place.
- **A system panel wears the settings panel's title bar** (move, its title, ×), flat and in a headset, in place of content's own close (the dock's minus in a circle, and its outline, are left to the frame: `panelopen` says `framed`). Flat, a drag by the bar moves it and it reopens where you left it, as the settings panel does; **holding** its button on the system bar (or the owl's, for the settings panel) puts it back under the bar (`systemhold`, after `HOLD_MS`). `<tosi-b3d-panel chrome="none">` for content with chrome of its own; `titled3d(content, { title, handleClose })` gives any SVG the same bar.
- **The demo inventory is on the system bar** (`demoLoadout`, the inventory-box page): a button (Lucide's person-standing) that opens the loadout with its bag. The small closed loadout over your shoulder is gone.
- **The rig's spots are named pins, empty by default**: `left-shoulder`, `right-shoulder`, `overhead`, `waist`, `wrist`, demonstrated on the b3d-panel page. The placeholder Inventory, Journal, Quick Access and Menu panels no longer ship; declared `<tosi-b3d-panel>`s are the set.
- **Panels are tighter.** A control row pads ¾ as much above and below (40 px, was 46), rows in a `panel3d` stack half the theme spacing apart (4, was 8), the icon bar is its buttons plus 2 px either side (36, was 46 plus a caption band), and the gap under a pinned header is halved. A panel shows about a fifth more in the same height. `gap` on `panel3d` restores the old space between rows; the rows themselves and the icon bar stay tighter (a larger `--w3d-padding` grows the rows), so a panel given a fixed height comes out with room to spare.
- **Icon-bar captions are tooltips.** The first word under every icon is gone; hovering (a mouse, or a controller ray) shows the whole title in a tooltip drawn in the SVG, so a texture shows it too.
- **Panels and popups share one outline**, the corner toolbar's light line (`panelRim`: white at 60%, 4 units wide, heavy enough to pop a panel off a dark sky), in place of a popup's grey rim, since nothing in a scene casts a shadow to separate them.
- **Popups are alpha-blended quads like every other panel**, not opaque meshes with cut corners, so their outline and corners are the SVG's and a translucent theme shows through them. They still write depth (`b3dSvgPlane` `transparent: 'depth'`, new: blended, depth-written, empty pixels discarded), so stacked popups do not swap order as you orbit.

## Added

- **Icons: `book`, `bookOpen` (Feather's), `personStanding` (Lucide's), `backpack` and `loadout` (ours).** The inventory dock wears the panels' outline, open and closed (closed, its line scaled to the small picture). `<tosi-b3d-panel icon>` / `FramePanelSpec.icon` is a system panel's button.
- **The settings panel has a title bar**: move, its name and close, in the band that was empty headroom. `panelTitle` on `<tosi-b3d>` names it (the demos' title rows moved there, a row each saved); flat, the panel can be dragged by the bar, stays where you put it across rebuilds, and its × closes it (close is no longer in the icon bar). The DOM panel shows the title in its head. `panel3d` takes `title` and `handleClose` (a close glyph it handles itself, so every presentation gets it) and exposes `gripHit(x, y)`, the bar less the close target, for a host that drags it. Frame panels pinned with `screenAnchor` move with a drag on that grip, writing `left`/`top` into the anchor.

- **The settings panel is in the scene** (flat): the same panel the headset gets, as a `ui`-layer frame panel pinned under the corner toolbar, and its popups (Perf, errors, …) are made in the same layer, hanging from it (`b3dSvgPlane`'s new `layer`, taken by a popup from its opener; `panelLayerOf`). A press on the background still closes it; a press a panel took does not (`pointerClaimedByPanel`, since Babylon cancels every canvas press, so `defaultPrevented` cannot tell). The glass gamepad, which stays HTML and so sat over in-scene panels and took their presses, steps aside while the settings panel or a pause is up. `flat-ui="dom"` keeps the HTML panel (#3307).
- **The respawn panel is the scene's modal too, and so is the pause in a headset**: a death's panel (`b3dDeath`) and the pause are one modal, over everything so terrain and the wreck's smoke cannot bury it: flat in the middle of the screen, in a headset in front of you a little below eye level, riding your body frame. One that is open when you enter or leave VR comes with you. Both come through `b3d.showModal(svg, height, fallback)`: where the scene has no modal to give (`flat-ui="dom"` on a monitor, a custom `setupXr` rig) it calls `fallback`, the caller's own presentation (the pause's DOM host, the respawn's world plane), including after entering or leaving VR, so a respawn panel never simply vanishes. Two open at once are stacked, the newer nearer and on top (#3307).
- **Pause is in the scene** (flat): the same panel as a `modal`-layer frame panel pinned to the middle of the screen, square to it, over the world and the ui layer, drawn and pressed first. The reasons it once moved to the DOM (occlusion, a line-of-sight placement, a raycast to press it) are each answered by the layer and the screen pins. The scene panel, open behind it, can still unpause (its header's play button). `flat-ui="dom"` keeps the DOM pause (#3307).
- **The corner toolbar is in the scene** (flat): settings, Enter VR and the new **full-screen** button are a panel in the `ui` layer pinned to the top-left corner, the same in-scene UI a headset gets. It mirrors the HTML buttons rather than redoing them (`systemBar`): what shows, what is enabled, the icon, and a press is that button's own `click()`, so VR entry and full screen keep one definition and still run inside the user's press. `<tosi-b3d flat-ui="dom">` keeps the HTML overlay (#3307).
- **System bar icons carry their names**: each button's `title` (or `aria-label`) is its SVG `<title>`, kept current. A texture does not draw it, and everything else can read it. This is the first step of "icons first, never nameless" (UI-DESIGN-NOTES).
- **Full screen** (`fullscreenButton` part): the scene element, not the page; the standard API with the webkit fallback, and no button where neither exists (iPhone Safari). Toggles, and says which way.
- **UI layers: `world`, `ui`, `modal`.** A frame panel's `layer` (and `<tosi-b3d-panel layer>`) puts it in a Babylon utility layer drawn over the whole world with its own depth, and given the pointer first: a nearer wall can neither hide it nor take its press. `modal` is over `ui`. Made in pairs per scene (`panelLayerScene(scene, layer)`, exported so a game can promote its own objects); a layered panel's stand-in rides its frame in the main scene and the drawn copy takes its pose each frame. The demo loadouts are `ui`. **In a headset too**: Babylon's XR controller ray picks the world and only its own default layer, and lets a nearer world hit win, so while it picks each frame a ray that hits one of our layers (modal first) returns that pick: it beats the wall, the laser stops at the panel, and the press lands (`pickPanelLayers`, exported). Checked in the emulated headset with a box between the controller and the loadout: the plain pick hits the box, the controller's pick is the panel, and the press opens it (#3307). ⚠️ It does this by wrapping `scene.pickWithRay` from the start of each XR frame until it renders: a pick of yours in that window that crosses a `ui` or `modal` panel returns the panel, whatever your predicate says (#3327, fixed in the next patch).

## Fixed

- **A `<tosi-b3d>` removed and added back keeps running.** Its system bar was kept as 'the same buttons' across the teardown, so the re-added scene had none, threw in its render loop and froze; an open system panel is now closed with the scene too.
- **A system-bar panel declared in markup alone** (`preset="system-bar"` and a `title`, no JS `svg`) was dropped silently; it now gets its button and opens a card with its title, as a pinned panel does. `flat-ui` has a row in the attribute table, and a value other than `scene` or `dom` warns once.
- **Title bars: the title is centred, and the move and × glyphs are centred in the bar with the same margin at the side as at the top** (they were pulled into their corners). The × is drawn larger than the move glyph so the two read the same size: Feather's × covers 12 of its 24 units and the move arrows 20. The HTML panel centres its title too. This is all `chromeLayout`, so popups, `panel3d`, `titled3d` and the settings panel get it alike.
- **A focused frame panel no longer swells and shrinks with your head** in a headset: its fit to the view is worked out once per focus (and per content size), not every frame.

- **A sky with its own moons no longer draws Earth's.** At night the skybox drew its built-in moon on the replayed day arc and lit the scene from it, even when `<tosi-b3d-moon>`s gave the sky other moons: on Io (Land and Sky) a bright disc sat low in the east under Jupiter and read as the sun, while Jupiter was lit, correctly, by the real sun set in the west. Now a sky's own moons replace the built-in one, and the night light comes from the first of them, as bright as its sunlit face (Jupitershine).
- **A popup opened from the in-scene settings panel can be moved and closed, and fits the screen.** Its × and title bar were tested by a pick in the main scene, but it lives in the `ui` layer's own scene (which also keeps the press from the main scene's observers), so neither did anything; popups are now picked in their own scenes, layers first. A screen-pinned panel's popup is built no taller than the screen (a layer host's `roomFor`; it scrolls past that) and kept on it, where it used to hang from its row at up to 480 px and run off the bottom (the solar system's 27-body picker).
- A press on a popup opened from the in-scene settings panel (Perf, errors…) no longer closes the settings panel: in-scene planes claim their presses as frame panels do (`claimPointer`).
- The glass gamepad really steps aside for a menu: `suppress` hid it with `visibility`, which parts of the pad override, so bits of it still drew and took presses meant for the panel under it. It uses `display` now.
- Full screen: a scene removed and re-added no longer gets a second toggle on its button (one press went in and straight back out), and a refused request no longer throws an unhandled rejection.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1104.9 KB raw / 376.3 KB gz, +2.11% on 0.10.6.

Source: https://3d.tosijs.net/v0.10.7/

# 0.10.6

## Added

- **Flat panels can be placed in screen terms**: `screenAnchor` (on `b3dPanel` and frame panels) pins a panel to the view's edges in pixels, a fraction of the axis (`'5%'`) or of the shorter side (`'3vmin'`), with an anchor point, and `height` sets its size on screen. It is solved with `anchorLayout` every frame and placed square to the screen in the head-locked frame, so a resize or a different window shape keeps it where you put it; it wins over `flatAnchor`'s degrees, which suit a headset, where a panel is around you. The demo loadouts use it: 64 px in, 2vmin down, 14% of the screen tall. Opened, a screen-pinned panel comes to the middle of the screen square to it, not tilted up from below eye level.
- **A box scrolls with a pointer alone**: a scrollbar on its right edge when its content overflows a fixed height (drag the thumb; press the track to page). A wheel scrolls a box on a page, but a panel in a scene gets no wheel and a headset has none, so a long list was cut off with no way to reach the rest. **Sticky children** (`sticky: true` on a leading run) stay put while the rest scrolls under them: the inventory list's heading and drop row (#3290).
- **The Biped Playground has the loadout, and the pistol lives on your hip.** Firing mode follows where the pistol is: in a hand the gun is up, on the hip it is down, in the bag or dropped there is nothing to raise. The weapon button draws it from the hip or holsters it, and dragging it into a hand does the same. `b3dBiped`'s new `whenWeapon` (JS) lets a game answer the weapon button itself and call `setGunplay`; `demoLoadout({ equip })` starts with things worn and returns its `inv` (#3305).
- **The Biped Playground has a pool**: 14 x 10 m, 3.5 m deep, in the far corner past the catwalk, with a shelving ramp at one end to walk in on (where `isSwimming`'s hysteresis is tested) and caustics on the floor. Sunk into the ground, because a biped swims anywhere below the water's height: `b3dGround`'s new `holes` (JS) cuts rectangles out of it, keeping its texture unbroken around them. `playground({ pool: false })` leaves it out.
- **A drop target.** `inventoryPanel`/`inventoryDock` `handleDrop(item, kind, from)` adds a **drop** row at the top of the list: a thing dropped there leaves the inventory, after the game has had its say (return reasons to refuse and it springs back; otherwise put it in the world). Both demos have one (#3290).
- **`ui.anchorLayout`, the third layout** beside the flow: positioned and layered. An item is pinned to any edge with an offset (units or a fraction, `'50%'`), with a natural or fixed size; between two pins its size is what they leave and a stated size is a minimum. Its anchor (`anchorX`/`anchorY`, `anchor: 'center'`; default the top left) is the point a pin places and the way a minimum that does not fit overflows. `within` pins it inside a rectangle of the container (a window in the artwork). Paint order is the order given or `z`. Pure and unit-tested; the box mode that uses it is next (#3309).
- **Things have pictures, and say what they are.** An item kind's `icon` (SVG markup) is drawn on its tile: beside the name in a list, alone and filling a socket, and as the ghost a drag carries. Pointing at a thing, or selecting it with a gamepad, shows an info floater (its name, `description`, mass and what it adds by default; `info` replaces that), drawn in the ghost's layer so nothing clips it. `carryTile` takes `icon` and `info`. The demos load one picture per kind from `/item-icons.json` (#3290).
- **A frame panel can come to you.** Content that dispatches `panelfocus` (`detail: { focus: true }`) on its SVG brings its panel front and centre (`focusAnchor`, default straight ahead and a little low), enlarged (`focusScale`, default 1.9, at 0.75 m) and always revealed; `focus: false` sends it back. A focused panel never sits inside the camera's near plane (it is pushed out and scaled to look the same size) and is never bigger than the view (it fits 92% of it, allowing for being off-centre), so a monitor shows all of it. `flatAnchor` places a panel somewhere else in the flat view (the shoulder is off a monitor's edge), and `<tosi-b3d-panel>` takes `svg`, `flatAnchor`, `focusAnchor` and `focusScale` as JS properties. A frame panel also grows with its SVG's viewBox now, so content that opens wider gets a wider plane. `inventoryDock` asks for focus as it opens, and the main `tosi-b3d` demo pins your loadout up and to the left (over the shoulder in VR, the top left flat): touch or click it and it comes front and centre with your bag (#3290).
- **An inventory in 3D: `inventoryDock`.** A loadout that lives on a plane in the scene, flat and in a headset. Closed, it is the schematic alone, small; a tap opens it, with the list beside it (a bag) to drag to and from, and a button closes it. Both are drawn in one SVG, so a drag between them is one plane with one ghost (`carryGhostLayer`). Without a `list` it opens to the schematic alone (a craft fitted from a carrier's stock). Demo: "In 3D" on the inventory-box page, where the loadout replaces the "Inventory" placeholder over your shoulder (top left flat) and a touch brings it front and centre (#3290).
- **A two-handed weapon shows in both hands**: `inventoryPanel`'s `alsoIn(item, kind, at)` names the other slots an item takes up, where it is drawn faded (and can be picked up from either). The game decides which; the panel only draws it (#3290).
- **Drag and drop, as a model and on a panel** (INVENTORY-DESIGN step 1). `createCarry` is picking up and putting down with nothing drawn: what is carried and from where, the target under the pointer, and its verdict as REASONS; drop is all or nothing; dragging and two taps are one model, and one carry spans every panel. `carryTile`, `carrySocket` and `carryPanel` draw it on a box: things with decorations (a status bar, a damaged or broken outline, a badge), sockets that light when the held thing would fit, dim when not and say why, and a ghost that follows the pointer. A drag goes from one panel to another (they share the carry), and letting go outside every panel puts the thing back.
- **An inventory model** (`createInventory`, INVENTORY-DESIGN step 2): pure, with the game's catalogue, rules, contributions and prices plugged in. Holders hold slots (a paper doll, hardpoints, mounts), lists (a bag, a stock) and grids (a hull of boxes). A move is checked against every rule on a copy and kept only if all pass, so it happens completely or not at all; it can swap, split a stack, take from the catalogue, or pay. `stage()` is a draft that may be incomplete (a cart, a barter, a design not yet committed); `totals` adds up what is fitted (and what its mount adds); `damage` crosses off a system's boxes. `craft` runs a recipe (inputs used up, tools required but kept, outputs made, one move) and `compile` turns a finished design into a new kind (a ship class, a learned spell, a forged sword). Tested against a party, a loadout, a starship design, a shop and a smithy.
- **`inventoryPanel`**: one holder of an inventory on a panel, with drag and drop wired to the model, so a socket lights, dims and explains with the game's own rules. Panels sharing an inventory and a carry are a party, a trade or (with `moveFor` adding a price) a shop.
- **Schematics**: `inventoryPanel({ schematics: { body: svgText } })` draws a container as art, and its slots go where the art's sockets are (`data-slot="…"`, or ids in a `Sockets` group; `readSchematic` reads one). Sockets on art draw nothing at rest, outline when what is held fits, darken when not, and name themselves and the reason on hover. Demos: equip a person, arm a Manta from a carrier's counted stock, and a shop (its goods left, yours right, the deal in the middle: one `move` that buys, sells and pays, or does none of it). Panels take `height` (a scrolling list), `only`/`hide` (split one holder across panels) and `refuse` (a view's own reasons), and show the holder's purse.
- **A schematic is drawn at the art's own scale**, cropped to what it draws and shrunk only when the panel is too narrow (`schematicFit`), so a socket designed 44 units square is a 44-unit target, not whatever the file's margins left of it.
- **The demo schematics are coloured by CSS variables** with defaults for a dark panel (`--schematic-body`, `--schematic-socket`, `--schematic-socket-edge`, `--schematic-label`): a host restyles them on the page, and a texture draws the defaults.
- **A box child can be placed** (`at: { x, y }`): over the flowed child before it, at that offset, taking no flow space and hit first. Sockets on a schematic are this.

## Changed

- **The closed loadout is a small picture**: no heading over it and no sockets drawn, only what is in them (all return when open), corners rounded well past the panel's own, 0.125 m wide (was 0.3; `focusScale` 4.56 keeps the opened size), and flat it sits nearer the top-left corner (18° up, was 10°), square to the screen. Frame panel anchors gain `flatOn` (parallel to the frame's view plane rather than turned to face the eye) and `tiltDeg` (tip it about its own horizontal axis without moving it) (#3290).
- **Inventory list rows are full width**, so a row is a button you can hit anywhere along it. **Swimming starts chest deep** (0.65 submerged, down to 0.5 to stand again; it was waist deep, 0.5 and 0.35), and a swimmer rides a little higher than the last change (12 cm of water above the head bone, was 20; treading unchanged) (#3290).
- **The opened dock's list is as tall as the loadout beside it** (it scrolls), not a fixed 540 that made the whole dock taller than its picture. `height` still sets it explicitly (#3290).
- **An inventory panel's heading sits over its schematic's top left** (title, totals, the container's name) instead of stacked above it, so the picture is larger, which matters most on the small pinned loadout. A panel whose first container is not a schematic keeps its heading above (#3290).
- **SVG panels are mipmapped** (`SvgTexture` `mipmaps`, default `true`: trilinear, anisotropic 4). A panel is nearly always drawn smaller than its texture (1024 px over ~300 px of a Quest 3's view at arm's length), and unfiltered its hairlines broke up and its text crawled; the small pinned loadout's socket outlines were visibly broken and now draw whole. Every in-scene panel, popup and HUD goes through it. Mip generation measured under 0.1 ms per repaint at 1024 px; it costs a third more texture memory. `mipmaps: false` for a texture always seen at about a texel per pixel.
- **An inventory panel on a page fits the space it is given** instead of being cropped (`fit`, default on): side by side they shrink in proportion, in a column it is no wider than the column, never taller than its container, never larger than drawn, always the same shape. Anything the page sets inline on the host wins (#3290).
- The default body panels are an inventory over the left shoulder and a **journal** over the right (both were "Inventory") (#3290).
- `panelScene`'s orbit camera stops at half its starting distance (`camera.minRadius`), so zooming cannot pass through the panel (#3290).
- **A planet's edge has a golden hour.** Where you see its air edge on and the sun is low over it, the air takes the colour left when its own is scattered out: Earth's goes gold, Mars's dusty air goes blue. The whole lit rim takes it together, by how far the sun has gone behind the planet from where you are: lit from the side, the rim (its "poles" included) stays the air's own colour. Face on, nothing changes (#3285).
- **The Solar System's sky is tilted as ours is**: the planets orbit about 60.2° to the galaxy's plane, so the Milky Way crosses the orbits steeply instead of running along them (`spaceBackdrop({ tilt })`).
- **While you carry something, the sockets that would take it light up**, the one under the pointer brighter and named, and the rest go dark. The ghost hangs above the pointer, so the socket you are over stays in sight (#3290).
- **A panel that shows one list takes a drop anywhere on it**, not just on its tiles or the "put in" row at the bottom of a scrolled list, and is outlined while it would take what you carry. Dragging a thing off a socket back into the bag is a drop on the bag (`carryPanel(box, carry, { fallback })`) (#3290).
- **A drop that does not land springs back.** Refused by its target, let go on nothing, or released outside every panel, the ghost returns to where it was picked up and shows why it was refused there for a moment. `carryPanel` now returns `dispose`, and `inventoryPanel` calls it on each rebuild (a rebuilt panel used to leave its old carry subscription behind) (#3290).

## Fixed

- **In a headset, a screen-pinned panel is where its VR anchor says** (found by the release review). Screen pins are for a monitor: in a session they were still applied, putting the loadout a metre ahead, sized from the flat canvas, instead of on your left shoulder. `presentationSpec(spec, flat)` is now the one rule every attach site uses (flat: the flat anchor and screen pins; in VR: neither). Checked in the emulated headset.
- **Two-tap works on a page** (found by the release review). The page examples cancelled the carry on every `pointerup`, and a tap pick-up happens ON a release, so it was put straight back. `carryOverlay` now cancels a drag let go over nothing itself, after the panels have had the release, and never a tap; the examples no longer add their own.
- **A press on a panel in the scene no longer also works the game's controls.** The biped reads mouse buttons (the left button is A, a jump), so every press on the playground's loadout made the hero jump, and with a weapon up could fire it. A frame panel now cancels the `pointerdown` it takes, which by the web's own rule stops the matching `mousedown`/`mouseup`; the scene's picking is pointer events and carries on.
- **A focused panel fits the view a looking-down camera actually has.** Its room was worked out from where it sits in its frame, which is level while a follow camera pitches down; it is now measured in the camera's own view.
- **Swimmers ride lower.** The water sat at the head bone (the base of the skull), which left a treader's shoulders and arms out and a swimmer's head, shoulders and back riding on top. It now sits 10 cm higher on a treader (at the jaw: the head out) and 20 cm on a swimmer (over the back: the head breaking).
- **Raising the weapon aims straight ahead.** The aim is the look pitch, which kept whatever it was left at (looking at the ground, the last dive), so the gun often came up pointing at your feet. `setGunplay(true)` levels it, flat only (in a headset the aim is the controller); lowering the weapon leaves the view alone.
- **First person shows the world, not the back of your head.** Sprinting leans the head 22° forward and swimming far more, and the back and underside of the skull filled the view (measured in the playground: half the screen while sprinting). The head bone is collapsed while in first person, the way first-person games do it, so the arms and body stay (your hands show as you swim); it is restored out of first person, and the shadow is headless while you are in it. The eye now sits along the head's own axes, 10 cm up the skull, rather than offset along the body's level facing (#3291).
- **Aiming down while swimming dives.** At the surface a swimmer's buoyancy (set so the swim pose floats on the waterline) lifted about as fast as a downward stroke sank, so pitching down with the right stick and swimming went nowhere, and up is capped at the surface by design: the stick seemed to do nothing either way. A stroke aimed down now takes the vertical from buoyancy in proportion to how steeply and how hard you swim (`diveBuoyancy`); let go and buoyancy surfaces you as before. Measured in the new pool: 1.3 m deeper in two seconds, where it was 0.3.
- **An open inventory survives entering or leaving a headset.** Opened flat, then into VR, the loadout came up small on its shoulder still showing the bag, and a tap did nothing (it was already open), there and back out. A session change rebuilds the frame panels, and the new one never heard the dock's `panelfocus`. Content now also marks its SVG `data-focus="true"` while focused, and a frame panel made later starts from it (#3290).
- **A sun's shadows can be turned off**: `<tosi-b3d-sun shadows="off">` (`'on'` by default; live, so a toggle works). The demos, the README and this repo's notes passed `shadowCascading: true`, which was never an attribute: shadows are always cascaded, and `shadowCascading: false` silently did nothing. It is gone from every example.
- **No more fine bands over every lit surface.** `<tosi-b3d-sun>`'s `shadowBias` default is 0.0005 (was Babylon's 0.00005). With `shadowNormalBias` at 0.02, which has to stay low or thin limbs lose their shadow, plain scenes (the primitives and getting-started demos) were striped with shadow acne on the ground, the boxes and the spheres. A character's shadow is unchanged. The attribute table also said `shadowNormalBias` defaulted to 0.05; it is 0.02.
- **The checker ground is checkered.** `b3dGround({ texture: 'checker' })` drew one flat grey: the texture clamped at its edge instead of repeating, so every tile past the first was the edge colour. It repeats now, and is mipmapped so it does not shimmer toward the horizon. Its dark squares are 70% of the ground colour (they were a fixed grey barely darker than the default ground).
- **Getting started opens on a running scene**: the first scene is a live example, and below it the same scene as plain HTML markup, live too.
- **A star system keeps real time.** Every day, month and year is the real one, and a new `timeScale` attribute (simulated seconds per real second, default 3600: an hour a second, an Earth day in 24 seconds) says how fast it runs; both demos have a log **time** slider from real time to a year every ten seconds. Planets used to turn once in about 80 seconds against a 60-second year, so they looked still, and moons took longer to go round their planet than the planet took to go round the Sun. Now `SystemPlanetSpec.day` (Earth days, negative backwards) and `SystemBodySpec.period` (a moon's month in days, negative backwards) carry the truth for Sol (Venus and Uranus turn backwards, Triton goes round backwards); a generated moon gets Kepler's month for a true distance (`moonPeriod`), a generated rock an Earth day, a giant a Jupiter one. Orbits, months and days are angles of one clock (`spinAngle`), so they keep time together and stop together with `animate`.
- **Dragging on a frame panel no longer turns the camera.** Flat, the camera's own controls took the same pointer, so a drag across a panel orbited the view behind it. A press on a frame panel now holds the camera's controls until release (#3290).
- **A drag that leaves its panel at once still drags.** A press on a thing, then a pointer that was already over another panel by its next move (a controller ray moves in big steps; so does a fast flick), forgot the press and dragged nothing. Leaving a panel with a thing pressed now starts the drag. Found driving the loadout with an emulated controller (#3290).
- **A trigger press in VR always counts, whichever hand it is.** Babylon points with one controller, the first to connect, and a press on the other one only switched to it: the press was dropped, so the first press of a session (and any press after the headset swapped controllers) did nothing. Now the right hand points first, and a press on the hand that is not pointing switches to it and is delivered. It reads Babylon's private per-controller state; a Babylon upgrade that renames it brings back the dropped press rather than breaking anything (#3290).
- An inventory panel's totals line is always there, so the first thing worn no longer pushes the schematic down (#3290).
- **Dragging between inventory panels works with a finger or a headset's laser.** Both are captured by the element they press, so the moves and the release never reached another panel; `inventoryPanel` now lets the capture go as it arrives (a mouse was never captured, which is why it worked on a desktop). And on a page the ghost is drawn in one overlay above every panel (`carryOverlay(carry)`, with `carryPanel(…, { ghost: false })`), so it crosses from one panel to the next instead of being clipped by each. A panel on a 3D plane keeps its own ghost (#3290).

- **A thing can be dragged out of a socket** (it could only be dragged out of a list), and a thing in a list is itself a place to drop into that list, so a long, scrolled list takes a drop anywhere. A thing put back in a list joins a stack of its kind with room (a missile returned to the carrier is counted again); one drawn from a stack swaps with what a slot held.

Size: barrel (min, packages external) 1082.1 KB raw / 368.9 KB gz, +3.80% on 0.10.5.
